questions.question:
Select the physician who is most likely to direct the care of critically ill patients or
those admitted to the ICU:
questions.explanation:
The hospitalist most likely directs the care of patients admitted to areas of the hospital outside of
critical care.
The intensivist is most likely to direct the care of critically ill patients or those admitted to the
ICU.
Radiologist use imaging to diagnose and treat disease.
Gastroenterologists are a subspeciality of internal medicine; they focus on diagnosing and
treating diseases of the gastrointestinal tract and liver.

questions.question: A bloody tap during lumbar puncture can be due to?
questions.explanation:
Intracerebral hemorrhage generally does not present with blood in the CSF
If the aorta is accidently injured, the blood flow can be spurting but it is very rare unless the
needle was not in the midline. Injury to the intercostal artery is extremely rare during a lumbar
puncture
Blood observed after a LP in the first tube is usually traumatic and may be due to injury to the
spinal venous plexus
Often the fluid will clear as succeeding tubes are filled. If the red blood cells have been in the
spinal fluid for some time, xanthochromia will be present

questions.question:
A 40-year-old female presents with headache. She has been having forgetfulness on
occasion but no other past medical history. A tumor was found and resected via parieto-occipital
craniotomy with transcortical approach. Synaptophysin is strongly positive by immunohistochemistry.
Which of the following is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
¼ of cases occur in the third ventricle and ¾ occur in the lateral ventricles
The cerebral hemispheres are rarely the location
Central neurocytomas may contain calcifications and radiologically are well circumscribed
globoid
Sheets of small round to polygonal isomorphic tumor cells with distinct cell membranes are seen
microscopically

questions.question: In which of the following cases would a lesion cause unilateral hearing loss?
questions.explanation:
The auditory neural pathway starts at the Organ of Corti and progresses, in order to the spiral
ganglion, vestibulcocochlear nerve, cochlear nuclei, lateral lamniscus, inferior colliculus,
medial genicualte gyrus of the thalamus, and to the primary auditory cortex (Henschl's gyrus)
Both ears project to both sides of the brainstem cortex via sever commissures
These include the trapezoid body, inferior colliculus, and the one connecting the right and left
nuclei of the lateral lemniscus
Therefore; any lesion up to the superior olivary nuclei will produce an ipsilateral deafness

questions.question: In a surgical incision, epithelium usually forms within:
questions.explanation: Epithelium is formed within 24 hours after surgery

questions.question: Which of the following is a site of neurogenesis in adults?
questions.explanation:
Neurogenesis in adults occurs in the subventricular zone lining the ventricles and at the
subgranular zone at the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus
Neurons and glial cells are produced by multipotent stem cells

questions.question:
MRI of the brain shows two lesions, but hyperintense on T2WI. One involves the
cerebellum extending into cerebral peduncles. The other involves an optic nerve. Which
neurocutaneous syndrome is most likely present?
questions.explanation:
NF 1 is associated with multiple astrocytomas, which are hyperintense on T2 weighting
NF 2 is associated with bilateral "acoustic neuromas," typically in the CP angles
Cerebellum and optic nerve locations are common for NF 1 astrocytomas
Tuberous sclerosis is associated with subependymal giant cell astrocytomas

questions.question:
A patient with recent gastrointestinal illness now has complaint of weakness and
numbness in the lower extremities, with exam findings of absent deep tendon reflexes in both legs
with symmetric weakness in both legs and his facial muscles; his most likely diagnosis:
questions.explanation:
Guillain-Barre syndrome classically presents as an ascending bilateral weakness in the
extremities with loss of deep tendon reflexes and may progress to cause respiratory failure; it
often follows a viral illness; treatment is with plasmapheresis and immunoglobulin
Botulism is characterized by bulbar and proximal muscle weakness but normal sensation and
reflexes; treatment is with immune serum
Poliomyelitis is a flaccid paralysis of one or more extremities with areflexia but no sensory
changes

questions.question: Which organism is most often responsible of meningitis in patients with VP shunts?
questions.explanation:
The most common organisms for neonatal meningitis is streptococcus agalactiae
Hemophilus influenza was the most common organism before the introduction of vaccination
Neisseria meningitidis is most common in adults
Staphylococcus epidermidis is responsible for 75 percent of shunt related meningitis

questions.question: Aneurysms most typically present with:
questions.explanation:
The most common clinical presentation of aneurysm is when they rupture, causing SAH
If the aneurysm is at the ICA-PCOM artery junction, it can compress the occulomotor nerve,
presenting with CN III neuropathy (strabismus, diplopia [affected eye is "down and out"], and
ptosis)
Ruptured aneurysms cause 80-90% of non-traumatic SAH
While more asymptomatic aneurysms are being found incidentally on imaging done for other
reasons, this is not the most common presentation

questions.question: A CSF leak after transsphenoidal hypophysectomy is initially treated with?
questions.explanation:
Most CFS leak will stop spontaneously
Asymptomatic most likely requires no intervention

questions.question:
Which of the following is appropriate treatment of simple uncomplicated urinary
tract infection?
questions.explanation:
Escherichia coli is the most common cause of urinary tract infection
Fluoroquinolones are one the drugs of choice for uncomplicated urinary tract infection
Patients with pyelonephritis and systemic signs of infection who are unable to orally or are
pregnant should be treated with parenteral antibiotics
Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole is another commonly used antibiotic for UTIs

questions.question: Which form of hepatitis has the highest contracting risk from a needle stick?
questions.explanation:
30% of those with needle sticks contaminated with hepatitis B develop symptomatic infection
while 37 to 62% seroconvert.
Hepatitis C has a risk of 0.5 to 1.8% of seroconversion.
The risk is dependent on the amount of blood on the needle and the depth of the injury.

questions.question:
Which of the following substances, if suddenly discontinued, would most likely
result in a confused state?
questions.explanation:
Confusion often results from acute alcohol withdrawal.
Delerium tremens may also be life-threatening.
Opiate withdrawal, although uncomfortable, does not result in delirium.

questions.question:
A patient with right sided conductive hearing loss will have Weber test lateralized
to the:
questions.explanation:
A patient with right-sided conductive hearing loss will have Weber test lateralized to the right
side

questions.question:
In an HIV male, which of the following is the most common cause of both lung and
brain abscess?
questions.explanation:
Cryptococcus initially always causes an infection followed by development of meningitis
Cryptococcus can cause pneumonia, pulmonary nodules or poorly defined mass lesions.
The clinical presentation of meningitis may include headache, seizures, confusion or gait
problems.
After the lung and brain abscesses, cryptococcus can also affect the skin resulting in nodules,
ulcers and vasculitis lesions.

questions.question: All of the following drugs act on cell membrane of microbes, except:
questions.explanation:
All but clarithromycin act on cell membrane on microbes
Clarithromycin inhibits protein synthesis of bacteria
Amphotericin B inhibits ergosterol synthesis on fungal cell membranes
Oxacillin and imipenem act on cell wall of gram-positive bacteria

questions.question:
A male has had a 4 year history of headaches but has developed generalized
seizures and bilateral leg weakness. CT shows calvarial hyperostosis and a mass. Biopsy of the mass
shows whorls and psammoma bodies. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
15% of intracranial tumors are meningiomas that originate from dura mater or arachnoid
They are benign and grow slowly presenting with mass effect
They cause osteoblastic reaction in the skull

questions.question:
The pedunculopontine nucleus has as its major neurotransmitter which of the
following?
questions.explanation:
Acetylcholine is responsible for the shift towards REM sleep
The nucleus basalis of Meynert is the main nucleus of acetylcholine predominance
The pedunculopontine nucleus (PPN) is one of the main components of the reticular activating
system
The PPN's functions include arousal, attention, learning, reward, and locomotion

questions.question: Diabetes insipidus should not be treated with?
questions.explanation:
Management for diabetes insipidus should aim to first replace free water deficit and give
vasopressin or desmopressin if needed

questions.question: Which statement is most accurate regarding the use of patient restraints?

answers.A: They are the preferred way to manage agitated patients
answers.B: They are used instead of sedative medications
answers.C: They are the best way to preserve a patient's autonomy
answers.D: They are indicated when a patient's behavior poses a significant risk of damage to equipment

questions.printed_answer_heading:
They are indicated when a patient's behavior poses a significant risk of damage to
equipment
questions.explanation:
Patient restraints are indicated when a patient's behavior poses a significant risk of damage to
equipment or injury to himself or others
They violate a patient's autonomy and should be used only when other methods of behavior
control have failed
Sedatives should generally accompany the use of restraints

questions.question:
Which one of the following signs and symptoms is not seen in type I
hypersensitivity reactions?
questions.explanation:
Type I reactions are secondary to vasoactive mediators released by mast cells and basophils.
Pruritus and urticarial rash are common.
Flushing, angioedema of the face, extremities, or laryngeal tissues can also occur
Hypotension, rather than hypertension, is also one feature of a type 1 reaction.

questions.question: Phagocytic cells in the brain are known as:
questions.explanation:
Microglia are the resident macrophages of the brain and spinal cord. They make up nearly 20%
of the total glial cell population
Microglial cells are constantly scavenging for virus, plaques and damaged neurons
There are no antibodies in the brain and thus these cells are effective and efficient
Microglia are also sensitive to electrical changes and their movements are controlled by influx
of potassium

questions.question:
A 17-year-old male hit on the head with a baseball bat. Deep painful stimulus
causes him to open his eyes and withdrawal and he mumbles incomprehensibly. What is his Glasgow
coma scale score?
questions.explanation:
The Glasgow coma scale standardizes assessment and allows for documations of findings and
clinical course. It also is predictive of prognosis.
The maximum score is 15 and is comprised of best verbal response, best motor response, and
eye opening.
Scores of 8 or less for 6 or more hours is associated with severe neurologic injury.
This patient received 2 points for opening his eyes to pain, 4 points for withdrawing from pain,
and 2 points for mumbling incoherently for a total of 8 points.

questions.question: Which of the following is false regarding carotid cavernous fistulas (CCF)?

answers.A: Commonly presents with diplopia and ophthalmoplegia
answers.B: Indirect CCFs are most common in men
answers.C: Barrow types A, B, and D involve the internal carotid artery
answers.D: Commonly presents on imaging with a dilated superior ophthalmic vein

questions.printed_answer_heading: Indirect CCFs are most common in men
questions.explanation:
CCFs are shunt between ICA, +/- ECA and the cavernous sinus.
Indirect CCF is a dural venous fistula with multiple feeder arteries, these are more common in
females.
Direct CCF is typically made up of one feeder vessel (ICA most common) and one fistula
resulting in direct high flow, these are most common in males.
Endovascular therapies with balloon detachment (direct CCF) or TV coil embolization (indirect
CCF) are the most common.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a feature of opioid toxicity?
questions.explanation:
The classic triad of morphine toxicity included depressed level of consciousness, depressed
respiration and miosis
Others may present with drowsiness, conjunctival injection and euphoria
Hypotension is common with morphine due to peripheral vasodilatation

questions.question: At what rate is ketamine usually infused to treat neuropathic pain?
questions.explanation:
Neuropathic pain is normally described as short, shooting, burning, and localized
Pharmaceutical treatments include propofol, clonidine, and ketamine
Propofol is a GABA A receptor agonist
Ketamine intravenous infusion at rate of 6 mg per kg per minute

questions.question:
The most important factor in perioperative adverse drug reaction in the elderly
population is:
questions.explanation:
More than 50 percent of elderly individuals treated with multiple medications experience a
variety of adverse side effects
Adverse side effects may range from short term, long term or idiosyncratic reactions that affect
cognition, gait, and the bodily functions
It is estimated that polypharmacy affects nearly more than 55% of elderly and causes 8-10% of
all adverse drug reactions
Besides age elderly patients have renal insufficiency, poor nutrition, liver disease and arthritis-
all factors that can increase severity of drug side effects

questions.question: Which of the following is used to treat hypothyroidism?
questions.explanation:
Hypothyroidism is treated with thyroxine hormone
Propylthiouracil is an antithyroid agent
Methimazole and propylthiouracil are contraindicated in hyperthyroidism

questions.question: Which of the following is not a cerebellar sign of dysfunction?
questions.explanation:
The cerebellum provides important feedback about muscle function and balance
Some common cerebellar signs of pathology include intention tremor, dyssynergia, dysmetria
and dysarthria
Dysthymia is mild depression that has been going on for at least 2 years

questions.question:
In people who develop Parinaud syndrome, the location of damage is usually
found in?
questions.explanation:
Parinaud syndrome is caused by lesion of the midbrain
Characterized by fixed pupils, lid retraction, and dissociation of light

questions.question:
During delayed surgery on a patient, the surgeon finds the two ends of a nerve.
Select the best option.
questions.explanation:
If a nonfunctioning nerve is discovered during surgery, the nerve should be stimulated to
determine if there is any distal muscle movement or action potential
In the absence of any transmission across the nerve, the two ends should be excised and
resutured without tension
If some nerve transmission is seen, then only neurolysis should be attempted

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common type of brain tumor in children?
questions.explanation:
Supratentorial low-grade astrocytoma is the next most common type of brain tumor in children
Medulloblastomas are the most common childhood brain tumor
Cerebellar astrocytomas are third most common types

questions.question:
Of the following statements, regarding the lipid bilayer (cell membrane) which is
false?

answers.C: Proteins are the most abundant based on weight

questions.explanation:
Phospholipids are the most abundant based on the number of molecules
Proteins make up the channels in the lipid bilayer

questions.question: Which is true of atelectasis?

answers.A: Is a rare post operative complication
answers.B: Is a common cause of early fever after surgery

questions.printed_answer_heading: Is a common cause of early fever after surgery
questions.explanation:
Atelectasis is a condition commonly seen after surgery. The condition usually presents with
collapse of part of the lung
Atelectasis can present with dyspnea and low-grade fever. Diagnosis is made by chest x-ray
Atelectasis usually occur when the large airways are blocked by mucus, secretions or foreign
body
Smoker should be asked to discontinue smoking 6 weeks prior to elective surgery to prevent
atelectasis

questions.question: Which is false about treatment of cerebral edema?
questions.explanation:
In the past, standared of car for head injury was fluid restriction to minimize the development
elevated ICP and cerebral edema
Fluid restriction will decrease intravascular volume and therefor decrease cardiac output
Decreased cardiac output is likely to cause decreased cerebral blood flow, and resultant
decreased brain perfusion
Fluid restriction is no longer recommended in patients with cerebral edema rather fluid balance
to achieve a euvolemic state.

questions.question: The local anesthetic, lidocaine, works by blocking:
questions.explanation: Local anesthetics block sodium channels that are responsible for action potential

questions.question: The development of the conus medullaris involves which of the following?

answers.A: The conus medullaris is above T12 at term
answers.B: The conus medullaris is at L2 by 18 weeks gestation
answers.C:
The difference between the growth rate of the spinal cord and the vertebral column accounts for
the ascent of the conus medullaris
answers.D: The level of the conus medullaris bears no relationship to the vertebral column

questions.printed_answer_heading:
The difference between the growth rate of the spinal cord and the vertebral column
accounts for the ascent of the conus medullaris
questions.explanation:
The conus medullaris ascends between 13 and 40 weeks of gestation
At term the conus medullaris is above the L2 vertebrae

questions.question:
Which of the following would be appropriate initial treatment for a herniated
cervical disc of the spine with cervical nerve root compression?
questions.explanation:
Acute nerve root compression with a herniated disc should be treated with bed rest and cervical
traction.
NSAIDs and ice are additional conservative treatments.
Persistent symptoms may require intrathecal steroids or surgical intervention.

questions.question: Which is not a symptom of sialidosis?
questions.explanation:
Sialidosis is an autosomal recessive disease
Characterized by blindness, seizure, and dementia

questions.question:
Patients on bed rest may be encouraged to periodically plantar and dorsiflex their
ankles. What is the rationale for this?

answers.D: To increase blood flow to the legs

questions.explanation:
Plantar and dorsal flexion of the ankles promotes venous return from the lower extremities
Venous stasis is a risk factor for deep venous thrombosis (DVT)

questions.question:
A newborn has a lumbar meningomyelocele. The neonate's weight is appropriate
for gestational age and has a vigorous cry. It has a good urine stream, clubfeet, and spontaneous
flexion and extension at the knees. A sterile dressing has been placed over the defect. Select the
correct statement about this patient.

answers.A: This was caused by a deficiency of folic acid
answers.C: The most common cause is gestational diabetes
answers.D: The mother probably drank alcohol during the first month of pregnancy

questions.explanation:
Known causes of neural tube defects are folate deficiency, maternal anticonvulsants, multiple
malformation syndromes, chromosomal disorders, and first trimester hyperthermia
85 to 90% of patients with meningomyelocele have Arnold Chiari malformations causing
hydrocephalus
This is treated with a ventriculoperitoneal shunt

questions.question: The best test to assess function of platelets is which of the following?
questions.explanation:
The platelet function time is a new method of assessing platelet function
This vital test measures time required for a platelet plug to occlude an aperture in a membrane
containing some collagen
The bleeding rime is no longer used today and is not satisfactory for use in children
Platelet aggregation has been used to evaluate neonatal platelet function but there is a lot of
difficulty in obtaining adequate blood from neonates without it first clotting

questions.question:
Select the choice that describes the pathway that hormones from the hypothalamus
reach the pars distalis.

answers.A:
Secretory granules - extracellular space - primary capillary plexus - hypophyseal portal system -
secondary capillary plexus - cells of the pars distalis
answers.B:
Secretory granules - primary capillary plexus - extracellular space - hypophyseal portal system -
secondary capillary plexus - cells of the pars distalis
answers.C:
Secretory granules - extracellular space - secondary capillary plexus - hypophyseal portal
system - primary capillary plexus- cells of the pars distalis
answers.D:
Secretory granules - extracellular space - hypophyseal portal system - primary capillary plexus -
secondary capillary plexus - cells of the pars distalis

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Secretory granules - extracellular space - primary capillary plexus - hypophyseal
portal system - secondary capillary plexus - cells of the pars distalis
questions.explanation:
Secretory granules - extracellular space - primary capillary plexus - hypophyseal portal system -
secondary capillary plexus - cells of the pars distalis
A key to understanding the endocrine relationship between hypothalamus and anterior pituitary is
to appreciate the vascular connections between these organs
Secretion of hormones from the anterior pituitary is under strict control by hypothalamic
hormones

questions.question:
A patient with depression is being started on a tricyclic antidepressant medication.
Which of the following is true about the medication?

answers.B: It will help decrease neuropathic pain
answers.C: It lowers the risk for seizures

questions.printed_answer_heading: It will help decrease neuropathic pain
questions.explanation:
Besides depression, tricyclics antidepressants can also relieve pain from a variety of disorders
Individuals with neuropathic pain or those who have difficulty sleeping may respond well to
tricyclic antidepressants
Tricyclic antidepressants usually take 2-3 weeks to work. All tricyclic anti depressants lower
the thresh hold for seizures and should be used with caution in individual with head trauma
Other common side effects of these medications include anticholinergic affects like dry mouth
and the orthostatic hypotension

questions.question:
The posterior division of the ventrolateral nucleus of the thalamus sends efferent
projections to the?
questions.explanation:
Cerebellar nuclei are the principal source of efferent fibers from the cerebellum projecting to the
dorsal thalamus, vestibular nuclei, red nucleus, and other brain stem nuclei.
The dentate nucleus receives projections from Purkinje cells in the cerebrocerebellum, and
collaterals from some of the pontocerebellar fibers.
Fibers from the dentate nucleus enter the brachium conjunctivum in the superior cerebellar
peduncle, cross at the level of the inferior colliculus, and terminate in the contralateral ventral
nucleus of the thalamus.

questions.question: Hemodialysis does not usually remove:
questions.explanation:
Phenytoin, carbamazepine, and valproic acid cannot be removed by dialysis
Amphetamines, phenobarbitol, and chlorporpamide are dialyzable

questions.question: What is the most common cause in the elderly of tremor?
questions.explanation:
2 to 5% of the population have benign essential tremor
Onset can be in adolescence or around age 50 years but incidence increases with age
Some patients have familial autosomal dominant disease
It affects males and females equally but females tend to have more head involvement while
males tend to have more hand symptoms

questions.question:
Tuberous sclerosis is a neurocutaneous syndrome associated with all of the
following except:
questions.explanation:
Sphenoid wing dysplasia is associated with neurofibromatosis.
Tuberous sclerosis also causes
Besides SGCT, in the brain tuberous sclerosis, also known as Bourneville disease, can show
subependymal nodules and cortical/subcortical tubers
In the kidney, besides angiomyolipomas, tuberous sclerosis also shows renal cysts,
oncocytomas, and rarely renal cell carcinoma

questions.question:
When educating an individual about a new medication it is most important to
teach:

answers.A: What the medication is for, amount to take, and how often to take it
answers.B: How the medication is processed in the body
answers.C: Possible interactions with food and other medications
answers.D: How to manage an allergic reaction or side effects

questions.printed_answer_heading: What the medication is for, amount to take, and how often to take it
questions.explanation:
The most important information is what the medication is for, amount to take, how often to take
it.
Other information can be shared after the key points are covered.

questions.question: Which is false about bupivacaine?

answers.C: Toxicity is related to sodium channel blockage

questions.explanation: The drug is an amide degraded by the liver

questions.question:
A 4 year old is brought in with persistent nausea, vomiting, and failure to thrive.
MRI of the brain shows an intensely enhancing mass in the left lateral ventricle and hydrocephalus.
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Choroid plexus papilloma is most commonly in a lateral ventricle in children and in the 4th
ventricle in adults
In children, it can cause hydrocephalus
Complete excision results in 84% survival at 2 years but subtotal resections result in an 18%
survival at 2 years

questions.question: Hemiplegic migraines are best described by which of the following statements?

answers.A: Auras are only manifested by motor deficits
answers.B: Such migraines always have an autosomal dominant inheritance
answers.C: Such migraines are never confused with ischemic strokes
answers.D: Attacks of such migraines can occur in children as young as 5 years old

questions.printed_answer_heading: Attacks of such migraines can occur in children as young as 5 years old
questions.explanation:
Hemiplegic migraines are a rare subtype that presents with neurologic signs and symptoms
indistinguishable from an ischemic stroke, with deficits persisting for hours to days
The mean age of onset is in the teens, but they can also occur in toddlers, usually occurring
sporadically or in an autosomal dominant pattern

questions.question: Which is the most effective way to prevent atelectasis after surgery?
questions.explanation:
Post-operative patients should have an incentive spirometer at their bedside so it is available for
frequent use (eg, every 1 to 2 hours)
Incentive spirometry is one of the most effective noninvasive methods to prevent atelectasis

questions.question: What substance is required to release the neurotransmitter?
questions.explanation: Calcium is considered a second messenger

questions.question:
A 4 year-old boy is brought to the emergency room after a fall. Lateral skull X-ray
a symmetrical oval defect of the right parietal bone. Which of the following is the most likely
diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The patient has parietal foramina, a defect in ossification around the parietal notch.
There is normally a fibrous membrane covering the opening.
These tend to ossify with age.
This condition can be an isolated finding or with syndromes such as Saethre-Chotzen or
proximal 11 p deletion syndrome.

questions.question:
Opioids have a variety of uses in medicine. Which of the following would be most
appropriate clinical use of opioids?

answers.C: Analgesic, sedatives, adjunct to psychotic therapy

questions.explanation:
Opioids are strong analgesics that are also useful in treating cough and diarrhea at low doses.
There is flexible as there is no maximum dose. They are increased gradually to relieve pain as
overdose can cause respiratory depression.
There is tolerance to side effects of sedation and constipation.
Hydrocodone and codeine are used for cough, diphenoxylate and loperamide for diarrhea, and
morphine for almost everything else.

questions.question: Which analgesic is not used in patient controlled analgesia pumps?
questions.explanation:
Fentanyl is a good analgesic for PCA
Morphine has multiple adverse effects
Hydromorphine has high potency
Oxycodone is not commonly used

questions.question:
A patient with rheumatoid arthritis develops vertigo, occipital pain, tinnitus, and
dysphagia. Which of the following may be the cause?
questions.explanation:
25 to 80% of patients with RA may develop atlantoaxial instability
Symptoms can include decreased range of motion, brainstem signs, and myelopathy
Excessive movement can compress the spinal cord or brainstem

questions.question: What part of the brain is affected in Parkinson disease?
questions.explanation:
Parkinson disease is caused by depletion of dopaminergic neurons from substantia nigra
It result in bradykinesia and postural instability

questions.question:
A head trauma patient develops anisocoria in the ER. Which of the following
statements is false about uncal herniation?

answers.A: There is compression of 3rd cranial nerve along the edge of the tentorium incisura
answers.B:
Compression of parasympathetic fibers on surface of 3rd cranial nerve causes unopposed
sympathetic dilation of pupil
answers.C: Progressive compression of 3rd cranial nerve leads to oculomotor paralysis
answers.D: The eye is usually deviated inferiorly and medially

questions.printed_answer_heading: The eye is usually deviated inferiorly and medially
questions.explanation:
Uncal herniation occurs when the uncal portion of the medial temporal lobe is pushed through
the tentorium compressing cranial nerve III which lies along the edge of the tentorium, The
parasympathetic fibers being on the surface of cranial nerve III are affected first. Unopposed
sympathetic activity causes pupillary dilatation which becomes fixed as the herniation
progresses.
The underlying brain injury causing the herniation leads to contralateral hemiparesis/plegia to
the dilated pupil. Sometime Kernohan's notch will prevail causing ipsilateral
hemiparesis/plegia. This occurs as the herniation compresses the midbrain corticospinal tract
against the opposite tentorium before the motor fibers cross.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep MAP > 60 mmHg?

answers.B: Allows better perfusion to the extremities
answers.C: Allows better perfusion to vital organs
answers.D: Increases blood flow to the central nervous system

questions.printed_answer_heading: Allows better perfusion to vital organs
questions.explanation:
Vital organs of the cardiac and renal systems require a minimal MAP to sustain adequate
functioning of organs

questions.question: What is the most common cause of status epilepticus (SE)?
questions.explanation:
The most common cause of SE is a change in antiseizure medication
SE is a neurological emergency
SE is an acute, prolonged seizure crisis
Diazepam is usually the drug of choice for treatment of SE in the prehospital setting

questions.question: Severe bleeding caused by heparin overdose can be reversed by:
questions.explanation:
Protamine binds to heparin and reverses the bleeding caused by it
Dipyridamole is anti-platelet medication
Aminocaproic acid can antagonize the effects of thrombolytic medications

questions.question: Of the following, which local anesthetic has the longest duration of action?
questions.explanation: Bupivicaine has the longest duration of action (2 to 4 hours)

questions.question:
A patient with chronic headache, stiff neck, and fever has lumbar puncture which
reveals bright green CSF color. You would suspect that he has:
questions.explanation: Pseudomonas meningitis is known to cause green CSF

questions.question: Select the choice which is FALSE concerning the Affordable Care Act:

answers.D: Passed by Congress and signed into law by President Obama in March 2010

questions.explanation:
Comprehensive health insurance reform is the goal of the Affordable Care Act.
Affordable Care Act emphasizes strong consumer protections.
The Affordable Care Act was intended to hold insurors accountable, lower health care costs,
guarantees more choice, and enhance the quality of health care for all Americans. Retrieved
from: www.whitehouse.gov
The Affordable Care Act was passed by Congress and signed into law by President Obama in
March 2010.

questions.question: If someone has bitemporal hemianopsia, the lesion is most likely at:
questions.explanation: Bitemporal hemianopsia is commonly associated with a lesion of the optic chiasm.

questions.question: How does one test function of cranial nerve XI?

answers.B: Have the patient shrug his or her shoulders while you resist the movement
answers.C: Have the patient stick out his or her tongue and move it from side to side
answers.D: Touch the pharynx with a cotton applicator

questions.printed_answer_heading: Have the patient shrug his or her shoulders while you resist the movement
questions.explanation:
Cranial nerve (CN) XI is the accessory nerve.
It is tested by having the patient shrug his or her shoulders while you resist the movement.
Having the patient say "ah" tests CN X, the vagus nerve.
Touching the pharynx with a cotton applicator tests CN IX, the glossopharyngeal nerve.

questions.question:
A 72-year-old male is admitted to the hospital for elective bowel surgery. The
patient claims that his wife died of a pulmonary embolus and it is decided to treat the patient
prophylactically to prevent a deep vein thrombosis. The least effective way to prevent a deep vein
thrombosis is :
questions.explanation:
Mechanical compression with compression stocking is widely used but the latest evidence
indicates that it must be combined with a pharmacological method to prevent DVT
Aspirin alone is not recommended and it does not help prevent DVT. Compared to LMWH,
aspirin fared worse than placebo
Both heparin and LMWH can be used as prophylaxis against DVT. LMWH have a long half-life
and less tendency to induce HIT. LWMH does not need any monitoring and is cost effective
Graded intermittent pneumatic stockings are also widely used and effective in preventing DVT

questions.question:
In a patient who has just aspirated during induction of anesthesia. Which of the
following is of no benefit?
questions.explanation:
Aspiration pneumonitis can occur during anesthesia and can add to morbidity
One can place an NG tube to suction of the stomach and place the patient on mechanical
ventilation
Hydration and maintenance of hemodynamics is vital
Corticosteroids have not been shown to be of benefit in patients who aspirate

questions.question: Which is not seen in Huntington disease?

answers.B: Involuntary movements, dementia, cognitive and behavioral change
answers.D: Loss of neurons in the thalamus, causing progressive chorea

questions.printed_answer_heading: Loss of neurons in the thalamus, causing progressive chorea
questions.explanation:
Loss of neurons in the basal ganglia and cortex are responsible for progressive chorea,
dementia, behavioral and cognitive deterioration
5-10% has a juvenile onset, likely acquired from father
Adult onset >20 years likely acquired from mother

questions.question: Walking on toes is controlled by:
questions.explanation:
L2 nerve root innervates hip flexion
Leg extension is indicative of L4 nerve root
L4 controls heel walking
S1 controls toe walking

questions.question:
A 33 y/o female with multiple sclerosis has a severe relapse which results in
bulbar involvement leading to intubation for respiratory support. High dose IV steroids do not help.
What would be an additional therapy to reverse the symptoms?
questions.explanation:
Plasmapheresis is a procedure that offers some possibility of therapeutic relief during this acute
attack. It is extracorporeal therapy and involves removing the blood products from the plasma. In
traditional plasmapheresis, the blood products are reinfused and the plasma is treated removing
antibodies before returning it to the patient
A more common approach, plasma exchange, involves separating the blood from the plasma. 2-
3L of plasma is usually replaced with a combination of saline and albumin reducing the disease
producing autoantibodies
Complications include bleeding, suppression of immune system, and risk of transfusion
transmitted diseases if donor plasma is used instead of saline

questions.question: In which of the following is osteoblastoma most commonly found?
questions.explanation: Osteoblastoma most commonly affects the vertebral column and posterior spinal elements

questions.question:
In the operating room, what is the most common source of electric current
leakage?
questions.explanation: The most common current leakage is the electrical conductor

questions.question:
Which of the following is the most common tumor that metastasizes to the brain in
which a primary tumor is not known at time of presentation?
questions.explanation:
Approximately 2/3 of all metastatic tumors to the brain in which a primary is not known turn out
to be lung carcinomas
All the above can commonly metastasize to the brain
Small cell lung cancers have a greater predilection for cerebral metastasis
Brain biopsy may be required if tumor type cannot be identified from cancer screening

questions.question: Which of the following bodily fluids can transmit HIV?
questions.explanation:
HIV can be spread by contact with blood, blood containing fluids, semen, and vaginal secretions
HIV cannot be contracted from saliva, sweat, or tears

questions.question:
A patient presents with ascending paralysis after a short period of diarrhea. Which
of the following investigations would most likely yield a positive result in this patient?
questions.explanation:
The patientis most likely having Guillain-BarrÃ© syndrome
Lumbar puncture would reveal raised serum protein level in GBS
MRI and other imaging techniques would not reveal any finding
Sometimes MRI enhancement may be seen but not in every case

questions.question:
A patient has a vertebrobasilar stroke and cannot speak or move. He can move his
eyes and is alert and oriented. What is the name for this condition?
questions.explanation:
Occlusion in the vertebrobasilar system can result in locked-in syndrome
The patient is unable to speak or move anything but the eyes
Total locked-in syndrome includes the eyes
The patient is alert and oriented in both conditions

questions.question: Sumatriptan belongs to which of the following classes of medication?
questions.explanation:
Sumatriptan is an example of a 5-HT receptor agonist
It is commonly used for treatment of Migraines
Sumatriptan should not be used in pregnant mothers

questions.question: Select the incorrect statement about spontaneous intracranial hypotension.

answers.A: It most often resolves with conservative management
answers.B: It typically lasts more than 1 month
answers.D: It has been effectively treated with fibrin glue epidural injection

questions.printed_answer_heading: It typically lasts more than 1 month
questions.explanation:
Spontaneous intracranial hypotension often resolves in 2 weeks with conservative treatment
Supine positioning reduces CSF pressure and allows the meninges to heal
The condition is most common in females over the age of 40 years

questions.question: The cause of Meleney gangrene is:
questions.explanation:
Meleney is a postoperative infection that results in gangrene
The gangrene is often the result of interaction between staphylococcus and streptococcus
Meleney gangrene is very painful and requires urgent debridement with broad spectrum
antibiotic coverage

questions.question:
A 65 year old having a nerve block may develop vasospasm when he is treated
with which method?
questions.explanation:
Alcohol delivery is commonly associated with vasospasm especially if there is accidental
intraarterial injection

questions.question:
A patient has been on prednisone for a few months and is now undergoing a
surgery. What corticosteroid should be administered to prevent adrenal collapse during surgery?
questions.explanation:
In general, patients who are on steroids and undergo surgery should be administered 100 mg IV
q 8h
After surgery, patients can resume their usual dose of corticosteroid
It should be remembered that hydrocortisone is 4 times less potent than prednisone

questions.question: Which of the following would be a permissible physician practice?

answers.A: Being a primary care provider for an immediate family member
answers.B: Writing personal prescriptions for controlled substances
answers.C: Treating an immediate family for anxiety with benzodiazepines

questions.explanation:
Physicians should not treat immediate family members, unless it's an emergency or another
qualified physician is not available
Personal prescriptions for controlled substances should not be written, except in case of
emergency
Same is true for immediate family members
Physicians should not be primary care providers for immediate family members

questions.question:
A patient has an ulcer on the heal that is through the dermis but stops at the
underlying subcutaneous tissue. What stage is the wound?
questions.explanation:
Stage I is erythema of the skin that does not resolve when pressure is removed
Stage II shows partial thickness skin involvement
Stage III has full thickness skin involvement and can extend to but not through the fascia
Stage IV shows breakdown of the underlying fascia

questions.question: Which lesion is associated with alexia with agraphia?
questions.explanation: Parietal lobe lesion can cause alexia with agraphia

questions.question: What would be the effect of a lacunar stroke involving the corona radiata?
questions.explanation:
Lacunar strokes affect non-cortical parts of the brain stem and cerebellum and are caused by
occlusion of the penetrating branches of cerebral arteries
Obstruction can be embolic or secondary to lipohyalinosis
Lacunar stroke affecting the internal capsule, pons, or corona radiate can cause ataxia
hemiparesis

questions.question:
What is the most likely mechanism of blockage of neuronal hyperexcitability by
topiramate?
questions.explanation:
Topiramate is used for migraine prevention as it suppresses neuronal excitability at the cortex
Multiple mechanisms are involved including the 3 listed in the question
Additional mechanisms are voltage-dependent sodium channel blockage and ANPA/kainate
blockage
These mechanisms are probably involved in chronic daily headache suppression

questions.question:
A patient is on a medical floor and wants to leave against medical advice. Which
of the following is not an option for a psychiatrist?

answers.A: Speak to the consulting caregiver about the issue
answers.B: Assess for competency and speak with the consulting caregiver
answers.C: Speak to the patient and do a mental status examination
answers.D: Discuss the criteria for involuntary commitment with the consulting physician

questions.printed_answer_heading: Assess for competency and speak with the consulting caregiver
questions.explanation:
Only a court or a court officer can make the legal determination of competency
Involuntary commitment generally requires a treatable mental illness in addition to a danger to
self or others
Assessing the patient's mental condition and understanding the clinical situation is the best
option

questions.question: Contact urticaria to latex is common in children with which condition?
questions.explanation: Children with spina bifida are somehow very sensitive to latex

questions.question: Which of the following nerves does not lie in the wall of the cavernous sinus?
questions.explanation:
The cavernous sinus is a large collection of thin-walled veins.
It is bordered by the sphenoid and temporal bones creating a cavity.
The wall contains the abducens nerve and the maxillary and ophthalmic divisions of the
trigeminal nerve.
The mandibular division is not in this area.

questions.question:
Which of the following breathing pattern is characterized by four to five breaths of
equal tidal volume followed by apnea?
questions.explanation:
Biot's respiration is an abnormal respiratory pattern characterized by apnea followed by 4-5
normal breaths then apnea.

questions.question:
A 63 year old suffers a stroke. The cause is emboli from the heart. The patient
expires and the autopsy reveals softening of the brain and edema. The type of necrosis is defined as:
questions.explanation: Liquefaction necrosis is transformation of solid tissue into fluid

questions.question: The diagnosis of myasthenia gravis is made by which agent:
questions.explanation:
Edrophonium is often used to make a diagnosis of myasthenia gravis
A positive response is not specific for myasthenia gravis as edrophonium can also increase
strength in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
Once the airway is secure, a patient is given a test dose of edrophonium. Patients with MG
respond dramatically with increased muscle strength and regain facial function
Sometimes cooling may improve neuromuscular transmission in patients with myasthenia gravis

questions.question:
After a stroke a patient has memory defects, contralateral sensory loss, thalamic
pain syndrome and homonymous hemianopsia. Which vessel was most likely involved?
questions.explanation:
Occlusion of the posterior cerebral artery can result in memory defects, contralateral sensory
loss, thalamic pain syndrome and homonymous hemianopsia

questions.question:
A 74-year-old female presents with headaches and CT of the head shows a right
hemisphere mass with associated overlying skull hyperostosis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Most brain tumors cause thinning of the bone
The exception in meningiomas, where hyperostosis can occur without bone infiltration
Calcifications inside brain tumors are most common in meningiomas, oligodendrogliomas,
astrocytomas, or metastatic lesions
17% of medulloblastomas have calcifications evident on CT scan

questions.question:
Select the structure that is in the midline of the brainstem from the medulla to the
midbrain.

answers.B: Mesencephalic tract and nucleus of V

questions.explanation:
The nucleus raphe magnus distributes serotonin throughout the brain
It is located adjacent to the midline of the reticular formation
The inferior olive is in the superior portions of the medulla and the central tegmental tract is
superolateral to the inferior olive
The mesencephalic tract and nucleus of V is adjacent to the central gray in upper pons and
mesencephalon levels

questions.question: Which chemical is accumulated in dialysis dementia?
questions.explanation:
Aluminum accumulation is the most likely toxic cause of dialysis dementia
Characterized by progressive dementia, confusion, and seizure
Associated of bilateral spike wave in 80 percent of patients

questions.question:
Rapid correction of hyponatremia may cause which of the following problems
that can lead to seizures, pseudobulbar palsy, dysarthria, coma, and death?
questions.explanation:
Central pontine myelinolysis (CPM) is an acute demyelinating condition that primarily affects
the pons, although some cases have concomitant extrapontine myelinolysis
It commonly occurs in alcoholic or malnourished patients who undergo rapid correction of
chronic hyponatremia
The clinical picture includes seizures, dysphagia, dysarthria, pseudobulbar palsy, behavioral
abnormalities, hyperreflexia, quadriplegia, and coma
The incidence of CPM is extremely low if the serum sodium is corrected slowly

questions.question:
Which of the following is most important when calculating maintenance IV fluid
for patients?
questions.explanation:
Urine output is vital information used to assess hydration status.
Blood pressure and pulse rate can be misleadingly normal.
Mucus membranes could dry out due to other reasons such as medications or NPO status.

questions.question:
Which of the following is false about pseudotumor cerebri (benign intracranial
hypertension)?

answers.A: May be associated with certain medications

questions.explanation:
There are multiple causes of pseudotumor cerebri.
These include medications such as cimetidine, corticosteroids, levothyroxine, minocycline,
nalidixic acid, tamoxifen, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, danazol, isotretinoin, lithium,
nitrofurantoin, and tetracyclines
It is most common in obese females age 20 and 50 years.
Withdrawal of corticosteroids, vitamin A toxicity, and tetracycline are causes in children but
recovery is spontaneous.

questions.question: Anaphylaxis usually does not present with which finding?
questions.explanation: Signs of anaphylaxis include rash and wheezing

questions.question: The major inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain is?
questions.explanation: GABA is the major inhibitory transmitter in the mammalian central nervous system

questions.question:
A paitient who a week earlier had several cold sores develops lethargy, high
fever, seizures and headaches. CT scan shows swelling of the temporal lobes. CSF has normal
glucose, elevated protein and elevated WBCs, predominantly lymphocytes. Cultures are negative. A
viral etiology is suspected. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
HSV is the most common cause of viral encephalitis. 90% caused by HSV-1 and 10% by HSV-2
HSV classically causes swelling in the temporal lobes while most other viral infections produce
diffuse cerebral edema.
A definitive diagnosis can many times be established by testing the CSF with a combined
indirect ELISA (enzyme linked immunoabsorbent assay) and immunoblotting assay checking for
intrathecal synthesis of IgG antibodies to HSV

questions.question: Hip flexion is innervated by:
questions.explanation:
L2 nerve root innervates hip flexion
Leg extension is indicative of L4 nerve root
L4 controls heel walking
S1 controls toe walking

questions.question:
A 23-year-old female volunteered at a school carnival for a day and had to stand
for 8 hours. She noted that her right foot felt cold and her right leg had pins and needles. The
symptoms resolved in about a week. She had mild low back pain but no symptoms at the left lower
extremity. 3 years ago the patient had optic neuritis that responded to treatment with corticosteroids
and has not recurred. MRI at that time was normal. She has no other past medical history but is on
oral contraceptives. She does not use illicit drugs but drinks alcohol occasionally. Exam shows
Babinski in the left, brisk reflexes, and clonus at the left ankle. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
16% of patients with optic neuritis and normal MRI develop MS within 5 years
MS is most commonly diagnosed in patients age 15 to 45 years and is seen in females at more
than twice as much as males
These findings would not occur with a TIA and a TIA would last more than 24 hours
Lumbar disc disease is a less likely possibility

questions.question:
A 27 year old female with SLE on prednisone daily presents to the emergency
department with a 10 day history of headaches and low grade fever. Basic CT is normal and lumbar
puncture shows 200 WBC/µL, mostly monocytes. Protein is 220 mg/dL, glucose 50mg/dL, and there
were no RBCs. Select the test that is most likely to provide the diagnosis.
questions.explanation:
The patient is immunosuppressed with findings suggestive of cryptococcal meningitis
Diagnosis is made by India ink stain or latex agglutination
N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor subunit NR2 (anti-NR2) antibodies are seen in SLE
related neuropsychiatric pathology but this is not the most likely diagnosis
A patient with bacterial meningitis is unlikely to have survived symptoms for 10 days

questions.question: Which is the most common extra cranial solid tumor of childhood?
questions.explanation:
Neuroblastoma is the most common tumor of infancy and the mosgt common extra cranial cancer
of childhood.
It arises from neuroblasts or pluripotent sympathetic cells. It is embryonal and derives from the
sympathetic nervous system
The adrenal gland is the most common location.
Elevatetion of catecholamines in urine confirms the diagnosis.

questions.question: Which is not associated with the use of tramadol?
questions.explanation:
Tramadol has analgesic and antidepressant effect
It is also associated with seizures
Respiratory depression is not seen

questions.question:
All of the following drugs are used to control elevated intracranial pressure
EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Atracurium is a non-polarizing neuromuscular blocking agent to be used when a patient is
posturing or bucking the respirator which can raise ICP
Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic but must be used with caution in order to not reduce the
intravascular space too much which could reduce perfusion to the brain
Pentobarbital can be sedating besides improving cerebral tissue oxygen tension and reducing
neuronal activity of an injured brain. Caution must be exercised to not drop BP too low

questions.question:
An immunocompromised male presents with 3-month history of seizures. MRI
reveals a temporal lobe lesion. CSF fluid analysis reveals multinucleated giant cells with
intranuclear inclusions. The most likely cause is:
questions.explanation:
Sporadic viral encephalitis is most commonly caused by the Herpes virus. The virus has a
predilection for the temporal lobe
Herpes can cause aseptic meningitis and fever or rapidly progressive and severe encephalitis
with altered consciousness
Histology shows focal necrotizing vasculitis lymphocytic infiltration of perivascular regions and
the meninges.
Neurons and glial cells can show eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding preoperative evaluations is correct?

answers.A:
A patient with a previous coronary bypass graph 2 years earlier should undergo cardiac stress
testing before clearance, regardless of the presence of cardiac symptoms
answers.B: Urine pregnancy testing should be done for women of childbearing age
answers.C: Coagulation studies should be included in your laboratory assessment of all surgical candidates
answers.D:
Patients who have had angioplasty within 6 months are not required to have further cardiology
assessment

questions.printed_answer_heading: Urine pregnancy testing should be done for women of childbearing age
questions.explanation:
The most important preoperative evaluation is the history. It was commonplace to do extensive
labs, radiographs, and cardiac evalutions in the past.
Many of these have been found have no effect on outcomes.
The test that most important is a urine pregancy test as all women of childbearing years should
be consided pregnant until proven otherwise. Many patients deny sexual activity and are
pregnant.
Other specific tests should be guided by patient history, age, and facility requirements.

questions.question:
Which of the following patients does not need a CT or MRI before lumbar
puncture?
questions.explanation:
Antibiotic therapy should be started as soon as possible with suspected bacterial meningitis
Imaging before a lumbar puncture is to avoid herniation secondary to increased intracranial
pressure
Contraindications to lumbar puncture without CT are papilledema, history of recent head trauma,
suspected intracranial lesions such as known malignancy, focal neurologic findings, or
depressed level of consciousness
Kerning or Brudzinski signs imply meningeal irritation and not elevated intracranial pressure

questions.question:
A spinal trauma patient loses the ability to use rib or abdominal muscles but is
still able to breath because the diaphragm contracts. Which of the following levels is consistent with
this description?
questions.explanation:
The phrenic nerve originates from C3 to C5
A lesion at T5 would spare the respiratory muscles of the ribs
A C2 lesion would paralyze the diaphragm

questions.question: Which best defines nociceptors:

answers.A: Are specialized organelles at the ends of A-delta neurons.
answers.B: Originate from neuronal cell bodies in ventral horn of spinal cord.
answers.D: Are only found in skin and fatty tissue.

questions.explanation:
Nociceptors are not specialized structures; they are free nerve endings of A-delta and C neuron
axons
They arise from neuronal cell bodies located in the dorsal horn ganglia of the spinal cord or the
trigeminal ganglia.
They respond to mechanical, temperature, and chemical stimuli.
They are located in many parts of the body, including skin, subcutaneous tissues, joints,
periosteum, most organs, and walls of blood vessels.

questions.question: Which of the following occurs as a result of tearing of bridging cortical veins?
questions.explanation:
Subdural hematomas are most commonly a result of tearing of bridging cortical veins and
typically appear as a crescentic shaped fluid collection, which crosses sutures.
Most commonly supratentorial and extends but does not cross the falx.
Patients can experience a lucid interval similar to the presentation of an epidural hematoma.
Typically has a poor outcome with midline shift >20mm associated with significant morbidity
and mortality.

questions.question:
Which subtype of craniosynostosis is caused by premature closure of the sagittal
suture?
questions.explanation:
Premature fusion of sutures is called craniosynostosis.
More than half of craniosynostosis involve the sagittal suture.
Premature infants are most likely to develop scaphocephaly.
If both coronal sutures fuse prematurely his is brachycephaly and there is increased biparietal
diameter.

questions.question:
Which muscle is attached to the transverse processes of the upper cervical
vertebrae?
questions.explanation:
The levator scapulae is located on the posterior lateral neck
It arises from the transverse processes of the axis and atlas as well as the transverse processes
of the 3rd and 4th cervical vertebrae
It inserts on the scapula

questions.question:
Collagen synthesis in a wound after 10 to 13 days would have collagen
synthesis. Which of the following would be evidence of this?
questions.explanation: Collagen synthesis would be evidenced by presence of hydroxyproline

questions.question: What is the most frequent mode of transmission in nosocomial infections?
questions.explanation:
Contact transmission is the most common and frequent cause of nosocomial infection
Hand washing is the single most important measure of infection prevention
Isolation precautions also prevent transmission by common routes

questions.question: Pseudotumor cerebri is associated with increased pressure in the:
questions.explanation:
Pseudotumor cerebri causes increased intracranial hypertension
It is most common in obese women in their third decade but can occur at any age

questions.question: Which is false about Parkinson disease?

answers.B: Individuals who take selegeline should have the dose of levodopa reduced
answers.C: Muscle rigidity is ideally treated with an antispasmodic

questions.printed_answer_heading: Muscle rigidity is ideally treated with an antispasmodic
questions.explanation:
Parkinson disease is initially treated with medications. Levodopa is combined with carbidopa
as carbidopa reduces peripheral conversion of levodopa into dopamine. This results in higher
levels in the CNS.
Levodopa improves about 75% of patients and is most helpful for bradykinesias and rigidity.
Tremor does not respond as well.
Selegeline is an irreversible MAO-B inhibitor that takes time to have effect. Levodopa dosage
should be reduced in patients started on selegeline.
Tremor and rigidity can be treated witrh anticholinergics.

questions.question:
Which of the fives risk categories that all drugs have been assigned to in
pregnancy is not correct? (Five risk factor categories (A, B, C, D, and X) have been assigned to all
drugs based on risk to the fetus)

answers.A:
Category B drugs are those that have either demonstrated no fetal risk in animal studies or shown
an adverse effect in animal reproduction studies that has not been confirmed in controlled human
studies
answers.B:
Category C drugs are those for which neither animal nor human studies are available or drugs
for which animal studies have shown an adverse effect but there are no human studies
answers.C:
Category D drugs are those that have been shown to have adverse human effects but the benefits
of using the drugs may outweigh the risks
answers.D: Category X drugs can be used only under dire circumstances that involve a risk to the mother

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Category X drugs can be used only under dire circumstances that involve a risk to the
mother
questions.explanation: Category X drugs are contraindicated during pregnancy

questions.question: Which of the following is not true of appropriate medical documentation?

answers.A:
Documentation is essential to support the medical necessity and level of care for all services or
supplies provided at a specific time
answers.B: Protects the provider against allegations of malpractice
answers.C: After the fact documentation is acceptable when practitioners are especially busy
answers.D: Errors must be corrected when they come to the practitioners' awareness

questions.printed_answer_heading: After the fact documentation is acceptable when practitioners are especially busy
questions.explanation:
Documentation is essential to support the medical necessity and level of care for all services or
supplies provided at a specific time.
Documentation protects the provider against allegations of malpractice.
After the fact documentation is not acceptable; appropriate documentation takes place as soon as
practically possible upon the practitioner completing the action or activity.

questions.question:
A 25 year old obese female with 4 weeks of daily headaches accompanied by
nausea, vomiting, and blurred vision has papilledema on funduscopic exam but normal head CT and
CSF; her likely diagnosis:
questions.explanation:
Pseudotumor cerebri aka idiopathic intracranial hypertension is most common in obese women
of childbearing age
Patients will have increased opening pressure on lumbar puncture
Treatment includes weight reduction, acetazolamide for diuresis, and serial lumbar punctures for
ICP reduction

questions.question: Trigonocephaly involves deformity of which cranial suture:
questions.explanation:
Craniosynostosis is the premature fusion of the skull sutures.
Craniosynostosis is classified by the affected suture.
Trigonocephaly is the term to describe fusion of the metopic suture.

questions.question: Which spinal nerve is involved with the finger abduction?
questions.explanation:
Elbow flexion involves C5 and C6
Wrist extension involves C6, C7, and C8
Finger abduction involves C8 and T1
Flexion of the hip involves L2, L3, and L4

questions.question: Which is false about head trauma?

answers.A: Epidural hematoma can be intracranial or spinal
answers.B: Epidural hematomas are more common than subdural hematomas
answers.C: Skull fractures are often associated with epidural hematomas
answers.D: Spinal epidural hematomas may follow a lumbar puncture

questions.printed_answer_heading: Epidural hematomas are more common than subdural hematomas
questions.explanation:
Epidural hematomas are less common than subdural hematomas
Epidural hematoma should be suspected in any individual who sustains head trauma and has an
associated lucid interval
Spinal epidural hematomas may present with localized back pain, weakness, numbness, urinary
and fecal incontinence
The middle meningeal artery is involved in epidural hematomas over the temporoparietal area,
and the anterior ethmoidal artery nay be involved in frontal epidural hematomas.

questions.question:
Which of the following diseases particularly presents with lambdoid
craniosynostosis?
questions.explanation:
Patients affected by Carpenter syndrome have brachycephaly
This is caused by concurrent coronal, sagittal, and lambdoid craniosynostosis

questions.question:
A 62-year-old male has a one-week history of nausea, vomiting, and
paresthesias of the right hand and foot. The day of admission he had a generalized seizure followed
by a headache that increases when he bends forward. There is right facial droop and loss of double
simultaneous tactile stimulation. MRI shows a primary brain tumor. Which cell is most likely the
source of the tumor?
questions.explanation:
The most common brain tumor in adults is astrocytomas
Primary brain tumors make up 2 to 5% of all neoplasias
Children more commonly have tumors of the posterior fossa
Children most often have optic gliomas and cerebellar astrocytomas

questions.question: Which of the following is least associated with white matter lesions ?

answers.A: Mitochondrial myopathy, encephalopathy, lactic acidosis and stroke (MELAS)
answers.C:
Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy
(CADASIL)

questions.explanation:
White matter lesions are seen in women with severe migraines but not men.
MELAS and CARDASIL both cause white matter lesions.
Multiple sclerosis often has white matter lesions, especially in the periventricular areas.
Herpes virus but not EBV can cause white matter lesions.

questions.question:
A 48-year-old female presents with dizziness and MRI shows a cyst that
occupies almost half of the posterior fossa. There is inferior incomplete fusion of the cerebellum but
no hydrocephalus. What is her life expectancy?
questions.explanation:
The findings described are of Dandy-Walker malformation
Without obstructive hydrocephalus the patient may never have symptoms
With obstructive hydrocephalus, infants show macrocephaly and developmental delays
70% of patients have other associated anomalies including dysgenesis of the corpus callosum,
holoprosencephaly, dysplasia of the cingulate gyrus, malformation of the cerebellar folia, and
schizencephaly

questions.question: Which is least likely to be found in a patient with hemorrhagic shock?
questions.explanation:
Hemorrhagic shock is caused by hypovolemia
It is accompanied by a compensatory increase in heart rate

questions.question: Which of the following is false about filum terminale?

answers.B: Consists of two parts -the upper and lower
answers.C: Provides longitudinal support to the spinal cord
answers.D: Many nerves exist at the terminal filum

questions.printed_answer_heading: Many nerves exist at the terminal filum
questions.explanation:
The filum terminale is a delicate strand of fibrous tissue, about 20 cm in length and proceeds
downwards from the conus medullaris
The upper part is continuous with the pia matter and surrounding nerves
The lower part is adherent to the dura
The most inferior nerves exits the spinal cord at the level of the conus medullaris and not the
filum terminale

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes tremor?

answers.A: Violent, flinging movements typically involving the shoulder
answers.B: Very rapid, involuntary, repetitive contractions of a muscle or group of muscles
answers.C: Sustained simultaneous contraction of agonist and antagonist muscles
answers.D: Continuous, rhythmic, oscillatory movement of a body part occurring at rest or with movement

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Continuous, rhythmic, oscillatory movement of a body part occurring at rest or with
movement
questions.explanation:
Tremor is defined as a continuous, rhythmic, oscillatory movement of a body part occurring at
rest or with movement
Essential tremor is a familial form of tremor that improves with alcohol intake

questions.question:
A patient develops paralysis of the facial muscles on the left side. A
neurological exam by her provider reveals that the forehead muscles are not involved. What would be
the most appropriate intervention?

answers.B: Start IV antiviral such as acyclovir
answers.C: Order an immediate CT scan of the brain

questions.printed_answer_heading: Order an immediate CT scan of the brain
questions.explanation:
With a true Bell palsy it would not be possible to wrinkle the forehead
The supranuclear nuclei cross innervate the upper third of the face
The exam suggests a brain lesion as the cause of the facial findings

questions.question: Which of the following is false regarding aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage?

answers.A: Aneurysmal SAH is the most common cause of non-traumatic SAH
answers.B: Rebleeding in the first 2 weeks is commonly seen in 40% of patients
answers.C: The most useful imaging finding is hyperdense sulci on noncontrasted CT
answers.D: Vasospasm of associated vessels is present in >60% of cases

questions.printed_answer_heading: Rebleeding in the first 2 weeks is commonly seen in 40% of patients
questions.explanation:
Rebleeding, while common, is only seen in 20% of cases within the first 2 weeks following an
aneurysmal SAH.
Aneurysmal SAH most commonly presents with a sudden onset severe headache resulting in
50% mortality.
The best imaging exams to evaluate SAH are non-contrasted CT and CTA.
The most common locations for pooling blood include the cisterns and ventricles.

questions.question:
Which of the following is most likely the cause of a brain abscess in a patient
with AIDS?
questions.explanation:
Cerebral candidiasis can sometimes occur in people with severe immune damage
Candidiasis of the brain is not common, but could mimic the symptoms of toxoplasmosis brain
abscesses
Very rarely, Candida can spread to other organs such as the eye, liver and kidney
Other pathogens include Toxoplasma gondii, Aspergillus, and and Nocardia

questions.question:
Which of the following during the first trimester can cause congenital
hydrocephalus?
questions.explanation:
Infection with rubella or mumps during the first trimester can cause aqueductal stenosis leading
to hydrocephalus
The 3rd and 4th ventricles are connected by the aqueduct of Sylvius
The 3rd and lateral ventricles enlarge, as the CSF does not flow to the subarachnoid space for
reabsorption

questions.question: Which of the following is not a reversible cause of dementia?
questions.explanation:
Multiple conditions that cause altered mental status may resemble dementia. In order to make the
diagnosis, reversible causes due to endocrine, metabolic, or infectious etiologies should be
ruled out.
Multi-infarct dementia is a consequence of multiple strokes. Prompt diagnosis and treatment of
vascular disease is essential in order to prevent further cognitive deficits. Multi-infarct dementia
is considered irreversible.

questions.question: Upper cervical pain is associated with which dermatome?
questions.explanation: Upper cervical pain often involves C2 and C3 dermatome

questions.question: Which is true about brain abscess?

answers.A: The majority of infections are from spread elsewhere in the body
answers.B: Upper respiratory infections often result in brain abscess
answers.C: Most people have multiple brain abscesses
answers.D: Brain abscess are usually treated with antibiotics

questions.printed_answer_heading: The majority of infections are from spread elsewhere in the body
questions.explanation:
Brain abscess typically occur after spread from other parts of the body including the heart, lung,
kidney or within breast tissue
The presenting features are those of elevated ICP and can present with confusion, seizure,
hemiparesis and headache. A stiff neck and fever are common
Most common organisms include proteus, strep, pseudomonas, meningococcus or fungi. In AID
patients, TB, toxoplasma and Cryptococcus are common
The diagnosis is made with a CT scan that shows a ring-enhancing lesion. Treatment is
antibiotics plus drainage. H influenza and TB abscess usually are treated only with antibiotics

questions.question: Which factor can promote wound healing?
questions.explanation:
Zinc is an essential trace element and necessary for proper enzymatic functions in the body
Zinc deficiency has been associated with depressed growth, diarrhea, alopecia, impaired wound
healing, delayed sexual maturation and a variety of skin lesions
Zinc is readily available from food
Foods rich in zinc include sesame, celery, mustard, and a variety of seeds

questions.question:
A 40 year old male complains of progressive left sided headaches. The only
examination finding is a right sided drift. CT and MRI of the brain show a round, homogeneously
enhancing, calcified, dural-based lesion with compression of the left frontal lobe. Select the most
appropriate treatment.
questions.explanation:
The patient described has a meningioma
Surgery would confirm the diagnosis and allow for complete resection
Gamma knife is used for some meningiomas that cannot be resected safely but whole brain
radiation is not used
Chemotherapy is not effective for treatment of meningioma

questions.question: For L5 disk herniation, the best imaging study is?
questions.explanation:
CT is indicated for vertebral fractures
MRI is the best study for disk herniations

questions.question:
Surgical resection is most likely to successfully treat seizures for which of the
following?
questions.explanation:
Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumors, small low-grade gliomas, and small cryptic vascular
malformations have a 70 to 80% surgical success rate for resolution of seizures
Surgical resection of hippocampal sclerosis shows a 62% success rate
Surgical resection of large AVMs shows a 50% success rate
Gross cortical dysplasia rarely responds to surgical treatment

questions.question:
Which of the following tests would be best to identify the leakage of CSF
associated with spontaneous intracranial hypotension?

answers.A: MRI of the brain with contrast
answers.C: CT scan of the lumbosacral spine

questions.explanation:
Spontaneous intracranial hypotension is secondary to a spinal CSF leak
Symptoms include positional headache, MRI of the brain showing diffuse pachymeningeal
enhancement, and low CSF opening pressure
MR myelography or radioisotope cisternography can identify the leak
MR myelography is noninvasive and does not involve ionizing radiation but the images may be
affected by motion, paravertebral veins, fat, or CSF pulsatile flow

questions.question:
A 44 y/o patient has been taking steroids for years for sarcoidosis. Recently the
dosage was increased due to worsening of symptoms. He has noticed recently weakness in using his
shoulder muscles and walking. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Chronic use of steroids can cause myopathy. It mainly affects the upper/lower proximal muscles
and neck flexors.
Acute myopathy results from high dose corticosteroids which causes rhabdomyolysis.
This condition is more common with fluorinated steroids and dexamethasone than non-
fluorinated steroids or prednisone.

questions.question:
A 66 year old patient develops a thrombotic stroke and needs a thrombolytic. He
already received streptokinase 1 year before for a similar problem. Which of the following clot
busters can be safely used in this case?
questions.explanation:
The nonspecific clot busters are associated with hypersensitivity reactions
Streptokinase is antigenic, and can cause immunologic sensitization and allergic reactions,
particularly with repeat administration
Alteplase can be safely given since it is a recombinant tissue plasmin activator (TPA)

questions.question: What information do the posterior spinal cord columns convey?
questions.explanation:
Vibration, two point discrimination, proprioception, and vibration are conveyed by the posterior
columns
Temperature and pain are conveyed by the spinothalamic tract

questions.question: What type of duration of action is associated with lorazepam?
questions.explanation:
Lorazepam is a long acting benzodiazepine
It is used for status epilepticus, anxiety, and for short term insomnia

questions.question: Which is not a sign of an infection after a transsphenoidal hypophysectomy?
questions.explanation:
Nuchal rigidity, headache, and fever are all signs of meningitis post transsphenoidal
hypophysectomy

questions.question: Which one of the following is the primary sensory strip?
questions.explanation:
The postcentral gyrus within the parietal lobe is the primary sensory strip.
The cingulate gyrus is located immediately superior to the corpus callosum and is part of the
limbic system.
The precentral gyrus located within the frontal lobe is the primary motor strip.
The inferior frontal gyrus includes Broca's area.

questions.question: Which is a central cause of vertigo?
questions.explanation:
Stroke is a central cause of vertigo.
Vestibular neuronitis, Meniere disease, and benign positional vertigo are all peripheral causes
of vertigo.

questions.question:
Which of the following diagnosis most commonly has associated pulsatile
tinnitus?
questions.explanation:
Pulsatile tinnitus, unilateral or bilateral, is reported by up to 60% of those with IIH
The tinnitus is synchronous with heart rate and generally resolves when pressure is normalized
It is theorized that blood turbulence of flow from the intracranial space into the lower pressure
of the jugular vein is responsible
Intracranial bruit, dural AV fistula, or other CV disorders with audible increased flow may be
causes of pulsatile tinnitus

questions.question: Which pattern of injury is not seen in spinal cord trauma?
questions.explanation: Short cord is seen with labor, when the umbilical cord is short

questions.question: The normal intracranial cerebrospinal fluid volume in adults is?
questions.explanation: Intracranial CSF volume is about 75 mL

questions.question: What is the drug of choice to terminate status epilepticus?
questions.explanation:
It is necessary to rapidly treat of status epilepticus to prevent neurologic and systemic damage.
The treatment goal is should be diagnosis and termination of the seizures
Medications should be given intravenously for most rapid central nervous system therapeutic
levels. Benzodiazepines are very efficacious to treat both acute seizures and status epilepticus.
Lorazepam is consider the drug of choice as it is most effective, has a longer half life, and is not
a prodrug.
Benzodiazepines inhibit g-aminobutyric acid (GABA) by binding to the benzodiazepine-GABA
receptor.

questions.question:
Select the correct statement about primary angiitis of the central nervous system
(PACNS).

answers.B: Presentation is of headaches and infarcts causing focal deficits
answers.D: Patients often have malaise, weight loss, and fever

questions.printed_answer_heading: Presentation is of headaches and infarcts causing focal deficits
questions.explanation:
PACNS is characterized by headaches and infarcts causing focal deficits rarely accompanied by
malaise, weight loss, or fever
60 to 80% of patients show luminal irregularities, occlusion, or beading on catheter angiography
MRI can show mass lesion, diffuse white matter disease, hemorrhage, ischemic lesions, or
leptomeningeal enhancement
MRI, angiography, and CSF may not be diagnostic so brain biopsy may be needed

questions.question:
Which of the following patients is at greatest risk for developing a pressure
ulcer?

answers.D: Good range of motion with capillary refill of 3 seconds

questions.explanation:
Obese and confused patients may be at risk bu limited mobility is generally the greatest risk
factor.
