questions.question: Which of the following structure does not rise from neural crest cell?
questions.explanation: Neural crest cells give rise to dorsal root ganglia

questions.question:
Which of the following neurogenic tumors does not arise arise from sympathetic
ganglia?
questions.explanation:
Neurogenic tumors are most commonly seen in the posterior mediastinum.
They commonly originate from sympathetic ganglia, intercostal nerves, or the paraganglia cells.
Sympathetic ganglia give rise to neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma, and ganglioma.
Intercostal nerves give rise to neurosarcoma, neurolemmoma, and neurofibroma. Paraganglia
cells give rise to paraganglioma.

questions.question:
What would be the long term goal after rehabilitation for a patient with spinal
cord injury at T5?

answers.A: Moderate assistance for transfers and self-care
answers.B: Minimal assistance for transfers and independent self-care
answers.C: Moderate assistance for transfers and independent self-care

questions.explanation:
A patient with SCI at T5 usually have sufficient upper extremity strength, trunk balance, and
coordination to become independent for transfers and self-care
Patients with high thoracic or low cervical SCI often require assistance for self-care and
transfers
Patients with high cervical SCI usually will dependent for transfers and self-care

questions.question:
A patient with potassium of 2.7 mEq/L has no symptoms. Which of the following
is the appropriate action?
questions.explanation:
Oral potassium is adequate treatment for mild hypokalemia as defined as 2.5 - 3.5 mEq/L
If the potassium is difficult to correct the low magnesium may be a factor
EKG findings include flattened or inverted T waves, ST segment depression, and U waves

questions.question: Which area has the most epidural hematomas from trauma?
questions.explanation:
More than 75% of epidural hematomas are at the temporoparietal region. Skull fractures in this
area cross the middle meningeal artery
Frontal and occipital epidural hematomas account for about 20% of the cases
Two thirds of epidural hematomas are arterial and one third are from venous bleeding.
<20% of patients will initially be lucent with neurological worsening occuring subsequently.

questions.question:
An adult male is found to have a positive glabellar reflex. He may be
predisposed to developing:
questions.explanation:
Myerson's sign is also known as the glabellar reflex
When the patient is tapped on the glabellar, he is unable to resist blinking
The glabella is the area above the nose and eyebrows
Glabellar reflex is an early feature of Parkinson's disease but can be seen in other dementias

questions.question:
Which of the following is the most appropriate management of a patient with
raised intracranial pressure without any other structural abnormalities?
questions.explanation:
After ruling out herniation and other structural damages, lumbar puncture should be performed
Lumbar puncture can be both diagnostic and therapeutic
Lumbar puncture is a therapeutic option for pseudotumor cerebri

questions.question:
Select the condition that would be a contraindication to manual percussion with
postural drainage.
questions.explanation:
Postural drainage involves placing the head lower than the body and is contraindicated in
patients with increased intracranial pressure
The other options are indications for postural drainage

questions.question:
A 6 month old infant is brought to the emergency department after 3 generalized
seizures. The child had been healthy up this point. She had a one day history of loose stools. Exam
shows a temperature of 39.0°C, a stiff neck, and lethargy. Which of the following is indicated?
questions.explanation:
The infant has meningitis until proven otherwise
Lumbar puncture should be done to check opening pressure, cell count and differential, culture
and sensitivity, glucose, protein, latex agglutination, Gram stain, fungal stain and culture, and
AFB stain and culture
Antibiotics should be started if there is any sign of infection
The most common bacteria isolated in this age group are N. menigitidis, S. pneumoniae, and H.
influenzae

questions.question:
When discussing organ donation, families involved with the decision making
process should meet with:
questions.explanation:
Organ donation is decided on by family of the patient, organ procurement coordinator and the
patient's healthcare provider

questions.question: What is the most common seizure disorder in childhood?
questions.explanation:
Febrile seizures are the most common seizure disorder in childhood
They are categorized as simple or complex
Viral illnesses account for the majority of febrile seizures
Assurance is usually the treatment, although prophylactic antiseizure medications may be
considered with subsequent fevers

questions.question:
Select the best estimates of outsourced dollars spent on Disease Management by
2010
questions.explanation:
The costs of Disease Management were estimated to be $20 billion by 2010 according to theThe
Boston Consulting Group.
The compound annual growth rate of revenues for disease management organizations was 28%
in the years 2000-2005.
The growth percentage of employer-sponsored health plans offering disease management
programs at 58% in 2003 as reported by Mercer Consulting.

questions.question: Surgical anesthesia is provided in what stage?
questions.explanation:
The stages of anesthesia are analgesia, excitement, surgical anesthesia, and medical paralysis.
These stages do not depend on the method of delivery of anesthesia.
They are determined by body movements, oculomotor reflexes, muscle tone, and respiratory
rhythm.

questions.question:
What is the best treatment of severe metabolic alkalosis refractory to the usual
treatment?
questions.explanation:
HCL is sometimes used to treat severe metabolic alkalosis
HCL is indicated when there are arrhythmias, encephalopathy, or digoxin toxicity

questions.question:
An obese 45 year old undergoes gastrectomy. 5 days later, he has a foul smelling
discharge from his wound. All the following are contributing factors except:
questions.explanation:
Anyone can develop a wound infection postoperatively
Individuals at high risk for wound infections include diabetics, those on corticosteroids, and are
malnourished
Both radiation therapy and use of chemotherapeutic drugs are also risk factors
There is no correlation between type of suture used and wound infections as long as the proper
technique of closure has been utilized

questions.question:
A patient had traumatic brain injury in the past but has recovered to a high level
of cognitive function. To maintain independence the patient may still require assistance:
questions.explanation:
A patient with TBI at RLA level 10 will be able to do options 1, 2, and 4 but may have
problems when additional stress is present

questions.question:
The formation of the notochordal process begins with cells invaginating through
which structure during gastrulation?
questions.explanation:
The regional thickening of cells anterior of the primitive streak is Hensen's node
Cellular signals essential for gastrulation are secreted by Hensen's node
Gastrulating cells migrate anteriorly to form tissues in the future head and neck

questions.question: What does ageusia mean?
questions.explanation:
Ageusia is the loss of sense of taste
Anosmia is the loss of the sense of smell

questions.question:
A patient complains of dull, chronic headaches in the ocular area. The pain was
initially intermittent but has become constant. Sleep often relieves the pain but comes back in the
morning. Head movements often exacerbate the pain. There is plantar extension on the right. This is
most consistent with?
questions.explanation:
Awakening with a headache should be a warning sign of intracranial tumor
The pain is often constant, dull, and boring, and increased by coughing or straining
Focal localizing signs may be transient or absent
CT or MRI is indicated in patients with unexplained or prolonged headaches

questions.question: What is the typical presentation of an acoustic neuroma?

answers.B: Acute onset of vertigo lasting days to weeks

questions.explanation:
Acoustic neuroma presents as unilateral hearing loss and tinnitus which is constant and
progressive.
Symptoms of facial weakness, vertigo, and ataxia may occur with continued growth of the tumor.

questions.question: Foot drop is caused by:
questions.explanation:
The peroneal nerve wraps around the neck of the fibula and can become entrapped
This can be secondary to traction or stretching of the nerve, tight casts, Bakers cysts, ganglions,
total knee replacement, tight and the fabella
L5 nerve root compression can lead to foot drop

questions.question: Control of cerebellar proprioception is which of the following?
questions.explanation:
The cerebellum receives input from the dorsal nucleus of Clark
The information travels in the ipsilateral dorsal spinocerebellar tract
Conscious proprioception is from the dorsal column

questions.question: The most common mediastinal tumors in children and infants is?
questions.explanation:
Unlike adults, children and infants are more prone to neurogenic tumors in the mediastinum
The other tumors in children include foregut cysts, germ cell tumors, lymphomas and angiomas

questions.question:
A 28 year old male has surgical removal of a tumor by parieto-occipital
craniotomy using a transcortical approach. Immunohistochemistry shows synaptophysin. Select the
most likely diagnosis.
questions.explanation:
Central neurocytoma occur along the septum pellucidum in about 75% of cases
Radiographs generally show sell circumscribed globoid tumors with enhancement and
occasionally calcification
They show solid sheets of isomorphic cells that are polygonal or small and round resembling
honey combs
Synaptophysin is seen on immunochemistry

questions.question: The diagnosis of Bell palsy is made by:
questions.explanation:
Bell palsy is a clinical diagnosis and no imaging studies are required
However, imaging studies will be required to exclude any secondary compressive lesions.
Both CT scan and MRI are used to look at the brain to rule out tumor, non-cancerous mass,
infection and bone growth or metastasis

questions.question:
A 33 y/o female has an acute migraine headache lasting 5 hours with nausea and
vomiting. She had an inkling of an impending attack 24 hours earlier. Some relief was achieved in a
dark room with no sound. What symptom is not present in her symptom complex?
questions.explanation:
A migraine is a moderate to severe unilateral headache pulsating in nature lasting 4-72 hours.
There may be associated nausea, vomiting, phonophobia, and photophobia.
Women are more prone by a 3:1 ratio. 1/3rd have an aura, a transient visual, sensory, or motor
disturbance. It develops over 5-20 min. lasting for 60 minutes or less and the cephalgia starts
within 60 minutes.
Prodrome occurs 40-60%. It precedes headache several days before with altered mood or
irritability
Preventive treatment involves a variety of drugs including beta-blockers, calcium channel
blockers, antiepileptic medications, and tricyclic antidepressants. Early treatment involves using
triptans, NSAIDs, and ergotamines

questions.question:
Which of the following is true of the provider's ability to contain healthcare
costs?

answers.A: Acting as a gatekeeper in managed care plans
answers.C: Effective and efficient use of resources

questions.explanation:
Providers act as a gatekeeper to contain costs in the managed care system.
Providing appropriate and timely care is one of the many ways providers contain healthcare
costs.
The effective and efficient use of resources is among the ways providers contain healthcare
costs.

questions.question:
When assessing a mental status exam in a 71 year old, which question might you
ask to determine his remote memory?

answers.B: "What time did you get here today"

questions.explanation:
Remote memory is verbalized after hours, days, or years and may be assessed by asking a client
his or her mother's maiden name.
Asking questions about things that happened today, such as how long the patient has been at your
office, what time the patient arrived, and what he or she ate for breakfast, tests recent memory.

questions.question: Which anatomical organ is not involved in the oculocardiac reflex arc?
questions.explanation: The afferent pathway of the oculocardiac reflex involves the orbit and associated cranial nerve

questions.question: How does intracranial pressure change during a craniotomy with dura resection?
questions.explanation: With dura incision, the ICP is zero

questions.question: The diagnostic tests when suspicious of a prolactinoma should include:
questions.explanation: Prolactinomas are best visualized with an MRI

questions.question: Which of the following is not a test to diagnose myasthenia gravis?

answers.B: EMG/SFEMG (single fiber EMG) using repetitive nerve stimulation
answers.D: Testing for antibodies to beta-adrenergic receptors

questions.printed_answer_heading: Testing for antibodies to beta-adrenergic receptors
questions.explanation:
Serology testing for antibodies to acetylcholine receptors at neuromuscular junction is positive
in close to all of patients but is negative in 50% of ocular MG. Ice tends to strengthen weakened
muscles.
IV edrophonium (Tensilon) inhibits cholinesterase which blocks the breakdown of acetylcholine
leading to an increase of this transmitter.
EMG/NCV tests fatigability of muscles which is sensitive but not specific.
CT scan is ordered to exclude thymoma.

questions.question: Which of the following fact(s) about halo vest maintenance are correct?

answers.A: Treat pin sites with antiseptic and antibiotic ointment
answers.B: If pins become loose, re-torque to proper value
answers.C: 4-11% develop pressure sores underneath the vest

questions.explanation:
There should be routine inspection for pressure sores. If present, ensure patient changes position
regularly and treat locally. Sometime the vest may have to be refitted
Any readjustment or refitting of the vest requires monitoring neurological exam and getting post
adjustment cervical x-rays while maintaining neck alignment.
Instruments to remove vest should be taped to vest in case of need to remove in an emergency
such as cardiac arrest.

questions.question: The drug of choice during CPR is:
questions.explanation:
Many alpha-adrenergic drugs have been used for CPR
Today, epinephrine has been proven to be the most successful

questions.question:
The classic "Adam's" triad in a patient with normal pressure hydrocephalus
includes?

answers.D: Urinary incontinence, dementia and gait disturbance

questions.printed_answer_heading: Urinary incontinence, dementia and gait disturbance
questions.explanation:
Normal pressure hydrocephalus should be suspected when gradual progressive onset
incontinence, dullness of thought and memory disturbance, and gait disturbance or apraxia are
seen
Differential diagnosis includes Parkinson's and Alzheimer's for which it is often confused

questions.question:
What is the unilateral termination of a physician-patient relationship by the
physician?
questions.explanation:
Abandonment is the unilateral termination of a physician-patient relationship by the physician
Assault is a threat to do bodily harm
Battery involves touching another person without consent

questions.question:
A designated individual who can make healthcare decisions for someone other
than themselves is:

answers.B: A member of an ethics board

questions.explanation:
A designated health-care proxy is a person authorized to make health care decisions for another
person in the event they are unable to make their own due to health or emergent circumstances

questions.question: Cord astrocytomas most commonly occur in the ________ segment of the cord
questions.explanation:
Astrocytomas in the cord are derived from cord astrocytes
They are most common early in life
They account for 90% of intramedullary tumors in children less than 10 years old
They account for 60% of adolescent intramedullary tumors; most are cervical and upper thoracic
in location

questions.question:
55 year old man over 14 years develps protrusion of brows, increasing foot size,
and coarse facial features. Which pair of hormones may be responsible for his clinical features?
questions.explanation:
Patient most likely has a growth hormone secreting pituitary adenoma causing acromegaly.
A small percentage of patients have a non-pituitary GHRH (growth hormone releasing hormone)
tumor primarily located in the pancreas, lungs and adrenal gland
GHRH normally regulates GH production and is produced in the hypothalamus

questions.question:
A patient makes an appointment to establish. He has a 10-year history of a
seizure disorder. MRI of the brain shows mesial temporal sclerosis. Which of the following is true?

answers.B: The majority of mesial temporal seizures begin with generalized seizures
answers.D:
Secondary generalized seizures are usually suppressed with antiepileptic drugs but most patients
will continue to have partial seizures

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Secondary generalized seizures are usually suppressed with antiepileptic drugs but
most patients will continue to have partial seizures
questions.explanation:
Most mesial temporal seizures begin with visceral aura
There can be olfactory aura, a feeling of dÃ©jÃ  vu, or visual changes where objects grow
larger or smaller with aura followed by complex seizures
Oral alimentary automatisms are lip smacking, swallowing, chewing, and puckering
Upper extremity automatism are fumbling or picking

questions.question: Which of the following is an unusual cause of a brain abscess?
questions.explanation:
Etiologic causes of brain abscess are often polymicrobial
Gram positives and anaerobes are common causes
Gram negatives such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa are seldom implicated

questions.question:
A 30-year-old woman is involved in a motor vehicle accident. She complains of
neck pain and is 32 weeks pregnant. How should she be transported?

answers.D: Supine on a backboard with her right hip elevated

questions.printed_answer_heading: Supine on a backboard with her right hip elevated
questions.explanation:
The supine position can compress the great vessels after 20 weeks of gestation
This can decrease systolic blood pressure as much as 30 mmHg, stroke volume 30%, and uterine
blood flow
The left lateral decubitus position decreases this effect
Due to concerns about the neck, using a back board and elevating the right hip is the best option

questions.question:
Which of the following should be done for a very apprehensive elective surgery
patient who is about to undergo general anesthesia?

answers.A: Explain to the patient that negative thoughts can lead to a poor recovery
answers.B: Reassure the patient that the surgery will likely go smoothly
answers.C: Allow the patient to express his or her fear
answers.D: Recommend that the patient wait and discuss his or her fears with family members

questions.printed_answer_heading: Allow the patient to express his or her fear
questions.explanation: It is important to allow the patient to express his or her fears and listen to and support the patient

questions.question: Which of the following agents has minimal analgesic activity?
questions.explanation:
Nitrous oxide also known as laughing gas is known for its euphoric effects
Nitrous oxide is widely used in dentistry but it has poor analgesic activity
Nitrous oxide has the ability to diffuse into spaces and thus it is not recommended for use in
patients with bowel obstruction, pneumothorax, or pneumocephalus
When used as an anesthetic, nitrous oxide has to be combined with another analgesic agent

questions.question: Which is false about blunt trauma injuries to the neck?

answers.A: Stroke risk may be increased with fractures of C-spine levels 1-3
answers.B: Blunt trauma to the neck can also cause damage to the carotid artery
answers.C: C-spine fracture with subluxation can be associated with a vascular or neurological injury
answers.D: Methylprednisone must be given within 1 hr of cervical spine injury

questions.printed_answer_heading: Methylprednisone must be given within 1 hr of cervical spine injury
questions.explanation:
Today, there is insufficient evidence to support routine use of steroids in spinal cord injury
If available, CT scan is much more sensitive than plain C spine x-rays at evaluating spine
fractures
Cervical spine injury may be associated with injuries to the carotid artery or cervical nerves

questions.question:
A 70 y/o has a stroke. Neurological exam discovers homonymous hemianopsia
and loss of contralateral pain and temperature sense. Which arterial branch is most likely involved?
questions.explanation:
The posterior cerebral artery supplies the occipital lobe. An infarct of the left occipital lobe
will lead to right homonymous hemianopsia.
PCA stroke can also lead to ischemic injury or infarct of the thalamus where the spinothalamic
tract that transmits pain and temperature sensations terminates
The circle of Willis has three main branches from the internal carotid artery and basilar artery.
The anterior and middle cerebrals come off the ICA and the posterior cerebral artery directly
branches off the basilar artery
There are numerous smaller branches coming off all three large tributaries which results in a
wide variety of stroke syndromes. Stroke symptoms involving the three larger vessels depend on
the extent and location of perfused brain structures that are involved

questions.question:
Which of the following is the most accurate description of Traumatic Brain
Injury (TBI)?

answers.A:
A form of acquired complex injury to the brain usually caused by sudden trauma with a broad
spectrum of symptoms and disabilities
answers.B:
A form of damage to the brain that may result in a bad headache, altered levels of alertness, or
unconsciousness
answers.C: Any injury to the spinal cord that is caused by trauma instead of a disease
answers.D: Any injury resulting in fracture of the skull

questions.printed_answer_heading:
A form of acquired complex injury to the brain usually caused by sudden trauma with
a broad spectrum of symptoms and disabilities
questions.explanation:
A form of acquired complex injury to the brain usually caused by sudden trauma with a broad
spectrum of symptoms and disabilities
A form of damage to the brain that may result in a bad headache, altered levels of alertness, or
unconsciousness defines a concussion.
Spinal cord injury (SCI) is any injury to the spinal cord that is caused by trauma instead of a
disease.
Any injury resulting in a fracture of the skull is a skull fracture.

questions.question: Disequilibrium is best described as:

answers.C: A sensation of loss of balance

questions.printed_answer_heading: A sensation of loss of balance
questions.explanation:
Disequilibrium is a sensation of a loss of balance or of unsteadiness.
It can be caused by vestibulocerebellar tract lesions.
Orthostasis is lightheadedness upon standing or from sitting up from a recumbent position.
Presyncope is a sensation of impending fainting. A sensation of spinning is vertigo.

questions.question:
Which of the following disease processes do not cause compression on the
thecal sac on myelography images?
questions.explanation:
Astrocytomas are intramedullary
Intramedullary lesions expand the thecal sac, and do not compress the thecal sac
The remaining options are all extradural

questions.question: Seizures are usually not treated with?
questions.explanation:
Lithium is therapy for bipolar disorder
Lorazepam is the drug of choice for status epilepticus
Phenytoin and valproic acid are used to prevent generalized seizures.

questions.question:
A patient complains of numbness and tingling of his left 4th and 5th fingers for 5
months. His past medical history is unremarkable. Physical exam shows normal neurologic exam but
there is mild wasting of the intrinsic muscles of the left hand. The only laboratory abnormalities are a
fasting blood sugar of 155 mg/dL and a hemoglobin A1C of 7.2%. Select the most likely cause of the
patient's symptoms.
questions.explanation:
The findings are most likely secondary to pathology at the nerve roots of C8 or T1
Diabetic neuropathy is a possibility but it is more commonly symmetric
Neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome results from compression of the lower brachial plexus
Diagnosis is made by EMG, CT, or MRI

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is not true about the development of the human
skull?

answers.A: The neurocranium and the viscerocranium are the two parts of the skull
answers.B: The viscerocranium is formed from the cartilage of the two pharyngeal arches
answers.C: The flat bones of the skull are formed from the viscerocranium
answers.D: One part of the neurocranium is the chondrocranium that forms the base of the skull

questions.printed_answer_heading: The flat bones of the skull are formed from the viscerocranium
questions.explanation:
The neurocranium forms the flat bones that surround the brain and the base of the skull
The viscerocranium forms the 14 facial bones

questions.question:
A patient has herniation of a lumbar disc at L3-L4 with right lower extremity
weakness. Pain occasionally requires opioids but she is able to do her usually activities and work.
Which of the following would be the indication for surgery?

answers.B: Absent deep tendon reflexes on the left
answers.D: MRI shows L4-L5 herniation, as well

questions.explanation:
The four indications for herniated discs are incapacitating nerve root pain, signs of spinal cord
compression, progressive muscle weakness, and recurrent incapacitating nerve root pain
Nighttime pain, loss of deep tendon reflexes, and multiple level disc herniations are common
and not indications for surgery

questions.question: The most common location of germ cell tumors in the central nervous system is?
questions.explanation:
Central nervous system germ cell tumors are most common in children and adolescents, with a
peak incidence between 10 and 12 years of age
They are more common in males than females, with an overall male to female ratio of 2.5/1
The most common locations of germ cell tumors are the suprasellar and the pineal regions
Occasionally, these tumors may occur in the thalamus, basal ganglia, and other sites in the
central nervous system

questions.question:
An 18-year-old man sent to the ER with multiorgan injuries from MVA. Why
would the emergency room physician decide to withhold the use of sedatives?

answers.A: The drugs may affect his eye movements
answers.B: There may be a need for surgery
answers.C: The patient may be a drug seeker
answers.D: Mental status needs to be unaltered for baseline neurological exam

questions.printed_answer_heading: Mental status needs to be unaltered for baseline neurological exam
questions.explanation:
It is impossible to obtain an accurate neurological exam and GCS after a patient is given
sedatives or analgesics

questions.question: The Glasgow coma scale does not evaluate which of the following?
questions.explanation:
The GCS ranges from 3-15 and is a neurological evaluation of a trauma patient assessing eye
opening, verbal response and motor response and assigning specific numbers based on the exam
The quantitative value can be recomputed daily establishing a trend that helps establish
prognosis
A number of 8 or less is indicative of a severe head injury
9-12 is a moderate head injury and 13 or greater is a mild insult

questions.question: During a midline lumbar puncture, which layer is not traversed by the needle?
questions.explanation: The needle transverse skin, fat, supraspinous and interspinous ligament

questions.question:
Select the true statement about the straight leg raise when evaluating low back
pain.

answers.A: Back pain referred from visceral organs will cause a positive reverse straight leg raise
answers.B:
If the foot is passively dorsiflexed during the straight leg raise it will show entrapment of the
contralateral nerve root
answers.C: A more specific version of the test is the crossed straight leg raise
answers.D: If there is restricted range of motion of the affected limb the test is positive

questions.printed_answer_heading: A more specific version of the test is the crossed straight leg raise
questions.explanation:
If flexion of one leg reproduces the pain in the opposite leg or buttock the crossed straight leg
raise is positive
The affected nerve is always on the painful side
Raising the leg on the side with the pain and passively dorsiflexing the foot puts further traction
on the sciatic nerve and is called Leseque sign
The reverse straight leg raise stretches the L2-L4 nerve roots and is done with the patient
standing, passively extending the leg with the knee flexed

questions.question: Which of the following statement about scopolamine is false?
questions.explanation:
Scopolamine is a tropane alkaloid, like tropine and has similar effects
Scopolamine is an effective agent for motion sickness and also blocks short term memory
Scopolamine is used as an adjuvant in anesthesia
Scopolamine is not used for induction of anesthesia

questions.question: Which does not make up the stellate ganglion?
questions.explanation: T2 root nerve is not part of the stellate ganglion

questions.question: Which is not a characteristic of patient with locked in syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Locked in syndrome is characterized by impairment of horizontal eye movement and complete
paralysis
Vertical eye movement is intact

questions.question: A true statement about diabetes insipidus (DI) is:

answers.A: DI is never caused by neoplastic processes
answers.B: Vasopressin administration causes a large increase in urine osmolality with nephrogenic DI
answers.C:
Vasopressin administration after dehydration causes a greater than 9% increase in urinary
osmolality with central DI
answers.D: Recent head trauma is an unlikely cause

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Vasopressin administration after dehydration causes a greater than 9% increase in
urinary osmolality with central DI
questions.explanation:
Diabetes insipidus (DI) is associated with inappropriate release of (central) or response to
ADH (nephrogenic tubular insensitivity.)
DI is associated with intracranial or neoplastic processes of the hypothalamus, hypothalamic
surgery, aneurysms, and head injury.
In central DI there is a greater than 9% increase of urine osmolality after dehydration and
vasopressin administration.

questions.question: CT scan of the head is not required in trauma patient with?

answers.D: Neurologically intact person with very mild confusion

questions.printed_answer_heading: Neurologically intact person with very mild confusion
questions.explanation:
CT scan of the head is recommended for patients with minor head injuries if they have a GCS
less than 14, have evidence of a skull fractures or have vomiting episodes
Other reasons for a CT scan include age over 65, amnesia lasting 30 mins and having been
ejected from a car or falling from a height
Minor head injury is defined as witnessed loss of consciousness or witnessed disorientation in a
patient with a GCS of 13-15

questions.question: What order of neuron is contained in the accessory cuneate nucleus?
questions.explanation:
The clarks nucleus contains second order neurons
The accessory cuneate nucleus also contains second order neurons

questions.question: Lesions of the skull bone are best investigated with:
questions.explanation:
CT is the best test to identify any bone pathology
CT scan can be used to determine bone pathology anywhere in the body

questions.question: What is the most likely cause of brain stem injury in an alpha coma patient?
questions.explanation:
Alpha coma is most often caused by vascular disease
It is usually due to damage of the brainstem

questions.question: All the following statements about central vertigo are correct EXCEPT:

answers.A: Gradual onset and usually milder than peripheral vertigo

questions.explanation:
Nystagmus is multidirectional and not suppressed by optic fixation. Other symptoms include
slurred speech, dysphagia, diplopia, extremity weakness, and ataxia.
Causes include VBI, migraine, lateral medullary syndrome, posterior fossa tumors, some drugs,
and neurodegenerative disorders.
Central vertigo results from pathology of pons, medulla and cerebellum.

questions.question:
Which of the following structure lies immediately posterior and superior to the
sphenoid sinus and medial to the cavernous sinus?
questions.explanation:
The pituitary gland is an endocrine gland at the base of the brain
It rests in the sella turcica which is a small, bony cavity and is covered by a dural fold.
It lies immediately posterior and superior to the sphenoid sinus and medial to the cavernous
sinus
The pituitary gland secretes many hormones including oxytocin and vasopressin from the
posterior portion and growth hormone, TSH, LH, FSH, MSH, ACTH, prolactin, and beta
endorphin from the anterior portion.

questions.question:
A tumor mass found in the cord on MRI is more likely an astrocytoma than an
ependymoma if:

answers.C: The lesion has a craniocaudal extent greater than six vertebral segments
answers.D: The lesion has a polar cyst

questions.printed_answer_heading: The lesion has a craniocaudal extent greater than six vertebral segments
questions.explanation:
Astrocytomas tend to have a longer craniocaudal extent than ependymomas, more than six
vertebral segments
Both astrocytomas and ependymomas show mixed enhancement
Astrocytomas rarely show marginal hemorrhage
Astrocytoma cysts are typically internal, not adjacent, to the lesion

questions.question: Abnormal doppler color flow in a compression ultrasonography suggests:
questions.explanation:
Abnormal Doppler color flow in compression ultrasonography suggests DVT
Abnormal compressibility of the vein is another evidence of DVT
The presence of an echogenic band is also considered evidence of DVT

questions.question:
A 65-year-old female is examined in the neurology clinic. When the dorsum of
the forearm in supine position is stroked in the area of the distal radius, there is abduction of the hand
and flexion of the fingers. The patient may have:
questions.explanation:
The Bekhterev-Jacobsohn reflex involves stroking the supine forearm. This results in abduction
of the hand and flexion of the fingers
The test is similar to the Bekhterev Mendel reflex in the lower extremity

questions.question: The best antidote for a patient with acute bleeding from excess warfarin is:
questions.explanation:
Warfarin, po, causes synthesis of nonfunctional versions of vitamin K dependent clotting factors
(II, VII, IX, X)
Warfarin toxicity includes bleeding, teratogenic abnormalities and skin ulcerations
Antidote to warfarin is vitamin K and fresh frozen plasma

questions.question:
A 1 year old child was brought by his mother because of high grade fever. On
examination his anterior fontanel is bulging. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial
management of this patient?
questions.explanation:
Young children with meningitis may present with bulging anterior fontanelles
Pyogenic meningitis should be ruled out by CSF analysis
Bulging fontanelle is a sign of raised intracranial pressure
It is not a contraindication against lumber puncture

questions.question:
Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) is characterized by what
dermatological presentation?
questions.explanation: DIC presents as petechiae and purpura resulting from pathological coagulation

questions.question: All of the following statements about ICP monitoring are correct EXCEPT?

answers.A: Subarachnoid screws are prone to being blocked by brain tissue
answers.B:
Intraparenchymal brain monitor has a transducer in the tip that enters the brain and does not need
to be zeroed prior to being introduced
answers.C: Intraventricular ICP is placed into the ventricle with a catheter which can drain CSF
answers.D:
If the intraventricular ICP monitor does not function, ICP can then be determined by adjusting the
level of the drainage bag

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Intraparenchymal brain monitor has a transducer in the tip that enters the brain and
does not need to be zeroed prior to being introduced
questions.explanation:
The intraparenchymal brain monitor must be zeroed to the atmosphere prior to being introduced
into the brain
Another monitor is the epidural monitor which is placed into the epidural space. Caution must be
employed to ensure that the cranial bone does not kink the catheter
The disadvantage of the intraventricular ICP monitor is of precisely entering the ventricular
system and the relative risk of an infection and hemorrhage. A major advantage is the ability to
withdraw CSF as an option to reduce elevated ICP

questions.question: When the bleeding times are prolonged, the patient is usually taking?
questions.explanation:
Bleeding time is a test done to assess platelet function
Bleeding time is measured by making a small cut on the patient's hand and observing how it long
it takes the bleeding to stop
Bleeding time is usually affected by von Willebrands disease, hemophilia, and DIC
Aspirin and other NSAIDS can prolong the bleeding time, but sometimes the bleeding time may
also be prolonged with warfarin

questions.question:
A year old infant has lethargy and a fever. Kernig and Brudzinski signs are
present. What routine health measure could have prevented this disease?

answers.C: A polysaccharide vaccine with 23 different antigens

questions.explanation:
The disease described is consistent with bacterial meningitis
The only listed and routinely administered childhood vaccine that prevents meningitis is the
Haemophilus influenza vaccine, which is a conjugate polysaccharide protein vaccine
The polysaccharide vaccines are not routinely administered to babies because of poor
immunological response

questions.question:
Select the symptom that would not be associated with a lesion of the
pterygopalatine ganglion.

answers.A: Loss of general sensation to the hard palate
answers.B: Loss of general sensation to the lacrimal gland
answers.D: Loss of general sensation to the soft palate

questions.printed_answer_heading: Loss of general sensation to the lacrimal gland
questions.explanation:
Sensation of the lacrimal gland is from the lacrimal branch of the ophthalmic nerve
This is the first division of the trigeminal nerve
The maxillary nerve provides sensation to the hard and soft palate
The maxillary nerve sensory fibers transverse the pterygopalatine ganglion

questions.question: What effect would a lesion in the anterior cingulate circuit have?
questions.explanation:
Reduced drive, apathy, decreased motivation and initiative result from lesions in the anterior
cingulate circuit
The circuit has origin at the anterior cingulate gyrus, projects to the ventral striatum including the
olfactory tubercles, nucleus accumbens and parts of the putamen and caudate
Afferents travel from the ventral striatum to the substantia nigra and the globus pallidus, the
circuit continues to the medial dorsal thalamus and then back to the cingulate gyrus
Bilateral lesions of the anterior cingulate circuit can cause profound apathy and akinetic mutism

questions.question:
Multiple "punched out" lesions seen in the skull by x-ray, associated with
monoclonal gammopathy and amyloidosis are features of:
questions.explanation:
The first stage of Paget disease is osteolytic with the skull showing "osteoporosis circumscripta"
or punched out lesions.
The next stage involves excessive bone formation causing cortical thickening and osteosclerosis.
Radiographically this can appear as "cotton wool" sclerotic lesions with surrounding
demineralization.
The final stage shows diffuse sclerosis. Patients often are initially diagnosed due elevated
alkaline phosphatase on routine screening blood tests.

questions.question:
A patient undergoes a lumbar puncture and is found to have blood in the CSF .
He may have:
questions.explanation:
When a lumbar puncture is performed in a patient suspected of subarachnoid hemorrhage, 3
tubes should be collected
If a high number of red cells are equally present in all three bottles, the diagnosis is certain
If the number of red cells decreases per bottle, one should think of a traumatic tap
CT scan can confirm the presence of subarachnoid hemorrhage

questions.question: What is the best pharmacological treatment for a small prolactinoma?
questions.explanation:
Small prolactinomas are treated with bromocriptine
Large prolactinomas are treated with transsphenoidal resection
Radiation has a limited role as only 25% of patients show response

questions.question:
A patient has blunt head trauma and on presentation Glasgow coma scale is 13,
he is hemodynamically stable, and his pupils are equal and reactive. 2 hours later his left pupil is
larger and his blood pressure is 180/105 mmHg. What is the next step in management?

answers.A: Stat uninfused CT of the head

questions.explanation:
The patient has increased intracranial pressure and herniation
The first step is to secure the airway
Hyperventilation will lower intracranial pressure
CT and neurosurgical consults are then indicated

questions.question: To become culturally competent:

answers.A: Encourage continuation of folk beliefs and practices
answers.B: Explain the facts about the illness using medical terminology so the individual understands
answers.C: Learn fundamental words and phrases in the individual's native language
answers.D: Explain to the individual why your cultural beliefs should be followed

questions.printed_answer_heading: Learn fundamental words and phrases in the individual's native language
questions.explanation:
To become culturally competent it can be helpful to learn fundamental words and phrases in the
individual's native language, to participate in cultural activities, and learn more about a different
culture's beliefs.

questions.question:
What is an important modifiable factor in maintaining patient body temperature
in the operating room?
questions.explanation: The temperature of the operating room should be adjusted for the comfort of the patient

questions.question:
Select the condition NOT characterized by CSF with predominantly
mononuclear cells.
questions.explanation:
Early bacterial meningitis usually shows neutrophils in the CSF
Partially treated meningitis may show a predominance of monocytes
Early viral meningitis may show neutrophils but there is a shift to monocytes

questions.question:
Medications in patients with Parkinson disease usually provide relief for what
time period?
questions.explanation:
Unfortunately, medications only provide good relief from major PD symptoms for 4-6 years
After this, the disability progresses and one may have to try any different treatment approaches

questions.question: Cerebrospinal fluid is produced by the?
questions.explanation: The ependymal cells secrete cerebrospinal fluid

questions.question:
Bilateral facial paralysis accompanied by fever, rash, and arthralgias is
suggestive of which of the following types of infection?
questions.explanation:
Erythema migrans is the characteristic rash associated with Lyme disease.
The initial infections is secondary to a deer tick (Ixodes) bite. Borrelia spreads hematogenously
and can result in fever, headache, migratory arthralgias, and adenopathy.
Late manifestations of the disease can involve the heart, joints, or nervous system.
The most common neurologic manifestation is facial nerve paralysis that does not respond to
corticosteroids. This is bilateral in up to 25% of patients.

questions.question:
Which of the following is not true regarding radiocontrast media (RCM)
reaction?

answers.A: Hypersensitivity reactions are independent of rate of infusion
answers.B: Seizures and arrhythmias are noticed in RCM reaction
answers.C: Physiologic reactions are related to the chemical properties of RCM agents
answers.D: Physiologic reactions are dependant on rate and dose of infusion

questions.printed_answer_heading: Seizures and arrhythmias are noticed in RCM reaction
questions.explanation:
Hypersensitivity reactions to radiocontrast are idiosyncratic and largely independent of rate of
infusion
In contrast, chemotoxic, or physiologic, reactions are related to the chemical properties of
radiocontrast agents and are dose and infusion rate dependent
Vasovagal reactions, seizures, arrhythmias, and organ toxicity are features of physiologic
reactions

questions.question: In a patient with diabetes insipidus, one will observe:
questions.explanation:
Diabetes insipidus is associated with antidiuretic hormone deficiency
It is characterized by high urine output

questions.question: Why would atropine sulfate be given pre-operatively?
questions.explanation:
Atropine sulfate reduces oral and respiratory secretions so it often is given pre-operatively to
protect the airway during anesthesia

questions.question: Which type is a chronic spinal muscular atrophy?
questions.explanation:
Type I spinal muscular atrophy his characterized by acute onset with onset between birth and 6
months
Type II is a chronic condition usually diagnosed between 6 and 12 months
Type III is usually diagnosed between 2 and 5 years
There is no type IV

questions.question: Oxycodone breakdown into which substance?
questions.explanation: Oxymorphine is the metabolite of oxycodone

questions.question: Klumpke's palsy is due to:

answers.A: Damage to the upper brachial plexus

questions.explanation:
Klumpke's Palsy is paralysis of the eighth cervical and first thoracic nerves
Characteristic signs are claw hand, weakness of the hand intrinsics and numbness in the ulnar
distribution
Horner's syndrome which involves,all on the same side, drooping eyelid, decreased sweating of
the face and miotic pupil is sometime associated with Klumpke's

questions.question: Which of the following is not consistent with the diagnosis of cortical blindness?

answers.A: Loss of vision in both eyes
answers.C: Absence of pupillary constriction to light

questions.printed_answer_heading: Absence of pupillary constriction to light
questions.explanation:
Pupillary constriction to light and to convergence is maintained with cortical blindness
Retinal structures are generally preserved, unless blindness is caused by prenatal or perinatal
injury

questions.question:
In a young male less than 40 years of age who presents with tremor, rigidity and
bradykinesia, what blood work is vital?
questions.explanation:
Serum ceruloplasmin levels should be obtained to make sure that the patient does not have
Wilson disease
Patients under 40 with parkinsonian symptoms should also have measurement of urinary copper
and a slit examination of the eye

questions.question: The most common organism isolated from surgical site infections is:
questions.explanation:
Staphylococcus is the most common offending organism found in surgical site infections after
both clean and some clean-contaminated surgery procedures
Although the infection rate is relatively low for these procedures, they are the majority of
surgery procedures performed and thus account for a large number of surgical site infections

questions.question:
Which one of the following types of fluids is not to be used for irrigation of
wounds?
questions.explanation:
Chlorinated solutions can irritate the skin and delay wound healing.
Normal saline is the preferred fluid used to clean up wounds.

questions.question: The diagnosis related groups (DRGs) provide:

answers.A: reimbursement rates for Medicare part A
answers.B: reimbursement rates for Medicare part B
answers.C: reimbursement rates for Medicare part D

questions.printed_answer_heading: reimbursement rates for Medicare part A
questions.explanation:
DRGs provide reimbursement rates for Medicare part A, the hospital insurance portion of
Medicare
DRGs are an effort to reign in upwardly spiraling hospital care costs
DRGs don't take into account the severity of illness
DRGs can be higher or lower than a hospital actually charges for services

questions.question:
A 77 y/o female is seen in the ER for fever, diplopia, headache and very tender
scalp. The temporal artery is swollen and painful to palpation. An ESR is elevated >60 mm/hr
indicating the presence of an inflammatory condition. What would be the most appropriate next step
to prove the diagnosis of suspected temporal arteritis?
questions.explanation:
The gold standard is temporal artery biopsy. Some radiological studies are being proposed as
alternatives such as ultrasound of the artery showing halo sign and 3T MRI with super high
resolution imaging and contrast injection
Temporal arteritis also called giant cell arteritis is an autoimmune inflammation of the medium
to large arteries of the head, neck, upper body and arms.
There may be decreased pulses throughout. Blindness may occur from arteritic anterior ischemic
optic neuropathy.
It is a medical emergency. Treatment is high dose prednisone which can be tapered down over
several weeks. Treatment should given while awaiting biopsy. Some patients may require a
maintenance dose for 1-2 years.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Good Samaritan Law?

answers.A: Allows health professionals to practice in any state

questions.explanation:
A person that provides healthcare services with good intention under emergent situations is
exempt from civil liability unless acting improperly with intent to harm

questions.question: The most common intracranial complication of untreated otitis media is:
questions.explanation:
The most common intracranial complication of otitis media is meningitis
Other complications include facial nerve paralysis, mastoiditis, temporal abscess, otitis,
hydrocephalus, CSF leak and encephalocele

questions.question: Which is not recommended for the treatment of pressure ulcers?
questions.explanation:
Pressure ulcers develop at pressure points, which are most commonly located over bony
prominences
Treatment includes strategies to reduce the pressure at the ulcer sites
Egg crate mattresses, air mattresses, and frequent patient turning are all useful strategies to
minimize the pressure at ulcer sites

questions.question: What agent is added to increase the half-life of imipenem?
questions.explanation:
Cilastatin inhibits of renal dehydropeptidase I.
This enzyme causes the hydrolysis of imipenem compounds with no antibacterial activity that are
nephrotoxic.
It has no antimicrobial activity itself but maintains serum and urine levels of the intact
medication.

questions.question:
Which of the following individuals can give informed consent to refuse or accept
treatment?

answers.A: A 25-year-old confused and disoriented male status post motor vehicle accident
answers.B: A 30-year-old man with a blood alcohol level of 90 mg/dL
answers.C: A married, pregnant 16 year old brought to the emergency room in labor
answers.D: A 17 year old male with a broken arm brought to the emergency department by his parents

questions.printed_answer_heading: A married, pregnant 16 year old brought to the emergency room in labor
questions.explanation:
The 17 year old is a minor and not able to consent or refuse treatment.
The inebriated man and the man with the closed head injury are not capable of understanding and
consenting to treatment
The 16 year old in labor, while still a minor is considered emancipated, as she is married. She
can consent for treatment.
In a life-threatening emergency, consent would be implied and a signed form is not needed

questions.question:
What is the best method of preventing atelectasis in a patient post
transsphenoidal hypophysectomy?
questions.explanation:
Deep breathing is the best method to prevent atelectasis formation
Coughing is contraindicated after transsphenoidal hypophysectomy

questions.question: The stellate ganglion is located where in the body?

answers.B: At the bifurcation of the carotid artery
answers.C: At the neck of the first rib and C7 transverse process

questions.printed_answer_heading: At the neck of the first rib and C7 transverse process
questions.explanation:
The stellate ganglion is between the transverse process of the 7th cervical vertebra and the neck
of the first rib.

questions.question: Foot drop is typically caused by a lesion of the:
questions.explanation:
The peroneal nerve travels around the neck of the fibula and can become entrapped resulting in
foot drop.
Other lesions that can affect the common peroneal nerve include Baker cysts, tight casts,
ganglions, and abnormalities of the fabella.
Common peroneal nerve injury causes impaired dorsiflexion and eventually foot drop.

questions.question: Which one of the following tests is not used to assess dementia?

answers.D: UCD ADC clinical neuropsychiatry test battery

questions.explanation:
The NPI evaluates 12 common neuropsychiatric disturbances seen in dementia.
UCD ADC neuropsychological test battery performs 27 separate tests
Other clinical exams are Blessed Roth dementia rating scale and functional activities
questionnaire (FAQ) that rate 10 functional activities
The mini-mental status examination (MMSE) is a good screening tool that evaluates orientation,
attention, calculation, recall, praxis and language. SENAS stand for Spanish and English
neuropsychological assessment scale

questions.question: The most frequent location of choroid plexus papillomas in children is?
questions.explanation:
The site of predilection for the development of choroid plexus papillomas in children is the
lateral ventricle
In adults it is the fourth ventricle

questions.question:
A patient with a history of pseudotumor cerebri (PTC) has been shunted in the
past. She now complains of headache. Funduscopic exam shows papilledema. Which of the following
is most likely?

answers.B: There is no reason for concern
answers.D: The patient should be started on Diamox

questions.explanation:
PTC is usually normal on MRI. Occasional flattening of the globe is seen
Early treatment if there is no vision loss can be with Diamox
PTC shunt malfunction can result in blindness
PTC is most common in young overweight women

questions.question: Delayed wound healing is seen in patients with:
questions.explanation:
Excess cortisol impairs collagen matrix
Cushing disease is characterized by excess cortisol

questions.question: For chronic pain, which medication class is least recommended?
questions.explanation: Opioids are not recommended for chronic nonmalignant pain due to addiction and side effects

questions.question:
Ventriculoperitoneal shunt malfunction for hydrocephalus is unlikely to present
with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Shunt malfunction will increase ICP, which may lead to increase of head circumference

questions.question:
A patient has a severe allergy to procaine. Which of these local anesthetics (LA)
is contraindicated?
questions.explanation:
Tetracaine, an ester LA, is contraindicated in patients with a procaine allergy. Procaine is the
prototype of the ester class of LA. There is class based cross-reactivity in ester LA.
Other common ester LA are chloroprocaine and cocaine.
Lidocaine, bupivacaine and prilocaine are all members of the amide class of There is also
class-based cross-reactivity in amide LA.
There is no cross-reactivity between the two classes of LA.

questions.question: Which of the following is incorrect about Lhermitte sign?

answers.A: The sign implies ventral column irritation
answers.B: The sign implies dorsal column irritation

questions.question:
All of the following statements about the dura and meninges are correct
EXCEPT:

answers.A:
The dura is a tough fibrous tissue that covers the brain and has three dural infoldings, falx
cerebri, tentorium cerebelli, and sella diaphragm
answers.B: Dura is formed by two layers in which the outer layer is the inner bones periosteum
answers.C: Pacchionian bodies are small arachnoid villi that allow the return of CSF to the vascular system
answers.D:
Pia mater is delicate and firmly adherent to brain and spinal cord composed of flat cells and
fibrous tissue. It closely follows the brain's contour into the gyri and sulci

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Pacchionian bodies are small arachnoid villi that allow the return of CSF to the
vascular system
questions.explanation:
Pacchionian bodies are large arachnoid granulations that become calcified. Arachnoid is a
transparent membrane that has a cushioning effect and covers the pia mater. It has flat cells and
fibrous tissue impermeable to CSF and does not follow the brain's convolutions. CSF is between
the pia mater and arachnoid and called the subarachnoid space. Both of these layers are called
leptomeninges. Arachnoid villi are small protrusions that enter the dural sinuses in which to
drain CSF into the vascular space
Blood vessels and capillaries pierce the pia mater in order to supply the brain. This is where the
blood brain barrier (BBB) is formed by endothelial cells that form tight junctions at the
capillaries and arterioles. The BBB also involves the choroid plexus which is made up of
numerous capillaries with modified ependymal cells that filter the blood allowing liquid to
become CSF. There is active transport both in and out of CSF
Dural sinuses are formed between the 2 layers of dura and are conduits for venous return. These
dural tubes are lined with endothelium

parasympathetic innervation
Trauma is a common cause of arterial dissection in the neck

questions.question: Visual sensation is mediated by the:
questions.explanation:
Proprioception is relayed by the ventroposterior lateral nucleus
Visual system is relayed by the lateral geniculate nucleus
Taste is relayed by the ventroposterior medial nucleus

questions.question:
A 22 year old has suffered a basilar skull fracture. Which of the following
findings would not be seen in such a patient?
questions.explanation:
Features of skull base fracture include battle's sign, which is ecchymosis around mastoid
process
Raccoon eyes is periorbital ecchymosis or black eyes
CSF otorrhea, cranial nerve palsies, bleeding from nose and ears is also common
About 10 percent of patients suffer ocular nerve entrapment

questions.question:
The most likely diagnosis of a patient with intentional tremor otherwise normal
neurological exam is:
questions.explanation: Action tremors are usually benign familial tremor

questions.question: Select the least accurate statement about chemical synapses.

answers.A: Active zones are specialized regions where depolarization occurs
answers.B: Chemical synapses can be inhibitory or excitatory
answers.D: Transmission through chemical synapses is rapid

questions.printed_answer_heading: Transmission through chemical synapses is rapid
questions.explanation:
Chemical synapse transmission shows a slight delay
They are unidirectional and can be inhibitory or excitatory
Fusion of synaptic vesicles at active zones result in release of neurotransmitters
The neurotransmitters attach to receptors at the post synaptic cleft

questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of documenting a chain of evidence?

answers.A:
Properly labeling an observed urine sample of a suspected impaired driver for the police,
personally handing it to the arresting officer, and getting a receipt
answers.B:
Properly documenting in a medical record including dates, signatures, and making sure mistakes
are lined out, initialed, and dated
answers.C: Documenting vaginal fluids in a rape case where obtained, labeled, initialed, and sent to the lab
answers.D: Properly recording all medications and treatments in the medical record

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Properly labeling an observed urine sample of a suspected impaired driver for the
police, personally handing it to the arresting officer, and getting a receipt
questions.explanation:
"Chain of custody" has a specific legal definition.
It is done in order to be used to prevent allegations of tampering in legal proceedings.
Each specimen must be clearly labeled, dated, and delivered personally to the next person in the
chain, documented in the medical record, and receipt obtained.

questions.question: What is the total possible score for the eye component of Glasgow Coma Scale?
questions.explanation:
The maximum score of GCS is 15
Four for eye movement
Five for verbal response
Six for motor moment

questions.question: Ligamentous injury cannot be inferred on noting:

answers.A: Asymmetry of the dens in the C1 ring on perfectly positioned image

questions.explanation:
Bilateral facet lock implies ligamentous injury
Unilateral facet lock does NOT
With all ligaments intact, on a perfectly positioned film, the dens should be symmetrically
positioned with respect to the C1 ring
Posterior element widening implies tearing of posterior ligaments

questions.question: Which of the following head trauma patients requires surgery?

answers.D: Those with cerebral edema that is not causing profound brain compression

questions.explanation:
Elevations in ICP can occur in head trauma and if severe can cause cerebral ischemia.
Moreover, uncontrolled ICP can lead to herniation. Just a finding of cerebral edema is usually
not an indication for surgery
Intra axial hematomas which are large or depressed skull fractures usually need surgery
Any temporal or cerebellar hematomas larger than 3 cm are also treated with surgery
Fewer than 10% of patient with head trauma need surgery. Fluid restriction is contraindicated in
patients with head trauma and most require head elevation and sedation for recovery

questions.question:
All the following statements about herpes simplex encephalitis are correct
EXCEPT:

answers.B: CT scan shows temporal lobe edema
answers.C: Diagnosis can be confirmed by CSF polymerase chain reaction (PCR)

questions.explanation:
90% are caused by HSV 1 which produces cold sores and 10% by HSV 2. Other symptoms
include confusion, decreased level of consciousness, fever, headaches, drowsiness, and general
weakness.
Condition results in increased WBCs in CSF with primarily lymphocytes. EEG shows temporal
lobe abnormalities which when apparent in one lobe will develop in the other temporal lobe in
7-10 days.
One third of time CT scan may not show any swelling.
Treatment involves IV acyclovir for 10 days.

questions.question: Which injury is most common in rear end motor vehicle accidents?
questions.explanation:
Hyperextension-hyperflexion neck injuries are most common in rear end motor vehicle accidents
These injuries are also termed "whiplash"
Cervical vertebral fractures may occur, but are much less common
Rear end accidents don't usually cause rotational neck injuries

questions.question: Muscle movements are transmitted by which nerve fibers?
questions.explanation: The corticospinal tract transmits signals for muscle control

questions.question: Which is the least preferable method of administering IV fluids?
questions.explanation:
Peripheral lines started with a 12-16 gauge needle can deliver volumes of fluid very fast,
compared to central lines. Moreover, peripheral lines can be inserted without complications
Central lines can be inserted into the jugular or subclavian veins and directed to the right atrium.
Nevertheless, one also needs expertise. Central line can deliver medications that are irritating to
peripheral veins and can also be used for TPN
Central lines also carry risk of pneumothorax, air embolism and puncture of carotid artery
Complications of peripheral lines include phlebitis, infiltration and infection

questions.question: Which is false about malignant hyperthermia?

answers.A: Creatinine kinase levels are used to follow patients
answers.D: May be triggered by local anesthetics

questions.printed_answer_heading: May be triggered by local anesthetics
questions.explanation:
Diagnosis of malignant hyperthermia is based on clinical features. Tachycardia is usually the
first feature followed by rise in end CO2 levels and muscle rigidity
Core body temperature tends to rise in most patients. Local anesthetics do not cause malignant
hyperthermia
Blood may show hyperkalemia, elevated creatine kinase and increased phosphate
Severe rhabdomyolysis may lead to renal failure

questions.question: The primary neurotransmitter in the raphe nucleus is?
questions.explanation:
The dorsal and median raphe nuclei distribute ascending serotonin projections diffusely
throughout the brain as the spinal cord and brainstem receive descending serotonin projections
form other raphe nuclei
The midbrain,in the substantia nigra pars compacta and in the ventral segmental area provide
dopamine
GABA, being an inhibitory neurotransmitter is found throughout the brain
The locus ceruleus of the pons and midbrain contain neurons with norepinephrine

questions.question: Overdosing with baclofen is unlikely to cause?
questions.explanation:
Withdrawn from baclofen may include hyperthermia, hypotension, confusion, and increased
muscle tone
Overdose of baclofen may cause headache, nausea, muscle weakness, seizure, and respiratory
depression

questions.question: Pain or nociceptive stimuli are transmitted via what type of fibers:
questions.explanation:
Low threshold nociceptive stimuli are transmitted via A fibers
Nociceptive stimuli are transmitted via C fibers
Preganglionic signals for the autonomic system are carried by the B fibers

questions.question: When is one is likely to see Bruns ataxia?
questions.explanation:
Bruns ataxia is a form of ataxia in patients with bilateral frontal lobe disease.
The ataxia is characterized by inability to initiate walking, despite normal power and
coordination of legs.
The gait is usually broad based with short steps.
There is a great tendency to fall backwards.

questions.question: Horner syndrome presents with all the features except:
questions.explanation:
Horner syndrome is caused by a lesion of the oculosympathetic nerve pathway. This can occur
anywhere between the eye and the hypothalmus.
Horner syndrome is characterized by pupillary meiosis, facial anhidrosis, and ptosis.
There can be enophthalmos, heterochromia of the irides if congenital, paradoxical contralateral
eyelid retraction, increased amplitude of accommodation, changes in tear viscosity, and transient
decrease in intraocular pressure
Congenital Horner syndrome is typically diagnosed around two years due to heterochromia and
absence of a horizontal eyelid crease on the affected side.

questions.question: Ischemic optic neuropathy may occur after surgery on the?
questions.explanation: Ischemic optic neuropathy occurs most frequently with spinal and heart surgery

questions.question:
Select the sign that is unique to meperidine overdose rather than opiate
overdoses in general.
questions.explanation:
Meperidine, in toxic levels, causes several adverse responses that are not typically seen with
other opiates. They are hypertension, seizures and psychotic-like state.
Respiratory depression, constipation and biliary spasm can occur to varying degrees with all the
opiates.
It is important to note that naloxone, the antidote for opiate overdose, may increase the risk of
seizures, when given for meperidine overdose.

questions.question:
A 30 year old male had resection of a low-grade astrocytoma followed by
radiation. 6 years later he developed transient episodes of speech difficulty and right sided weakness.
Neither anti epilepsy drugs nor antiplatelet medications improved the situation. He also started
having new headaches with intermittent confusion. A few months later he had right hemiparesis and
the MRI showed enhancement at the left parietal region of the cortical ribbon. The MRI findings and
hemiparesis resolved in 3 weeks. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.B: Mitochondrial encephalopathy lactic acidosis and stroke-like symptoms (MELAS)
answers.C: Stroke-like migraine attacks after radiation therapy (SMART)
answers.D:
Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy
(CADASIL)

questions.printed_answer_heading: Stroke-like migraine attacks after radiation therapy (SMART)
questions.explanation:
SMART is seen in patients as a delayed consequence after cerebral irradiation
Symptoms can include visual changes, sensory and hemi-motor deficits, seizures, confusion,
aphasia, and headaches
MRI shows diffuse, transient unilateral cerebral gyri cortical enhancement at the area of
radiation
Ipsilateral EEG slowing is sometimes seen but full recovery occurs in days to weeks

questions.question:
What drug is part of the long term armamentarium in modifying a gradual
deteriorating progressive course in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis?
questions.explanation:
Fingolimod is an immunomodulating drug. Other drugs include interferon beta-1a, Avonex, and
interferon beta-1b, Betaseron
In addition, the following agents are added: Glatiramer, non-interferon non-steroid
immunomodulator, mitoxantrone, immunosuppressant, and natalizumab (Tysabri), monoclonal
antibody. These drugs have serious side effects to include liver toxicity
Corticosteroids are effective in short term treatment and management.
Azathioprine is used for transplant rejection and plasmapheresis is preferred for a severe
relapse not responding to steroids

questions.question:
A patient has spinal cord injury and is to start feeding herself. Select the best
adaptive equipment for this patient.
questions.explanation:
The patient will not have hand function so a universal cuff will be needed
Some patients may benefit from a scoop dish or mobile arm support
Large handled utensils would not be of help

questions.question: What is the most common cause of galactorrhea?
questions.explanation:
Lactation in the absence of pregnancy is called galactorrhea
Pituitary gland prolactinoma is the most common cause
Psychotropic medications, opioids, antihypertensive drugs (a-methyldopa), hypogonadism,
nipple stimulation, bronchogenic carcinomas, herpes zoster, hypothyroidism, and trauma are all
other causes
Prolactin levels and MRI of sell turcica are recommended

questions.question: Select the true statement about head trauma and hematomas

answers.A: Epidural hematomas usually are from veins
answers.B: At presentation, most patients with epidural hematomas are unconscious
answers.C: The elderly often can develop epidural hematomas with minor head trauma
answers.D:
Subdural hematomas often require arterial ligation due to the rapid increase in intracranial
pressure

questions.printed_answer_heading: At presentation, most patients with epidural hematomas are unconscious
questions.explanation:
Acute subdural hematomas have a venous source and are more common with aging
Epidural hematomas are secondary to arterial bleeding and require craniotomy and ligation
Approximately 1/3rd of patients with acute subdural bleed will be lucid and then be come
obtunded
Small subdural hematomas are often asymptomatic and do not require evacuation

questions.question: Which of the following is "false" about partial agonist antagonists?

answers.A: Generally produces less euphoria compared to morphine
answers.B: Pentazocine can cause blood pressure elevation
answers.D: May block analgesic activity of morphine

questions.explanation:
Partial agonist antagonists stimulate one receptor but block another
These drugs have some agonist activity but cause less euphoria
These agents should not be used with morphine since they can block the analgesic activity
Tolerance and dependence develop with repeated use

questions.question: What is the average age onset of temporal arteritis?
questions.explanation:
Average age onset of temporal arteritis is around 70
Treatment is with corticosteroids that can prevent blindness

questions.question:
An 18-year-old boy has a past medical history of fractures and optic gliomas. He
now came with projectile vomiting and headache. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The presentation is typical of Neurofibromatosis type-1
Multiple neurofibromas may be seen on skin
Optic glioma and other brain tumors may occur frequently in this disorder

questions.question:
An enlarged cisterna magna, hypoplastic vermis, and ventriculomegaly are seen
on fetal ultrasound, what malformation is this likely to represent?
questions.explanation:
Dandy Walker malformation is rare and is described as agenesis or hypoplasia of the cerebellar
vermis, massive dilatation of the 4th ventricle, hydrocephalus, and elevation of the confluence of
sinuses (torcular herophili).
Chiari II malformation can be distinguished from Dandy Walker by the low-lying confluence of
sinuses.
Dandy Walker malformation likely results from obstruction to flow in the foramina of Magendie
and Luschka.
Multiple syndromes are associated with Dandy Walker and thus MR is recommended for
evaluation.

questions.question:
A 33 y/o female returns to the doctor stating that after taking the prescribed drug,
ergotamine tartrate (Ergostat), for the migraines, her headaches have become more frequent and
painful. What is the most likely problem?
questions.explanation:
Rebound headaches occur when the patient takes more than the prescribed maximum dosage of
2-3 per week
This results in a vicious cycle in which the patient takes more and more of the drug to combat
ever increasing cephalgia
Ergotamine should not be given to patients with CAD, uncontrolled hypertension, peripheral
vascular disease, or arrhythmias.

questions.question: Pseudotumor cerebri is characterized by abnormal:
questions.explanation:
Pseudotumor cerebri has normal ventricle size on imaging.
It is more common in the young.

questions.question:
A left sided disc herniation at the L5-S1 level will present with which of the
following?

answers.B: Right sided weakness in the leg

questions.explanation:
A left sided lumbar disc herniation at L5-S1 usually causes ipsilateral problems
The individual will have left sided back pain that radiates down the left leg
The individual will also have weakness of dorsiflexion and absent ankle reflex of the left foot

questions.question: What type of tumor often arises from Rathke's pouch:
questions.explanation:
Craniopharyngioma is derived from pituitary gland embryonic tissue and is known as Rathke's
pouch tumor or adamantinoma
Due to optic chiasm compression the tumor may present with bitemporal inferior
quadrantanopsia progressing to bitemporal hemianopsia

questions.question: The best initial step in management in a patient with oliguria is?
questions.explanation: Fluid challenge is the initial treatment for patients with oliguria

questions.question:
Which assessment tool is used to rate level of consciousness by assigning a
numerical score to the behavioral components of eye opening, verbal response, and motor response?
questions.explanation:
The Glasgow coma scale is an assessment tool that rates the level of consciousness by assigning
a numerical score to the behavioral components of eye opening, verbal response, and motor
response.
The Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) tests orientation, registration, attention and
calculation, recall, and language.
Brudzinski's sign tests nuchal rigidity, which indicates meningeal irritation.
The CAGE questionnaire is a screening tool for alcoholism.

questions.question:
Where in the brainstem would the lesion be found for a patient with contralateral
loss of temperature and pain; dysphagia, ataxia, and dysarthria; ipsilateral Horner syndrome and
paresis of the vocal cord and pharynx, and ipsilateral loss of sensation of the face?
questions.explanation:
Lateral medullary syndrome is cause by occlusion of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery or
vertebral artery
It is characterized by contralateral loss of temperature and pain; dysphagia, ataxia, and
dysarthria; ipsilateral Horner syndrome and paresis of the vocal cord and pharynx, and
ipsilateral loss of sensation of the face
The damage is to the inferior cerebellar peduncle and dorsolateral medulla, descending spinal
tract, nucleus of the trigeminal nerve, nuclei and fibers of the vagus nerves and
glossopharyngeal, descending sympathetic tract fibers, spinothalamic tract, and vestibular nuclei

questions.question:
A patient is found to have a dilated and fixed pupil after falling from a 2-story
building. Which type of herniation is most likely?
questions.explanation:
Herniations are classified as either supratentorial or infratentorial
Uncal herniation affects the inner most segments of the temporal lobe-the uncus which applies
pressure on the brain stem and mid brain.
The uncus can squeeze the 3rd cranial nerve and also affects the parasympathetic input to the eye
causing the pupil to dilate. The eye will be deviated down and out due to loss of ocular muscle
activity (except lateral rectus)
Compression of the posterior cerebral artery wall causes ischemia of the ipsilateral visual
cortex and contralateral visual deficits in both eyes resulting in homonymous hemianopsia

questions.question: Which is not a factor for poor outcome in patients with head trauma?

answers.C: Presence of fixed and dilated pupil

questions.explanation:
Over the years many factors have been analyzed for prognosis after head trauma
In general, advanced age, initial GCS less than 6, presence of fixed and dilated pupil, prolonged
hypotension or hypoxia or the presence of a surgical intracranial mass lesion are poor
prognostic factors
The most controversial point of head trauma is the minimum desirable cerebral perfusion
pressure. Today it is believed that cerebral perfusion pressure of 60 mmHg is sufficient
Most experts indicate that if the admission GCS is less than 6 on admission, the prognosis is
very poor after head trauma

questions.question: Body heat loss during general anesthesia is least likely via which route?
questions.explanation: Temperature must be monitored for the entire duration of the case

questions.question: Which of the following is not used to treat essential tremor?
questions.explanation:
Essential tremor does not necessarily need treatment
If only occasional treatment is necessary, one alcoholic beverage may suffice but this is not
recommended for regular use
Propranolol can be used on an as needed or daily basis
Primidone is the most common anticonvulsant prescribed while severe cases may require
surgery

questions.question: Which of the following does not present in children with a craniopharyngioma?
questions.explanation:
Craniopharyngioma is a tumor of the anterior pituitary gland and it can lead to hypopituitarism.
Since the tumor is located just above the optic chiasm, it can cause bitemporal hemianopsia.
Galactorrhea can occur as a side effect of antipsychotic drugs or hyperfunctioning pituitary
tumors.

questions.question:
What is the most efficient method to prevent spread of infection in hospitalized
patients?
questions.explanation: Hand washing is the most efficient way to prevent infection spread

questions.question:
A 3 year old has been complaining of vision difficulties and keeps on bumping
into things at home. The slit lamp examination reveals an ectopic lens. What is the most likely disease
that may cause such a finding?
questions.explanation:
Homocystinuria is an inherited autosomal recessive disorder that is caused by defect in
methionine metabolism.
Severe myopia is the first sign of ectopia lentis and may precede lens dislocation by several
months to a year or even longer.

questions.question:
Which of the following would most likely show midbrain and cerebral cortical
atrophy on MRI?
questions.explanation:
