PSP may not show specific findings on MRI but midbrain and cerebral cortical atrophy are more
common than with the other diagnoses
In more advanced cases there may be atrophy of the colliculi, thinning of the midbrain tegmentum
and tectum, and enlargement of the sylvian fissures
Multisystem atrophy shows cerebellar atrophy
Corticobasal degeneration shows atrophy of the basal ganglia and the cerebral cortex

questions.question:
Which of the following is an appropriate expected level of feeding independence
for a spinal cord injury at C3?

answers.D: Directing a caregiver as to portion size and preferred head position

questions.printed_answer_heading: Directing a caregiver as to portion size and preferred head position
questions.explanation: A patient with SCI at C3 will not have arm strength and will dependent on caregiver for feedings

questions.question: A patient who fails a heel to toe, tandem gait exam, has which condition?
questions.explanation:
The inability to do this exam could suggest a variety of clinical conditions to also include such
pathologies as polyradiculopathy and vestibular dysfunction
It is necessary to do a complete neurological evaluation in order to pinpoint the exact disease
entity

questions.question:
A retired math teacher has been having difficulties with tasks she used to find
easy. She cannot calculate as easy nor remember words and her handwriting has deteriorated. She has
very poor short-term memory but can remember events from 10 years ago much easier. These
symptoms have been progressing slowly over time but started suddenly when her blood pressure
became nearly uncontrollable. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Multi-infarct dementia is the second most common cause of dementia in the elderly
It is the result of the cumulative effects of multiple small and large vessel occlusions
Most cases are caused by hypertensive cerebrovascular disease

questions.question:
Which of the following are the most common types of primary brain tumors in
children?
questions.explanation:
Children may have meningiomas but they usually are not symptomatic until they become adults
Neurofibromas are not considered primary brain tumors
15 to 20% of tumors seen in childhood are of the CNS
They are second only to leukemias

questions.question:
The corneal reflex or blink reflex involves two cranial nerves. Which of the
following lists the 2 cranial nerves involved?
questions.explanation:
The blink or corneal reflex occurs when the cornea is touched and the eye blinks.
The nasociliary branch of the ophthalmic division, CN V1, senses the stimuli and CN VII
initiates motor through the orbicularis oculi.

questions.question: A whiplash injury is best described as?
questions.explanation:
A typical whiplash injury is characterized by hyperextension of the neck
Common in motor vehicle accidents
Symptoms usually appear after twelve hours
Possible muscle injury to the sternocleidomastoid, scalene, and the longus colli

questions.question:
If subarachnoid hemorrhage is predominantly seen within the sylvian fissure,
where most likely is the aneurysm?
questions.explanation:
A MCA bifurcation aneurysm rupture will most likely cause SAH in the sylvian fissure (lateral
sulcus) in which the artery courses.
On noncontrasted CT SAH in the sylvian fissure will be hyperdense in the acute phase and
isodense in the subacute phase.
An ICA-PCOM aneurysm rupture would present with hemorrhage in the suprasellar cistern.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a correct association?

answers.A: Neurogenic shock - impaired descending sympathetic pathways in the lower thoracic cord
answers.B: Neurogenic shock - loss of vasomotor tone and sympathetic innervation to the heart
answers.C:
Neurogenic shock - expect vasodilation and hypotension with failure of tachycardia as a
response (may have bradycardia)
answers.D: Spinal shock - flaccidity and loss of reflexes

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Neurogenic shock - impaired descending sympathetic pathways in the lower thoracic
cord
questions.explanation:
Neurogenic shock is caused by impaired descending sympathetic pathways in cervical and upper
thoracic cord

questions.question:
A patient with a spinal cord injury develops anxiety, hypertension, headache,
diaphoresis, chills, nasal congestion, bradycardia, and flushing. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation:
The symptoms described are characteristic of autonomic dysreflexia
It is a sympathetic discharge secondary to strong sensory input
It is a medical emergency that should be treated by placing the patient in an upright position,
loosening and constricting clothing, and with antihypertensive medication

questions.question:
A neonate is noted to have cystic swelling over the base of the spine with
hyperpigmentation of the skin and coarse hair. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Meningocele and myelomeningocele result in a cystic swelling over the base of the spine
Myelomeningocele is characterized by extrusion of neural and meningeal elements together with
a mucocutaneous defect
A Mongolian spot is a nonpathologic discoloration at the base of the spine
There is no herniation of the meninges with spina bifida occulta so there is no cystic swelling

questions.question: Which muscle innervation is intact with a C5 spinal cord lesion?
questions.explanation:
A C5 spinal cord lesion is characterized by the intact functioning of the rotator cuff, biceps, and
deltoid muscles

questions.question:
A fried egg appearance of the perinuclear halo on CT brain scan is highly
indicative of:
questions.explanation:
An oligodendroglioma commonly present as a fried egg appearance of the perinuclear halo on
CT head
Oligodendrogliomas account for about 5 percent of primary intracranial neoplasms
The most common type of intracranial tumor is metastatic

questions.question: Concurrent injuries occur in which percentage of thoracic spine injuries?
questions.explanation: There are frequent complications of hemothorax and pneumothorax with thoracic spine injuries

questions.question:
What is the most likely cause of decreased urine output in a postoperative
patient?
questions.explanation:
Hypovolemia from insensible losses, blood loss and third spacing are the most common cause of
postoperative oliguria in a patient with normal kidneys
Sepsis in a clean case would be extremely rare

questions.question: After a laminectomy, the caregiver should focus on?
questions.explanation:
Post laminectomy can result in spinal nerve compression
Neurological status must be monitored

questions.question: To prevent a surgical infection, the best time to administer an antibiotic is:
questions.explanation:
Surgical infections are reduced if parenteral antibiotics are administered less than one hour
before the incision is made.
The choice of the antibiotic should be based on the likely pathogens to be encountered
There is no benefit seen in dosing prophylactic antibiotics 24 hours beyond the surgery

questions.question: Which is the most common side effect of valproic acid?
questions.explanation:
Nausea is seen in 31% of patients
Followed by weight gain in 50% of the patients
Tremor is seen in about 10% of the patients

questions.question:
Which is correct about white matter lesions seen on MRI in asymptomatic
individuals?

answers.A: They are best seen on T2 weighted or FLAIR MRI sequences
answers.B: Asymptomatic individuals rarely have periventricular lesions
answers.C: The majority of patients will develop multiple sclerosis.
answers.D: They are very uncommon in asymptomatic individuals

questions.printed_answer_heading: They are best seen on T2 weighted or FLAIR MRI sequences
questions.explanation:
White matter lesions are best seen on T2-weighted or FLAIR sequences and are nonspecific.
They can be caused by demyelination, ischemia, or gliosis.
Periventricular lesions are less likely to be associated with demyelinating or ischemic disease
than deep lesions.
Larger and confluent white matter hyperintensities indicate more extensive pathology.

questions.question: What is the definitive treatment for cervical spondylosis?
questions.explanation:
A cervical collar may help to immobilize the neck but surgery represents a cure by
decompressing the nerves and fusing the vertebrae
Indications for surgery include progressive neurologic deficits, documented compression of the
cervical nerve root and/or spinal cord, or intractable pain
Initial treatment includes pain medication, soft cervical collar, physical therapy, and traction

questions.question: All the following statements about pneumococcal meningitis are true EXCEPT:

answers.A: There is a vaccine for pneumococcus
answers.B: Patients with no spleen have more severe infections
answers.C: 2nd most common cause of meningitis in adults

questions.printed_answer_heading: 2nd most common cause of meningitis in adults
questions.explanation:
S. pneumoniae is the most common cause of meningitis in adults and 2nd most common in
children >6 years. S. pneumoniae resides in nasopharynx of 5-10% of adults and 20-40% of
children
The bacteria have developed drug tolerances to many agents. For many the treatment requires
advanced cephalosporins, such as ceftriaxone, or with another antibiotics or respiratory
fluoroquinolones, levofloxacin and moxifloxacin
10-20% die from this infection. Symptoms include high fever, nausea, vomiting confusion, stiff
neck, and excruciating headache

questions.question: What is the primary concern of temporal arteritis?
questions.explanation:
Average age onset of temporal arteritis is around 70
Treatment is corticosteroids used to prevent blindness

questions.question: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VRE) infection is treated with:
questions.explanation:
Linezolid can be used to treat Staphylococcus aureus including MRSA or Streptococcus
pneumonia
It is also used for treatment of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VRE) infection
The other medications would not be effective for a high profile resistant bacteria such as VREs

questions.question: All "amide" local anesthetics are metabolized in which of the following?
questions.explanation: All amide anesthetics are metabolized in the liver

questions.question: DVT prophylaxis is not required in:

answers.A: An 18-year-old female who uses oral contraception and undergoes an appendectomy
answers.B: A 55 year old with rectal cancer requiring bowel surgery
answers.C: A 78 year old requiring a hip replacement

questions.explanation:
Today many formulas have been developed to categorize people at risk for DVT
Individuals at low risk include those undergoing minor surgery, young age, and those who are
active in life
Any individual undergoing major surgery, is over the age of 60, has a family history of DVT,
uses oral contraceptives or is immobilized needs DVT prophylaxis

questions.question:
Which of the following types of craniosynostosis is caused by premature closure
of the sagittal suture?
questions.explanation:
50 to 58% of patients with craniosynostosis have premature fusion of the sagittal suture or
scaphocephaly.
It is most common in premature infants.
If both coronal sutures fuse this it termed brachycephaly.
Patients will have increasing biparietal diameter.

questions.question: Bromocriptine therapy is used for:

answers.B: Reduction of symptoms from prolactin secreting adenomas

questions.printed_answer_heading: Reduction of symptoms from prolactin secreting adenomas
questions.explanation:
Treatment with bromocriptine is used to decrease symptoms associated with prolactin secreting
adenomas prior to surgical intervention
It is used in acromegaly to decrease growth hormone production

questions.question: In a one year old child, an enhancing suprasellar mass is most likely a:
questions.explanation:
Although all of the choices can present as a suprasellar mass:
in this age group craniopharyngiomas are much more common with this presentation

questions.question:
Which one of the following oculomotor muscles is not innervated by the 3rd
cranial nerve?
questions.explanation:
The oculomotor nerve controls most of the eyes movements, constriction of pupil and maintains
an open eyelid
Sympathetic postganglionic fibers also join the nerve and are distributed to the smooth muscle of
the levator palpebrae superioris
The oculomotor nerve controls constriction of the pupil and thickening of the lens

questions.question: In the recovery room after elective surgery, vitals should be obtained?
questions.explanation: Vitals are normally taken every fifteen minutes in the PACU

questions.question: Thermal sensation travels along which nerve tracts?
questions.explanation: Thermal sensation is controlled by the lateral spinothalamic tract

questions.question: With regard to sudden death, pulmonary embolism (PE) is second only to:
questions.explanation:
PE is second to only cardiac death as a cause of sudden death
It is a complication of venous thromboembolism, which is most commonly deep venous
thrombosis (DVT)
Diabetes and hypertension have no association with PE

questions.question: Select the correct statement about enkephalin.

answers.A: Enkephalin is only involved with the basal ganglia indirect pathway
answers.B: Enkephalin is only involved with the basal ganglia direct pathway
answers.C: Enkephalin is involved with both the direct and indirect pathways of the basal ganglia
answers.D: Enkephalin is not involved with either the direct or the indirect pathways of the basal ganglia

questions.printed_answer_heading: Enkephalin is only involved with the basal ganglia indirect pathway
questions.explanation:
The putamen has spiny neurons that use enkephalin and GABA in the indirect pathway to the
external segment of the globus pallidus
The external segment of the globus pallidus sends projections to the sub-thalamus that are
GABAergic
Glutamate is the neurotransmitter that is produced by the neurons of the sub-thalamus to the
substantia nigra and the internal part of the globus pallidus
It is theorized that the direct and indirect pathways of the basal ganglia form equilibrium

questions.question:
A newborn is noted to have a cyst containing the lower part of the spinal cord.
Select the correct term for this malformation.
questions.explanation:
The patient has a meningomyelocele, a situation where there is spina bifida cystica with
elements of the spinal cord in the cyst
A meningocele is similar but there is only meninges and CSF in the cyst
The Chiari malformation involves displacement of the cerebellar tonsils into the spinal cord
An encephalocele involves brain tissue projecting from the skull

questions.question:
A patient received a neuromuscular blockers and had neuromuscular paralysis
for more than 13 hours. Which of the following is false?

answers.A: The most likely agent is succinylcholine
answers.B: Blockade may be prolonged in patients with genetic variation of microsomal P450 enzymes
answers.C: Succinylcholine has a half-life of a few minutes
answers.D: It is usually given as a continuous infusion

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Blockade may be prolonged in patients with genetic variation of microsomal P450
enzymes
questions.explanation:
Succinylcholine is a very short acting depolarizing neuromuscular blocker. It binds with
cholinergic receptors at the motor endplate to cayse depolarization.
It is given in continuous infusion on long cases. In patients with partial deficiency of
pseudocholinesterase, one dose may cause paralysis for 5 to 60 minutes.
For those who are homozygous for the defect the paralysis can last for hours.
Mechanical ventilatory support is needed.

questions.question: Which is the principal efferent neuron layer of the cerebral neocortex?
questions.explanation:
The cerebral neocortex is divided into six layers based on a laminar pattern of organization. The
horizontal pattern of incoming afferents, size, and distribution of neuronal cells provide the
divisions.
The principle efferent layer of the cortex is layer V. It has pyramidal cells with axons that run
through the white matter.
These travel through the internal capsule and to all subcortical sites with the exception of the
thalamus.
The thalamus receives fibers from layer VI.

questions.question:
A patient with degenerative disc disease and inability to walk on his toes has
pathology of:
questions.explanation:
S1 sensory: lateral foot, S1 motor: walking on toes
L4 sensory: medial aspect of the leg, L4 motor: ask the patient to squat and rise (knee flexion
and extension)
L5 sensory: medial forefoot and lateral aspect of the leg, L5 motor: heel walking
L3 sensory: distal thigh, L3 motor: hip flexion, adduction and knee extension

questions.question: Following spine surgery what is the incidence of infection?
questions.explanation:
Although risk is low there must be a high index of suspicion
C reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate are important indicators

questions.question: What skull injury is consistent with Battle sign?
questions.explanation:
Battle sign is result of subcutaneous blood pooling
It is associated with basilar skull fracture
Another common sign of basilar skull fracture is raccoon eyes

questions.question:
Which of the following is not a cause of the changes seen in diffusion weighted
MRI in acute stroke?

answers.C: Increase in the apparent diffusion coefficient

questions.printed_answer_heading: Increase in the apparent diffusion coefficient
questions.explanation:
MRI diffusion weighted imaging allows in vivo measurement of the translational mobility of
water
The apparent diffusion coefficient is reduced in tissue that is ischemic
The energy deficit due to lack of perfusion causes failure of the sodium potassium pump
This allows increased sodium and water into the glial and neural cells

questions.question: Which of the following statements about total parenteral nutrition (TPN) is true?

answers.A: Lipid emulsions can lead to fatty emboli and are not added to TPN solutions
answers.B: Electrolytes should be monitored closely until stable
answers.C: In most cases, TPN is administered through peripheral access
answers.D: Equivalent amounts of calories can be delivered via a central or peripheral access

questions.printed_answer_heading: Electrolytes should be monitored closely until stable
questions.explanation:
TPN is nutritional support given intravenously to patients who suffer from malnutrition. TPN
provides all nutrition.
Peripheral veins can be used but this has limitation as to concentration of components and time
so central access is preferred.
Indications for TPN can include malnourishent preoperatively, inflammatory bowel disease, or
coma.

questions.question: Which factor increases the risk of developing a post dural puncture headache?
questions.explanation:
The risk is lower in elderly adults, compared to young adults.
It is increased by using a cutting-edge, compared to a pencil-point needle.
It is decreased by using a smaller bore, compared to a larger bore needle
It is not influenced by ambulation immediately after the dural puncture.

questions.question:
A 63-year-old left-handed female complains of shaking of her right hand for 6
months. It is worst at rest but she can stop the tremor by concentrating. It does not interfere with her
life. She denies and problems with speech, swallowing, or behavior. Exam shows a resting tremor of
the right hand, mildly tremulous handwriting, and contralateral activation causes bilateral cogwheel
rigidity. Rapid alternating movement on the right is bradykinetic. Select the structure that is probably
involved.

answers.B: Anterior horn of the spinal cord

questions.explanation:
The patient has rigidity, tremor, and bradykinesia; classic signs of Parkinson disease (PD)
PD is caused by loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta in the
midbrain
Other pigmented nuclei are also involved
Pathologic findings include Lewy bodies

questions.question:
Which is a rare complication in a patient with autosomal dominant polycystic
kidney disease?
questions.explanation:
Despite the potential for death, subarachnoid hemorrhage is a very rare occurrence in patients
with ADPKD
The aneurysms in the brain do not always rupture as once believed
The major cause of death in these patients is cardiac disease

questions.question: After a spinal cord injury what type of shock develops?
questions.explanation:
Cardiogenic shock is results of reduced cardiac output
Hemorrhagic shock is results of blood loss
Neurogenic shock is results of reduced sympathetic neural input
Hypovolemic shock is results of reduced intravascular volume

questions.question: A patient with a positive Hoffmann sign may have a lesion in the:
questions.explanation:
The Hoffmann sign indicates upper motor neuron disease similar to the Babinski sign
Hoffman sign involves tapping nail or 3rd or 4th finger and getting an involutary flexing of end
of thumb and index finger

questions.question:
Which of the following would not be appropriate steps in managing
hypokalemia?
questions.explanation:
Hypokalemia can be worsened with administration of insulin and glucose
Administration of insulin and glucose pushes potassium into cells

questions.question:
What is the major risk in a patient who has suffered a subarachnoid hemorrhage
from a rupture aneurysm?
questions.explanation:
After subarachnoid hemorrhage from an aneurysm, there is always the risk of a rebleed
However, the most common complication after a subarachnoid hemorrhage is vasospasm of the
intracranial blood vessels
Vasospasm of the vessel can lead to worsening of ischemic and hypoxic injury
The late consequence of subarachnoid hemorrhage is fluid accumulation or hydrocephalus,
which may require a shunt

questions.question:
The most common cause of fever on postoperative day one following surgery
under general anesthesia should be managed by which of the following actions?

answers.B: Instruct the patient to inhale deeply 10 times per hour or to use an incentive spirometer
answers.C: Change the dressing and culture the incision site

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Instruct the patient to inhale deeply 10 times per hour or to use an incentive
spirometer
questions.explanation:
Mild temperature elevations postoperatively are most commonly due to atelectasis from
anesthesia
Post operative respiratory infections typically present within the first 48 hours following surgery

questions.question: Which statement is false about local anesthetics?

answers.D: First sign of CNS effect is seizure

questions.printed_answer_heading: First sign of CNS effect is seizure
questions.explanation: The first sign of toxic CNS effects of local anesthetics is perioral numbness

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to cause positional headaches?
questions.explanation:
Colloid cysts of the 3rd ventricle will obstruct CSF flow through the foramen of Monro when the
patient is standing upright causing a headache
The headaches are generally frontal, severe, intermittent, and transient
They are most common in males in the 3rd to 5th decade
It can progress to acute hydrocephalus and sudden death if not treated

questions.question:
Lesions in the sella or adjacent cavernous sinus can cause all of the following
signs except:
questions.explanation:
The inability to close one's eye is evidence of a CN VII lesion, usually Bell palsy
Anisocoria, unequal pupil size, can be seen with lesions involving CN III, which supply
pupillary and superior eye lid opening
Jaw pain suggests involvement of the mandibular division of CN V. Involvement of CN VI
prevents lateral gaze, creating unopposed in-turning of the eye
CNs III, IV, V1, V2, and VI travel in the cavernous sinus (also: Carotid Artery)

questions.question: Constricted pupils are indicative injury to the:
questions.explanation:
Sympathetic nerve innervates pupil dilation
Parasympathetic controls pupil constriction

questions.question: Which of the following is the direct result of assessment?
questions.explanation:
The action plan, plan of care and implementation of care is based on the diagnosis.
The diagnosis is the direct result of the assessment.
Evaluation of care occurs at the end of the assessment, diagnosis, implementation and evaluation
cycle.
Interviews are largely used in the assessment phase of the APIE cycle.

questions.question: In a newborn, the spinal cord ends at?
questions.explanation: In a newborn, the spinal cord ends at L3

questions.question:
A 41 y/o develops a tremor of the left hand. There are no other symptoms and his
neurologist can find no other abnormality in his exam. His grandfather had a similar tremor. What is
the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Tremor is an involuntary somewhat rhythmic muscle contraction and relaxation producing an
oscillatory movement. There are many causes for tremors.
Essential tremor is the most common and usually begins after 40 years. Children of a parent with
this condition have a 50% chance of getting it
It is associated with no known pathology and begins on one side but involves both by 3 years. It
may involve the hand, head, leg, and trunk.
Some patients may develop a mild gait disturbance. This tremor develops with exertion of the
affected muscle(s). Physical and mental stress can worsen it

questions.question: The diaphragm receives its motor innervation from:
questions.explanation:
The diaphragm is innervated by the phrenic nerve, which is formed from cervical nerves C3-C5
The phrenic nerve contains motor, sensory and sympathetic fibers
Pain arising from the diaphragm may be felt at the shoulder and is referred to as kehr's sign
The right phrenic nerve passes over the subclavian artery and the left phrenic nerve passes over
the pericardium to pierce the diaphragm

questions.question: Huntington's chorea occurs when there is damage to the:
questions.explanation:
Huntingon's chorea appears to affect the basal ganglia, which is composed of the caudate nucleus
and putamen
These areas appear to lose their neurons and spiny cells
The basal ganglia plays a key role in movement and behavior
Autopsy findings indicate that patients with HD have significantly less CREB binding protein

questions.question: Visual information from the retina is usually processed by the:
questions.explanation:
The lateral geniculate nucleus is the primary processing center for visual information from the
retina
From the LGN axons are seen passing through the optic radiation to the primary visual cortex
The lateral geniculate nucleus also refines certain receptive fields

questions.question: Which following feature is not seen with postoperative morphine overdose?
questions.explanation:
When there is morphine overdose respiratory depression is common. Besides shallow breathing,
the respiration rate also starts to slow down
Head injury patients should not be give morphine because there are reports that it can cause an
increase in intracranial pressure
Biliary colic is also a common complication reported but there is little clinical evidence to
support this

questions.question: The posterior pituitary secretes which of the following?
questions.explanation:
ADH is secreted from the posterior pituitary
The posterior pituitary is a modified nerve cell that stores and releases ADH
GH, TSH, and ACTH are all secreted from the anterior pituitary

questions.question: Select the EXCEPTION in disclosing Protected Health Information-PHI:
questions.explanation:
In cases of suspected child or elder abuse PHI must be disclosed as required by law.
Facilitation of treatment, payment, or health care operations allows for disclosure of Protected
Health Information-PHI.
Authorization from the individual allows for PHI to be disclosed.
Only the pertinent and minimum information related to the covered entity may be disclosed under
Protected Health Information-PHI.

questions.question:
Select the most likely bacterial pathogen causing meningitis after traumatic skull
fracture.
questions.explanation:
50 to 70% of meningitis after traumatic skull fractures is caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae
This has even occurred years after the trauma
It has been recommended that patients with closed head trauma and CSF leakage should receive
pneumococcal vaccine

questions.question:
A patient has been fasting for 3 days days and his glucose level is 60% of his
normal level. The patient feels fine because his central nervous system is utilizing what alternative
energy source?
questions.explanation:
Acetoacetate, acetone, and beta-hydroxybutyrate are ketones produced by the liver by beta
oxidation of fatty acids
Transported by the blood to the kidneys, muscles, brain, and other organs; they are used as an
alternative energy source
Small amounts of glucose are needed by the brain to function

questions.question: Which of the following tests are used to confirm HIV infection?
questions.explanation:
ELISA is the most common screening test used to detect HIV
The Western blot detects HIV antibodies to specific HIV proteins and glycoproteins
Confirmatory test is always done by Western blot
Polymerase chain reactions is also used for confirmation

questions.question: Rate of absorption of a drug is inversely proportional to which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Rate of absorption of a certain drug is always inversely proportional to its particle size
If the particle size is bigger absorption is always slower
Absorption of alkaline drugs is increased in higher pH
Absorption of acidic drugs is increased by lower pH

questions.question: Which of the following is not a reason that epinephrine is used for anaphylaxis?

answers.B: Augmentation of the release of mediators

questions.printed_answer_heading: Augmentation of the release of mediators
questions.explanation:
Epinephrine raises blood pressure, antagonizes mediators in the system, and inhibits the release
of mediators
Bronchospasm is also decreased with epinephrine
Epinephrine should be given IM in the vastus lateralis

questions.question:
Which patient is not at increased risk of vasospasm following subarachnoid
hemorrhage (SAH)?

answers.D: Large volumes of blood in the subarachnoid space

questions.explanation: Females have increased risk of vasospasm

questions.question:
Which of the following statements concerning the anatomy of the spinal cord is
false?

answers.A: Spinal cord ends around L2 as the conus medullaris
answers.B:
Corticospinal tract - posterolateral, controls motor power on the same side, tested by voluntary
muscle contractions.
answers.C:
Spinothalamic tract - anterolateral, pain and temperature opposite side, tested by pinprick and
light touch
answers.D:
Posterior columns - posterior, position and vibration on same side, tested by position sense in
toes and fingers or vibration using a tuning fork

questions.printed_answer_heading: Spinal cord ends around L2 as the conus medullaris
questions.explanation: Spinal cord ends at L1 as the conus medullaris

questions.question:
What is the correct diagnosis for a patient who is not arousable but flexes the
extremities with painful stimuli?
questions.explanation:
The decorticate patient flexes the extremities with painful stimuli
Decerebrate patients extend the extremities to painful stimuli
Lethargic patients are arousable at times

questions.question:
A patient suffers complete spinal cord transection at T5-T6. Which muscle
should be strengthened prior to working on transfers?
questions.explanation: The latissimus dorsi is in the T5-T6 area but innervated from cervical spine nerves

questions.question: Select the incorrect statement about pediatric spinal cord injury?

answers.A: The most unstable part of the child's cervical column is segments C3/C4
answers.B: Subluxation of the vertebrae by more than 8 mm is abnormal
answers.C: Pseudo-subluxation tends to resolves when the x-ray is done with the child in a sniffing position
answers.D: Normal spine x-rays are commonly seen in at least 70% of children with spinal cord injury

questions.printed_answer_heading: The most unstable part of the child's cervical column is segments C3/C4
questions.explanation:
C2-C3 is the most unstable area of children's cervical spine because of their relatively larger
heads.
Pseudosubluxation or anterior displacement is present in 40% of those <7 years and 20% of
those <16 years. 3 mm of motion of C2 on C3 is normal.
If the head is placed into a sniffing, neutral position, it can be corrected radiographically.
Cervical spine radiographs in children are only 66% sensitive for spinal cord injuries.
Of these patients, half of them have delayed onset of symptoms and paralysis can occur 4 days
after the injury.

questions.question:
Which one of the following drugs should be administered to treat anaphylaxis
following a bee sting?
questions.explanation:
Epinephrine is the treatment for anaphylaxis
It relaxes the respiratory tract smooth muscle and stimulates the heart to increase cardiac output
Epinephrine increases cyclic AMP levels preventing mast cell degranulation.
Diphenhydramine,a H1 histamine receptor antagonist, is not effective for anaphylaxis.

questions.question: Which spinal nerve innervates the brachioradialis?
questions.explanation:
Shoulder pain is related to C5 spinal nerve injury
C5 controls muscle innervation to the biceps and brachioradialis
C6 injury relates to numbness of lateral forearm and hand
C7 controls medial two fingers

questions.question: Testing proprioception should be done:

answers.A: At the end range of a joint
answers.B: At the midrange of a joint
answers.C: At the point pain is elicited
answers.D: At the point the stretch reflex is elicited

questions.printed_answer_heading: At the midrange of a joint
questions.explanation:
Proprioception testing should be done at the midrange of a joint
Pain and the stretch reflex should be avoided
The movement should be about 10 degrees per second

questions.question:
A patient has a painful left arm. During the exam pain is produced with light
touch. What is this condition called?
questions.explanation:
Hyperpathia is when a nociceptive stimulus produces an exaggerated pain response
Allodynia is a pain response to light touch
Dysesthesias are disagreeable sensations
Mononeuritis multiplex is an asynchronous, asymmetrical motor and sensory neuropathy that is
painful

questions.question:
It takes the greatest amount of applied force to injury which of these vertebral
levels?
questions.explanation:
The thoracic spine is protected/reinforced by the rib cage
Therefore, of the above choices, T4 is the most supported vertebral level and requires the most
force to injure

questions.question:
Which pathology is typically found in the autopsies of more than 50% of
hospitalized patients?
questions.explanation:
More than 650,000 patients have pulmonary embolisms in the U.S. each year making it the 3rd
most common cause of death.
It is possibly the second most common cause in most age groups of unexpected death. It is
common in hospitalized patients.
Autopsy studies show that up to 60% of patients that die in the hospital had pulmonary
embolisms but it had only been diagnosed in 30%.
It is recognized as a common complication postoperatively but also is common in medical
inpatients.

questions.question:
Which of the following anomalies are not associated with VACTERL
association?
questions.explanation:
VACTERL or VATER association of disorders encompasses a wide range of anomalies
Vertebral defects, anal atresia, cardiovascular defects, tracheoesophageal fistula, renal defects,
and limb are common with this condition
Aniridia is not part of VATER association
Radial dysplasia is another typical feature of this disease

questions.question:
An acute cerebrovascular accident (CVA) characterized by left-sided
hemiparesis but no expressive aphasia is most consistent with occlusion of:
questions.explanation:
A stroke in the right middle cerebral distribution would cause left-sided hemiparesis but not
expressive aphasia.

questions.question:
A child exposed to a loud noise extends and abducts her arms. What reflex is
being described?
questions.explanation:
The startle or Moro reflex is characterized by external rotation, extension, and abduction of the
arms in response to a loud noise or being dropped
The gallant reflex is elicited by stroking along the spine and results in curving the spine in this
direction
The flexor withdrawal reflex is response to pain and results in flexion
The rooting reflex is elicited by stroking the corner of the mouth and results in turning of the head
and extension of the tongue to prepare for latching on to the nipple

questions.question: Select the correct statement about the internal segment of the globus pallidus.

answers.A: It is only involved in the basal ganglia direct pathway
answers.B: It is only involved in the basal ganglia indirect pathway
answers.C: It is involved in both the direct and indirect pathways of the basal ganglia
answers.D: It is not involved with either the direct or the indirect pathways of the basal ganglia

questions.printed_answer_heading: It is involved in both the direct and indirect pathways of the basal ganglia
questions.explanation:
The putamen has spiny neurons that project to the internal segment of the globus pallidus directly
using GABA and substance P
The indirect pathway uses GABA and enkephalin projections to the external segment of the
globus pallidus, which in turn sends GABAergic projections to the sub-thalamus
The subthalamic nucleus has projections to the internal part of the globus pallidus with glutamate
as the neurotransmitter
It is theorized that the direct and indirect pathways of the basal ganglia form equilibrium with the
indirect pathway increasing output from the substantia nigra internal segment of the globus
pallidus

questions.question: Epidural steroid injections are most effective for lower back pain when?

answers.A: Pain has lasted for more than 12 months
answers.B: Pain has been poorly controlled with oral narcotic

questions.explanation:
Epidural steroid injections for lower back pain are most effective in the presence of radicular
pain
Radicular pain usually indicates presence of nerve root inflammation, which may respond to
anti-inflammatory effects of corticosteroids
Epidural steroids are most effective for low back pain that has been present for less than 3
months duration. Steroids generally do not work if the pain has gone on for more than 1 year
Epidural steroid injections are usually not indicated for low back pain, which is poorly
controlled and/or persists after surgery, unless there is associated radicular pain

questions.question: The best screening test for detecting deep venous thrombophlebitis is:
questions.explanation:
Compression ultrasound is a very sensitive and specific modality for diagnosis of lower
extremity DVT
The technique is portable, cheap and readily available
The study can be accomplished within minutes at the bedside

questions.question: What disease is associated with Argyll Robertson pupil?
questions.explanation: Argyll Robertson pupil is associated with syphilis infection

questions.question: Which of the following sites for lumbar disc herniation is most common?
questions.explanation:
Approximately 95% of disc herniations in the lumbar area occur at L4-L5 or L5-S1.
About 4% are at L3-L4 and <1% are at L1-L2 or L2-L3.

questions.question: What is true about Erb's palsy?

answers.A: Involves injury to the 5th and 6th cervical nerves
answers.B: Most infants who suffer this injury have a good prognosis
answers.C: The limb is abducted, supinated and externally rotated
answers.D: There is wasting of thenar muscles

questions.printed_answer_heading: Involves injury to the 5th and 6th cervical nerves
questions.explanation:
Erb's palsy occurs when there is injury during childbirth to the 5th and 6th cervical nerve roots
The injury is often severe and full recovery of function is unlikely.
The injury presents with a straight hand, arm hangs at the side and is rotated medially while the
forearm is extended and pronated.
Thenar muscle wasting is a sign of median nerve compression

questions.question: The adenohypophysis is derived from:
questions.explanation:
Rathke's pouch is a depression in the roof of the developing mouth.
Rathke's pouch gives rise to the anterior pituitary.
Rathkes' pouch eventually loses the connection with the pharynx.
Craniopharyngiomas are neoplasms that arise from rathke's cleft.

questions.question: A patient with meralgia paresthetica has inflammation of which nerve:
questions.explanation:
Meralgia paresthetica is an inflammation of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve
It is usually caused by nerve compression

questions.question: Which of the following statements is not true about cerebral palsy?

answers.A: It is a non progressive encephalopathy
answers.B: It describes a disability of motor function seen in early infancy
answers.C:
Patients usually demonstrate problems with muscle tone (typically spasticity), ataxia, or
involuntary movements
answers.D: Cognitive, behavioral, and sensory problems must be present to make the diagnosis

questions.printed_answer_heading: Cognitive, behavioral, and sensory problems must be present to make the diagnosis
questions.explanation:
Cerebral palsy is a non progressive encephalopathy that leads to hypertonic muscles and ataxia
Cognitive and behavioral problems are not necessary to make a diagnosis

questions.question: Which of the following is not a component of malpractice?
questions.explanation:
Malpractice components center around an obligation to maintain an established standard of care.
A departure from care standards in which the client suffers harm is generally seen with
malpractice.

questions.question:
An 8 year old without significant past medical history has sudden onset of a
headache and then falls. Exam shows right facial weakness and right hemiparesis. There is conjugate
ocular deviation to the left. Select the most probable diagnosis.
questions.explanation:
The patient most likely has had a thromboembolic event with middle cerebral artery occlusion
Hemiparesis with gaze toward the lesion makes this most likely
This can be secondary to hypercoagulable state, congenital structural disorders, metabolic
disorders, arteritis, trauma, or infection
Hemiplegic migraine is usually seen in patients with a history of migraine

questions.question: What type of inheritance pattern is followed by tuberous sclerosis?
questions.explanation:
Tuberous sclerosis is an autosomal dominant disorder.
Patients commonly have mental retardation and seizure disorders.
Links to chromosome nine and sixteen.

questions.question: Which may be present in severe head injury?
questions.explanation:
ECG changes, seizures, paralysis, abnormal posturing, respiratory depression, Cheyne stokes
breathing, and Cushing triad may be present in severe head injury

questions.question:
Which of the following aphasia is characterized by non-fluent aphasia with poor
repetition but good comprehension?
questions.explanation:
Broca aphasia results from a lesion of the inferior frontal lobe, Brodmann 44, 45
An inability to recall proper names and names of objects is called anomic aphasia
In patients with transcortical aphasia there are various impairments but the patient is able to
repeat words relatively well

questions.question: Which of the following patients with head trauma does not require admission?
questions.explanation:
Many patients with head trauma have a variety of presenting features. Besides concussion,
headache, nausea, vomiting, memory loss or dizziness, others may have emotional lability or
sleep disturbances
In most cases a negative CT scan and a period of observation of 8 hrs is sufficient and patients
can be discharged. Alcoholics or those who are under the influence of drugs and have head
trauma should undergo CT scan and be observed for at least 12-24 hours
A neurologic exam is vital for all patients with head trauma. The initial GCS provides a
classification of patients with head injuries. Individual who cannot sleep after head trauma do
not necessarily have to be admitted if the CT scan is clear
Other indications of hospital admission include severe penetrating head injury, prolonged loss of
consciousness, severe headache, seizure, skull fracture or the individual has no one at home. If a
head CT is not available, consider admitting the patient

questions.question:
Which of the following is true regarding the spiritual associations related to
body parts and strength?

answers.A: Body parts may be associated with certain physical and spiritual strengths
answers.B: Organ donation and cremation are forbidden by some cultures and religions

questions.explanation:
Body parts may be associated with certain physical and spiritual strengths in some cultures and
religions.
Organ donation and cremation are forbidden by some cultures and religions.
Patients' cultural and religious beliefs must be considered if care to meet the needs of the "whole
person."

questions.question:
Select the patient that would be the best candidate for treatment of Parkinson
disease with deep brain subthalamic stimulation.

answers.A:
A 40 year old patient with idiopathic, L-dopa responsive disease with L-dopa induced
dyskinesias and no mood problems or behavioral issues
answers.B: A 50 year old patient with idiopathic, L-dopa unresponsive disease with disabling tremor
answers.C:
A 45 year old patient with idiopathic, L-dopa responsive disease with medication resistant
tremor and severe depression
answers.D:
A 50 year old patient with idiopathic, L-dopa responsive disease with dyskinesias and cognitive
impairment

questions.printed_answer_heading:
A 40 year old patient with idiopathic, L-dopa responsive disease with L-dopa
induced dyskinesias and no mood problems or behavioral issues
questions.explanation:
Deep brain subthalamic stimulation is best suited for patients with L-dopa responsive disease
but disabling motor fluctuations resistant to medications or L-dopa induced dyskinesia
Patients should not have mood problems, behavioral issues, or significant cognitive impairment

questions.question:
Which of the following is a serious complication of spinal anesthesia which
requires immediate intervention?
questions.explanation:
With spinal anesthesia there is risk of causing respiratory paralysis
Artificial ventilation is required in such cases

questions.question: Which is the most common acquired cause of growth hormone deficiency?
questions.explanation: Although all are causes, CNS tumors are the most common

questions.question:
An African American female comes to the emergency room with facial
weakness. The right side started yesterday and the left side today. She has hand no constitutional
symptoms or rashes. She lives in Chicago and has no pets. She is employed in an office and has no
hobbies with exposures to chemical. She has hypertension and is on hydrochlorothiazide. Blood
pressure is 130/85 mm Hg, pulse is 85, respirations 16, and she is afebrile. The right side of the face
is paralyzed but she can raise her eyebrow on the left. Chest radiograph has bilateral hilar
lymphadenopathy. MRI with gadolinium show enhancement of the 7th cranial nerve and meninges
bilaterally. Lumbar puncture yields CSF with an opening pressure of 12 cm H2O, with no red cells,
21 white cells with 82% lymphocytes and 28% neutrophils, protein 72 mg/dL, and glucose 62 mg/dL.
Gram stain is negative. Select the most likely diagnosis.
questions.explanation:
5 to 10% of patients with sarcoidosis have neurologic manifestations
The presenting complaint of sarcoidosis is neurologic symptoms half the time
The most common neurologic findings are cranial nerve involvement, basilar meningitis,
myelopathy, and anterior hypothalamic disease
Treatment initially would be prednisone 0.5 mg/kg daily

questions.question:
A middle aged man complains of headaches and lateralizing weakness. CT scan
of the brain reveals an irregular mass in the left cerebral hemisphere confirmed as glioblastoma.
Which of the following statements regarding glioblastoma multiforme is true?

answers.A: It originates from the nerve sheath.
answers.B: It arises from the malignant degeneration of astrocytes
answers.D: It is the most common tumor in children

questions.printed_answer_heading: It arises from the malignant degeneration of astrocytes
questions.explanation:
Glioblastoma multiforme is a grade IV astrocytoma or anaplastic astrocytoma which is the most
common form of primary intracranial neuroepithelial tumor derived from glial cells.
These tumors are most commonly found in the cerebral hemispheres during the fifth decade of
life. CT and MRI scans typically reveal an irregular lesion with hypodense central necrosis and
peripheral ring enhancement with edema and mass effect.
Median survival is 1 year. Treatment involves surgery followed by radiation therapy.

questions.question:
What is the most likely cause of dizziness and light headedness in a patient with
a history of a spinal cord injury?
questions.explanation:
Patients with spinal cord injuries often have problems with orthostatic hypotension
They may not be able to tolerate being upright and may need a reclining back wheelchair
A gradual program working toward being able to tolerate being upright may be needed

questions.question: What is the estimated mortality of nosocomial pneumonia?
questions.explanation:
The mortality associated with nosocomial pneumonia is fairly high at 30-50%
Risk factors include indwelling urethral catheters, intravascular catheters, use of broad-spectrum
antibiotics, intubation, previous hospital stay and recent thoracic or abdominal surgery
Most common etiologic organisms are gram-negatives such as Pseudomonas, Klebsiella, E. coli,
and Enterobacter
MRSA, Strep, Candida, anaerobes, and polymicrobial infections are other causes

questions.question:
A 41 y/o female notices mild paresthesias of the arms and legs with some
intermittent incoordination. When she takes a hot bath, the symptoms temporarily become more
debilitating. Bending her neck forward causes an electrical shock down the back of her spine.
Symptoms resolve eventually. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
MS can begin with many different neurological symptoms and trends
The development of mild symptoms that remit is a common scenario
Pain radiating down the spine with cervical flexion is Lhermitte sign seen is MS and other
conditions.

questions.question: Select the true statement about ED50.

answers.A: It is the amount of a drug that would cause toxicity in 50% of patients
answers.B: It is the amount of a drug that would be effective in 50% of patients
answers.C: It is the amount of a drug that would provide 50% of maximal effect
answers.D: It is the amount of a drug that would cause erectile dysfunction in 50% of patients

questions.printed_answer_heading: It is the amount of a drug that would be effective in 50% of patients
questions.explanation:
ED is the "effective dose"
ED50 means that 50% of patients would have the desired therapeutic effect at the given dose
ED75 means that 75% of patients would have the desired therapeutic effect at the given dose

questions.question: All of the following tumors can arise from the pineal gland EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Additional tumors that can arise from the pineal area are choriocarcinoma, pineocytoma,
germinoma, pineal cyst, and astrocytoma

questions.question:
A patient has serum potassium of 2.7 mEq/L but no symptoms. What is the
treatment of choice?
questions.explanation:
Asymptomatic patients with potassium levels greater than 2.5 mEq/L can be treated safely with
oral potassium
Very low potassium levels can be treated with intravenous potassium
Both oral and intravenous potassium can be used simultaneously
Difficult to correct hypokalemia can be secondary to hypomagnesemia

questions.question:
When evaluating or moving a patient with a possible cervical spine injury,
which technique is safest?

answers.A: Maintain inline traction and log roll

questions.printed_answer_heading: Maintain inline traction and log roll
questions.explanation: Inline tracking and log rolling protects the spinal column and keeps the body in alignment

questions.question:
A patient has been stable on drug A for several years and is started and drug B.
Drug B is a competitive antagonist of drug A. What will occur?

answers.A: There will be a change of potency of drug A
answers.B: There will be a change of efficacy of drug A
answers.C: Drug B will bind irreversibly to the receptor, competing with drug A
answers.D: Drug B will bind at a different site than drug A

questions.printed_answer_heading: There will be a change of potency of drug A
questions.explanation:
The decrease in potency of drug A is due to competitive inhibition by drug B
The efficacy of drug A as drug B will bind reversibly to the same site as A

questions.question: In a 46 year old with pulsatile unilateral tinnitus, one would suspect?
questions.explanation:
When tinnitus is pulsatile and unilateral, it is important to rule out a cerebellopontine tumor or
paraganglioma

questions.question:
A patient with a left CVA has homonymous hemianopsia. Where would the
visual defect be found?

answers.A: Right eye nasal and left eye temporal
answers.C: Left eye nasal and right eye temporal

questions.printed_answer_heading: Left eye nasal and right eye temporal
questions.explanation:
A patient with a left CVA loses the right side of vision
This would involve the right eye temporal half and the left eye nasal half

questions.question:
Where in the brainstem would the lesion be found for a patient with contralateral
hemiplegia also involving the lower face, ipsilateral oculomotor paresis, ptosis, and dilated pupils?
questions.explanation:
Ischemia of the ventral midbrain would result in contralateral hemiplegia also involving the
lower face, ipsilateral oculomotor paresis, ptosis, and dilated pupils
The main blood supply of the midbrain is from the posterior cerebral artery with contribution
from the superior cerebellar artery

questions.question: Patients with sulfa allergy should not be given one of the following medications:
questions.explanation:
Celecoxib is COX-2 inhibitor NSAID used for pain relief and to prevent familial colon polyps
It is preferred for use in patients who cannot tolerate aspirin
It has no effect on platelet aggregation
Since it has a sulfa component, it is not indicated for use in patients with sulfa allergy

questions.question:
Which type of Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome is associated with rupture of blood
vessels?
questions.explanation:
Ehler-Danlos syndrome is a group of connective-tissue disorders with joint hypermobility,
hyperextensibility, and cutaneous fragility
Type 4 involves type III collagen leading to vascular disease
Over 10 types exist with over 10 gene mutations identified affecting various types of collagen

questions.question:
In which one of the following disorders should one take extreme precautions in
handling tissue because of potential for infection:
questions.explanation:
BSE is also known as mad cow disease. It is a fatal neurodegenerative disease that causes
spongy degeneration of the brain
The infection is most commonly acquired by eating meat (esp the brain) from contaminated cattle
It appears that cattle acquire the infectious prion by eating animal byproducts
Jacob Creutzfeldt is related to BSE and has a rapid course. Individuals develop a variety of
mental and physical disturbances, Ataxia, muscle spasms and dementia are common

questions.question: Hemodialysis is effective to remove:
questions.explanation:
Carbamazepine, phenytoin, and valproic acid cannot be removed by dialysis
Phenobarbitol is dialyzable

questions.question:
When evaluating the oculocephalic reflex, which direction do the eyes turn when
the head turns to the left?
questions.explanation: In the oculocephalic reflex, the eyes turn in the opposite direction of the head

questions.question:
Which of the following radiographic studies is best to examine basilar artery
infarcts?
questions.explanation:
The first study usually obtained is CT due to availability and has greater than 95% sensitivity for
detecting hemorrhage but has low sensitivity for early ischemia
MRI/MRA is much more sensitive for detecting vascular occlusion and early ischemia
Transcranial Doppler is relatively insensitive for this diagnosis

questions.question: Which of the following is a component of a stress reaction?
questions.explanation:
Components of a stress reaction include release of adrenalin and ACTH and relaxation of the
bronchial tree
Another component of the reaction is slowing of the digestive process
The stress reaction prepares the body to react efficiently to a stressor

questions.question: Which of the following is the ideal strategy to manage a language barrier?

answers.A: Use a language computer to translate
answers.C: Meet with an interpreter before and during the clinical visit
answers.D: Provide written information in multiple languages to be translated

questions.printed_answer_heading: Meet with an interpreter before and during the clinical visit
questions.explanation: Talking with the interpreter prior to and during the visit improves communication.

questions.question:
A patient involved in a motor vehicle accident suffers traumatic brain injury and
the Glasgow Coma Scale score is 6 out of 15. Select the most probable prognosis.

answers.A: Mild impairment with good rehabilitation potential
answers.C: Severe impairment with moderate rehabilitation potential
answers.D: Severe impairment with poor rehabilitation potential

questions.printed_answer_heading: Severe impairment with poor rehabilitation potential
questions.explanation:
A Glasgow Coma Scale of less than 8 indicates severe brain injury
The scale rates eye, verbal, and motor response and ranges from 3 to 15
It is used acutely in the emergency department and in intensive care to follow patients

questions.question: Which of the following is not a contraindication to a lumbar puncture?
questions.explanation:
There are some absolute contraindications to lumbar puncture like midline shift, coagulopathy,
brain abscess or elevated intracranial pressure
Other contraindications include a posterior fossa mass, loss of superior cerebellar cistern and
quadrigeminal plate cistern
Indications for brain CT prior to lumbar puncture include elderly patient, immunocompromised
host and those who have had a recent seizure
Indications for CT scan also include papilledema or a focal neurological deficit

questions.question: Which is false about primidone?

answers.A: Is often used to treat tremor in patients with Parkinson disease
answers.D: Is administered several times a day

questions.printed_answer_heading: Is often used to treat tremor in patients with Parkinson disease
questions.explanation:
Primidone is used to treat tremor secondary to epilepsy and essential tremor.
It can be used for essential tremor in those that cannot take propranolol or in addition.
The mechanism of action is not known and it does not improve the tremor from Parkinson
disease.
Active metabolites phenobarbital and phenylethylmalonamide (PEMA). Phenobarbital has
minimal effects on tremor and PEMA has none.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions could not produce decerebrate rigidity?
questions.explanation:
Decerebrate rigidity involves opisthotonos, head and back arched backwards, and rigid
extension of arms and legs with internal rotation.
This occurs with damage to the midbrain below the red nucleus.
Other conditions that can lead to brainstem damage are some brainstem strokes, brain tumors,
intracranial hematoma, encephalopathy, and supratentorial infarcts.
Most of these conditions have the potential to produce mass effect and edema which elevates the
intracranial pressure to the point that there is downward pressure compressing the midbrain and
lower structures resulting in severe distortion of the anatomy and ischemia.

questions.question:
Which finding is least likely on MRI in patients with intracranial hypotension
associated headaches?
questions.explanation:
Distal transverse sinus narrowing is more likely to be seen in patients with idiopathic
intracranial hypertension
Intracranial hypotension will most likely show pachymeningeal enhancement, intracranial
venous distension, subdural fluid collections, and sagging of the brain
Another response to intracranial hypotension can be cervical or thoracic spinal meningeal
diverticula

questions.question:
Which of the following is a contraindication to receiving tPA in a 66 year old
patient?
questions.explanation:
A history of cerebral hemorrhage is a contraindication to administration of thrombolytics
because the risk of hemorrhage may be further increased

questions.question: All of the following statements about ICP wave forms are correct EXCEPT?

answers.A: Individual wave form is broken down to P1, P2, and P3
answers.B: B wave reflects changes in body position
answers.C:
C waves also called Traube-Herring-Mayer waves reflect low frequency blood pressure waves
modulated by central and peripheral baroreceptors and chemoreceptors
answers.D:
A waves, called plateau waves, show a rapid rise to 50-100 mm maintained for a variable
period before a rapid fall to baseline.

questions.printed_answer_heading: B wave reflects changes in body position
questions.explanation:
B waves reflect changes in respiration
A waves are pathological indicating brain compliance is deteriorating and impending herniation
is a strong possibility
P1 is a percussion wave secondary to pulsations from choroids plexus. P2 indicates relative
brain volume and P3 is the downward trend after the dicrotic notch

questions.question: Where in relation to the lumbar spine will one find the sympathetic chain?
questions.explanation:
The lumbar sympathetic chain is located on the anterolateral border of the spine
It is composed of pre and postganglionic nerves

questions.question: All of the following are true regarding cyanosis except:

answers.A: It is usually is a sign of hypoxemia
answers.B: It is most often seen and detected on the eyelids
answers.D: It occurs when unoxygenated hemoglobin content reaches 5 g/dL

questions.printed_answer_heading: It is most often seen and detected on the eyelids
questions.explanation:
Cyanosis is a blue or purple tinge to skin or mucous membranes that is most often detected on
finger tips and lips
Peripheral vasoconstriction as occurs with Raynaud phenomenon can cause peripheral cyanosis
Evaluation of a patient with cyanosis requires measuring oxygen saturation and arterial blood
gases
Cyanosis can be caused by methemoglobin, which cannot release oxygen, producing a normal
oxygen saturation and decresed PO2

questions.question:
A patient is diagnosed with idiopathic intracranial hypertension. Select the
treatment that will preserve vision.
questions.explanation:
Optic nerve sheath decompression will preserve vision but not address other problems
associated with idiopathic intracranial hypertension.
VP or lumboperitoneal shunts are effective treatments.
Intracranial venous sinus stent placement preserves vision and lowers intracranial pressure.

questions.question:
Which of the following apply to clinical pathways and their use in managed
care?

answers.A:
Clinical pathways are widely used in managed care to promote the most effective and efficient
course of treatment
answers.B:
Clinical pathways were developed and used in academic settings for medical students and house
physicians before being introduced into mainstream medical and surgical medicine

questions.explanation:
Clinical pathways are widely used in managed care to promote the most effective and efficient
course of treatment.
Clinical pathways were developed and used in academic settings for medical students and house
physicians before being introduced into mainstream medical and surgical medicine.
Traditional medicine was initially reluctant to use clinical pathways. They were often referred
to as crib sheets and "cookbook medicine" before becoming a prominent feature of contemporary
medicine.

questions.question: Symptomatic lumbar disc herniation are most common in the:
questions.explanation:
Posterolaeral lumbar disc herniations are most likely to impinge on the nerve root causing
symptoms.
Posterolateral lumbar disc herniations are also more likely given the posterior longitudinal
ligament.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is true regarding the nuclei of the trigeminal
nerve?

answers.A: The trigeminal nerve has two sensory nuclei
answers.B:
Most small fibers from the spinal tract of the trigeminal nerve terminate in the main sensory
nucleus
answers.C: The spinal nucleus carries information about pain and temperature
answers.D: The motor nucleus innervates the muscles of mastication via its maxillary division

questions.printed_answer_heading: The spinal nucleus carries information about pain and temperature
questions.explanation:
The trigeminal nerve has three sensory nuclei.
There is a main sensory nucleus.
The spinal nucleus of the trigeminal nerve is extends from the point of entry of the nerve to the
upper spinal cord.
The mesencephalic nucleus is in the rostral pons.

questions.question: Which is not a characteristic of the Balint syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Balint syndrome is associated with lesion at the parietooccipital area
Characterized by agnosia, optic ataxia, and apraxia

questions.question: The rate-limiting step for serotonin synthesis is which of the following enzymes?
questions.explanation:
The rate-limiting enzyme for serotonin synthesis is tryptophan hydroxylase
Most serotonergic neurons are in the raphe nuclei

questions.question:
Which of the following lab values would be abnormal in parathormone (PTH)
deficiency?
questions.explanation:
Parathyroid hormone or parathormone (PTH) is made by the parathyroid glands in the neck
It regulates calcium and phosphate concentrations
It does not affect sodium or potassium

questions.question: Which of the following is a common side effect of valproic acid?
questions.explanation:
Valproic acid may cause a fulminant liver failure
Children who are taking other hepatotoxic medications are at increased risk
Other side effects of this medication is weight gain and thrombocytopenia

questions.question: What is the most sensitive sign of high intracranial pressure?
questions.explanation:
Loss of consciousness is often the first presenting sign of high intracranial pressure
It is also the most sensitive sign

questions.question:
What type of necrosis is most often associated with central nervous system
infection?
questions.explanation: Liquefactive necrosis is common in CNS infection
review_required: Question text and options repeated elsewhere in source PDF

questions.question:
A patient complains of double vision when he moves his head to the left
shoulder but this is improved by tilting the head away from the unaffected side. The patient most
likely has:
questions.explanation:
Bielschowsky head tilt test is often done to assess damage to the 4th cranial nerve
There is double vision in patients with trochlear nerve palsy that is improved by tilting the head
towards the affected side
Tilting the head away from the affected side aggravates double vision

questions.question: A beta fiber is usually:
questions.explanation: A beta fiber is a large and myelinated sensory fiber

questions.question: A nurse practitioner can never:
questions.explanation: Nurse practitioners can do all of the above except certifying a death certificate

questions.question:
What degree of depression in a skull fracture is deemed necessary for elevation
by surgery?
questions.explanation:
Children are more likely than adults to require surgery for depressed skull fractures.
Surgery is usually done if depression is 5 mm or more. Dural tears, gross contamination, or
underlying hematomas are also indications.
Skull fractures should not be probed.
They should be assessed by direct visualization.

questions.question: Which of the following does not traverse the cavernous sinus?
questions.explanation:
The cavernous sinus contains CN III, IV, V1, V2, and VI but not V3
This venous structure between the temporal and sphenoid bones also contains the internal
carotid artery
If an aneurysm of the intercavernous portion of the internal carotid artery ruptures it may cause a
cavernous-carotid fistula associated with a pulsating, painful injected eye

questions.question:
When dealing with a terminally ill patient which stage of bereavement should
hospice care be discussed?
questions.explanation:
There are five stages of bereavement according to the Kubler-Ross model
It is best to discuss hospice care when patients accept their illness
It is difficult to intervene when patients are in a stage of denial
Not all patients go through the same sequence of bereavement

questions.question: Ropivacaine is supplied as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Ropivacaine is supplied as the S isomer. The active form of ropivacaine is the S isomer only

questions.question:
A patient has countercoup head injury with resulting problems understanding
speech and with hearing. Select the part of the brain that was most likely injured.
questions.explanation: Wernicke area and the primary auditory cortex are located in the temporal lobe

questions.question:
All of the following are true about the use of helicopters in Emergency Medical
Services EXCEPT:

answers.B: The pilot must decide if the conditions make it safe to fly
answers.C: Transfer between hospitals is more common than scene responses
answers.D: Barotrauma is a factor that must always be considered

questions.printed_answer_heading: Barotrauma is a factor that must always be considered
questions.explanation:
Helicopters are safer than ambulances per mile a patient is flown.
Barotrauma is usually not an issue since helicopters normally fly at altitudes less than 4000 feet.

questions.question:
If a patient has unilateral paralysis of the muscles of the lower portion of the
face, where is the lesion?

answers.A: Motor nucleus of the facial nerve
answers.C: The facial nerve at the acoustic meatus
answers.D: The facial nerve at the facial canal

questions.explanation:
Unilateral lower half facial paralysis Indicates a lesion in the descending motor pathway
Facial nerve damage at the facial canal would cause complete unilateral facial paralysis
Facial nerve damage at the auditory meatus would cause complete unilateral facial paralysis and
the nerve to the nasal, lacrimal, and palatine glands
A motor nucleus lesion would denervate all the facial muscles on one side

questions.question: The relative oxygen reserve of the brain is?
questions.explanation: The oxygen reserve of the brain is low at any given time

questions.question:
What would be finding on MRV in a patient with spontaneous intracranial
hypotension?

answers.C: Narrowing of the distal transverse sinuses
answers.D: Distension of the dominant transverse sinus

questions.printed_answer_heading: Distension of the dominant transverse sinus
questions.explanation:
Spontaneous intracranial hypotension or post spinal headache causes CSF depletion and
intracranial venous enlargement
The dominant transverse sinus will show the inferior margin of the midportion to have a
distended convex appearance
Cortical vein occlusion is very unlikely in such patients
Idiopathic intracranial hypertension can show narrowing of the distal transverse sinus

questions.question: What is the best response to a patient who has had an outburst?

answers.A: Ignore the patient's aberrant behavior and go on speaking
answers.B: Question the patient as to why he has made an outburst
answers.C: Give medication to sedate the patient

questions.printed_answer_heading: Question the patient as to why he has made an outburst
questions.explanation: The best response is to find out what caused the outburst from the patient

questions.question: Which of the following is the leading cause of death in the United States?
questions.explanation:
Complications of atherosclerosis such as stoke and myocardial infarction is the primary cause of
death in the US
The following are the next most common causes of death: Cancer, chronic lower respiratory
tract illnesses, accidents, diabetes, and Alzheimer

questions.question: In a patient with Bacteroides infection, the antibiotic of choice is:
questions.explanation:
Bacteroides bacteria are susceptible to metronidazole, carbapenems, chloramphenicol and other
beta lactam inhibitors
Clindamycin is very effective against anaerobes and also has good activity against some gram
positive bacteria
Quinolones did work against bacteroides but most species have now developed resistance to
these antibiotics
Cephalosporin esp. the first generation, are active against bacteroides

questions.question: Which is the most likely cause of fever within the first 24 hours postoperatively?
questions.explanation:
Postoperative atelectasis is an early cause of postoperative fever
It is usually due to poor lung expansion

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an advanced directive?
questions.explanation:
An advanced directive is a legal document that specifies what type of treatment a patient does
and does not want to receive
A living will is an example of an advanced directive
A DNR order is another example of an advanced directive

questions.question:
Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) can be treated with acetazolamide.
Select a possible alternative.
questions.explanation:
The efficacy of topiramate for treatment if IIH is comparable to acetazolamide
The mechanism of action could be decreased formation of CSF or weight loss
IIH is most common in obese females of childbearing years and 5 to 10% loss in weight can
markedly decreased intracranial pressure

questions.question:
A patient is seen in the emergency departement after head trauma. He suddenly
develops status epilepticus. The first step in his management is:
questions.explanation:
Common symptoms of head injury include coma, confusion, seizures, nausea and vomiting,
headache, and a lucid interval.
Treatment is based on size and signs of compression of the brain. Small ones are left alone.
Large hematomas are managed with intubation and hyperventilation, mannitol, and drainage.
Hyperventilation works by decreasing pCO2. Normally, cerebral circulation constricts when the
pCO2 is low. A small decrease in volume results in a large decrease in pressure.
Hyperventilation briefly slows herniation and is a bridge to surgery.

questions.question: The visual findings of uncal herniation do not involve compression of:
questions.explanation:
The uncus often compresses the 3rd cranial nerve and the parasympathetic input to the eye
The result is a dilated pupil that fails to constrict in response to light
The eye is down because of the pressure on the 4th nerve
The 6th cranial nerve which controls the lateral rectus is not affected by uncal herniation

questions.question:
A patient has benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Which of the following
interventions is employed to cure BPPV?

answers.D: Both the Semont and canalith reposition maneuvers

questions.printed_answer_heading: Both the Semont and canalith reposition maneuvers
questions.explanation:
Canalith reposition maneuver is also called Epley maneuver
The Brandt-Daroff exercises are done in conjunction as habituation exercises
The Epley maneuver is preferred as it is done at home by the patient instead of with a therapist

questions.question: What is not a common sign of cluster headache?
questions.explanation:
Cluster headaches are unilateral with autonomic symptoms
There is commonly meiosis not mydriasis

questions.question:
Cerebral edema that occurs after a stroke usually reaches maximal severity after
what time period?
questions.explanation:
Cerebral edema occurs in 10-15 percent of patients with ischemic strokes
The cerebral edema reaches a maximum intensity at about 96 hours
Thus, mannitol, hyperventilation and other modalities may need to be used for several days to
decrease edema

questions.question:
Select the best medication as the first-line drug in the initial treatment of status
epilepticus
questions.explanation:
Lorazepam has replaced diazepam as the drug of choice in the initial treatment of status
epilepticus. Lorazepam has a faster onset of action and is less irritating to the veins when given
IV than diazepam.
Phenytoin (or fosphenytoin) also plays a role in the acute treatment of status epilepticus. It is a
second-line drug and is given immediately after lorazepam. Although phenytoin is not as fast
acting as lorazepam, its duration is longer. Phenytoin provides continuing seizure suppression
after the effects of lorazepam have worn off.
Phenobarbital is considered a third-line drug in status epilepticus. It is commonly used when
seizures continue to occur after the administration of benzodiazepams and phenytoin.

questions.question:
A new adult patient is noted to be a Jehovah's Witness. Which is the most
appropriate response?

answers.A: Clearly document that he is a Jehovah's Witness in his medical record
answers.B: Encourage him to agree to accept blood
answers.C: Refuse to accept him as a patient
answers.D: Plan to administer blood only if an emergency situation arises

questions.printed_answer_heading: Clearly document that he is a Jehovah's Witness in his medical record
questions.explanation:
The finding that a patient is a Jehovah's Witness has major potential implications for his care, so
it must be clearly documented
There should be a frank discussion with Jehovah's Witness patients about their beliefs regarding
blood products and the various options that are available
Blood should not be administered in an emergency situation unless the patient agrees

questions.question: The lesser occipital nerve comes off which cervical spinal segment?
questions.explanation:
The greater occipital nerve comes off C2.
The lesser occipital nerve comes off C3..

questions.question:
A patient steps on a tack with her left foot. Which of the following would not
happen?
questions.explanation:
Pain elicits a withdrawal response
The hip and knee flexors on the ipsilateral side are activated
There is inhibition of the extensors and the ipsilateral side
The contralateral side exhibits extension

questions.question: When does wound dehiscence occur after surgery?
questions.explanation: Wound dehiscence occurs at seven days after surgery

questions.question:
A 2 year old is seen in the neurology clinic with protruding eyes and a distended
head. The mother claims that for the past 6 months, the child has been having bulging eyes and cries
all the time. CT scan reveals cerebellar tonsillar herniation. He most likely has:
questions.explanation: Arnold-Chiari malformation is associated with cerebellar tonsil herniation.

questions.question:
What is the most important and consistent predictor for cerebrovascular
accidents?
questions.explanation:
70% of strokes are in patients with hypertension
Hypertension increases atherosclerosis resulting in lipohyalinosis and arteriosclerosis and
stroke risk for both sexes and all ages
Treatment of all stages of hypertension from mild to severe decreases risk
Smokers have a relative risk of 1.5 to 1

questions.question: Which of the following is true of MEDLINE?

answers.A:
National Library of Medicine's premier bibliographic database covering the fields of medicine,
nursing, dentistry, veterinary medicine, the health care system, and the preclinical sciences
answers.B: Source of medical and dental supplies
