questions.explanation:
MEDLINE is the National Library of Medicine's premier bibliographic database covering the
fields of medicine, nursing, dentistry, veterinary medicine, the health care system, and the
preclinical sciences.

questions.question:
A patient has an acute compression fracture of T6 and is hospitalized after 2
days for pain control. The fracture is deemed stable and PT referral is made. Select the best initial
activity.

answers.A: Isometrics of the transverse abdominis while seated
answers.B: Knee to chest stretching while supine

questions.printed_answer_heading: Isometrics of the transverse abdominis while seated
questions.explanation:
Flexion activities may cause further compression and should be avoided
Maintaining neutral spine position is best
There will be increased pain with extreme extension so isometric exercises are best

questions.question:
In a patient with head trauma, which does not indicate rising intracranial
pressure (ICP)?
questions.explanation:
Rising ICP can present with many signs and symptoms including headache, nausea, vomiting,
ocular paralysis and loss of consciousness.
Cushing's triad includes elevated BP and decreased heart rate. In children, a slow heart rate is
an ominous sign of high ICP.
A swollen optic nerve is a good sign that the ICP is elevated.
Papilledema can lead to optic atrophy and visual problems. If not treated in time, it can lead to
permanent blindness.

questions.question:
Doctor discovers that the patient has profound weakness in shrugging the left
shoulder. What CN is involved?
questions.explanation:
CN XI controls the trapezius and sternocleidomastoid muscles affecting shoulder elevation and
turning the neck, respectively
CN XII controls tongue movement, CN VI controls lateral movement of the eye and CN II is the
optic nerve essential for sight

questions.question:
Of those cranial nerves traversing the cavernous sinus, which is most likely to
have an isolated palsy due to pathology OUTSIDE of the cavernous sinus?
questions.explanation:
The abducens nerve, CN VI, has the greatest likelihood of injury outside the cavernous sinus
because it has the longest course to reach the cavernous sinus
CN VI is also more tethered than other cranial nerves in the cavernous sinus
CN VI exists the caudal pons and turns superiorly and anteriorly at Dorello's canal at the
petroclival junction.
Therefore it is susceptible to brainstem mass effects and skull bases pathologies

questions.question: Which of the following nerves is involved with the ankle jerk reflex?
questions.explanation:
The genitofemoral nerve completes the arch for cremasteric reflex
The femoral nerve is responsible for the patellar reflex
The tibial nerve is responsible for plantar flexion of foot during the Achilles or plantar reflex

questions.question:
Which of the following extraocular muscles is innervated by a nucleus located
on the contralateral side?
questions.explanation:
General somatic efferent fibers of the oculomotor nerve arise from the oculomotor nucleus is
near the midline of the midbrain.
It is at the level of the superior colliculus. It gives rise to general somatic efferent fibers.
There is a subnucleus for each extraocular muscle. The subnucleus for the superior rectus muscle
is on the contralateral side.
Ipsilateral subnuclei innervate the inferior oblique, medial rectus, and inferior rectus muscles.
There is a medial subnucleus for the levator palpebral superioris muscle.

questions.question:
Which of the following should not be used to decrease increased intracranial
pressure (ICP)?

answers.C: Hyperventilation to achieve a pCO2< 30 mm Hg
answers.D: Intubation and hyperventilation to achieve a pCO2 of 30-35 mm Hg

questions.printed_answer_heading: Hyperventilation to achieve a pCO2< 30 mm Hg
questions.explanation:
Excessive hyperventilation can potentiate vasospasm and ischemia
Steroids such as dexamethasone are controversial, yet used

questions.question: Broca aphasia is also known as:
questions.explanation:
Broca's aphasia is also known as expressed aphasia
It is associated with upper motor neuron lesion of the right side

questions.question:
A 50 year old female alcoholic is transported by paramedics to the emergency
department with severe agitation. The initial diagnosis is delirium tremens treated with thiamine, IV
fluids and benzodiazepines. Serum sodium is found to be 112 mEq/L and is rapidly corrected with
3% saline. The patient develops quadriplegia, coma, and dies. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Central pontine myelinolysis is secondary to treatment of severe hyponatremia rapidly with
hypertonic saline
There is symmetric destruction of myelin sheaths at the basis pontis
There is no associated inflammation. It is more common in females and alcoholics
Prognosis is poor with those who survive requiring extensive rehabilitation

questions.question: The only identifiable risk factor for development of acoustic neuromas is?
questions.explanation:
The majority of patients with an acoustic neuroma have no known risk factors
Exposure to high doses of ionizing radiation is the only definitive environmental risk factor

questions.question: In a patient with decorticate posturing you are unlikely to see:
questions.explanation:
In decorticate posturing, you will see a mummified baby like response
The arms, elbow, wrists and fingers will be flexed and the legs extended
Decorticate posturing gets a score of 3 on the GCS
Decorticate posture indicates damage to the corticospinal tract

questions.question:
64 year old postoperative patient develops swelling and pain in left leg
consistent with deep venous thrombosis. Which of the following statements regarding duplex imaging
of the lower extremity is true?

answers.A: It lacks sensitivity below the thigh in asymptomatic patients.
answers.B: A negative venous duplex examination justifies no treatment
answers.C: Cannot differentiate between acute and chronic venous clots
answers.D: Presence of collaterals indicates presence of an acute venous thrombotic process

questions.printed_answer_heading: A negative venous duplex examination justifies no treatment
questions.explanation:
Duplex scanning (Doppler analysis and B-mode ultrasonography) is more than 95% sensitive
and specific in diagnosing DVT.
Negative duplex scan is sufficient to withhold anticoagulation.
Duplex scanning can differentiate between acute and chronic venous thromboses. Acute DVTs
are characterized by an enlarged non-compressible vein without collateral vessels whereas
chronic DVTs have normal-sized veins with significant collaterals.

questions.question: Nephrotoxic medications do not include:
questions.explanation: Acetaminophen is hepatotoxic

questions.question:
An asymptomatic patient with sodium of 112 after head trauma is best treated
with:
questions.explanation:
The treatment of hyponatremia depends on the cause. For those with no symptoms, water
restriction is adequate treatment
If there is volume depletion, intravenous normal saline may be effective
Aggressive correction of hyponatremia can lead to central pontine myelinolysis
Seizures associated with hyponatremia are usually treated with a bolus of 3% hypertonic saline

questions.question:
A 26 y/o sits at a desk all day working at a computer console. By late morning,
she experiences tightness in the shoulder muscles and mild throbbing along the posterior cervical
musculature. By the end of the day, she has a dull diffuse throbbing headache that feels like a tight
band around her head. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Tension-type headache is the most common type of cephalgia
Treatment includes massage, physiotherapy, heat packs to the tender muscles, rubbing an
appropriate ointment on symptomatic areas such and medications such as acetaminophen,
NSAIDs, and muscle relaxants

questions.question: Adding clavulanic acid to common antibiotics leads to:
questions.explanation:
Clavulanate is an inhibitor of beta lactamase enzyme produced by bacteria
With this medication the efficacy of the antibiotic is increased if the organism is resistant
Clavulanate has no effect on bioavailability or half-life
Clavulinate increases the likelihood of diarrhea

questions.question: What is the recommended starting dose of carbamazepine for adults?
questions.explanation:
Carbamazepine is metabolize by the liver
Initially the half life is from 25 to 65 hours but after autoinduction of metabolic enzymes this
drops to 10 to 20 hours
Starting dose is 200 mg BID

questions.question:
Which of the following factors have the greatest impact on the development of a
headache after a lumbar puncture?

answers.B: Duration of bed rest after a LP
answers.C: Amount of fluid intake after a LP
answers.D: Size of needle used for LP

questions.printed_answer_heading: Size of needle used for LP
questions.explanation:
The amount of CSF leakage is directly related to the size of the dural tear and the LP needle used
during the LP
The incidence of a headache is 70% when a 16 or 19 gauge needle is used, but only 12% when a
24 or 27 gauge needle is used
The other items listed have no correlation with the risk of developing a post-LP headache

questions.question:
A pharmaceutical representative offers a "drug dinner" or an opportunity to have
a gourmet meal with an accompanying lecture. Which of the following is the best option?

answers.C: Discuss the offer with legal counsel
answers.D: Report the pharmaceutical representative to the FDA

questions.explanation:
Pharmaceutical companies have been severely limited in their abilities to provide compensation
to caregivers
"Drug dinners" are still allowed but of somewhat questionable value educationally
The money would be better spent subsidizing traditional conferences
review_required: Question text and options repeated elsewhere in source PDF

questions.question: Signs and symptoms of a blood transfusion reaction

answers.C: Decreased blood pressure and increased heart rate
answers.D: Decreased urine output and increased heart rate

questions.printed_answer_heading: Decreased blood pressure and increased heart rate
questions.explanation:
Blood transfusion reactions can compromise both circulatory and respiratory systems
(increasing pulse, respiratory rate, temperature and hypotension) managed immediately by
stopping transfusions and administering IV fluids

questions.question: Astereognosis is due to a defect in the:
questions.explanation: Asterognosis is associated with a lesion in the parietal lobe or dorsal columns

questions.question:
Nerve conduction velocity in a myelinated fiber is regulated by which of the
following parameters?

answers.A: Dendrite length, internode length, axonal diameter
answers.B: Axonal length, myelin thickness, dendrite length
answers.C: Axonal diameter, myelin thickness, internode length
answers.D: Myelin length, internode length, axonal diameter

questions.printed_answer_heading: Axonal diameter, myelin thickness, internode length
questions.explanation:
The thickness of the myelin sheath increases the velocity
The larger the axon diameter the faster the velocity
The fewer the nodes on an axon the faster the velocity

questions.question: Which of the following would reverse the effects of a morphine overdose?
questions.explanation:
Naloxone is indicated in overdose with opioids, such as morphine or heroin, and can quickly
reverse respiratory depression
Atropine is indicated for toxicity to organophosphate insecticides
Activated charcoal is indicated for many oral poisons
Flumazenil is indicated for reversal of benzodiazepine overdose/poisoning

questions.question: The stellate ganglion is found at the level of:
questions.explanation:
The stellate ganglion is formed by the inferior cervical and thoracic ganglia
It is located at the level of seventh cervical vertebra

questions.question: Which of the following local anesthetics has the longest duration of action?
questions.explanation:
The following local anesthetics have the following durations of action: Procaine (Novocaine):
<30 minutes, Bupivacaine (Marcaine): 180 to 360 minutes, the longest-acting anesthetic; good
for nerve blocks, Mepivacaine (Carbocaine): 45 to 75 minutes, Lidocaine (Xylocaine): 60 to
180 minutes
The use of epinephrine should be avoided in areas such as the fingers, nose, penis, and toes or
other distal appendages. The vasoconstrictive effect can lead to ischemic necrosis
The most common reason for inadequate anesthesia is not allowing enough time for the
anesthetic to take effect
In most cases, the surgeon should wait at least 5 minutes after injection before starting a
procedure

questions.question:
Which of the following sympathetic ganglia has to be removed for treatment of
reflex sympathetic dystrophy?
questions.explanation: Both T4 and T5 have to be excised for relief of pain

questions.question:
A 30 year old female presents with a moderate to severe headache. Exam is
normal except for neck stiffness. CT of the brain shows blood in the interpeduncular cistern. CT
angiogram and four vessel angiogram are normal. Cervical spine MRI with and without gadolinium is
normal. What is the next step in management?

answers.B: Discharge to home with office follow up.

questions.printed_answer_heading: Discharge to home with office follow up.
questions.explanation:
The patient has had a non-aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.
The CT angiogram confirmed that there was not an aneurysm of the circle of Willis.
The MRI is done to exclude a cervical dural AV fistula.
As the bleeding was most likely venous, no further investigation or treatment is needed.

questions.question: Tuberous sclerosis is transmitted in which pattern?
questions.explanation:
Tuberous sclerosis is transmitted through autosomal dominant trait with variable penetrance
Spontaneous mutation rates may be observed in more than 50% of patients

questions.question:
Which of the following is the most common source of primary intraventricular
hemorrhage?

answers.A: Hemorrhagic transformation of adjacent ischemic infarct

questions.explanation:
The most common primary source of hemorrhage is rupture of the subependymal veins.
pIVH is rare in adults and common in neonates <32 weeks of GA.

questions.question:
A 6-year-old child developed double vision and projectile vomiting. What is the
most likely cause of his condition?
questions.explanation:
Increased ICP causes projectile vomiting and double vision
Brain tumors should be considered in such cases
The most common site of brain tumors in children is infratentorial

questions.question: Which of the following confirmatory tests is a reliable indicator of brain death?
questions.explanation:
A clinical exam plus a confirmatory test is generally needed to confirm brain death.
Four vessel cerebral angiography or radionuclide scanning are confirmatory exams of brain
death
EEG can be used as a supportive test but there can be no evidence of any analgesic or sedative
drugs.
Other tests to assess brain death include brain stem evoked potentials and transcranial doppler

questions.question: A patient with neurogenic shock is least likely to present with?
questions.explanation:
Neurogenic shock is associated with spinal injury.
It is consistent with signs of hypovolemia.

questions.question:
Pulsatile exophthalmos is found in patients with which of the following
disorders?
questions.explanation:
Pulsatile exophthalmos is due to sphenoid wing hypoplasia and resultant temporal lobe
herniation into the orbit.
Sphenoid wing hypoplasia is a common manifestation of neurofibromatosis type 1.

questions.question: What is the agent of choice to reverse heparin?
questions.explanation: Protamine reverses the action of heparin

questions.question:
A 68 year old male with history of hypertension presents with drooping of the
left eye, left facial numbness, ataxic gait and right arm numbness; his diagnosis is:
questions.explanation:
Wallenberg's syndrome (lateral medullary syndrome) is an infarct of the vertebrobasilar or
posterior inferior cerebellar arteries and presents with ipsilateral loss of pain and temperature
on the face, contralateral loss of these sensations on the body, ataxia, and often an ipsilateral
Horner's syndrome

questions.question: What sign is not associated with pulmonary embolism?
questions.explanation:
PE is associated with tachycardia, tachypnea, oxygen desaturation, and pleuritic chest pain
Plain chest radiographs are generally normal although occasionally Hampton hump (a shallow
wedge-shaped opacity) is seen
The diagnostic test of choice is a spiral CT of the chest
Pulmonary angiography is the gold standard and rarely nuclear medicine ventilation perfusion
scans are done

questions.question: What is the most effective treatment for essential tremor?
questions.explanation:
Thalamotomy and deep brain are equally efficacious for essential tremor but the complications
of thalamotomy include dysarthria, ataxia, or gait disturbance in 42%
Most adverse effects of DBS are eliminated by adjustment of settings
Medications used include ethanol, beta blockers, topiramate, anticonvulsants, neuroleptics, and
antidepressants

questions.question:
All the following statements about cavernous sinus thrombosis are correct
EXCEPT:

answers.A: Can occur from infections of nose, teeth, ear, and sinus
answers.D: The 3rd cranial nerve is most commonly involved

questions.printed_answer_heading: The 3rd cranial nerve is most commonly involved
questions.explanation:
Other causes are carotid-cavernous fistula, cavernous sinus aneurysm and tumors both primary
and metastatic
Additional symptoms include exophthalmos, headaches, fever, paralysis of cranial nerves III to
VI, retinal hemorrhages, blindness, ptosis, and sensory loss of ophthalmic and maxillary
branches

questions.question:
A 28 year old female that weighs 130 kg presents with a headache and blurred
vision of 10 days duration. The patient has no focal neurologic signs, vomiting, or diplopia. The
funduscopic exam shows marked papilledema but no hemorrhages. MRI shows no mass lesion,
normal ventricles, and enlarged optic nerve sheaths. Lumbar puncture is done. Which of the following
is most likely to be observed?

answers.A:
Opening pressure 200 mm H2O, glucose 70 mg/dL, protein 250 mg/dL, 50 WBC/µL, 200
RBC/µL, IgG 8 mg/dL, appearance yellow
answers.B:
Opening pressure 50 mm H2O, glucose 70 mg/dL, protein 50 mg/dL, 0 WBC/µL, 0 RBC/µL,
IgG 18 mg/dL, appearance clear
answers.C:
Opening pressure 20 mm H2O, glucose 140 mg/dL, protein 200 mg/dL, 0 WBC/µL, 50
RBC/µL, IgG 5 mg/dL, appearance yellow
answers.D:
Opening pressure 200 mm H2O, glucose 70 mg/dL, protein 50 mg/dL, 0 WBC/µL, 0
RBC/µL, IgG 5 mg/dL, appearance clear

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Opening pressure 200 mm H2O, glucose 70 mg/dL, protein 50 mg/dL, 0 WBC/µL,
0 RBC/µL, IgG 5 mg/dL, appearance clear
questions.explanation:
The patient has idiopathic intracranial hypertension or pseudotumor cerebri
It is most common in obese females of childbearing years
MRI can show normal or slit like ventricles
There is usually elevated opening pressure but no risk of herniation

questions.question: Which is the least common organism to cause viral meningitis?
questions.explanation: Viral meningitis is mainly caused by enterovirus, arbovirus, and herpes simplex virus

questions.question: Select the correct statement about the external segment of the globus pallidus.

answers.A: It is only involved in the basal ganglia direct pathway
answers.B: It is only involved in the basal ganglia indirect pathway
answers.C: It is involved in both the direct and indirect pathways of the basal ganglia
answers.D: It is not involved with either the direct or the indirect pathways of the basal ganglia

questions.printed_answer_heading: It is only involved in the basal ganglia indirect pathway
questions.explanation:
The indirect pathway uses GABA and enkephalin projections to the external segment of the
globus pallidus, which in turn sends GABAergic projections to the sub-thalamus
The subthalamic nucleus has projections to the internal part of the globus pallidus with glutamate
as the neurotransmitter
It is theorized that the direct and indirect pathways of the basal ganglia form equilibrium with the
indirect pathway increasing output from the substantia nigra internal segment of the globus
pallidus

questions.question:
Select the term meaning the nondisclosure of information except to those
authorized to access it:
questions.explanation:
Confidentiality is an ethical priciple and legal right that dictates those with information protect
the information and limit disclose to authorized persons.
Constraint is the restriction of a person or entity.
Coercion involves forcing or intimidating another to act in manner that is involuntary to their
wil.
Conversion involves a change in beliefs or form.

questions.question:
A patient undergoes a lumbar puncture and 10 cc of fluid is removed. How long
will the brain take to replenish the lost fluid?
questions.explanation:
Normal CSF production is about 0.3 ml/min and most of the fluid is produced by the choroid
plexus. The total amount of fluid in the brain is 120 cc
Most of the fluid removed during a lumbar puncture is easily replaced within one hour
The normal route of clearance of CSF is to the lateral ventricles, then to the interventricular
foramen of Monroe, to the cerebral aqueduct of sylvius and then to the subarachnoid space, dural
sinus and into venous drainage

questions.question:
How long should initial assessments take at the scene of a mass casualty
incident?
questions.explanation:
Initial assessments at the scene of a mass casualty incident should take <60 sec
Systems used at mass casualty incidents are designed to be carried out very quickly
2 to 4 minutes is too long to take to triage at a mass casualty incident

questions.question: What is the most common location of brainstem astrocytoma in children?
questions.explanation:
Astrocytoma is the most common brainstem tumor in children
Most commonly found in the pons

questions.question: Select the brainstem's principle visceral nucleus.
questions.explanation:
The nucleus solitarius is the brainstem's principle visceral nucleus
It receives afferent visceral information from the GI tract, lungs, and heart
It also receives taste information

questions.question: What is the mechanism for syncope in hyperventilating patients?
questions.explanation:
Cerebral blood flow is regulated by arterial CO2 level
Cerebral vasoconstriction occurs when arterial CO2 decreases
Arterial O2 level does not normally regulate cerebral blood flow
Hyperventilation is often used as a therapy to reduce elevated intracranial pressure.

questions.question: Where would you attempt a second IV start if the first is unsuccessful?

answers.B: To the left or right of the first

questions.explanation:
A second attempt should be made superior to the first site
Technically, there is a chance of blood leakage from the first attempt site
Never make a second attempt in the same place as the first attempt

questions.question: Which of the following would be least likely to cause deep venous thrombosis?
questions.explanation:
Any condition that results in prolonged immobility can result in DVT
Complex regional pain syndrome causes pain, not immobility, or DVT

questions.question: Status epilepticus is treated with?
questions.explanation:
Lorazepam has a longer duration of action
Lorazepam is the drug of choice for status epilepticus

questions.question: What is an acceptable statistic significant p value?
questions.explanation: An acceptable p value is five percent

questions.question: What is the innervation of quadriceps muscles?
questions.explanation:
L5 nerve root innervates dorsiflexion of foot
Quadriceps weaknesses is indicative of L4 nerve root
S1 controls plantar flexion of foot

questions.question: What factor has the greatest affect on MRI artifacts?
questions.explanation:
As magnet strength increases susceptibility artifacts increase as well.
A 3T MRI has the potential for greater artifacts than a 1.5T MRI.

questions.question: Select the best description of vertigo.

answers.C: A sensation of loss of balance

questions.explanation:
Vertigo is a spinning sensation, in which the environment seems to spin around the patient, or the
patient has the sensation of spinning.
Dizziness is very subjective and may mean many different things.
It is important to better characterize the complaint of dizziness in order to develop a better
differential diagnosis and treatment plan.

questions.question: In which situation is an urgent brain CT scan not indicated?

answers.A: Acute closed head injury with right homonymous hemianopsia
answers.C: Acute closed head injury with nausea, vomiting, and lethargy
answers.D:
A supraorbital, throbbing headache of acute onset, which is exacerbated by light and attempts at
visual accommodation

questions.printed_answer_heading:
A supraorbital, throbbing headache of acute onset, which is exacerbated by light and
attempts at visual accommodation
questions.explanation:
A throbbing, supraorbital headache that is worsened by exposure to light in either eye or
attempts at visual accommodation is most suggestive of ocular pathology; it therefore does not
require an urgent brain CT scan
An intracranial hematoma should be suspected in any closed head injury, unless the trauma was
minor
Risk factors for an intracranial hematoma include advanced age, young age (children), and
anticoagulation
The absence of localizing factors does not rule out an intracerebral hematoma; an urgent brain
CT is generally indicated for all closed head injuries except for minor trauma in non-intoxicated
patients

questions.question:
Ask the patient to open is fingers wide apart and check for abduction and
adduction against resistance. In this test, you are normally checking for what nerve function?
questions.explanation:
Branches of the ulnar nerve divide into deep and superficial in the forearm
The superficial ulnar nerve supplies cutaneous fibers to the anterior surface of the medial hand
and one-half of digits
The deep branch supplies motor fibers to hypothenar muscle, medial two lumbricals, adductor
pollicis muscle and all interosseous muscles
Adduction and abduction of finger, adduction of thumb and flexion and adduction at wrist are
controlled by the median nerve

questions.question: Which patient is least likely to have a specific cortical brain lesion?

answers.A: A patient who is unable to identify a key placed in his hand
answers.B: A patient with sudden unilateral loss of vision
answers.C: A patient with sudden onset of hemiplegia
answers.D: A patient who reports that a llama walks by her a few times per week

questions.printed_answer_heading: A patient with sudden unilateral loss of vision
questions.explanation:
Unilateral vision loss is most likely due to a lesion distal to the optic chiasm
Agnosia (the failure to recognize tactile, auditory, or visual input) occurs with some parietal
lobe lesions
Visual hallucinations are often caused by major cerebral pathology, such as alcohol withdrawal

questions.question:
Which of the following imaging studies is the best method to evaluate basilar
artery infarcts?
questions.explanation:
Diffusion weighted imaging shows hyperintensity of the pontomesencephalic region
Absence of flow void within the basilar artery would be evident

questions.question: Which of the following compounds has inhibitory property?
questions.explanation:
The inhibitory compounds include glycine, taurine, and GABA
Excitatory compounds include hemocysteic acid, glutamic acid, and aspartic acid

questions.question:
A 78-year-old female has had a 2-year history of urinary incontinence and
progressive problems with ambulation. Her provider felt she had stress urinary incontinence after
urine studies were normal. For the past 4 months she has become withdrawn, confused, and forgetful.
On exam, she is unable to recall 3 items and her gait shows short steps and is wide based. When she
turns she almost falls over. What is CT of the brain likely to show?

answers.C: Enlargement of the frontal and temporal horns of the lateral ventricles
answers.D: Atrophy of the frontal and temporal lobes

questions.printed_answer_heading: Enlargement of the frontal and temporal horns of the lateral ventricles
questions.explanation:
The patient has signs and symptoms of normal pressure hydrocephalus
The etiology of the condition is unknown but may be secondary to subarachnoid hemorrhage,
infection, or prior trauma
The apraxic gait is not secondary to weakness but patients often have problems lifting their feet
from the floor
Lumbar puncture can be diagnostic and treatment is with shunting

questions.question:
A 5 year old is evaluated with CT of the brain after a fall. Oval defects are
noted in the parietal bones. Which of the following statements is true?

answers.A: The patient has parietal foramina and these are not of concern
answers.B: There is a fibrous membrane that remains throughout life
answers.C: These oval defects are only seen as an autosomal dominant trait
answers.D: This most likely represents eosinophilic granuloma

questions.printed_answer_heading: The patient has parietal foramina and these are not of concern
questions.explanation:
Parietal foramina (PFM) reflect deficient or delayed ossification around the parietal notch
PFM has a fibrous membrane that tends to ossify with age
PFM can be seen as in a syndrome such as Saethre-Chotzen with proximal deletion of 11p or as
an isolated finding inherited as an autosomal dominant trait

questions.question: Periorbital ecchymosis is suggestive of:
questions.explanation:
Periorbital ecchymosis is suggestive of basilar skull fracture
It is also called raccoon eyes
It can also seen post-craniotomy and with cancers such as neuroblastoma and multiple myeloma
Blindness, tooth fractures and migraines have no association with periorbital ecchymosis

questions.question: What is the leading cause of pain in the elderly population?
questions.explanation:
Musculoskeletal pathology is the leading cause of pain in the elderly population
Cancer pain is the second most common cause

questions.question:
A patient presents with an intense headache, nausea and persistent vomiting that
has been ongoing for 2 months. Examination reveals that he has difficulty with upward gaze and is
unable to converge his pupils. The blood work is not very remarkable. The patient most likely has:
questions.explanation:
Pinealoma are located near vital neural and vascular structures. The position accounts for most
of its symptoms
When a tumor of the pineal gland occurs, it may present with Parinaud syndrome, which is palsy
of upward gaze, failure of convergence and dissociation of light and accommodation
MRI is the preferred radiological modality of choice
Other symptoms may include hydrocephalus, precocious puberty and gait problems

questions.question:
A patient is diagnosed with a right middle cerebral artery thrombosis. Which of
the following would not be affected?
questions.explanation:
The posterior cerebral artery supplies the visual receptive area
The middle cerebral artery supplies the lateral brain
The precentral gyrus is involved with motor function, the postcentral gyrus is involved with
sensation, and the transverse temporal gyrus processes auditory information

questions.question: Which nerve when paralyzed lead to diplopia in multiple directions?
questions.explanation:
Paralysis of the 3rd nerve often results in diplopia in multiple directions
Another clue to 3rd nerve involvement is that pupil is involved

questions.question: Which of the following is an incorrect nerve - muscle relationship?

answers.D: C8 - Finger extensors to middle finger

questions.printed_answer_heading: C8 - Finger extensors to middle finger
questions.explanation:
C8 provides finger flexors to middle finger,
T1 supplies small finger abductors,
L2 supplies hip flexors while L3-4 supplies knee extensors.
L4-L5 supplies ankle and big toe dorsiflexors and S1 supplies ankle plantar flexors and knee
flexion.

questions.question: Spinal epidural abscess are commonly caused by?
questions.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is the most common cause of spinal epidural abscess

questions.question:
A young child is seen in the clinic with hypertension. He also is found to have
large hemangiomas on his face, eyes and his trunk. Work up reveals that he has a pheochromocytoma.
He most likely has which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Von Hippel Landau shows autosomal dominant inheritance.
It is characterized by hemangioblastomas of the brain and spinal cord, retinal angiomas,
angiomas and cysts of the liver and kidney, and renal cell carcinoma.
It is associated with pheochromocytomas.

questions.question:
In the setting of acute ischemic stroke, a persistent systolic blood pressure at
what level may need treatment?
questions.explanation:
Generally, elevated blood pressure is not treated within 48 to 72 hours after an acute ischemic
stroke unless the systolic pressure is consistently above 220 mmHg or the diastolic pressure is
consistently above 120 mmHg.

questions.question: Cauda equina syndrome is:

answers.B: Inflammation of the spinal nerve roots
answers.C: Develops with end stage rheumatoid arthritis
answers.D: Develops following a compression of the heart

questions.printed_answer_heading: Inflammation of the spinal nerve roots
questions.explanation:
Inflammation causes low back pain or disturbances of feeling in the buttocks
Patients may also develop altered bowel and bladder functioning

questions.question: Which of the following medications has the least anti-inflammatory properties?
questions.explanation: Acetaminophen has very limited anti-inflammatory effect

questions.question:
All the following statements about the respiratory center in the brainstem are
correct EXCEPT:

answers.A: Medullary rhythmicity area includes the inspiratory and expiratory centers
answers.B: Pneumotaxic center controls both rate and pattern of breathing
answers.C: Apneustic center controls depth of inspiration
answers.D: Herring-Breuer reflex prevents elevated carbon dioxide levels

questions.printed_answer_heading: Herring-Breuer reflex prevents elevated carbon dioxide levels
questions.explanation:
Herring-Breuer reflex prevents lungs from overinflating by sending inhibitory impulses to the
inspiration center. Chemoreceptors in aortic arch and carotid artery send back information on
carbon dioxide and oxygen levels to respiratory center which may alter the breathing pattern
Inspiration center in dorsal part of medulla causes inspiration when stimulated. Expiration
center in ventral part of medulla generally causes expiration and sends inhibitory impulses to
apneustic center
Pneumotaxic center in upper pons controls both rate and pattern of breathing and limits
inspiration. Cortical input can override automatic control.
Apneustic center in lower pons controls depth of inspiration and activates inspiration unless
cancelled out by pneumotaxic center when breathing rate increases

questions.question:
An agitated patient after craniotomy who is pulling out his IV lines should have
what intervention?

answers.A: Tie wrist restraints to the bed rails
answers.B: Apply mitts to the patient's hands
answers.C: Use a draw sheet to confine the patient's arms
answers.D: Tie down the arm with the IV

questions.printed_answer_heading: Apply mitts to the patient's hands
questions.explanation: The intervention least likely to increase the patient's anxiety would be to apply mitts.

questions.question:
Which of the following is true regarding a medical provider passing a motor
vehicle accident (MVA)?

answers.A: No moral obligation to render assistance
answers.B: Legal obligation to assist and malpractice can result if duty neglected

questions.explanation:
No legal obligation to assist exists as there is no patient-physician relationship
There is a moral obligation to assist
Malpractice does not pertain to this situation as there is no patient-physician relationship
There is no duty to care in the above scenario

questions.question:
In a 33-year-old HIV male with a CD4 count of 340, one would expect to find
what type of brain mass?
questions.explanation:
Lymphomas are commonly seen in HIV individuals and other people who are on chronic
immunosuppressive therapy

questions.question:
An AIDS patient has presented with a seizure and has a ring-enhancing lesion
with edema but no mass effect on CT scan. He has been on treatment for toxoplasmosis for 3 weeks
and follow up CT is unchanged. CSF was negative at the time of the lumbar puncture and all cultures
for viruses, bacteria, and fungus were negative. The patient has had no further seizures. Which of the
following choices is appropriate?
questions.explanation:
Without response to treatment or definitive diagnosis biopsy is indicated
If EBV DNA had been found, CNS lymphoma would be most likely
Treatment for lymphoma or toxoplasmosis is unreasonable without diagnosis
Dexamethasone would only be used if there were mass effect

questions.question:
Which of the following is incorrect about the derivatives of the ectodermal germ
layer?

answers.A: Ectoderm overlying the notochord forms the neural plate
answers.B: The ectoderm is a tube-like process at the beginning of the 3rd week
answers.C: Both anterior and posterior neuropores close by the 27th day
answers.D: The rudimentary spinal chord and brain vesicles have formed by the 28th day

questions.printed_answer_heading: The ectoderm is a tube-like process at the beginning of the 3rd week
questions.explanation:
The neural folds elevate by the end of the third week
A tube-like structure is starts forming on day 20 but complete neurulation does not happen until
day 28

questions.question:
There are several cranial nerves traversing the cavernous sinus. Which is most
medially positioned?
questions.explanation:
The abducens nerve, CN VI, travels in the cavernous sinus proper, medial to the ICA
CN II does not travel in the cavernous sinus
CNs III, IV, V1, and V2 travel in the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus

questions.question: Which artery supplies the head of the caudate nucleus?
questions.explanation:
The lenticulostriate arteries are part of the anterolateral group of the circle of Willis and supply
the head of caudate nucleus.
They also supply the claustrum, external capsule, putamen, and globus pallidus.

questions.question: Benzodiazepine overdose can be reversed by:
questions.explanation:
Flumazenil is an antidote for benzodiazepine overdose
Flumazenil competitively inhibits the activity at the benzodiazepine recognition site on the
GABA/benzodiazepine receptor complex
Naloxone and naltrexone are opioid receptor antagonists
Deferoxamine is given in iron overdose

questions.question:
Where in the brainstem would the lesion be found for a patient with loss of
vibratory and position sense, contralateral hemiplegia, and ipsilateral tongue deviation?
questions.explanation:
Medial medullary syndrome is characterized by loss of vibratory and position sense,
contralateral hemiplegia, and ipsilateral tongue deviation
It is caused by anterior spinal artery occlusion or the vertebral artery that gives rise to it
There is damage to the hypoglossal nerve, corticospinal tract, and the medial meniscus
The hemiplegia spares the face

questions.question:
A newborn is noted to have a meningomyelocele. Which finding would be of
most concern?
questions.explanation:
Nystagmus would raise concern about brainstem dysfunction
Vigorous symmetrical Moro reflex, flat anterior fontanelle, and a strong urinary stream are
reassuring findings

questions.question:
Rupture of the middle meningeal artery in the cranial cavity causes which type of
hemorrhage?
questions.explanation:
An epidural hematoma is secondary to traumatic brain injury with rupture of the middle
meningeal artery.
The blood collects between the dura mater and the skull.
This can be fatal in about 10 to 15% of patients due to increased intracranial pressure.
Patients may initially be lucid and have rapid deterioration later.

questions.question: Battle sign is indicative of a:
questions.explanation:
Battle sign is indicative of a basilar skull fracture
It is also called mastoid ecchymosis
It presents as a palpable bogginess and bruising behind the ear
Migraines may occur with or without aura

questions.question: Spinal cord ischemia can be minimized by?
questions.explanation: Hypothermia protects the spinal cord during an ischemic episode

questions.question: Which of the following medications will prolong the bleeding time?
questions.explanation:
Bleeding time is a function of platelet number and function
From the above choices, only aspirin can compromise the function of platelets
Inhibition of thromboxane-2 by aspirin prevents effective aggregation

questions.question: All of the following statements about the corpus callosum are correct EXCEPT:

answers.A: The corpus callosum is the second largest white matter structure next to the internal capsule
answers.B: The corpus callosum connects the two hemispheres
answers.C: The corpus callosum anatomy from anterior to posterior includes the genu, splenium and rostrum
answers.D: The genu connects both prefrontal cortices

questions.printed_answer_heading:
The corpus callosum is the second largest white matter structure next to the internal
capsule
questions.explanation:
The CC is the largest white matter structure
The splenium connects premotor and motor areas while the rostrum connects somatosensory
information to include visual activity of the occipital lobes
Disruption of the CC causes decreased spontaneity of speech, decreased use of non-dominant
hand and slight difficulty connecting words and images
Frequently, these problems become less prevalent over time

questions.question: Why are patients with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome at increased risk for headaches?
questions.explanation:
Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type IV is secondary to mutations of type II procollagen and leads to
vascular lesions
There is abnormal elastic tissue in vessels that can cause arterial dissection and cerebral
aneurysms
Subarachnoid hemorrhage secondary to aneurysms can present as sudden onset of a severe
headache
There is no increased reactivity of cerebral vasculature or risk of thrombosis

questions.question: Select the correct statement about glycine.

answers.A: Glycine is only involved with the basal ganglia direct pathway
answers.B: Glycine is only involved with the basal ganglia indirect pathway
answers.C: Glycine is involved with both the direct and indirect pathways of the basal ganglia
answers.D: Glycine is not involved with either the direct or the indirect pathways of the basal ganglia

questions.printed_answer_heading: Glycine is involved with both the direct and indirect pathways of the basal ganglia
questions.explanation:
The direct and indirect pathways from the putamen to the globus pallidus use different
neurotransmitters
The putamen has spiny neurons that use substance P and GABA in the direct pathway to the
substantia nigra pars reticulate and the internal segment of the globus pallidus
The putamen has spiny neurons that use enkephalin and GABA in the indirect pathway to the
external segment of the globus pallidus
Glycine is not involved with either the direct or the indirect pathways of the basal ganglia

questions.question: In patients with diabetes insipidus, what parameter is of least concern?
questions.explanation:
Patients with diabetes insipidus must have urine output monitored closely
Patients with DI should have blood pressure and electrolytes monitored
Food intake is of secondary importance

questions.question:
What is the best radiologic modality in the evaluation of annular tears of spinal
disc?
questions.explanation: An MRI is the best radiologic evaluation of annular tears of spinal disc

questions.question:
A male with HIV presents with confusion and general malaise. Blood work
reveals that he is anemic and a CT scan shows that he has generalized brain atrophy. The most
common type of HIV disorder of the brain is?
questions.explanation:
HIV dementia, HIV encephalopathy, and AIDS dementia complex refer to the same condition.
It is a metabolic encephalopathy caused by HIV infection with immune activation of microglia
and brain macrophages.
These cells secrete neurotoxins of both viral and host origin.
Patients can have disabling cognitive impairment, motor dysfunction, behavioral changes, and
speech problems.

questions.question:
A patient is seen in the ER for a concussion. The only complaint is a mild
headache. Neurological exam is normal. As he is being discharged, what is the most important
recommendation given?

answers.B: Keep him awake for at least 12 hours
answers.C: Periodically check him for any physical or symptom changes from baseline
answers.D: Plan to bring him back to the ER in the morning irrespective of status

questions.printed_answer_heading: Periodically check him for any physical or symptom changes from baseline
questions.explanation:
If his headaches become worse with nausea or he is now not very oriented or he cannot answer
simple questions or his balance is now very unstable return to the ER is recommended
The patient should also be on cognitive rest, meaning that a few days off school or work is
warranted

questions.question:
Which of the following is not typically associated with von Hippel-Lindau
disease?
questions.explanation:
Renal artery stenosis is not seen in patients with von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease. It can be
seen in other phakomatoses including neurofibromatosis.
VHL disease is an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by multiple CNS
hemangioblastomas, renal, pancreatic, and hepatic cysts, adenomas, renal cell carcinoma, and
islet cell tumors.
The cerebellum is the most common site of the hemangioblastomas associated with VHL.

questions.question:
All of the following statements about arteriovenous malformation hemorrhages
are correct EXCEPT:

answers.B: The initial presentation of ½ of AVMs is a hemorrhage
answers.C: Longitudinal studies show a 4% per year rate of bleeding from asymptomatic AVMs
answers.D: Seizures only develop after an AVM bleeds

questions.printed_answer_heading: Seizures only develop after an AVM bleeds
questions.explanation:
Seizures and headaches can occur from an AVM that has not bled depending on size, location,
and degree of ischemia from shunted blood
Symptoms from an AVM hemorrhage depend on the size and location of hematoma and may
include hemiparesis, dysphasia, hemisensory abnormalities, visual deficits, cognitive
dysfunction, memory loss, incoordination, and ataxia
Hydrocephalus may develop after a hemorrhage

questions.question: Which is the maximum possible score for Glasgow Coma Scale?
questions.explanation:
The maximum score of GCS is 15
Four for eye movement
Five for verbal response
Six for motor moment

questions.question: What kind of documentation is POMR?
questions.explanation: A problem oriented medical record is commonly used for documentation

questions.question:
What is the most likely diagnosis of a 65-year-old male with dementia and
visual hallucinations?
questions.explanation:
Visual hallucinations with dementia is highly suggestive of Lewy body dementia
Other signs include delusions and misidentification
10 to 20% of dementia is caused by Lewy bodies but this is on autopsy studies

questions.question:
Two days after undergoing bowel surgery, the patient presents with confusion,
disorientation and paranoia. He is extremely agitated and starts to pull out all his intravenous lines
and catheter. Examination reveals normal vital signs but mental status evaluation is not possible.
Blood work is within normal limits. The most likely cause of his behavior is:
questions.explanation:
Delirium is an acute confusional state characterized by severe changes in behavior and
cognition.
Patients with delirium may present with visual hallucination, delusions and frank psychosis.
Most patients who develop delirium are alcoholic and those who use illicit drugs.
Delirium has many causes and in the elderly, a simple urinary tract infection can trigger it. The
disorder commonly occurs in ICU patients.
Delirium sometime needs pharmacological therapy. Anti psychotics and benzodiazepines may
help most individuals.

questions.question: Which is not a currently accepted management of pressure ulcers?
questions.explanation:
Pressure ulcers usually develop on bony prominences
The goal is to reduce the pressure on pressure points
Egg crate, air mattress, and frequently turning are the best initial methods

questions.question:
The transverse humeral ligament holds which of the following structures in
place?

answers.A: The tendon of the pectoralis muscles

questions.explanation:
The transverse humeral ligament is responsible for holding the biceps tendon in place at the
bicipital groove
If this ligament is ruptured, the biceps tendon can slip out the groove causing irritation

questions.question: What is the normal level of calcium in the body?
questions.explanation:
Normal levels of calcium vary between 9 and 11 mg/dl
Mild hypocalcemia occurs when levels are between 7-9 mg/dl
Hypercalcemia is defined as any calcium level of more than 11 mg/dl
If the serum calcium level is below 7 mg/dl seizures or tetany may occur

questions.question: All of the following are true of a multispecialty group practice, except:

answers.A: Current trends show increasing numbers of groups
answers.C: They are the most common type of group practice
answers.D: They offer added convenience for their patients

questions.printed_answer_heading: They are the most common type of group practice
questions.explanation:
The total number of multispecialty group practices is on the rise
They are not the most common type of group practice
They afford physicians enhanced communication and collaboration
They afford patients "one stop shopping" and added convenience when scheduling appointments,
referrals and lab testing

questions.question:
An infant is diagnosed with hydrocephalus with generalized intracranial
calcifications and chorioretinitis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Signs in the classical triad suggestive of congenital toxoplasmosis include hydrocephalus,
intracranial calcifications and chorioretinitis
Primary infection during pregnancy is considered a very high risk for fetal infection
Pregnant mothers with previous infection do not transmit the disease to their unborn babies
Pregnant mothers should not eat raw meat and they should limit their contacts with cats and
avoid changing cat litter if at all possible

questions.question:
Nosocomial pneumonia in patient on mechanical ventilation is most likely
caused by:
questions.explanation:
Gram negative rods are the most common cause of nosocomial pneumonia in patient on
mechanical ventilation

questions.question:
A patient has a stage 2 decubitus ulcer over the sacrum measuring 1.5 cm. There
is no discharge, odor, or surrounding erythema. Select the most important treatment to promote
healing.
questions.explanation:
Decubitus ulcers are caused by pressure leading to ischemia
Frequent turning of immobilized patients is needed for prevention
Once an ulcer has formed, avoidance of pressure over the area is needed for healing
The area should be kept clean and moist, so hydrocolloid dressings can be helpful

questions.question:
An old man has progressively declined over the last 5 years. Lately, he becomes
lost on the way home, he cannot remember how to pay bills, and he becomes confused at night. He
forgets names. His vision, hearing, strength and gait are intact. Likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Alzheimer disease is the most common form of dementia
Early warning signs are memory loss that disrupts life, difficulty with problem solving and
completing tasks, confusion with place and time, trouble understanding visual images and spatial
relationships, new problems with speaking or writing, misplacing things and losing ability to
retrace steps, poor judgment, withdrawal from social activities, and changes in personality.
It can double warfarin levels and triple theophylline levels
It also raises the concentration of diltiazem, propranolol, methadone, carbamazepine, and
clozapine

questions.question: Which spinal nerve injury innervates the brachioradialis?
questions.explanation:
Shoulder pain is related to C5 spinal nerve injury
C5 controls muscle innervation to the biceps and brachioradialis
C6 injury relates to numbness of lateral forearm and hand
C7 controls medial two fingers

questions.question: Which of the following statements is not true?

answers.A: The normal range of CSF pressure is 100 to 200 mm H20
answers.B: Arnold-Chiari type II malformations are associated with myelomeningocele
answers.C:
A type III Arnold-Chiari malformation consists of a high cervical myelomeningocele with
herniation of cerebellum
answers.D: Arnold Chiari type 1 malformations are associated with hydrocephalus

questions.printed_answer_heading: Arnold Chiari type 1 malformations are associated with hydrocephalus
questions.explanation:
Arnold-Chiari type I malformation can be characterized by recurrent headaches, primarily over
the frontal and occipital regions but often is asymptomatic
Neck pain, difficulty swallowing, and ataxia are other common features
A type III Arnold Chiari malformation consists of a high cervical myelomeningocele with
herniation of cerebellum and is not usually compatible with life
Arnold-Chiari type II malformations are similar to type I, but are associated with
myelomeningocele

questions.question: Which is not typically seen with acromegaly?

answers.C: Thickening of bones of jaw and digits
answers.D: Insulin resistance or Type 2 diabetes mellitus

questions.explanation:
Onset is usually in adulthood
Organomegaly of liver, spleen, and heart, as well as thyroid problems may be seen

questions.question:
Which of the following conditions is known to cause raised intracranial
pressure?
questions.explanation:
Lead poisoning can lead to raised intracranial pressure
Vitamin A toxicity, not deficiency is also another common cause of raised intracranial pressure
Penicillin allergy and Addison disease are not associated with raised intracranial pressure

questions.question: The makeup of abscess or pus consists of:

answers.A: Dead neutrophils and protein rich fluid

questions.printed_answer_heading: Dead neutrophils and protein rich fluid
questions.explanation:
Pus is the yellowish liquid at the center of the abscess
The pus content is protein rich fluid with dead neutrophils
Pus or abscess is common after staphylococcus infections
Pus can appear green when the infection is caused by pseudomonas

questions.question: A blister larger than 0.5 cm in diameter is a:
questions.explanation: By definition, a bulla.

questions.question: Hyperventilation causes the PCO2 to do which of the following?

answers.D: The change depends on the oxygen saturation

questions.explanation: Hyperventilation results in low carbon dioxide

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the "resource-based relative value"
used by Medicare is correct?

answers.A: It is based on previous payments for care
answers.B: There is no evidence that it helps control healthcare costs
answers.C: National standard fees are used in the calculation
answers.D: It is a simple calculation that uses amount of time and cost of supplies

questions.printed_answer_heading: There is no evidence that it helps control healthcare costs
questions.explanation:
The RBRVS is supposed to help manage the rising cost of healthcare, but there is no evidence
that it works.
The RBRVS computes a set fee plan for services in advance.

questions.question: Which of the following studies will detect denervation first?
questions.explanation:
Denervation can be detected earliest with T2 weighted MRI
There will be a hyperintense signal

questions.question:
A patient had transsphenoidal resection of a suprasellar tumor. 2 weeks later she
develops dizziness and lethargy and on exam is dehydrated. Laboratories show sodium is 125 mEq/L,
potassium is 6.0 mEq/L, and glucose is 45 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most probable
diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The hyperkalemia and hypernatremia are secondary to deficient mineralocorticoid activity
The hypoglycemia is due to the lack of glucocorticoids

questions.question:
A 54-year-old man underwent transcochlear excision of a 4-cm meningioma
earlier in the day. He was extubated postoperatively and did well for the first 4 hours. Now, the
patient is confused, not following commands, and experiencing respiratory depression. Emergency
CT scans show findings consistent with a posterior fossa hematoma. Which of the following should
not be included in emergency management?

answers.A:
At the bedside, undress the wound and remove the sutures or staples to allow possible
evacuation of hematoma allowing some brainstem decompression
answers.B:
Order an emergency MRI to determine additional information regarding the posterior fossa and
the wound
answers.C:
Call the operating room for emergency surgery in order to evacuate the hematoma causing
brainstem compression
answers.D: Protect the airway to prevent aspiration

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Order an emergency MRI to determine additional information regarding the posterior
fossa and the wound
questions.explanation:
This patient has a posterior fossa hematoma that is causing brainstem compression with
subsequent respiratory depression
Removing the staples and/or sutures would allow for the possible evacuation of some or all of
the hematoma. Providing adequate respiratory support for both oxygenation and prevention of
aspiration is obviously indicated
Taking the patient emergently to the operating room for wound exploration, evacuation of
hematoma, and control of the offending bleeding source if present is certainly a reasonable plan
An MRI would not provide any useful additional information that the CT scan did not provide.
Obtaining the MRI also delays treating the life-threatening hematoma

questions.question: Focal calcifications on CT at the junction of globe and optic nerve are due to:
questions.explanation:
This is a classic location for drusen. Drusen are tiny accumulations of extracellular material that
build up in Bruch's membrane, the innermost layer of choroid
Optic gliomas typically don't calcify; hemangiomas do not typically involve the optic nerve or
globe
Retinoblastoma calcification is within the retinal tumor

questions.question:
Which of the following is not part of the triad of findings represented by the
Cushing response?
questions.explanation:
As the ICP values become higher, the heart rate and blood pressure will dramatically increase
A sudden drop in the heart rate with the widened pulse pressure means that brain herniation is
imminent
It is a terminal event unresponsive to any interventions
Many of these patients are intubated so irregular respirations are not observed

questions.question: What is the chief determining factor governing cerebral perfusion?
questions.explanation:
The cerebral perfusion pressure equals the mean arterial blood pressure minus intracranial
pressure

questions.question: Which spinal nerve injury innervates the triceps?
questions.explanation:
C7 provides innervation to the triceps and extensor in muscles
C8 injury released to pain in the medial forearm and little finger
T1 provides innervation to intrinsic hand muscles

questions.question: Which organism is most often responsible for meningitis in adults?
questions.explanation:
The most common organism for neonatal meningitis is streptococcus agalactiae
Hemophilus influenza was the most common organism before the introduction of the HIB vaccine
Neisseria meningitides is most common in adults
Staphylococcus epidermidis is responsible for 75 percent of shunt related meningitis

questions.question:
Data suggest that occurence of a stroke after a TIA is usually within what time
period?
questions.explanation:
About 10% of patients with a TIA will have a stoke
Most of these strokes occur within 90 days
However more than 50% of these strokes occur within 48 hours

questions.question: What skull injury is consistent with the battle sign?
questions.explanation:
Battle sign is result of subcutaneous blood pooling
It is associated with basilar skull fracture
Another common sign of basilar skull fracture is the raccoon's sign

questions.question:
Select the incorrect statement about MPTP (1-methyl4-phenyl-1,2,3,6
tetrahydropyridine).

answers.A: MPTP is a neurotoxin that causes a Parkinson like disease with less resting tremor
answers.B: MPTP can accidently contaminate methamphetamine, made on the streets
answers.D: MPP+ is actively taken up by dopaminergic neurons and causes cell death

questions.printed_answer_heading: MPTP can accidently contaminate methamphetamine, made on the streets
questions.explanation:
MPTP is an accidental contaminant of the synthetic opioid MPPP
It is taken up by astrocytes, oxidized to MPP+, and taken up by dopamine transporters causing
cell death
It causes a Parkinson like disease with less resting tremor
The major effect is at nigrostriatal neurons

questions.question: White rami communicans contain which of the following fibers?
questions.explanation:
White rami communicans contain preganglionic unmyelinated and myelinated sympathetic fibers.
The 12 thoracic and the first 2 lumbar nerves contribute a white ramus communicans to
sympathetic ganglion.
The preganglionic sympathetic myelinated fibers arise from cell bodies in the intermediolateral
cell column in the spinal cord.

questions.question:
After abdominal surgery, the risk of pulmonary complications is heightened by
all of the following except:

answers.B: Reduced tidal volume from inadequate pain control

questions.explanation:
Postoperative atelectasis is the major cause of pneumonia
Diaphragm dysfunction and prolonged artificial ventilation may also cause pneumonia

questions.question:
What is the current gold standard of care for suspected pulmonary embolus
(PE)?
questions.explanation:
The American College of Radiology considers chest CTA the current standard of care for
suspected PE
Venography is utilized in the diagnosis of DVT
A V/Q scan becomes more important when CT scanning is not available or when there is a
contraindication to IV contrast
CXR findings are nonspecific in the diagnosis of PE

questions.question:
What is the most preferred action to take when facing a stable patient with
accidental poisoning at home?
questions.explanation:
Calling the poison control center is the best method of dealing with accidental poisoning
Administration of ipecac syrup has been disfavored nowadays due to lack of supportive data
advocating for its use
Activated charcoal administration is to be done at health care settings

questions.question:
Why would a licensed healthcare provider not be included in the National
Practitioner Data Bank ?

answers.B: The are not licensed to practice in the United States
answers.D: They have not had a malpractice claim

questions.printed_answer_heading: They have not had a malpractice claim
questions.explanation: Malpractice claim defendants are listed in The National Practitioner Data Bank

questions.question: Staphylococcus aureus is best treated in inpatients with:
questions.explanation:
Any infection with S. aureus should be presumed to be MRSA until sensitivities are available.
Any patient ill enough to require admission should be treated with vancomycin.
As vancomycin can only be given IV, outpatient infections are often treated with
trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole or minocycline

questions.question: Which of the following is not a risk for perioperative deep venous thrombosis?
questions.explanation:
Other risk factors include malignancy, oral contraceptives, long surgical duration, and genetic
hypercoagulability

questions.question: Which of the following describes decerebrate posturing?

answers.A: Flexed arms that are internally rotated with extended legs and clenched fists
answers.B: Rigid extension of extremities with retraction of the head and neck and pointed toes
answers.C: Rigid rotation of the neck with the chin on the shoulder
answers.D: Involuntary flexion and extension of arms

questions.printed_answer_heading: Rigid extension of extremities with retraction of the head and neck and pointed toes
questions.explanation:
Decerebrate posturing is caused by damage at the level of the upper brainstem or midbrain
Decorticate posturing is described in choice 1 and is caused by damage to the corticospinal tract
Choice 3 refers to torticollis

questions.question: The most common complication of spinal cord stimulator implant is?
questions.explanation:
The most common complication of SCS implantation is spinal fluid leakage
Followed by migration of device
Persistent pain is the third most common complication

questions.question:
A patient is going for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. How many days
before surgery should aspirin be stopped?
questions.explanation:
Patients are advised to stop NSAID three days before surgery
Patients are advised to stop aspirin ten days before surgery

questions.question:
Eye position information reaches the abducens nucleus from neuronal integrator
neurons coming from?

answers.A: Rostral interstitial nucleus of the medial longitudinal fasciculus

questions.explanation:
The abducens nucleus is the site of horizontal versional control
Once the eye reaches a new eccentric position at the end of the saccade, stimulation of the
abducens nucleus by the parapontine reticular formation burst neurons is substituted by a tonic
gaze-holding mechanism to maintain the eccentric position
A neuronal network integrates a velocity-coded signal into a position-coded signal, which is
referred to as the neural integrator, which includes the horizontal gaze center, the medial
vestibular nucleus, and the nucleus prepositus hypoglossi

questions.question:
What would be the MRI findings for a patient with one month of headaches,
worse in the morning and neurologic exam findings of right-left confusion, finger agnosia, agraphia,
and acalculia?
questions.explanation:
Gerstmann syndrome (alexia, agraphia, acalculia, right-left confusion and finger agnosia) is seen
with parietal lobe lesions
Temporal lobe lesions cause seizures, behavioral changes, olfactory or gustatory hallucinations
and automatisms (lip smacking, fiddling with clothing or other objects, repeating short phrases)
Frontal lobe lesions cause personality changes and cognitive decline
Occipital lesions are associated with visual defects

questions.question:
Precocious puberty and papilledema in an 8 year old girl is consistent with
which of the following?
questions.explanation:
The pineal region is the source of an extraordinarily diverse group of tumor types ranging from
astrocytomas to chemodectomas
Germ cell tumors arise from the tissues in this region as well presumably from embryonal cell
rests
Pineal tumors are rare representing only 1 percent of childhood tumors
Papilledema suggests occlusion of CSF circulation or significant mass effect

Postoperative deep vein thrombosis prevention is best accomplished by which

SCDs and aspirin are not sufficient for DVT prevention

A 53-year-old male presents with unilateral hearing loss, tinnitus, and mild

questions.question:
A patient is noted to have fine twitching of the muscles of the tongue and atrophy

questions.question: Meningococcal meningitis in adults should be treated with:

questions.question:
Which of the following is correct about the use of steroids for acute bacterial

Steroids should be given with the first dose of antibiotics to decrease inflammation with the first

with N. meningitidis
Steroids have been shown to decrease mortality, hearing loss, and long-term neurologic

questions.question:
A patient has decreased sensation to pain and temperature in the distribution of

questions.explanation:
Spinothalamic fibers in the ventral commissure of the spinal cord are disrupted with

Dermatomes above and below the tumor a spared
Syringomyelia, intramedullary tumor, and hyperextension in a patient with cervical spondylosis

questions.question: A contrecoup brain injury occurs:

questions.explanation:

Prolactin regulates lactation after birth
Progesterone is responsible for pregnancy maintenance

questions.explanation:

questions.question: Wilson disease is caused by the accumulation of:

A 45 year old with alcoholic liver cirrhosis is stabbed in the abdomen and

questions.explanation:
Fresh frozen plasma contains all coagulation factors but levels of factor 8 are low. The plasma

host reaction

questions.question: Which group has the highest risk for complications after minor surgery?
questions.explanation: Diabetic patients are at increased risk for surgery

questions.question:
A 49 y/o female informs the ER physician that she has the worst headache of her

questions.explanation:
This is a classic presentation of a SAH if the patient is awake and able to describe the symptoms

questions.question: A lesion in which area can bes associated with gait disturbance?

questions.question: The sural nerve is often found superficially in what part of the leg?

lateral malleolus

Sensation from the skin to the central nervous system is carried by which of the

questions.question: Which statement regarding the treatment of status epilepticus is least accurate?

answers.A: Phenytoin is contraindicated in the presence of 2nd or 3rd degree AV block

answers.D: Seizures due to isoniazid overdose should be treated with intravenous pyridoxine

questions.printed_answer_heading: Refractory seizures should be treated with pancuronium

Benzodiazepines are the initial drug of choice for status epilepticus

questions.question:
You are educating a student on spinal cord injuries. Which of the following
statements should send you back to the books?

answers.A:
Central cord syndrome - greater loss of motor in upper extremities, with variable sensory loss;

questions.question: Which of the following is a cardinal sign of Parkinson disease (PD)?
