Depressed skull fractures are most common in the frontoparietal areas, followed by the
temporal, occipital and mixed
The majority of depressed skull fractures are open fractures

questions.question:
What are typical CNS findings in a patient with suspected toxoplasmosis of the
brain?
questions.explanation: Typical CNS observation in patients with toxoplasmosis include multiple ring enhancing lesions

questions.question: Which is false about Parkinson disease?

answers.A: Selegeline can delay the need for levodopa therapy
answers.B: Selegeline can be used as adjuvant with levodopa in advanced disease
answers.C: Rigidity is best treated with muscle relaxant

questions.printed_answer_heading: Rigidity is best treated with muscle relaxant
questions.explanation:
Levodopa is usually combined with carbidopa. Carbidopa works in the periphery todelay the
conversion of levodopa into dopamine resulting in higher levels in the brain.
Levodopa is effective in about 75% of patients with Parkinson disease. It is especially
particularly effective for bradykinesia and rigidity with marginal improvement of tremor and
balance. Anti-cholinergics may help tremor and rigidity.
Other dopaminergic agents include bromocriptine, pramipexole, and ropinirole. The antiviral
drug amantidine also helps in reducing dyskinesias
Selegeline is an irreversible MAO-B inhibitor. Muscle relaxants do not improve the rigidity
associated with this condition.

questions.question:
The most important vascular structure that passes within the cerebellopontine
angle is:
questions.explanation:
The anterior inferior cerebellar artery is an important vessel, which passes through the
cerebellopontine angle

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common cause of viral encephalitis?
questions.explanation:
Enteroviruses the most common causes of viral encephalitis known
Echovirus is one of the Enteroviruses
Coxsackie A and B viruses are also Enteroviruses
Aseptic meningitis commonly presents with increased CSF protein and a normal glucose count

questions.question:
A 70 y/o chronic alcoholic presents to the ER with malnutrition and Wernicke
encephalopathy. He is given IV thiamine. What is the next necessary medication to give before
starting IV dextrose?
questions.explanation:
There may be no response to thiamine with hypomagnesemia
The magnesium should be given on an empirical basis
Glucose is necessary as these patients have low blood sugar and glycogen stores
If given before the thiamine, the encephalopathic condition may worsen and Korsakoff psychosis
may be precipitated

questions.question: Which muscle weakness is not associated with the Dejerine Klumpke palsy?
questions.explanation:
The Dejerine-Klumpke palsy associated with injuries to C8 and T1
Leads to muscle weakness of hand intrinsic muscles and wrist flexion
It can be seconary to birth trauma or during a fall with over adduction of the arm
It is also known as Klumpke palsy

questions.question: Which is the risk of major fetal deformity in the normal population?
questions.explanation:
There is a five percent of fetal deformity in mother who is taking an antiepileptic medication
The average patient has a 2% risk
This risk increases to seven percent with carbamazepine or valproic acid
Valproic acid has been linked to neural tube defects, cleft palate, and atrial septal defects

questions.question:
A daughter brings her elderly mother to the provider because of a constellation
of symptoms that appear to be getting worse. She tells the doctor that her mom has become neglectful,
unable to remember things told to her, poor abstraction, frequently disoriented and faulty judgment.
What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
These symptoms fit a pattern of dementia which worsens over time. Loss of cognitive ability is a
profound feature. Psychosis and incontinence may develop. Depression occurs in 20-30% of
cases
A strictly depressed patient can have some of the same symptoms. They tend to find no pleasure
in things, self-hatred, poor concentration, insomnia, and memory disturbances. Generally a
depressed patient should be able to answer questions testing mental capabilities and
computational ability
A depressed patient may complain of memory difficulty while a patient with advanced dementia
may be unaware and unconcerned about memory lapses

questions.question: Which neural pathways are responsible for transmitting light touch?
questions.explanation: The anterior spinothalamic transmits pressure and light touch sensations

questions.question: Examples of crystalloid fluids include all of the following except?
questions.explanation:
The principal component of all crystalloids is sodium chloride. When administered, it follows
the same distribution as extracellular fluid and helps expand the interstitial volume.
Isotonic saline has slightly higher chloride than plasma and so hyperchloremic metabolic
acidosis is a potential risk when used in large volumes.
Lactate Ringers contains potassium and calcium and has less sodium than isotonic saline. The
calcium in Lactate Ringers can bind to drugs and inactivate anticoagulants.
Plasmalyte has a buffer and contains more magnesium. Albumin is the most common colloid
solution to expand volume. Each cc of albumin expands the volume 4-5 times.

questions.question: During neck trauma, which cervical disc is most likely to herniate?
questions.explanation: The most common cervical herniations are C6-C7 due to trauma

questions.question: Which of the following would be most dense on an unenhanced CT of the brain?
questions.explanation:
The densest material on a CT of the head is bone
Blood causing a hematoma is much denser than CSF, gray matter, or white matter
The dura matter may have some calcification making it denser than the brain

questions.question: Arterial supply to the hippocampus is mostly from:
questions.explanation: The PCA gives off the hippocampal artery branch, which supplies the hippocampus

questions.question:
Scheuermann kyphosis has been associated with which of the following
conditions?
questions.explanation:
Isthmic spondylolisthesis is associated with Scheuermann kyphosis
The increased lumbar lordosis caused by the thoracic kyphosis leads to stress fractures of the
pars interarticularis and thus increased incidence of spondylolisthesis

questions.question:
A patient with a spinal cord injury at C6 is receiving therapy for sitting balance.
How should the hands be positioned when being used for support?

answers.B: Fingers extended and abducted with wrists extended
answers.C: Fingers flexed and adducted at the MP joints only
answers.D: Fingers extended and adducted with wrists extended

questions.explanation:
Fingers should be flexed at all joints when weight bearing
This prevents overstretching of finger flexors and claw hand deformity

questions.question:
The patient is complaining of vertigo. The provider performs the Hallpike test in
order to rule out which condition?
questions.explanation:
The Hallpike is also referred to as the Dix-Hallpike test and Nylan-Barany test
A positive test is highly indicative of BPPV (Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo). A sitting
patient has his head rotated 45 degrees and then is laid down with the head held in 20 degree of
extension.
The eyes are observed for 45 seconds. A positive response is rotatory nystagmus with the fast
component towards the ear closest to the floor. The fast component involves the top of the eye
Vertigo from vestibular neuritis last a long time while it is less than a minute for BPPV.
Vestibular neuritis usually has a history of a preceding viral infection. A negative Hallpike test
suggests a central etiology

questions.question:
The best classification of an astrocytoma of intermediate differentiation with the
presence of nuclear atypia and mitotic activity, but without endothelial proliferation or necrosis, is?
questions.explanation:
The World Health Organization has assigned four grades to the spectrum of astrocytic tumors:
grade I (pilocytic astrocytoma), grade II (diffuse astrocytoma), grade III (anaplastic
astrocytoma), and grade IV (glioblastoma multiforme)
Anaplastic astrocytomas are Grade III astrocytomas
They are characterized by an intermediate differentiation, increased nuclear pleo-morphism,
increased cellular density, and moderately increased nuclear hyperchromatism plus mitoses

questions.question:
Spontaneous intracranial hypotension can have serious complications causing
neurologic disability. Which of the following is most common?
questions.explanation:
Spontaneous intracranial hypotension is characterized by daily headache improved with
recumbency
There is inferior displacement of the brain with traction on cerebral veins and sinuses
This can cause a positional headache and result in subdural hematoma
These hematomas can cause neurologic disability and require neurosurgical treatment

questions.question: In a tonsillar herniation, the cerebellar tonsils are displaced through the:
questions.explanation:
In tonsillar herniation, the cerebellar tonsils are displaced inferiorly into the foramen magnum.
The tonsillar herniation causes compression of the lower brain stem and upper cervical cord.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a normal function of platelets?
questions.explanation:
The normal functions of platelets are to adhere, aggregate, and degranulate
They can be activated directly through glycoprotein VI of collagen or indirectly by von
Willebrand factor binding to glycoprotein 1b
Platelet granules have alpha granules containing multiple vasoactive factors, delta granules
containing ATP, calcium, and serotonin, and lambda granules containing hydrolytic enzymes

questions.question: Which of the following is false about neuromuscular blockers?

answers.A: Have increased the safety of anesthesia
answers.B: Small rapidly contracting muscles are most susceptible and are paralyzed first
answers.C: Patient must receive the neuromuscular blockers before general anesthesia for a full effect
answers.D: All of them have poor oral absorption

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Patient must receive the neuromuscular blockers before general anesthesia for a full
effect
questions.explanation:
Neuromuscular blockers have increased the safety of anesthesia since fewer anesthetics is
required to produce muscle relaxation
One must never administer a neuromuscular agent to an awake patient. These agents will stop
respiration by paralyzing the diaphragm
All patients must be mechanically ventilated prior to administrating these agents
Use of these agents should be limited to anesthesia and individuals in critical care medicine

questions.question: How many hours should patients be NPO before surgery?
questions.explanation:
Overnight fasting of at least 8 hours is recommended before surgery
Risk of aspiration is high if patients are not NPO before surgery
In emergency surgery gastric contents can be evacuated through NG tube

questions.question:
The pars distalis is composed of chromophils and chromophores. Acidophils
and basophils are the two types of chromophils. Select the correct association of hormone and cell
type.
questions.explanation:
The pars distalis basophils are corticotropic cells and secrete ACTH, thyrotrophs secrete TSH,
and gonadotrophs secrete FSH and LH
Acidophils are somatotrophs and mammotrophs secreting GH and prolactin respectively

questions.question: What is the incidence of syringomyelia with central pain syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Syringomyelia has the highest occurrence in central pain syndrome
About 70 percent of the time

questions.question: Which is an element of the pain (nociceptive) nerve pathways?
questions.explanation:
Immediately after the axons of nociceptive primary afferent neurons enter the dorsal horn of the
spinal cord, they may travel rostrally or caudally for one or two segments in the dorsolateral
tract of Lissauer before entering the grey matter
The lateral corticospinal tract is part of the motor system, containing axons of the upper motor
neurons
The lateral geniculate nucleus is part of the visual system; it receives afferent information from
the retina and transmits it to the visual cortex
The Locus Coeruleus is a brainstem ganglion that mediates sympathetic response to stress and
panic

questions.question: When compared to young adults, elderly patients:

answers.A: Have a slower rate of drug elimination

questions.printed_answer_heading: Have a slower rate of drug elimination
questions.explanation:
When compared to young adults, elderly patients have a slower rate of drug elimination
The dosages of common medications may be reduced up to 50% in elderly patients
The phenomenon is directly related to a decreased rate of drug elimination by the liver and
kidneys
The elderly usually weight more than younger patients. The resting heart rate is comperable.

questions.question: A lesion at the medial cerebral peduncle is known as:
questions.explanation:
A lesion at the lateral pontine area is known as the Marie Foix syndrome
Characterized by impairment of corticospinal and spinothalamic tracts
The Weber syndrome is caused by a lesion of the medial cerebral peduncle
It involves the oculomotor nerve and conatralateral hemiplegia or hemiparesis

questions.question: What is the most common cause of epidemic meningitis?
questions.explanation:
Streptococcus agalactia is the most common cause of neonatal meningitis
Escherichia coli is also a leading cause of neonatal meningitis
Neisseria meningitidis is the most common cause of epidemic meningitis

questions.question: The motor strip of the brain is more appropriately known as the:
questions.explanation:
Postcentral gyrus of parietal lobe is sensory cortex
Inferior frontal gyrus is Broca motor speech area
Calcarine cortex is primary visual cortex
Precentral gyrus is the motor strip on which one can imagine a homunculus.

questions.question: Which is false about complex regional pain syndrome?
questions.explanation: Complex regional pain syndrome sometimes responds to sympathectomy

questions.question: Restless leg syndrome involves:
questions.explanation: RLS is a sensory syndrome

questions.question:
A middle aged man with 4 week history of severe headaches has a contrast CT
scan which reveals several small, circular, hypodense lesions with ring like contrast enhancement.
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The incidence of metastatic disease is approximately 150,000-250,000 cases per year as
compared to primary intracranial tumors with 35,000 per year.
15% to 30% of cancer patients develop intracranial metastases during the course of their
disease. The most common tumors that metastasize to the brain parenchyma are lung, breast,
kidney, GI and melanoma.
Leukemia shows a predilection for the leptomeninges.
Immunocompromised patients are at increased risk for central nervous system lymphoma.

questions.question:
Which of these is not a standard used for financial incentives to providersby
managed care groups?

answers.A: Academic appointments at a medical school

questions.printed_answer_heading: Academic appointments at a medical school
questions.explanation:
Patient satisfaction is one of many defined criteria used by managed care groups to provide
financial incentives to physicians.
Quality standards are additional criteria managed care groups implement to provide financial
incentives to physicians.
Defined outcomes are specific criteria primary care physicians must meet to maximize their
financial return from managed care contracts.

questions.question:
Which of the following is not a sign of malfunction of a ventriculoperitoneal
shunt?
questions.explanation:
Shunt malfunction can result in downward deviation of the eyes with only part of the iris visible
In infants the anterior fontanelle may bulge or the scalp veins distend

questions.question:
A patient with a seizure disorder is admitted to the hospital. The patient is
ambulating with assistance in the hall and has a tonic clonic seizure. Which of the following would
not be appropriate acute management?

answers.A: Lower the patient to the floor
answers.B: Place the patient in the lateral decubitus position
answers.C: Place a rubber bite block in the mouth to prevent tooth breakage
answers.D: Put a pillow under the head

questions.printed_answer_heading: Place a rubber bite block in the mouth to prevent tooth breakage
questions.explanation:
A patient having a generalized seizure should be placed so as not to injure themselves
Lowering the patient to the floor, turning them to one side to clear oral secretions, and placing a
pillow under the head are all appropriate
Nothing should be put into the patient's mouth
Nearby objects should be moved to avoid the patient hitting them accidentally

questions.question: Which cranial nerve controls mastication?
questions.explanation: Cranial nerve V innervates mastication muscle

questions.question: How is amblyopia defined?
questions.explanation:
Amblyopia is reduced vision that cannot be corrected with glasses or contact lenses.
It is sometimes called a lazy eye.
It is almost only unilateral but there can be reduction of vision in both eyes.
About 3% of children under 6 years have this condition.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of cauda equina syndrome?
questions.explanation:
The cauda equina syndrome is characterized by low back pain, unilateral or bilateral sciatica,
saddle sensory disturbances, bowel and bladder incontinence and variable amount of motor and
sensory loss in the extremities
Cauda equina syndrome is due to lesions that compress nerve roots.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a symptom of autonomic dysreflexia?
questions.explanation:
Autonomic dysreflexia is seen in patients with spinal cord injuries
It results from a noxious stimuli and causes sympathetic nervous system over activity
Signs and symptoms include hypertension, severe headache, visual blurring or spots, flushing,
and perspiration
Pallor is not a usual finding

questions.question: Which is not suggestive of acute urinary retention?

answers.A: Urine output of 30 ml on Foley catheter insertion
answers.B: Post-void residual (PVR) urine o f>100 ml
answers.C: Straining to void with no urine output
answers.D: Suprapubic distention with lower abdominal discomfort

questions.printed_answer_heading: Urine output of 30 ml on Foley catheter insertion
questions.explanation:
PVR >100 ml, straining to void without urine output, and suprapubic distention with lower
abdominal discomfort are suggestive of acute urinary retention
30 ml urine out by Foley catheter does not suggest acute urinary retention

questions.question: What percent of patients with transverse myelitis have full recovery?
questions.explanation:
MRI is the best diagnostic test to confirm transverse myelitis
It is characterized by swelling of spinal cord and inflammatory changes
About one third of patients have full recovery, one third have partial recovery, and one third
show no improvement over time

questions.question:
Lhermitte sign is occasionally seen in multiple sclerosis patients. It can best be
described as:

answers.B: An electrical sensation radiating down the spine
answers.C: Forward flexion deformity of the spine

questions.printed_answer_heading: An electrical sensation radiating down the spine
questions.explanation:
Lhermitte's sign is evoked by forward flexion of the neck, which if positive, results in an
electrical sensation radiating down the spine or trunk
The etiology of this sensation in MS is most often a demyelinating plaque in the cervical or
upper thoracic region of the spinal cord
Lhermitte sign can be seen in other compressive or intramedullary lesions in the cervical spine
region such as with severe cervical spondylosis

questions.question:
A patient presents with a gradual onset of weakness in his arms and legs. The
weakness has now spread to his chest and he has difficulty breathing. He says the weakness initially
started in his extremities and now he is unable to swallow. He has lost about 15 lbs in weight over
the past 3 months. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation:
Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a disease of unknown origin
The disorder presents with slow progressive degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons
The disorder presents with hyper-reflexia, spasticity, weakness and fasciculation
ALS is fatal because of weakness of respiratory muscles

questions.question:
In a patient with a ventriculo-peritoneal shunt, the most common organism
responsible for meningitis is?
questions.explanation:
The most common organisms for neonatal meningitis is Streptococcus agalactiae
Staphylococcus epidermidis is responsible for 75 percent of shunt related meningitis
Neisseria meningitides is most common in adults

questions.question: Which of the following is not true regarding essential tremor?

answers.A: It is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait
answers.B: It is commonly seen in patients in their 20s or 30s
answers.D: Tremors get better with alcohol ingestion

questions.explanation:
Essential familial tremor is a common form of tremor
It is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait with a typical onset in the patient's teens
The diagnosis is usually evident by the time the patient is in his or her 20s or 30s
Essential tremors get better with alcohol ingestion

questions.question:
Meningitis associated with traumatic CSF leak is characterized by which of the
following?

answers.A: There is no increased risk for meningitis with pneumocephalus
answers.B: There is a lower incidence of meningitis with high flow leaks
answers.C: There is a lower incidence of meningitis with low flow leaks
answers.D: Low intracranial pressure is associated with lower incidence of meningitis

questions.printed_answer_heading: There is a lower incidence of meningitis with high flow leaks
questions.explanation:
There is a higher incidence of meningitis with low flow leaks
Low intracranial pressure is associated the higher incidence of meningitis
There is a higher risk for meningitis with pneumocephalus

questions.question:
In a patient following surgery, which of the following features will not be part of
the pain syndrome?
questions.explanation: Signs of pain include sympathetic changes

questions.question: After CVA, a patient has tongue deviation to the right from:
questions.explanation:
The hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) controls lingual movement and deviation is to the right when the
right nerve is affected
The glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) is largely a sensory nerve to the tongue and pharynx

questions.question: Incorrect sensory relationship?
questions.explanation:
C5-Area over deltoid
T4-Nipple, T8-xiphoid sternum, T10-Umbilicus, T12-Symphysis pubis, L4-Medial calf, L5- 1st
and 2nd toe webspace, S1-Lateral foot, S3-Ischial tuberosity, S4 and S5-Perianal region

questions.question: Where is the lesion responsible for Parinaud syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Parinaud syndrome is caused by lesion of the midbrain
Characterized by fixed pupils, lid retraction, and dissociation of light

questions.question: Which of the following bone disorders has been associated with tinnitus?
questions.explanation:
Paget is a rare cause of tinnitus
When Paget's disease involves the skull, patients may develop deafness, vertigo, tinnitus,
vertebral insufficiency and cranial nerve involvement

questions.question:
The stellate ganglion is located in what anatomical position in relation to the
right subclavian artery?
questions.explanation: The stellate ganglion is located anterior to the subclavian artery

questions.question: Which is false about status epilepticus?

answers.A: 2nd or 3rd degree AV block is a contraindication to phenytoin
answers.B: Benzodiazepines are the drug of choice
answers.C: Refractory seizures should be treated with pancuronium bromide
answers.D: Isoniazid overdose induced seizures may be stopped with IV pyridoxine

questions.printed_answer_heading: Refractory seizures should be treated with pancuronium bromide
questions.explanation:
Benzodiazepines are the drug of choice for status epilepticus.
Refractory seizures should be treated with IV phenytoin, phenobarbital, or general anesthesia.
Phenytoin may disrupt cardiac conduction and is contraindicated with 2nd or 3rd degree AV
block.
INH induced seizures are treated with IV pyridoxine.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an effect of opioid analgesics?
questions.explanation:
Opioid analgesics cause miosis not mydriasis
Other effects are analgesia, euphoria, depression of the cough reflex, emesis, respiratory
depression, and relaxation of the smooth muscle of the bladder

questions.question: Progesterone receptors are expressed in what cellular organ of meningiomas?
questions.explanation: Progesterone receptors are expressed in the nucleus of meningiomas

questions.question: The pharmacologic effects of morphine include all EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Morphine causes severe constipation and most patients require concomitant laxative therapy
In high doses, morphine can cause apnea
The side effects of morphine can be reversed with naloxone but this does not apply to
constipation
The white liquid often stings when injected, the pain which is relieved by use of lidocaine

questions.question: Which of following abbreviations is acceptable?
questions.explanation:
Abbreviations to avoid are U, MS, and QHS
They often lead to confusion resulting in medical errors

questions.question:
What is the best way to differentiate central from peripheral vestibular
nystagmus?

answers.A: The accentuation of central nystagmus with fixation
answers.B: The suppression of peripheral nystagmus with fixation
answers.C: The presence of a torsional component with central nystagmus
answers.D: The presence of increased nystagmus with gaze directed toward the slow phase of nystagmus

questions.printed_answer_heading: The suppression of peripheral nystagmus with fixation
questions.explanation:
Two main differences that differentiate peripheral from central nystagmus include the effects of
fixation on nystagmus as well as the direction of nystagmus
Fixation of the eyes suppresses peripheral but not central nystagmus
Also, peripheral nystagmus, particularly when vertical, usually has a torsional component
Pure vertical and torsional nystagmus are central

questions.question: Patients who develop a stroke and die within the first week, usually die from?
questions.explanation:
The majority of people who die within the first week after a stroke usually die from the stroke
itself

questions.question: Leg extension is innervated by:
questions.explanation:
L2 nerve root innervates hip flexion
L3 nerve root controls leg extension
L4 controls heel walking
S1 controls toe walking

questions.question:
A severed median nerve at the cubital fossa would cause all of the following
deficits except for which choice?

answers.A: The inability to flex the terminal phalanx of the 4th digit
answers.C: inability to flex the terminal phalanx of the thumb
answers.D: weakness in flexion at the wrist joint

questions.printed_answer_heading: The inability to flex the terminal phalanx of the 4th digit
questions.explanation:
The ulnar nerve controls flexion of the terminal phalanx of the 4th digit
The median nerve innervates the flexor pollicis longus that flexes the thermal phalanx of the
thumb
The median nerve innervates the pronator teres that allows pronation of the forearm
The median nerve innervates the flexor carpi radialis and the opponens pollicis that allow
opposition of the thumb

questions.question: What is not true regarding Guillain BarrÃ© syndrome?
questions.explanation: GBS involves demyelination with no sensory involvement

questions.question: Which medication is most likely to increase heart rate?
questions.explanation: Meperidine reduces cardiac output and increases pulse

questions.question:
A 71 year old female with a prior history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension is
seen in the emergency because of sudden onset of slurred speech it is suspected that she is developing
an acute stroke. Which of the following would absolutely contraindicate thrombolytic therapy with
tPA?

answers.B: History of diabetic retinopathy treated with laser a month ago

questions.explanation:
Absolute contraindications for ischemic stroke patients include uncontrolled hypertension,
history of cranial or spinal surgery within three months, history of head trauma or
cerebrovascular accident and bleeding diathesis
Thrombolysis with tPA can proceed within three hours of onset if head CT demonstrates no
intracranial bleed or AV malformation

questions.question: The agent of choice for Gram-negative meningitis is:
questions.explanation:
Ceftriaxone competes with bilirubin for binding with albumin. Reserve concentration of albumin
in newborn is decreased by 39% increasing the risk of bilirubin encephalopathy in high risk
neonates.
Cephalosporins have no activity against L. monocytogenes and Enterococci

questions.question: Why is vitamin C necessary for collagen synthesis?

answers.B: It is a cofactor in the hydroxylation of proline
answers.D: Secretion of procollagen into the extracellular matrix

questions.printed_answer_heading: It is a cofactor in the hydroxylation of proline
questions.explanation:
Procollagen is secreted into the extracellular matrix
Without hydroxyproline, the helical structure cannon form

questions.question: The most striking gross finding in Parkinson disease is:

answers.C: Loss of pigment in the substantia nigra

questions.printed_answer_heading: Loss of pigment in the substantia nigra
questions.explanation:
Parkinson disease is characterized by loss of pigmented dopaminergic neurons in the substantia
nigra.
This is most prominently in the ventral lateral substantia nigra.
Before Parkinson disease shows signs and symptoms about 80% of dopaminergic neurons are
lost.

questions.question: Where is the most common site of neurogenic gastrointestinal ulcer?
questions.explanation:
Esophageal ulcers are the most common results after neurogenic insults
Often located in the lower esophagus

questions.question:
Which of the following is a risk factor for developing normal pressure
hydrocephalus?
questions.explanation:
Subarachnoid hemorrhage is a risk factor for NPH in that it can cause scarring and occlusion of
the arachnoid villi preventing easy exit flow of the CSF
Other conditions placing one at risk for NPH include meningitis, encephalitis, traumatic brain
injury, aneurysmal rupture, brain surgery and cerebral carcinomatosis
NPH does not have a familial pattern of occurrence
Treatment in symptomatic patients consists of acetazolamide, intermittent lumbar puncture with
CSF drainage and CSF shunting

questions.question: MR imaging shows the pituitary gland as

answers.A: Showing a flat or mildly concave anterosuperior surface
answers.B: Showing less enhancement than a pituitary adenoma

questions.explanation:
Enhancement is promptly noted on T 1-weighted images in the anterior pituitary gland, the
infundibulum, and the cavernous sinuses
Microadenomas are generally hypointense compared with the normal gland on T1-weighted
images and display variable intensity on T2-weighted images
The pituitary gland can have variable appearance depending on sex and age. Its superior surface
may be slightly convex upward

questions.question:
An elderly patient scores 25 on the Mini-Mental Status Examination (MMSE).
The initial impression is which of the following?
questions.explanation:
The total possible score on the MMSE is 30.
The median score for persons age 18-59 is 29.
For persons aged 80 and above, the median score is 25.
A score of 20-25 indicates early Alzheimer's disease. A score of 10-19 indicates middle-stage
Alzheimer's disease.

questions.question: Which is a feature of intrathecal drug delivery?
questions.explanation:
Intrathecal drug delivery system avoids first pass side effect
It allows more direct delivery and more potency of drug

questions.question: What is the significance of a positive Brudzinski sign?
questions.explanation:
This sign is elicited by flexing the neck on a supine patient
A positive finding is nuchal rigidity suggesting meningitis. It is not very sensitive
Kernig sign involves flexing the hip and leg of a supine patient and then extending the leg
It is positive if spine pain is produced indicative of possible meningeal inflammation or
infection

questions.question: Which is false about subdural hematoma?

answers.A: Are often associated with skull fractures
answers.B: Most common in elderly individual who fall
answers.C: The hematoma should be evacuated surgically
answers.D: Prognosis is much better for chronic subdurals than acute cases

questions.printed_answer_heading: Are often associated with skull fractures
questions.explanation:
Subdural hematomas are common in elderly and can occur after minor injury. Skull fractures
very rarely cause subdural hematomas
The cause of subdural hematoma is tearing of the bridging veins between the dura and draining
venous sinuses
Acute subdurals often cause cortical damage and may be bilateral and hence the prognosis is not
very good
The onset of symptoms may be a few hours. CT will reveal a crescent shaped hemorrhage
compressing the cortex. Complications can include herniation, increased intracranial pressure
and seizures

questions.question:
A transsphenoidal hypophysectomy is done via a surgical incision posterior to
the:
questions.explanation:
Transsphenoidal hypophysectomy is performed with incision between the upper lip and gum
It transverses through the sphenoid sinus

questions.question: What symptom is not associated with myasthenia gravis?
questions.explanation: Muscle weakness normally improves with rest for myasthenia gravis

questions.question: A secondary blast injury is caused by:

answers.A: Direct effect of blast overpressure on tissue
answers.C: People flying through the air and striking other objects

questions.explanation:
Primary blast phase injuries are caused by direct overpressure on tissue
Secondary blast phase injuries are caused by flying objects striking people
Tertiary blast phase injuries are caused by people being thrown into other objects including the
ground
Quaternary blast phase injuries encompass all other injuries including burns, crush injuries and
toxic inhalations

questions.question: Which of the following is the feared side effect of carbamazepine?
questions.explanation:
Agranulocytosis is a rare but feared side effect seen with carbamazepine therapy
Other side effects include thrombocytopenia and aplastic anemia
Gingival therapy is seen with phenytoin therapy
Weight loss is a side effect of topiramate therapy

questions.question: During a subfalcine herniation, what lobe of the brain is affected?
questions.explanation:
In patients with subfalcine herniation, the cingulated gyrus on the medial aspect of the frontal
lobe displaces across the midline under the falx

questions.question:
Which of the following fills in the blank in the sentence "ABR (auditory brain
response) exam is a ______________ test of auditory brainstem function in response to auditory
(click) stimuli"?
questions.explanation:
"ABR (auditory brain response) exam is a neurological test of auditory brainstem function in
response to auditory (click) stimuli." Retrieved from: emedicine.medscape.com
ABR is the evoked potential generated by a brief click or tone pip transmitted from an acoustic
transducer in the form of an insert earphone or headphone. Retrieved from:
emedicine.medscape.com

questions.question: The commonest type of diabetic neuropathy is:
questions.explanation:
It is estimated that 47% of patients with diabetes have some peripheral neuropathy
Distal symmetric polyneuropathy is the commonest type of diabetic neuropathy observed
Radiculopathies/plexopathies and cranial neuropathies are also fairly common as well

questions.question:
Which kind of assistance is most appropriate for a patient with C8 spinal cord
injury?
questions.explanation:
Patient with C8 spinal cord injury should have intact upper extremity function
A manual wheelchair is most appropriate
Electrical wheelchair is unnecessary in this case

questions.question: The Achilles reflex is innervated by?
questions.explanation: The Achilles reflex involves S1 and S2 spinal nerves

questions.question: Which of the following pain pills is least likely to cause dysphoria?
questions.explanation:
All narcotics can cause dysphoria irrespective of the dose
Acetaminophen is a non-narcotic and does not produce dysphoria even in large doses

questions.question:
A 9-month-old child has a chronic cough and sputum production. He was placed
on an antibiotic and 5 days later, the mother noticed that his head was bulging. Examination revealed
that he has bulging anterior fontanels. The child was most likely given
questions.explanation:
Tetracyclines can cause benign intracranial hypertension which will cause bulging fontanels in
infants.
In children and adults it results in pseudotumor cerebri.
Tetracyclines are generally not used on children under 8 years due to dyscoloration of tooth
enamel.
They can also discolor thyroid glands or rarely cause abnormal thyroid function.

questions.question:
Which of the following substances can improve wound healing, increase
collagen deposition and enhances immune function?
questions.explanation:
L arginine is an amino acid, which has multiple functions
Arginine can generate nitric oxide
L arginine can also increase collagen deposition and enhance wound healing
L arginine can also boost the immune system

questions.question:
All of the following statements about the glial cells of the CNS are correct
EXCEPT:

answers.A:
Microglia comprise 15-20% of total cells of CNS whose main function is phagocytosis by being
CNS macrophages
answers.B: Largest and most common macroglial cells are the astrocytes
answers.C: Oligodendroglia are macroglial cells that anchor neurons to their blood supply
answers.D:
Microglial and macroglial cells, neuroglia, regulate the internal environment especially fluid
surrounding neurons and synapses and provide physical support

questions.printed_answer_heading: Oligodendroglia are macroglial cells that anchor neurons to their blood supply
questions.explanation:
Oligodendroglia produce the myelin sheath that enables faster electrical signals. Microglia are
the scavenger cells of the CNS. They form from hematopoietic precursors.
They are smaller than astrocytes and oligodendroglia. Astrocytes have numerous projections
which anchor the neurons to their blood supply.
They are felt to be the predominant cell that forms the blood brain barrier (BBB) and regulate
the external chemical environment by removing ions and recycling neurotransmitters. The
protoplasmic astrocyte is in the gray matter and is highly branched with short thick processes.
The fibrous astrocyte is in the white matter and is lightly branched with long thin processes.
Neuroglia cells outnumber neurons approximately 10 to 1

questions.question:
A 24-year-old male is involved in a MVA and suffers multi-organ trauma. He is
brought to the ER by EMS and found to be hypotensive, tachycardic and his abdomen is not distended.
He is disoriented and confused. He has a GCS of 9; his legs are warm and the pulses thready. His
CVP is 7 and his BP is 80/40. The most likely cause of his shock state is due to?
questions.explanation:
When the peripheral circulation vasodilates, it causes the SVR to drop. The cardiac output in
neurogenic shock is often increased because the BP is low but the body loses its ability to
regulate flow to other organs
The cardiac output is usually normal but there is a low BP. The peripheries are warm and there
are pulses
Individuals with neurogenic shock may show mental status changes, oliguria and lactic acidosis
Treatment of neurogenic shock requires a combination of inotropes and vasopressors like
dopamine

questions.question:
Providers prescribe adrenal hormone replacement therapy after which
procedure?
questions.explanation:
Adrenal hormone replacement is necessary for bilateral adrenalectomy
Unilateral adrenalectomy with gradually reestablish normal hormone level

questions.question: A normal infant shows head control when sitting while supported at what age?
questions.explanation:
A normal child of 2 months shows head control
Between 4 and 5 months an infant can lift the chest off the floor

questions.question: What infant age is associated with head lifting?
questions.explanation:
A four month infant can perform head lift
A six month infant can perform rolling
A seven month infant can perform crawling
A nine month infant can sit erect

questions.question: Which of the following statement is accurate regarding medulloblastomas?

answers.A: Medulloblastomas are the third most common malignant tumor in childhood
answers.C: Most originate in the cerebellum or posterior fossa
answers.D: On rare occasions the fourth ventricle may occlude

questions.printed_answer_heading: Most originate in the cerebellum or posterior fossa
questions.explanation:
Medulloblastomas are the most common primary CNS malignancy of childhood
These are PNET (primitive neuroectodermal tumors) and are highly malignant arising from the
cerebellum and posterior fossa most commonly
Occlusion of the fourth ventricle is often with symptoms of headache, nausea, vomiting and gait
ataxia prominent in most children
A combination of resection, radiation and chemotherapy is used with a 5 year prognosis
averaging 80 percent with treatment

questions.question: Air embolism does not occur after which surgery:
questions.explanation:
Most cases of venous air embolism are unrecognized. Very few present with obvious cardiac
and neurological dysfunction
Air embolism can occur anytime during certain surgeries including cannulation of the large veins
in the neck, orthopedic surgery, heart surgery and nasal surgery
Symptoms of air embolism include acute dyspnea, gasp reflex, nausea, substernal chest pain,
arrhythmias, increased CVP, hypotension and mill-wheel murmur.
Other causes include cervical laminectomy procedures where the patients are prone and when
patients are placed in Fowler's position

questions.question:
A patient with intact brainstem function is lying supine and her head is elevated
30°. The right auditory meatus is irrigated with warm water. What would be expected?

answers.D: Bilateral tonic eye deviation toward the left

questions.explanation:
This technique is called caloric stimulation and drives the inner ear endolymphatic fluid down
or up depending on the temperature of the water
Warm caloric stimulation causes the brainstem to interpret that the head is moving toward this
side and the eyes deviate to the opposite side
This breaks fixation so there is reflex nystagmus toward this ear
The pneumonic is COWS: cold opposite, warm same

questions.question:
Which of the following drugs should not be routinely discontinued prior to
surgery?
questions.explanation:
Psychosis in the perioperative period can be difficult to control and the patient can remove all
lines and monitoring equipment
Thus, all antipsychotic should be continued during major surgery
Lithium should be discontinued 2-3 days prior to major surgery

questions.question:
After a recent infarction, the expected myocardial re-infarction rate for non-
cardiac surgery is?

answers.A: At 3 months, there is no comparable difference
answers.B: At 6 months, the rate of re-infarction is 4-6 percent
answers.C: Once an infarct has occurred, the risk of re-infarction is always close to 100%
answers.D: Most people have no risk for re-infarction if they take an aspirin

questions.printed_answer_heading: At 6 months, the rate of re-infarction is 4-6 percent
questions.explanation:
The mortality rate from a perioperative AMI is about 30-40 percent. The majority of acute MI
occur within 48 hours after surgery. Individual who do not have surgery also face a risk of about
10% of a repeat MI
The majority of people who develop an MI after non-cardiac surgery present with sustained
hypotension. For patients with a previous AMI who require non cardiac surgery, the re-
infarction rate correlates directly to the amount of time elapsed after the original MI
If operated on within 3 months of an AMI, the re-infarction rate is 8% -15%. This decreases to
3-6 percent if the time period after an AMI is 3 to 6 months
Beyond 6 months, the re-infarction rate resembles the general AMI re-infarction rate

questions.question:
A patient is recovering from mild flu-like symptoms when she notices a rubbery
feeling in her legs with difficulty walking. There is a deep aching pain in the leg muscles and altered
sensation when she touches her legs. The next morning she is having trouble swallowing and
breathing and rushed to the hospital where she in admitted to the ICU and intubated for respiratory
support. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Guillain-Barre syndrome is an acute disorder usually beginning with weakness in the feet and/or
hands which migrates to the trunk. For some patients, it than ascends to the bulbar area causing
respiratory difficulty and oropharyngeal dysphagia.
The loss of sensation, pain and temperature is mild. There is significant aching in the weakened
muscles. There can be profound loss of proprioception and areflexia
All forms of GBS are due to an immune response to foreign antigens that that is mistargeted at
host nerves.
Treatment is supportive plus plasmapheresis and IV immunoglobulins.

questions.question:
A patient underwent a traditional transsphenoidal hypophysectomy earlier in the
day. Which is the least appropriate advice?

answers.D: Avoid vigorous flossing in the area around the incision

questions.explanation:
A traditional transsphenoidal hypophysectomy involves an incision in the upper gum where it
joins the lip
Upper dentures should not be worn until the incision has healed

questions.question:
Which of the following sympathetic ganglia have to be resected for treatment of
reflex sympathetic dystrophy?
questions.explanation:
Both T4 and T5 have to be excised for relief of pain
For axillary hyperhidrosis T4-5 ganglia have to be excised
Splanchinectomy for intractable abdominal pain requires a left sided thoracoscopic approach
and involves ganglia T7-8

questions.question:
A 42 y/o female is admitted to the Neuro ICU with a grade III subarachnoid
hemorrhage. What would be an appropriate medicine to put her on to prevent vasospasm?
questions.explanation:
Nimodipine is a calcium channel blocker and quite effective in reducing the complication of
vasospasm
Clazosentan, an endothelin receptor antagonist, is an investigational drug for the treatment of
vasospasm

questions.question: Lumbar puncture is sometimes therapeutic for which diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Pseudotumor cerebri is an idiopathic disorder occurring primarily in obese females of child
bearing age resulting in elevated ICP.
Papilledema can develop sometime without treatment
LP will temporarily reduce elevated ICP by withdrawing CSF. Many patients require a
permanent lumbo-peritoneal shunt

questions.question:
Which of the following serum concentrations of phenobarbital is recommended
for adequate control of seizures?
questions.explanation:
Daily doses of phenobarbital produce serum levels of 15 to 35 mcg/ml
This is generally adequate to control seizures
Higher serum levels result in increased drowsiness, respiratory depression and coma

questions.question: Where is the lesion is associated with the Balint syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Balint syndrome is associated with lesion at the parietooccipital area
Characterized by agnosia, optic ataxia, and apraxia

questions.question:
A 2-month-old infant is observed to symmetrically abduct and then adduct his
extremities after suddenly losing support. This reflex is known as:
questions.explanation:
The Moro test is used to detect neurologic or clavicular injury after birth. The neonate is placed
in a reclined supine position.
The head is allowed to fall gently back into the hand.
The arms abduct and externally rotate. The thumbs also flex.
The arms then flex. This is a primitive reflex.

questions.question: The most common cause of death in tricyclic antidepressant(TCA) poisoning is:
questions.explanation:
TCA poisoning causes severe hypotension, arrhythmias, and coma
Hypotension occurs due to peripheral vasodilation from blockade of alpha 1 adrenergic
receptors
TCA overdose-related mortality is due largely to refractory hypotension
Ventricular fibrillation is also commonly seen in such cases

questions.question: Select the correct statement about conus medullaris development.

answers.A: The conus medullaris is at the level of the L1 vertebrae at week 18
answers.B: The conus medullaris at term is below the L2 vertebrae
answers.C:
The conus medullaris ascends due to the difference in the growth rate of the spinal cord and the
vertebral column
answers.D: The ascent of the conus medullaris occurs between weeks 10 and 30

questions.printed_answer_heading:
The conus medullaris ascends due to the difference in the growth rate of the spinal
cord and the vertebral column
questions.explanation:
The ascent of the conus medullaris occurs between weeks 13 and 40
The conus medullaris at term is above the L2 vertebrae
The conus medullaris is at the level of the L4 vertebrae or below at week 18

questions.question: Skull fractures commonly occur in:
questions.explanation:
Temporal bone fractures account for 79% of all skull base fractures. Skull fractures may be
longitudinal, transverse, or mixed
Basilar skull fracture is usually a linear fracture in the skull base and is often associated with a
dural tear
Occipital condylar fractures usually occur from high-energy blunt trauma or lateral bending
Clivus fractures occur from high impact motor vehicle accidents. These fractures carry the worst
prognosis and often affect cranial nerves 6 and 7

questions.question: The first neurologic feature of lidocaine toxicity is?
questions.explanation:
Lidocaine is a myocardial depressant
First sign of central toxicity is periorbital numbness

questions.question: Which segment of the anterior spinal artery is the smallest in diameter?
questions.explanation:
The anterior spinal artery has the smallest diameter in the midthoracic level and largest in the
cervical level.

questions.question:
When doing selective debridement of a wound that is necrotic, which of the
following should be removed?
questions.explanation:
Selective debridement should include eschar and slough
Granulation tissue or tissue that is red or pink indicate healing and should not be removed

questions.question: Which are signs of neurogenic shock?
questions.explanation: Bradycardia, hypotension, with flushed warm skin are signs of neurogenic shock

questions.question: Select the choice which is FALSE concerning a co-morbid condition:

answers.A: There can be only one admitting or existing diagnosis
answers.B: A medical condition existing stimutaneously with another condition
answers.C: A co-morbid condition is a predictor of at least one day of extended LOS
answers.D: A condition or diagosis documented at admission aside from the admitting diagnosis.

questions.printed_answer_heading: There can be only one admitting or existing diagnosis
questions.explanation:
Patients may present with multiple diagnosis and conditions.
A co-morbid is a predictor of at least one day of extended LOS.
Co-morbid conditions may include two or more disorders existing stimutaneouly.
A co-morbid condition or diagnosis documented at admission aside from the admitting
diagnosis.

questions.question: Radiculopathy is rarely associated with?
questions.explanation: Radiculopathy is usually not related to hypersthesia

questions.question:
What is the main difference between the blood brain barrier at the choroid
plexus?
questions.explanation:
The blood brain barrier is endothelial at most areas
At the choroid plexus it is primarily epithelial

questions.question: Fracture of which bone is more likely to cause rhinorrhea:
questions.explanation:
Nasoethmoid fractures are usually due to a blow on the central aspect of the face
Rhinorrhea is often a common complication of basilar skull fracture. If not diagnosed, it can lead
to bacterial infection of the CNS
For all midface trauma surrounding structures should be evaluated. This includes the nasofrontal
ostium, cervical spine, the lamina papyracae, surrounding facial bones, and the globes
CSF rhinorrhea is most commonly caused by fracture of the ethmoid bone.

questions.question:
An MRI scan with gadolinium-based contrast agents can pose a risk to which
organ?
questions.explanation:
Gadolinium contrast can cause nephrogenic fibrosing dermopathy/nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
(NFD/NSF) in patients with renal failure.
NFD/NSF results in fibrosis of the skin of the trunk and extremities with occasional involvement
of the myocardium, striated muscles, and lungs.
Histology shows spindle shaped cells with deposition of mucin and collagen in the dermis.
Flexion contractures lead to wheelchair dependence within weeks in many patients.

questions.question: What is the common side effect of phenytoin?
questions.explanation:
Gingival hyperplasia is a common side effect of phenytoin
Nystagmus and ataxia can also occur with phenytoin therapy but it is dose dependent and
relatively rare
Hepatotoxicity is also another rare side effect of phenytoin

questions.question: What part of the brain controls body temperature?
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus control thirst, body temperature, and sex drive

questions.question:
Which of the following is the most appropriate management of Guillain-Barre
syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Intravenous IG is the most commonly used medication in GBS
It hastens recovery and prevents further progression of demyelination
Intubation and mechanical ventilation may be needed

questions.question:
An 8 year old female is brought in with 3 weeks of double vision, unsteady gait,
weakness, and problems swallowing. MRI shows a non-enhancing, low intensity lesion at the pons.
Select appropriate management.
questions.explanation:
The patient most likely has a diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
This is usually high grade and has a very poor prognosis
Treatment is with radiotherapy at doses from 54-60 Gy
Efficacy in children has not been proven

questions.question: A patient on IV vancomycin may experience?
questions.explanation: Vancomycin toxicity includes hearing loss, renal toxicity, and allergic reaction

questions.question: Which of the following condition does not increase bleeding times?
questions.explanation:
Bleeding time is no longer used to detect qualitative platelet defects in von Willebrand disease
It is not felt to adequately reflect risk of bleeding at surgery.
Evaluation of patients who report a bleeding tendency should include activated partial
thromboplastin time, prothrombin time, factor VIII activity, ristocetin cofactor activity, and
concentration of vWF antigen
Thalassemia does not change bleeding times.

questions.question:
Your client has experienced head injuries. Intracranial pressure is elevated and
the heart rate is dropping. Mannitol 1.5 gm/kg of body weight is administered intravenously over 60
minutes as prescribed. You know this medication will:
questions.explanation:
Mannitol will reduce intracranial pressure. Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic that reduces
intracranial pressure by reducing circulating volume
Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic and does not affect heart rate. Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic,
and lowering blood pressure would be a side effect
Mannitol is not an antimicrobial medication

questions.question: In a patient with a brain abscess, the one study which should not be done is?
questions.explanation:
A lumbar puncture is rarely needed and is contraindicated in patients with elevated intracranial
pressure.
Moreover, in brain abscess, the results of LP is unrewarding.
CT scan should always be done to ensure that there is no focal neurological mass that may cause
herniation during an LP.

questions.question:
A patient receiving intravenous morphine is particularly closely monitored for
which one of the following:
questions.explanation:
Patients who receive IV morphine are usually monitored with regard to their respiratory status
utilizing pulse oximetry

questions.question: The chief source of energy for the brain is from:
questions.explanation: Glucose is the main source of energy for brain and RBC

questions.question: Which of the following is not a symptom of acute anticholinergic overdose?
questions.explanation:
Flushing, dry skin, mydriasis with loss of accommodation, confusion, and fever are seen with
overdose of anticholinergics.
Sinus tachycardia, not bradycardia, is another sign.
Physostigmine can antagonize CNS side effects in anticholinergic poisoning.

questions.question: What is the most common etiology of chorea in children?
questions.explanation:
Sydenham chorea is the most common cause of chorea in children
Characterized by dysarthria, mood disorder, and hypotonia

questions.question:
64 year old brought to ER after complaining that he could not move his legs.
Denies any trauma, loss of consciousness, visual or speech problems. On examination, there is
significant motor weakness, numbness from the buttocks to the soles of the feet, no sensation in the
perineal area, absent rectal tone and full, distended bladder. What is the best test for this patient?
questions.explanation:
Classic cauda equina syndrome with leg weakness, bladder/bowel failure and hypesthesias from
buttocks to feet
MRI will give best view of cauda equina and lower spinal cord and quickly determine if a
compressive lesion is present requiring surgical intervention

questions.question:
All of the following statements about treating Huntington chorea are correct
EXCEPT:

answers.A: Treat hypokinesia and rigidity with Adderall
answers.B: Treat depression with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) antidepressants
answers.C: Treat psychosis and behavioral problems with atypical antipsychotics

questions.printed_answer_heading: Treat hypokinesia and rigidity with Adderall
questions.explanation:
For hypokinesia and rigidity use antiparkinson drugs.
Tetrabenazine is a VMAT inhibitor. VMAT transports monoamines, dopamine, norepinephrine
and serotonin, to the synaptic vesicles
Chorea can also be treated with benzodiazepines and neuroleptics/antipsychotics
The major concern is balancing the positive results vs. the undesirable side effects

questions.question: Essential tremor can be treated with which choice?
questions.explanation:
Treatment is not always needed and is based on severity of symptoms
Surgical treatment is reserved for refractory disabling upper extremity tremor
Stereotactic thalamotomy and thalamic ventralis intermedius nucleus deep stimulation are used

questions.question:
A 65 y/o male is brought to the ER. His neurological exam reveals coma,
pinpoint pupils, minimum withdrawal of extremities to painful stimuli, and hyperactive reflexes with
clonus. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.A: Rostral midbrain lesion from multiple sclerosis

questions.explanation:
Pontine lesions classically can cause pinpoint pupils with coma and tetraparesis with brisk
reflexes
The pinpoint pupils occur because the traversing sympathetic fibers are disrupted
Only the pons hemorrhage would have brisk reflexes with clonus and weakness of all 4
extremities
The rostral midbrain MS lesion should not result in miotic pupils but mid-size pupils

questions.question: Which spinal nerve is involved with the wrist extension?
questions.explanation:
Elbow flexion involves C5 and C6
Wrist extension involves C6, C7, and C8
Finger abduction involves C8 and T1
Flexion of the hip involves L2, L3, and L4

questions.question: The first sign of increased intracranial pressure?
questions.explanation:
Loss of consciousness is the last presenting sign of a high ICP.
Visual defect is the earliest and the most sensitive sign.

questions.question:
Which of the following is true about acute disseminated encephalomyelitis
(ADEM)?

answers.B: May mimic history and physical findings of multiple sclerosis
answers.C: Is rare in children <10 years of age

questions.printed_answer_heading: May mimic history and physical findings of multiple sclerosis
questions.explanation:
Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis is a demyelinating disease of the central nervous system
that usually presents with multifocal neurologic symptoms and encephalopathy.
It is usually preceded by a viral or bacterial infection, most often as an upper respiratory
infection.
Less than 5 percent of cases follow immunization.
The disease is commonly seen in children < 5 years of age.

questions.question:
A female without past medical history now presenting with new onset seizure,
fevers, headaches, personality change and hemorrhagic necrosis of the temporal lobes on CT should
be treated with:
questions.explanation:
This patient has symptoms of herpes simplex encephalitis which primarily affects the temporal
lobes
Lyme disease in its tertiary stage can cause an encephalopathy which is treated with ceftriaxone
or penicillin

questions.question:
Which artery supplies the inferior aspect of the anterior limb of the internal
capsule?
questions.explanation:
The recurrent artery of Heubner, a branch of the ACA, supplies the inferior aspect of the anterior
limb of the internal capsule, head of the caudate, and anterior lentiform nucleus.
The anterior limb of the internal capsule contains frontopontine and thalamocortical fibers.
Occlusion of the recurrent artery of Heubner results in contralateral weakness and sensory loss
in the face and arm, dysarthria, and gaze deviation.

questions.question:
Which of the following is not seen in patients with idiopathic intracranial
hypertension (IIH)?
questions.explanation:
IIH will show elevated opening pressure for most patients but CSF should show normal glucose,
cells, and protein
Eye findings can include palsy of CN VI, visual field defect, enlarged blind spot, and
papilledema
Neuroimaging should be done before making the diagnosis if IIH and performing lumbar
puncture
Rarely the neurologic and eye exam is normal so the diagnosis is made when the opening
pressure is high

questions.question: A patients with frontal lobe tumors will often show what type of gait problem?
questions.explanation:
Bruns ataxia or magnetic ataxia is seen in patients with frontal lobe disorders
It is characterized by inability to initiate process of walking, despite having normal power and
coordination of legs
The gait is broad based with short steps
It can be been in patients with stroke

questions.question: What percent of zonisamide is metabolized by the liver?
questions.explanation:
About 70 percent of zonisamide is metabolized by the liver
About 30 percent of topiramate is metabolized by the liver

questions.question:
What is assessed by asking a patient to analyze a proverb such as "People in
glass houses shouldn't throw stones"?
questions.explanation:
Evaluating a proverb would involve abstraction
The ability to understand one's illness is self-awareness
Asking a patient what one would do upon noticing a fire in the movie house would check
judgment and having the examinee count down from 100 by 7s is observing computational ability

questions.question:
Which of the following brain tumors is common in patients with
neurofibromatosis?
questions.explanation:
Astrocytomas occurring in the optic pathway are the most common CNS tumors seen in patients
with neurofibromatosis
Medulloblastomas are common brain tumors in children

questions.question: Vital centers are located in:
questions.explanation:
The lower medulla contains all the vital centers
Uncial herniation is dangerous because it directly impinges upon the lower medulla
The midbrain and pons are locations where most cranial nerves originate
The cerebellum is responsible for balancing motor coordination

questions.question:
Which of the following is least likely to be seen with overdose of baclofen by
intrathecal pump?
questions.explanation:
Baclofen overdose by intrathecal pump can cause confusion, seizures, hallucinations, psychotic
behavior, and respiratory depression
Hypotension is much more likely than hypertension

questions.question:
Which is the osmotic diuretic that is most commonly given to reduce elevated
intracranial pressure?
questions.explanation:
Mannitol is frequently prescribed as the diuretic to control intracranial hypertension and is given
IV push
It can be given as an IV drip

questions.question: What is the performance of an unlawful act?
questions.explanation:
Malfeasance is the commission of an unlawful act
Negligence is reckless disregard for another person's well being
Malpractice is the negligence of a professional individual
Assault is the act of inflicting bodily injury on another person

questions.question: The chief cause of death after morphine overdose is:
questions.explanation: Respiratory depression is the most common cause of death in acute opioid overdose.

questions.question:
A 36 year old right handed male has early morning headaches and papilledema.
MRI with contrast shows a tumor at the left frontal-temporal-parietal region. Which of the following
symptoms is most likely?
questions.explanation:
The left frontal-temporal-parietal region is responsible for language
Hemiparesis and neglect would be more likely in patients with right brain lesions
A right occipital lesion would result in left homonymous hemianopia

questions.question:
On a contrast enhanced T1 weighted MRI you identify a region of enhancement
in the left transverse sinus, which also contains multiple flow voids, what is the most likely etiology?

answers.D: Epidural hematoma due to dural venous tear

questions.explanation:
Chronic dAVF typically thrombose and contain a network of vessels which can be seen as flow
voids on MR
Adult dAVFs are more commonly acquired than congenital.
The Borden classification divides dAVFs into three types based on their venous drainage.

questions.question:
A 24-year-old male is involved in a MVA and suffers multi organ trauma. He is
brought to the ER by EMS and found to be hypotensive, tachycardic and his abdomen is flat. He is
disoriented and confused. He has a GCS of 9 and his legs are warm and the pulses thready. There is
minimum movement of the legs to painful stimuli. The most likely cause of his shock state is due to?
questions.explanation:
When the peripheral circulation vasodilates it causes the SVR to drop. The cardiac output in
neurogenic shock is often increased because the BP is low. In neurogenic shock, the body loses
its ability to regulate flow to other organs
The cardiac output is usually normal but there is a low BP. The peripheries are warm and the
pulses are palpable
Individuals may show mental status changes, oliguria and lactic acidosis
Treatment of neurogenic shock is a combination of inotropes and vasopressors like dopamine

questions.question:
An intrathecal delivery system is a viable alternative if a patient has a life
expectancy of:
questions.explanation:
Age is not a determination factor for intrathecal delivery system
Life expectancy must be longer than three months for interdigital delivery system to be
considered

questions.question:
Which one of the following medications is indicated in patients who are
diagnosed with subarachnoid hemorrhage?
questions.explanation:
Subarachnoid hemorrhage is bleeding in to subarachnoid space
The commonest cause is rupture of berry aneurysm
Nimodipine, a calcium channel blocker, is indicated to prevent vasospasm
Aspirin, heparin, and anistreplase are contraindicated

questions.question:
A 13-year-old male presents with a nose bleed. On examination, he is found to
have numerous telangiectasias on the oral mucosa, skin and conjunctiva. He many have:
questions.explanation:
Osler Weber Rendu is an autosomal dominant disorder that presents with telangiectasias,
recurrent epistaxis and a positive family history
Cerebral abscesses commonly occur due to impaired pulmonary vessels.
High output cardiac failure is largely due to large arterio-venous malformations
Majority of individuals present with severe epistaxis and many require blood transfusions

questions.question: Which of the following is not an aspect of wellness?
questions.explanation:
Aspects of wellness include psychological wellness, physical wellness, social wellness,
spiritual wellness, and economic wellness.

questions.question:
In a patient with elevated intracranial pressure, beyond what level of
hyperventilation is not considered safe to reduce the pressure?
questions.explanation:
The current guidelines indicate that hyperventilation should be used with caution to lower
intracranial pressure
Lowering of PCO2 leads to vasoconstriction
However, too much vasoconstriction can worsen a patient with an ischemic stroke
PC02 levels should be in between 32-36 mmHg

questions.question: A surgeon normally performs vertebroplasty to treat:
questions.explanation: Vertebroplasty is commonly performed for vertebral body fracture..

questions.question: All of the following statements about electromyography are correct EXCEPT:

answers.A:
EMG measures electrical activity generated by muscles when electrically or neurologically
activated.
answers.B:
EMG insertional stimulation results in the activation of many motor units, in which a motor unit
refers to one motor nerve and all related muscle fibers, producing a contribution of many action
potentials of varying amplitudes and rates (recruitment and interference pattern)
answers.C:
Neuromuscular junction disease will have easy fatigability with repetitive stimulation and single
fiber EMG, SFEMG, is very sensitive
answers.D:
Neuropathic causes with EMG will have decreased duration of action potential and decreased
amplitude of action potential

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Neuropathic causes with EMG will have decreased duration of action potential and
decreased amplitude of action potential
questions.explanation:
Nerve conduction velocity (NCV) is usually performed with EMG. This testing provides
valuable information in conjunction with neurological examination and other pertinent testing
towards making a diagnosis
EMG is useful in evaluating lower motor neuron disease that includes nerve root and peripheral
nerve, neuromuscular junction, and muscle disease
EMG suggests a neuropathic condition when duration and amplitude of action potential are
increased
EMG suggests a myopathic condition when duration of action potential is decreased, reduction
of area to amplitude ratio of action potential, and decrease in number of motor units

questions.question: Stevens-Johnson syndrome is a serious condition associated with:
questions.explanation:
Stevens-Johnson syndrome is potentially life-threatening and may present with the same target
lesions of erythema multiforme

questions.question:
The most likely causative agent of a pyogenic infection along a suture line after
surgery, which the laboratory reports preliminarily as a beta-hemolytic, catalase-positive, coagulase-
positive, gram-positive coccus is:
questions.explanation:
Of the choices, only streptococci and staphylococci are Gram-positive
The streptococci are catalase negative and staphylococci are catalase positive
Staphylococcus aureus is beta-hemolytic and coagulase-positive

questions.question: Opsoclonus in an infant is most likely seen in a case of?
questions.explanation:
Opsoclonus is a rapid, involuntary, multi-vectorial, and unpredictable conjugate fast eye
movement that stops during sleep
In the infant, neuroblastoma is the most common cause of opsoclonus as a paraneoplastic
phenomenon
Autoimmune brain stem encephalitis responsive to ACTH is also seen in infants
In adults, opsoclonus may occur as a paraneoplastic syndrome caused by lung, ovarian, or breast
cancer

questions.question: Select the true statement about animal testing.

answers.A: All drugs require long term testing
answers.B: Teratogenesis testing is done by the Ames test
answers.C: All drugs must be tested for acute toxicity
answers.D: Anticancer and HIV drugs require more safety evidence for approval

questions.printed_answer_heading: All drugs must be tested for acute toxicity
questions.explanation:
Two species lethal dose studies must be done on all drugs
Long term testing for chronic toxicity is required for most but not all drugs
The Ames test is for mutagenesis
HIV and anticancer drugs require less evidence of safety before approval due to the urgency of
need

questions.question:
A 76 year old female with chronic hypertension dies in a nursing home. The
family requests and autopsy and the cause of death is hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage. What is
the most likely location of the hemorrhage?
questions.explanation:
Hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhages occur in the thalamus or basal ganglia in 65% of cases
There is weakening of the arteriole walls which result in Charcot-Bouchard aneurysms
These can rupture causing fatal intracerbral hemorrhages
15% of hypertensive hemorrhages occur in the pons and 8% in the cerebellum

questions.question:
When a patient in the hospital falls because of spilt coffee, the nurse is
considered to be?
questions.explanation:
The fall of a patient is due to negligence of the nurse
This nurse is liable for malpractice

questions.question: Which of the following is not passed by autosomal dominant inheritance?
questions.explanation:
All of the choices show autosomal dominant inheritance except ataxia telangiectasia that shows
autosomal recessive inheritance
In ataxia telangiectasia there is a defect in a protein that stops the cell cycle in response to cell
damage
This leads to chromosomal instability and increased sensitivity to radiation

questions.question: What is a critical path?

answers.A: A planned exit route for a home
answers.B: A physical finding that the patient is becoming unstable
answers.C: An established plan of treatment for a specific diagnosis
answers.D: A document in the medical record

questions.printed_answer_heading: An established plan of treatment for a specific diagnosis
questions.explanation:
A critical path or pathway is a set of guidelines for treatment of a specific diagnosis
An example would be the goals for a patient with a knee replacement to be reached in a certain
number of days
These pathways improve care as they set standards and reduce need for documentation

questions.question: The cause of postdural puncture headache is?
questions.explanation: Postdural puncture headache is result of CSF loss at puncture site

questions.question: Consultation means:

answers.A: Individual identifies a problem and calls on a consultant for recommendations
answers.B: An ongoing supportive and educational relationship
answers.D: The individual must follow all the consultant's recommendations

questions.printed_answer_heading: Individual identifies a problem and calls on a consultant for recommendations
questions.explanation:
The consultant provides expert advice and recommendations that the individual may accept or
reject.

questions.question: Miller-Fisher syndrome is characterized by all of the following findings except:
questions.explanation:
Miller-Fischer syndrome is one form of Guillain-Barre syndrome with ophthalmoplegia, facial/
bulbar weakness, ataxia, and areflexia
Hyperreflexia is not present

questions.question:
Which of the following is produced by macrophages during nerve regeneration,
stimulating Schwann cells to produce nerve growth factor?
questions.explanation:
Macrophages produce the cytokine, IL-1 that stimulates nerve growth factor production by
Schwann cells
IL-2 is a leukocytotropic hormone that is instrumental in the body's natural response to microbial
infection
IL-3 stimulates the differentiation of multipotent hematopoietic stem cells into myeloid
progenitor cells
IL-4 causes the stimulation of activated B-cell and T-cell proliferation, and the differentiation of
CD4+ T-cells into Th2 cells

questions.question:
Which of the following effects of atropine is helpful for patients before
anesthesia?
questions.explanation:
Atropine is an anticholinergic drug given prior to anesthesia to reduce secretion and minimize
aspiration risk.
Adverse effects include tachycardia, urinary retention, and hypotension
It is contraindicated in patients with glaucoma and should be used with caution in patients with
BPH, cardiovascular disease, autonomic neuropathy, and hyperthyroidism.

questions.question:
A 55-year-old female on heparin following a massive traumatic blood clot in the
iliac vein requires protamine prior to her surgery. The side effects of protamine include all of the
following except:
questions.explanation:
Protamine is a drug that is often used to reverse the anticoagulant effects of heparin
Protamine used to be produced from sperm of shark but is now made by recombinant technology
Side effects of protamine include hypotension, bronchoconstriction and pulmonary hypertension
Protamine should be given in a peripheral IV. If it is administered in a central line, the drug will
enter the pulmonary circulation immediately and induce severe pulmonary hypertension

questions.question: How many cervical spinal nerves are there in a human body?
questions.explanation:
There are seven cervical vertebrae
There are eight cervical spinal nerves
There are twelve thoracic vertebrae
There are five lumbar vertebrae

questions.question: Which of the following is false regarding saccular aneurysms?

questions.explanation:
Saccular aneurysms most commonly affect the bifurcations of the circle of Willis.
Most common cause of non-traumatic SAH.
Associated with FMD, bicuspid aortic valves, autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease,
