questions.question:
A patient is brought to the emergency room with left sided weakness and facial
droop. He has an expressive aphasia and decreased sensation on the right side. He most likely has an
occlusion of which vessel?
questions.explanation:
Contralateral motor weakness and sensory deficit is characteristic of a middle cerebral artery
infarct.
Pure motor or sensory deficits are seen with a lacunar infarct,
Receptive or expressive aphasia is seen when the dominant hemisphere is involved.

questions.question:
Which of the following is true of the priorities of patient rights in financial
matters?

answers.A: The patient's needs and safe disposition is always first.
answers.B: The responsible use of resources is second in priority.
answers.C: The financial health of the system is the third priority.

questions.explanation:
The patient's needs and safe disposition is always first.
The responsible use of resources is second in priority.
The financial health of the system is the third priority.

questions.question: Which is NEVER appropriate for documentation?
questions.explanation:
Direct quotes from communications with patients, families, caregivers and those involved in the
case plan are always valuable and appropriate documentation.
Data is a clean and effective entry into the patient record.
Opinions and judgments are never appropriate entries.
Notifications are needed and necessary entries for effective documentation.

questions.question: The drug to decrease cerebral oxygen demand is?
questions.explanation: Barbiturates are the best agents to lower cerebral oxygen demand

questions.question: The gluteus maximus is innervated by which of the following nerves?
questions.explanation:
The inferior gluteal nerve arises from nerve roots L5-S2 and passes through the grater sciatic
foramen

questions.question: Which of the following is an inhibitory neurotransmitter?
questions.explanation:
GABA, ?-aminobutyric acid, is the chief inhibitory neurotransmitter central nervous system.

GABA-A receptors are ligand-activated chloride channels.

questions.question: What type of armrest would make sliding board transfers easiest?
questions.explanation: Detachable or swing away armrests would make sliding board transfers easier

questions.question: Which is not a feature common to all megaloblastic anemias?

questions.question:
The initial test of choice in a patient with suspected subarachnoid hemorrhage
is?
questions.explanation: The initial study of choice is an urgent CT scan without contrast.

questions.question: The reason why epinephrine is added to local anesthetics:
questions.explanation:
Vasoconstrictors can prolong the duration of anesthesia by preventing the anesthetic from
dispersing
Adrenaline can potentiate the effects of short acting anesthetics like procaine and lidocaine

Adrenaline should not be used on ear, nose, penis or any anywhere there is cartilage

questions.question: How many thoracic vertebrae are there in a human body?
questions.explanation:
There are seven cervical vertebras with eight cervical spinal nerves
There are twelve thoracic vertebra and five lumbar vertebra though a small percentage of people
have a extra lumbar 6 vertebra

questions.question: Hypothermia does not affect which cerebral parameter?
questions.explanation:
In hypothermia state, there is reduced glucose and oxygen demand
Cerebral blood flow also drops

questions.question:
Which of the following is not a late finding of the Cushing response which

questions.explanation:
The Cushing response indicates increasing ICP and towards its latter stages includes
hypertension, bradycardia and bradyapnea.

questions.question: Meperidine is?
questions.explanation: Meperidine is a weak acid

questions.question:
Emergency decompression of the brain with a subdural hematoma should be
evacuated if there is a midline shift of:
questions.explanation:
Surgery for decompression of subdural hematoma is done if there is a midline shift of more than
5 mm or greater
Surgery is also indicated if there is an acute subdural hematoma that exceeds 10 mm in thickness
Sometimes if the midline shift is 5 mm and there are no neurological deficits like dilated pupils

Surgery is recommended when a subdural hematoma is associated with compressed basilar

questions.question:
Needle stick exposures to hepatitis C result in transmission in what percentage

questions.explanation: Needle stick exposures to hepatitis C in health care providers cause a 3% rate of transmission.

questions.question: In an uncal herniation, what part of the brain is commonly affected?
questions.explanation:
Uncal herniation is a subtype of transtentorial herniation
In uncal herniation, the innermost segment of the temporal lobe squeezes through the tentorium
and compresses the brainstem
The uncus can cause dilatation of the eye by putting pressure on the 3rd cranial nerve. The eye
usually appears down and out due to loss of all muscles except cranial nerve 6
Compression of the posterior cerebral artery will cause ischemia of the ipsilateral primary

questions.question: Which is true of aspiration pneumonia?
questions.explanation:
Aspiration pneumonia presents an acute lung injury from inhalation of gastric contents. The
disorder may occur in individual with seizure, loss of consciousness, stroke, drug intoxication

Aspiration of large amounts of gastric contents is also known as Mendelssohn syndrome and can
result in severe respiratory compromise
Aspiration pneumonia are predominantly caused by anaerobic organisms. Hospitalized patients

The right middle and lower lung lobes are most common sites of infiltrates due to the more

questions.question:
A 22-year-old male has marked personality changes over a 10-day period. He
becomes verbally and physically abusive of his family. He is taken to a psychiatrist but becomes has

questions.explanation:
The most common cause of sporadic encephalitis in the U.S. is herpes simplex type 1
Initial symptoms are likely to be psychiatric in immunocompetent individuals
Temporal lobe involvement is usually evident on CT or MRI and EEG is often abnormal
PCR for the virus should be done but treatment with acyclovir should not wait for confirmation

questions.question:

questions.question: Which of the following is false regarding the lumbar sympathetic chain?

Lumbar sympathetic chain located anterior-lateral to the lumbar vertebra bilaterally and

questions.question: What is the first line treatment for postoperative delirium?

questions.question:
The incidence of heparin induced thrombocytopenia for unfractionated heparin is

questions.question: Which of the following is least likely to decrease serum cholesterol levels?
questions.explanation:

Cigarette smoking can lead to increased total serum cholesterol, increased serum LDL-

questions.question:

In the METTAG system, a black tag indicates a patient is deceased

questions.question: How many lumbar vertebrae are there in a human body?
questions.explanation:
There are seven cervical vertebrae

There are twelve thoracic vertebrae

questions.question:
A doctor is starting medication on a patient to treat extrapyramidal symptoms.

questions.explanation:

Besides amantadine, the anticholinergic drugs trihexyphenidyl and benztropine are commonly

Akathisia responds to beta-blockers and benzodiazepines

questions.question:
In a patient with sudden onset of fluctuating hearing loss, the ideal study of

An MRI is recommended in any individual who develop sudden or fluctuating hearing loss to

questions.question: Which metastatic brain malignancy is associated with the worst prognosis?
questions.explanation:
The combination of hemorrhagic transformation of metastases and inherent mortality of the

Glioblastoma multiforme carries a poor prognosis as well but is not metastatic
All metastatic malignancies listed average mortalities in less than a year
Choriocarcinomas and glioblastoma multiforme are also associated with significant cerebral
hemorrhages

questions.question:
Which of the following factors is not a major consideration in the use of

Age related changes in body temperature; subcutaneous fat, and skin fragility must be considered

questions.question:
What statement is false concerning Moya-Moya (idiopathic progressive
arteriopathy of childhood)?

Lateral projection, conventional angiography, demonstrates lenticulostriate and thalamoperforate

answers.D:

Moya-Moya means "hazy puff of smoke" in Japanese. This is the appearance on lateral

involving bilateral stenosis or occlusion of the terminal ICAs and/or the proximal ACAs and

questions.question: From where are Schwann cells derived?
questions.explanation:
Schwann cells supply myelin to the peripheral nervous system
They derive from neural crest cells and the primary glial cells of the PNS
Ganglion satellite cells, melanocytes, part of the cranial mesenchyme, and most of the peripheral
nervous system neurons are also derived from neural crest cells

questions.question: Which is best agent of choice for opiate overdose?
questions.explanation:
Naloxone is used to treat overdose of opiates
It is usually given intravenously but can be given via ET tube
Flumazenil is a benzodiazepine antagonist
Protamine is used to reverse heparin

questions.question:
A patient complains of low back pain with pain down the left leg. His symptoms
are worse with walking or standing and better with sitting or leaning forward. Select the most likely
diagnosis.
questions.explanation:
Spinal stenosis symptoms are improved with flexion as extension encroaches on the spinal
foramen

questions.question: Which is not a side effect of prolonged use of corticosteroids?
questions.explanation: Neuropathy is not a side effect of corticosteroids

questions.question: All of the following are tests for cervical spondylosis except:
questions.explanation:
C5 and C6 nerve roots are most commonly affected
Courvoisier sign is a palpable gall bladder without stones

questions.question:
A patient undergoes a major pelvic cancer operation and on postoperative day 5
develops unilateral leg swelling, tenderness and has a positive Homan's sign. The most likely

questions.explanation:
This patient has a DVT
Moses sign is calf pain when pressing on the muscle and may be indicative of a DVT
Homan's sign is calf pain in the with dorsiflexion of the foot but may lead to embolization

questions.question: The most common tuberculosis presentation intracranially is:
questions.explanation:

Imaging features are identical to pyogenic meningitis except for distribution
TB meningitis favors the basal cisterns and is associated with dystrophic calcifications along the

questions.question:
Which of the following factors is MOST helpful in distinguishing between
delirium and dementia?
questions.explanation:
Delirium and dementia have many features in common.
A helpful distinguishing feature is the duration of onset.
Abrupt onset is consistent with delirium, whereas insidious onset occurs with dementia.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a primary improvement that is often seen when using
clinical pathways?

answers.B: Routine clinical practices may be found to be unnecessary
answers.C: Routine clinical care is guaranteed to be effective
answers.D: Routine clinical care is given broad and unrestricted guidelines

questions.printed_answer_heading: Routine clinical practices may be found to be unnecessary

Clinical pathways question and research the benefit of routine clinical practices.

pathways.

questions.question: The tail of the caudate nucleus forms which of the following?

answers.A: Roof of inferior horn of lateral ventricles

questions.printed_answer_heading: Roof of inferior horn of lateral ventricles
questions.explanation:
The caudate nucleus is within the basal ganglia and is important for memory
The caudate nucleus is C shaped
The head and body from the floor of the anterior horn of lateral ventricle
The tail forms the roof of the inferior horn of the lateral ventricles

questions.question: Desensitization process is usually involve with area of:
questions.explanation: Desensitization process is usually involve with area of hypersensitivity

questions.question: Which of the following conditions is an indication for SBE prophylaxis?
questions.explanation:
Indications for SBE prophylaxis include the following: Previous episode of endocarditis,
Prosthetic cardiac valves, Congenital cardiac defects (except for those specified), Hypertrophic
cardiomyopathy, Previous valvular surgery and Rheumatic valvular dysfunction.
Indications for SBE include surgically constructed systemic pulmonic shunts or conduits, Dental
or surgical indications for SBE prophylaxis include dental or surgical procedures likely to cause
mucosal bleeding, tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy, surgery involving the respiratory or
gastrointestinal mucosa and rigid bronchoscopy
SBE prophylaxis is not necessary for ventricular septal defects, patent ductus arteriosus, and
isolated secundum atrial septal defects if they have been repaired for at least 6 months without
complications, physiologic murmurs, previous rheumatic fever without valve dysfunction,
history of coronary artery bypass surgery, coronary stent placement, transesophageal
echocardiogram, previous pacemaker or defibrillator placement, or history of Kawasaki disease
without valve dysfunction
Also, SBE prophylaxis is not necessary for dental procedures not likely to cause gingival
bleeding (fillings above the gum line, adjustment of orthodontic equipment, etc.), injection of
intraoral anesthetics, shedding of primary teeth, tympanostomy tube placement, skin biopsy,
cesarean section, endotracheal intubation, flexible bronchoscopy with or without biopsy, cardiac
catheterization, endoscopy with or without biopsy, routine urinary catheterization (no infection
present), dilation and curettage, uncomplicated vaginal delivery, abortion, insertion and removal
of intrauterine devices, sterilization procedures, or laparoscopy

questions.question: Postoperative DVT prevention is best accomplished by which answer?
questions.explanation:
Low molecular weight heparin has been shown to be effective in DVT prevention
Warfarin has more side effects and has a higher risk of intracranial bleeding
SCDs and aspirin are not sufficient for DVT prevention

questions.question:
A 4 month old infant is noted to have an abnormal shaped head. Select the most
likely diagnosis.

questions.question:
Which of the following does not possess any antagonist activity at the opioid
receptor?
questions.explanation:
Codeine is an alkaloid of opium.
Codeine is an effective cough suppressant and is also addictive
It is a pure agonist and does not possess any antagonistic properties

questions.question: A tumor in the quadrangular space is most likely to cause:
questions.explanation:
The quadrangular space is the axillary space in the arm

questions.question:
An 18-year-old college student living in a dormitory develops a fever and
headache. He takes acetaminophen but develops photophobia and neck pain though the day. That night
his roommate brings him to the student health center with increasing lethargy and disorientation. He

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Todd paralysis is correct?

questions.explanation:

It involves focal weakness of the extremities which can range from mild to severe

questions.question:
A trauma patient with a wide, fixed pupil and contralateral hemiplegia. This is
most likely due to:

the tentorium at the incisura

questions.question: Which of the following IV fluids is to be given with blood products?

solutions may cause hemolysis.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a feature of a sympathetic response?

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about vertebrobasilar insufficiency (VBI) is
not correct?

answers.D: Vertigo is the most common symptom
