questions.explanation:
25% of TIAs and strokes occur in the posterior circulation. Other symptoms may include gait
disturbances, diplopia, visual loss, dysesthesias, headaches, nausea, vomiting, and poor
coordination
The posterior circulation supplies the pons, midbrain, medulla, occipital lobe, cerebellum, and
part of the thalamus
Consequently, there is a wide variety of symptoms depending on which structures are affected
and the extent of the ischemia
VBI is caused by narrowing of the arteries and progressive hypoperfusion or inadequate blood
supply. Smaller arteries are prone to closing off from thrombotic changes

questions.question: Medicaid is:

answers.A: A federal program covering anyone making < $25,000 annually
answers.B: A federal program that covers charges above what private insurance will pay
answers.D: A healthcare program for the indigent funded jointly by federal as well as state governments

questions.printed_answer_heading:
A healthcare program for the indigent funded jointly by federal as well as state
governments
questions.explanation:
Medicaid is a healthcare program for the indigent funded jointly by federal as well as state
governments.

questions.question: Select the condition most commonly seen with secondary cough headache.
questions.explanation:
The majority of cough headaches are primary and not associated with underlying vascular or
anatomic abnormalities
Rarely, it can be associated with descent of the cerebellar tonsils descending below the foramen
magnum resulting in obstruction
Tonsillar descent more than 5 mm below the foramen magnum is defined as the Chiari type 1
malformation, most commonly found incidentally on MRI
Cough headache is characterized by sharp, splitting, or stabbing pain, are bilateral or occipital,
and occur after coughing, sneezing or straining

questions.question:
Which of the following may have an antiplatelet activity and should be stopped
before surgery?
questions.explanation:
Ginseng is believed by some to decrease the results of stress on the body. It does inhibit
platelets and should be held for 7 or more days before surgery.
Another herbal supplement that may interfere with platelets is ginkgo biloba
These effects demonstrate the importance of asking patients about vitamins and herbal
supplements

questions.question: Glioblastoma multiforme are often seen in patients in what age group?
questions.explanation:
Glioblastoma multiforme can occur at any age but are most common in the middle ages between
45-65
Less than 8% of these tumors occur in children

questions.question: Cranial nerve VI is also known as:
questions.explanation:
CN V is known as trigeminal nerve
CN VI is known as abducens nerve
CN VII is known as facial nerve
CN VIII is known as vestibulocochlear nerve

questions.question: Substance with absence of threshold include all of the following except:
questions.explanation:
A threshold effect exists when there is an exposure below which a toxic effect will not occur
A nonthreshold effect exists when there is no safe exposure below which no effect exists
Absence of threshold can mean a substance is mutagenic, carcinogenic, and/or teratogenic
Comedogenic refers to a substance's ability to promote acne

questions.question:
Which of the choices is not one of the reasons to perform a spinal tap in the
lower lumbar region?

answers.A: The dura and pia mater end at L1
answers.B: The spinal cord ends at L1-L2
answers.C: There is no overlap of the spinous processes
answers.D: When the lumbar region is flexed, the interspinous spaces widen

questions.printed_answer_heading: The dura and pia mater end at L1
questions.explanation:
The pia mater ends at L2 with the spinal cord
The lumbar spine has a wide interlaminar space

questions.question:
What type of radiculopathy would a patient likely experience with a left
paracentral disc herniation at L5-S1?
questions.explanation:
Below T1 nerve roots exit below their respective vertebral bodies. Thus, a left lateral or
paracentral herniation would affect the left S1 nerve root.
Compression of the S1 nerve root typically results in ipsilateral numbness and/or pain of the
lateral foot and a weak ankle jerk reflex.
Herniation with a free fragment can affect multiple levels, most typically at the level of
herniation and one nerve root below.

questions.question: Aspirin does not exhibit which of the following effects?
questions.explanation:
Aspirin inhibits the enzyme cyclooxygenase (COX), which leads to antipyretic and antiplatelet
effects

questions.question: Which drug is not commonly used to treat neuropathic pain?
questions.explanation:
Neuropathic pain is normally described as short, shooting, burning, and localized
Pharmaceutical treatments include propofol, clonidine, and ketamine
Propofol is a GABA A receptor agonist
Ketamine intravenous infusion at rate of 6 mg per kg per minute

questions.question: The major cause of middle cerebral artery stroke is:
questions.explanation:
Literature suggest that embolism is the most common cause of MVA strokes
Emboli from the heart account for more than 50% of MCA strokes
Atrial fibrillation has been recognized as the number one cardiac cause of stroke

questions.question: The mildest spinal dysraphism is:
questions.explanation:
Spina bifida, especially the occulta form, is typically asymptomatic
Meningocele, an extruding spinal sac containing meninges, is often symptomatic and requires
repair
Myelomeningocele, an extruding spinal sac containing both meninges and neural tissue, is more
severe than a meningocele
Caudal sac lipomas can be easily diagnosed on MR and CT, and in utero on US

questions.question:
Elderly male undergoing chemotherapy for leukemia develops headache, stiff
neck, fever and generalized malaise. Meningitis is suspected and LP reveals diptheroid-like gram-
positive rods. The most likely organism is:
questions.explanation:
Listeria usually causes septicemia and meningitis in patients with suppressed immune function
Most strains are sensitive to ampicillin and gentamicin

questions.question: Injury to the middle meningeal artery will most likely lead to:
questions.explanation:
Subarachnoid hemorrhage is most often due to tearing of bridge veins
Subdural hemorrhage is often due to tearing of tentorium
Epidural hemorrhage is common in middle meningeal artery injury

questions.question:
Which of the following evaluations is important in patients with bacterial
meningitis before discharge?
questions.explanation:
Bacterial meningitis is an extremely important cause of acquired sensorineural deafness
Audiometry is essential before discharge in all patients with meningitis
Another method of assessing hearing in younger infants would be auditory-evoked potentials
cochlear implants can be inserted if there is permanent neuronal damage

questions.question:
Which of the following is more likely to occur with neuraxial narcotics,
compared to intravenous opioids?
questions.explanation:
Itching occurs much more frequently with neuraxial opioids: up to 90% versus 15-20 percent
Proposed mechanism includes stimulation of an "itch center" in the medulla or stimulating opioid
receptors in the trigeminal nucleus
Sedation, nausea and/or vomiting, and respiratory compromise have approximately the same
incidences for both neuraxial and intravenous opioids

questions.question:
What is the most common cause of nontraumatic oculomotor nerve palsy with
pupillary involvement?

answers.C: Aneurysm at the junction of the internal carotid artery and the posterior communicating artery

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Aneurysm at the junction of the internal carotid artery and the posterior
communicating artery
questions.explanation:
The oculomotor nerve travels lateral to the posterior communicating artery in its course toward
the cavernous sinus
The pupillomotor fibers are situated in the periphery of the nerve and are affected early in case
of compression of the nerve by an aneurysm at the junction of the posterior communicating and
the internal carotid arteries
These aneurysms are the most frequent etiology of isolated third nerve palsy with pupillary
involvement
In cases of ischemic lesions, as with diabetes, the pathology is confined to the core of the nerve
and spares the peripheral pupillomotor fibers

questions.question: Which of the following is rarely a symptom of Sydenham chorea?
questions.explanation:
Sydenham chorea is the most common cause of chorea in children
Characterized by dysarthria, mood disorder, and hypotonia

questions.question: Which test is most useful to diagnose herpes simplex virus type 1 encephalitis?
questions.explanation:
The best test to diagnose herpes simplex virus type 1 encephalitis is a lumbar puncture to check
CSF for PCR for HSV 1
HSV1 antibodies may be present in the CSF and MRI may be abnormal but these are not as
sensitive
Brain biopsy is only done if the diagnosis is in question
Acyclovir is started before results are available

questions.question: An upper motor neuron lesion is characterized by:

answers.A: Flaccid paralysis, fasciculations, muscle atrophy, hyporeflexia, negative Babinski
answers.D: Spasticity, hyperreflexia, sensory loss, positive Babinski

questions.explanation:
Symptoms listed in the first option are those of lower motor neuron lesions (below the level of
the synapse); the affected nerve fibers are those traveling from spinal cord to specific muscles;
everything is DOWN
Upper motor neuron lesions (everything is UP) occur above the level of corticospinal synapses
in the gray matter
A myelopathy will cause loss of vibration and position sense (posterior columns) with
spasticity, hyperreflexia, and a positive Babinski

questions.question: Cushing disease is caused by dysfunction of which organ?
questions.explanation:
Cushing disease is caused by excess secretion of ACTH by the pituitary gland
The increased ACTH results in excess production of glucocorticoid by the adrenal gland
Excess circulating glucocorticoids produce signs and symptoms characteristic of Cushing
disease
Cushing syndrome is due to excess glucocorticoids secondary to endogenous or exogenous
causes. This can include autonomous adrenal adenomas.

questions.question: Which spinal nerve mediates reflexes of the triceps?
questions.explanation:
C5 mediates brachioradialis reflexes
C6 mediates biceps reflexes
C7mediates triceps reflexes

questions.question:
Which of the following choices is incorrect regarding pseudoseizures
(hysterical) and epileptic seizures?

answers.A: The corneal reflex is intact with pseudoseizures
answers.B: Incontinence is common with epileptic seizures
answers.C: The EEG does not differentiate epileptic from non-epileptic seizures
answers.D: Plantar extensor reflex may be present in the postictal state

questions.printed_answer_heading: The EEG does not differentiate epileptic from non-epileptic seizures
questions.explanation:
EEG is the best test to differentiate between pseudoseizures and epileptic seizures.
Paroxysms of abnormal cortical activity result in the abnormal behavior.
In pseudoseizures incontinence is rare.

questions.question:
Does sarcoidosis affect the spine? If so, which segment is most commonly
involved?

answers.A: Sarcoidosis is a multi-system disease, but it does not affect the cord
answers.B: Sarcoidosis preferentially involves the cervical cord
answers.C: Sarcoidosis preferentially involves the thoracic cord
answers.D: Sarcoidosis preferentially involves the lumbosacral cord

questions.printed_answer_heading: Sarcoidosis preferentially involves the cervical cord
questions.explanation:
Sarcoidosis mimics a plethora of other diseases, and should always be considered in a
differential
Sarcoidosis can involve the cord, most commonly the cervical cord
Sarcoid involvement is primarily intramedullary
Also the cervical area is preferred, sarcoid can involve the cord at any level

questions.question:
A 3-day-old male has an MRI showing a small posterior fossa with herniation
of the cerebellar vermis and brainstem through the foramen magnum. This was caused by an
encephalocele. Choose the correct statement below?

answers.A: This condition is more common in Asians
answers.B: This condition is more common in Caucasians
answers.D: Encephaloceles represent 30% of all neural tube defects

questions.printed_answer_heading: This condition is more common in Asians
questions.explanation:
Incidence is 1/3,000 in Southeast Asia, usually in the sincipital or frontoethmoid regions
Incidence in North America is 1/10,000, usually in the occipital location
Radiotherapy plays no role in treatment
Encephaloceles represent 10 to 15% of all neural tube defects

questions.question: Prolonged bleeding time is most likely to be caused by prior use of:
questions.explanation:
Bleeding time is a function of platelet number and function
From the above choices, only aspirin can compromise the function of platelets
Inhibition of thromboxane-2 by aspirin prevents effective aggregation
Bleeding time not a reliable measure of anticoagulation and should not be used routinely.

questions.question: What type of kinetic order is associated with phenytoin?
questions.explanation:
Phenytoin follows zero order kinetic
Elimination is independent of drug concentration

questions.question:
Which of the following studies would identify a condition often associated
with Chiari type 2 malformation?
questions.explanation:
Chiari type 2 malformation shows a small posterior fossa with the cerebellum herniating
caudally through the foramen magnum and results in elongation of the 4th ventricle
It is associated with lumbar myelomeningocele, a neural tube defect
This can be detected by MRI, CT, or ultrasound of the lumbar spine
The other options would not identify this condition

questions.question:
What is the treatment for respiratory depression caused by midazolam
overdose?
questions.explanation:
Overdose of benzodiazepines is treated with flumazenil.
Naloxone is an antidote for opiate overdose.
It is important to continue with resuscitation until there is full recovery.
Fentanyl can worsen respiratory depression if administered with benzodiazepines.

questions.question:
Which of the following is false regarding developmental venous anomalies
(DVA)?

answers.A: Risk of hemorrhage is approximately 5% per year and lesion
answers.B: Commonly found at the angle of ventricles
answers.C: DVAs constitute 60% of all vascular malformations
answers.D: On noncontrasted CT the drainage vein appears hyperdense

questions.printed_answer_heading: Risk of hemorrhage is approximately 5% per year and lesion
questions.explanation:
DVAs are the most common vascular malformation and are more commonly asymptomatic.
Appear as an upside-down "umbrella like" collection of white matter veins draining into a
single collecting vein.
Risk of hemorrhage is approximately 0.15% per lesion per year.

questions.question:
What must be ruled out in a patient with intense headache with neurological
signs?
questions.explanation:
Patients with the most severe headache of their life likely have with subarachnoid hemorrhage
The initial screening test is an uninfused CT of the brain but an LP may be necessary

questions.question: The most common initial presentation of Parkinson disease is:
questions.explanation:
Tremor is one of the first signs of PD. It is usually unilateral and in the upper extremity
The resting tremors is often associated with hand clumsiness
With time, the amplitude of the tremor increases and resolves during sleep

questions.question: What deficiency is presented in Wernicke Korsakoff syndrome?
questions.explanation: Thiamine deficiency is present in Wernicke Korsakoff syndrome

questions.question:
Patients with ventral cord syndrome due to an anterior spinal cord infarct will
have which nerve functions spared?
questions.explanation:
The dorsal columns are spared in the ventral cord syndrome
The dorsal columns are responsible for vibration and proprioception
The corticospinal tracts, spinothalamic tracts, and descending autonomic tracts are affected in an
anterior spinal cord infarct
This will affect motor strength, pain/temperature sense, and bladder sphincter function

questions.question:
Which of the following neurologic disorder is least likely to present with
anosmia?
questions.explanation:
Synaptic density loss may result in anosmia in Pick and Alzheimer diseases
Cervical spinal cord injury associated with severe flexion and extension injury have been
associated with anosmia. This is secondary to shearing of the olfactory nerves

questions.question: Which of the following is an anticoagulant?
questions.explanation:
Coumadin is an anticoagulant, which works by preventing carboxylation of vitamin K dependant
coagulation proteins
It specifically inhibits the enzyme epoxide reductase
Oxycel, Gelfoam, and Avitene are brand names of hemostatic agents

questions.question: Primary decoding of language occurs at which of the following locations?
questions.explanation:
It is generally accepted that primary decoding of language occurs at Wernicke area
Lesions in this area causes receptive aphasia
Wernicke aphasia results in long-winded speech that is jumbled

questions.question:
A 58 year old patient with hypertension presents after 30 minutes of left arm
and leg weakness and speech difficulty that resolved spontaneously; what is their diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
A transient ischemic attack is a neurologic deficit that resolves within 24 hours (most are much
shorter); this may be associated with abnormal CT findings and many patients will progress to a
stroke if left untreated
Lacunar infarcts cause varying degrees of pure motor or pure sensory deficits in association with
infarcts of small arteries; associated with hypertension and diabetes

questions.question:
What neck position allows for the most intervertebral foraminal separation
during mechanical cervical traction?
questions.explanation:
25° of flexion during mechanical cervical traction provides for the greatest degree of
intervertebral foraminal separation
More flexion or any extension decreases interforaminal space

questions.question: The N14 potential is generating at the:
questions.explanation:
The N9 potential is generated at the Erb point
The N14 potential is generated at the cervicomedullary area
The N20 potential is generated at the cortical region
The N22 potential is generated at the gray matter of the spinal cord

questions.question: The most common cause of subarachnoid hemorrhage is:
questions.explanation:
Berry aneurysms are the most common cause of subarachnoid hemorrhage.
Berry aneurysms are usually located at major branch points in the anterior circle of Willis.
After rupture of berry aneurysm, almost 50% of cases are associated with cerebral vasospasm.
Microaneurysms of small penetrating vessels usually are due to hypertension.

questions.question:
What is the likely cause for a 58 year old male found unresponsive, intubated
prior to hospital arrival with exam findings of disconjugate eye movements with rapid head
movement from side to side?
questions.explanation:
In a persistent vegetative state, upper portions of the brain are damaged and the brainstem is
spared; locked-in syndrome is caused by damage to specific portions of the lower brain and
brainstem with no damage to the upper brain
With oculocephalic reflex testing (doll's eyes), eyes will move conjugately with side to side
head movements if brainstem intact
Etiologies of locked-in syndrome include CVA (basilar artery), traumatic brain injury, central
pontine myelinolysis

questions.question:
A patient is having resection of a brain tumor while awake. The patient
suddenly experiences dyspnea, chest pain, and coughing. What is the most likely cause?

answers.B: Pulmonary embolus from deep vein thrombosis

questions.explanation:
The seated position for posterior fossa surgery or cervical spine surgery places the patient to
risk for venous air embolism (VAE)
This risk is increased by blood loss or dehydration
Administration of pure oxygen may enlarge the air bubble
Treatment should start with discontinuing nitrous oxide and placing a catheter into the right
atrium and aspirating the air

questions.question: Which of the following is not true about advanced directives?

answers.A: Once advance directives are given it can never be revoked by anyone
answers.B: It encourages communication about end-of-life decisions
answers.C: Discussion about advance directives can provoke anxiety
answers.D: Advance directives are an important part of perioperative care

questions.printed_answer_heading: Once advance directives are given it can never be revoked by anyone
questions.explanation:
The patient can revoke advanced directives any time.
End of life decisions can be clearly communicated with advance directives.
Advanced directives is a sensitive issue to discuss if not handled professionally.
Perioperative care should also include advance directives.

questions.question:
Which of the following is not an appropriate precaution for patients with
dysphagia?

answers.A: Any food remaining in the mouth should be washed down with liquid
answers.C: The patient should stay upright for at least 20 minutes after eating
answers.D: Avoid foods that are difficult to chew

questions.printed_answer_heading: Any food remaining in the mouth should be washed down with liquid
questions.explanation:
Food remaining in the mouth should never be washed down but should be removed
Remaining upright after eating reduces the risk of aspiration

questions.question: The diagnosis of cauda equina syndrome is made by:
questions.explanation:
Cauda equina syndrome is caused by nerve roots compression from L4 to S4
Associated with sphincter tone loss
Diagnosis is confirmed with MRI
Best the initial treatment option is surgery

questions.question: In intracranial atherosclerotic disease, which of the following is true?

answers.A: Most commonly affects ICA segment C4
answers.B: Most commonly affects ICA segment C5
answers.C: CTA is particularly effective in demonstrating mural calcifications
answers.D: Is the cause of cerebral thromboembolism in 70% of cases

questions.printed_answer_heading: Most commonly affects ICA segment C4
questions.explanation:
The most commonly affected intracranial arteries include the cavernous ICAs and distal basilar
artery.
NASCET criteria considers >70% stenosis flow limiting.
While digital subtraction angiography is the gold standard for evaluation of flow limiting
disease, CTA or MRA are effective screening tools.

questions.question: What is the characteristic appearance of a pituitary macroadenoma on MR?

answers.A: Appears as an area of T1 hypointensity
answers.B: Enhances less than a normal pituitary tissue
answers.C: Isointense to gray matter on T1-weighted images

questions.printed_answer_heading: Isointense to gray matter on T1-weighted images
questions.explanation:
Typically macroadenomas (pituitary adenomas >1cm) are easy to recognize on coronal T1WI as
lesions isointense to gray matter.
Pituitary macroadenomas frequently infarct due to marginal blood supply and thus can exhibit a
heterogenous appearance.
On delayed contrast enhanced MR scans the adenoma may appear hyperintense to the pituitary
gland.

questions.question: Which is true of pulmonary embolism (PE)?

answers.C: Diagnosis is easily made based on ECG
answers.D: All patients have an abnormal chest x-ray

questions.explanation:
The presentation of patients with PE is based on severity of pulmonary artery occlusion. These
category include massive embolus, acute pulmonary infarct or multiple pulmonary emboli
Acute pulmonary infarction occurs in 10% of patients and presents with pleuritic chest pain,
hemoptysis and dyspnea
The most common symptoms in the PIOPED study were dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, cough and
hemoptysis
Pulmonary infarction following an embolism is seen as a peripheral wedge shaped pleural-
based opacification on a CT scan

questions.question: What minimum score on the GCS correlates with severe injury?
questions.explanation:
Brain injury is classified as severe if the GCS is equal or less than 8
Brain injury is considered moderate if the GCS is between 9-12
The brain injury is considered mild if it is >13

questions.question: Before deciding on thrombolytic therapy for a stroke, the test of choice is:
questions.explanation:
Emergent non-contrast CT scan is mandatory to differentiate ischemic from hemorrhagic stroke
CT scan can also help rule out other disorders the possibility of a tumor and brain abscess
causing stroke like symptoms
A non-contrast CT scan can identify a hypodense area within the first 3 hours

questions.question: The direction of sound and maintenance of attention is processed by the:
questions.explanation:
The medial geniculate nucleus is part of the auditory thalamus
The medical geniculate nucleus represents the thalamic relay between the auditory cortex and
inferior colliculus
The medial geniculate nucleus is thought to be responsible for relating frequency and intensity of
sound to the cortex

questions.question:
Which of the following is not among the reports that must be submitted to the
National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB)?

answers.A: All adverse peer review actions against licenses
answers.B: All adverse actions against clinical privileges
answers.D: All professional society memberships of physicians

questions.printed_answer_heading: All professional society memberships of physicians
questions.explanation:
All adverse peer review actions against licenses, clinical privileges, and memberships must be
submitted to the National Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB).
All professional society memberships of physicians are not reportable to the National
Practitioner Data Bank (NPDB).

questions.question:
In a patient with postoperative hypothermia, which clinical feature will be
seen?
questions.explanation: Post-operative hypothermia leads to muscle shivering, which increases oxygen consumption

questions.question:
An adult has multiple cerebral contusions on head CT scan and is agitated with
stable hemodynamics of 85 bpm and MAP of 84 mm Hg. ICP monitor reveals 28 mm Hg. Which is the
most appropriate management regimen over the next few days?

answers.A: Hyperventilation to maintain a cerebral PCO2 of 25 to 30 mm Hg
answers.B: Administration of neosynephrine to increase his MAP
answers.D: Placement of patient in Trendelenburg position

questions.explanation:
Cerebral perfusion pressure the difference between MAP and ICP should be =or >70 mm Hg.
ICP should be 20 mm Hg or less.
Methods for reducing ICP include elevation of the head of the bed (reverse trendelenburg),
administration of mannitol or other diuretics, sedative to control agitation, prevention of
hypovolemia, maintainance of adequate CPP and keeping pCO2 in the proper range.
Hypercapnia causes vasodilation of the cerebral vessels, which increases intracranial volume
and pressure. Hyperventilation may be used for impending herniation to acutely lower ICP but
prolonged hyperventilation <35mm Hg decreases perfusion (secondary to vasoconstriction) to
an injured ischemic brain
The brain resets to the new target PCO2 within 48 to 72 hours, limiting the beneficial effects of
hyperventilation resulting in increased ICP when the PC02 later normalizes. Hypocapnia below
30 mm Hg cannot be recommended except in extreme circumstances.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common drug causing anaphylaxis?
questions.explanation:
Penicillin is the most common drug associated with anaphylaxis.
Bees, wasps, hornets, yellow jackets, and fire ants are the most common insect causes.
Peanuts, eggs, and shellfish are common food triggers. They may cause anaphylaxis even when
consumed in small quantities.

questions.question: What neurological defect is associated with vitamin B12 deficiency?
questions.explanation:
Posterior column defect is manifested in vitamin B12 deficiency
This results in impairment of vibratory sense

questions.question:
A female says she feels an upset stomach, turns her head to the left, makes
mouth movements that resemble chewing, and fumbles with her clothes as if she is picking lint off her
shirt. During the brief episode, she appears dazed. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Complex partial seizures sometimes start with an aura such as an odd feeling in the stomach and
automatisms such as mouth movements and picking at one's shirt

questions.question: Neglect of the contralateral body would most likely is caused by?
questions.explanation:
Damage to the right posterior parietal lobe causes neglect of the left side of the body
This neglect may have several dimensions: sensory, motor, cognitive, and attentional

questions.question: What is a threat to do bodily harm?
questions.explanation:
Assault is a threat to do bodily harm
Abandonment is the unilateral termination of a physician-patient relationship by the physician
Battery involves touching another person without consent
False imprisonment is the illegal confinement or restraint of an individual

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common cause of craniosynostosis?
questions.explanation:
Craniosynostosis is premature fusion of the skull sutures
The separation of the sutures normally allows for new bone growth to accommodate the growing
brain
When a suture closes prematurely, the skull will become asymmetrical
The overwhelming majority of cases are sporadic and nonsyndromic

questions.question:
Spinal cord stimulation initially controls pain but overtime becomes less
effective. Which of the following is not a cause of this feature?

answers.B: Formation of scar tissue around the lead(s)

questions.explanation: Scar tissue around the generator will not affect its output

questions.question:
A 65 year old male has had long term cognitive deterioration with impaired
judgment, personality changes, and disinhibition. MRI shows severe cortical atrophy of the anterior
two thirds of the temporal lobes and the frontal lobes. Select the most likely diagnosis.
questions.explanation:
Frontal lobe damage leading to with impaired judgment, personality changes, and disinhibition
is characteristic of frontotemporal dementia
The MRI confirms the atrophy pattern most commonly seen in Pick disease
Alzheimer disease shows impairment of memory, language, and learned movements with more
generalized atrophy

questions.question: Which spinal nerve mediates reflexes of the biceps?
questions.explanation:
C5 mediates brachioradialis reflex
C6 mediates biceps reflexes
C7 mediates triceps reflexes

questions.question:
The lumbosacral trunk is formed by the contribution of which of the following
nerves?

answers.A: Dorsal rami of the fourth and fifth lumbar nerves
answers.B: Dorsal rami of the fourth and ventral ramus of the fifth lumbar nerve
answers.C: Ventral rami of the fourth and fifth lumbar nerves
answers.D: Ventral rami of the fourth and dorsal ramus of the fifth lumbar nerves

questions.printed_answer_heading: Ventral rami of the fourth and fifth lumbar nerves
questions.explanation:
The lumbosacral trunk is connects the lumbar and sacral plexuses.
It is formed by the ventral rami of the fourth and fifth lumbar nerves.
It is located at the medial margin of the psoas major and extends distally joining the first sacral
nerve.

questions.question:
Which class of medication is the most common cause of adverse reaction
elderly population?
questions.explanation:
NSAIDS are most commonly used for pain control
They are also the most common cause of adverse drug reaction in elderly

questions.question: The most common presenting feature of a brain abscess is:
questions.explanation:
Headache is the most common presenting symptom in a patient with a brain abscess
Neurological deficits occur in about 50 percent of patients

questions.question: The nerve ending for pain sensation is:
questions.explanation: Pain and temperature nerves have free endings

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common persistent CSF cavity?
questions.explanation:
CSP is defined as separation of the leaflets of septum pellucidum containing CSF.
Present in all fetuses and 85% fuse by 6 months of age.
Large CSP is associated with schizophrenia and PTSD.

questions.question: Myelography can diagnose?
questions.explanation: Myelography can diagnose a disc herniation, disc bulge, spinal cord mass.

questions.question:
Select the choice which is FALSE concerning Protected Health Information-
PHI:

answers.A: Disclosures of PHI must be documented
answers.B: A select group of the workforce must be certified in PHI training
answers.C: A Privacy Official responsible for receiving complaints must be in place
answers.D: Individuals must be notified of PHI use

questions.printed_answer_heading: A select group of the workforce must be certified in PHI training
questions.explanation:
Individuals must be notified of PHI use and disclosure by covered entities.
All employees and members of the organization must be trained in PHI by covered entities.
A Privacy Official responsible for receiving complaints must be in place according to Protected
Health Information-PHI.
Individuals must be notified of Protected Health Information-PHI use by covered entities.

questions.question: Which is not a clinical presentation of neurogenic shock?
questions.explanation:
Neurogenic shock is associated with spinal injury
Consist with sign of hypovolemia

questions.question: Patients with hypovolemic shock may have all of these findings except:
questions.explanation:
Hypovolemic shock patients may experience tachycardia, hypotension, confusion or restlessness
Without correction can lead to acidosis

questions.question: Atlantoaxial instability does not occur in?
questions.explanation: Downs syndrome and rheumatoid arthritis are both risk factors of atlantoaxial instability

questions.question:
Which of the following medications are considered appropriate for herpetic
meningoencephalitis?
questions.explanation:
Acyclovir is the drug of choice for herpetic meningoencephalitis
It is given for three weeks at a dose of 20 mg/kg/dose
TK-resistant herpes viruses are resistant to acyclovir
Cidofovir is effective for acyclovir resistant cases

questions.question: Multiple sclerosis is associated with increased CSF:
questions.explanation:
Most MS patients have elevated IgG level and myelin basic protein in CSF
Lumbar puncture helps to confirm the diagnosis

questions.question:
A provider hears two other providers discussing a patient's condition in the
main hallway of a hospital ward. What should the provider do next?

answers.D: Report the providers to the ethics committee

questions.explanation:
It is inappropriate for any medical personnel to discuss personal information about a patient or
his condition in a public area
Patients have the right to confidentiality

questions.question: Which of the following is least likely to cause delirium?
questions.explanation:
Some antibiotics may cause delirium, however this adverse effect is very rarely seen with
cephalosporins.
Sulfamethoxazole, flouroquinones, and trimethoprim are more likely causes.
Other medications that are causative include opioids, benzodiazepines, steroids, and those with
significant anticholinergic effects.

questions.question:
Which of the following is not a complication of intrathecal baclofen pump
overdose?
questions.explanation:
Hallucinations, seizures, confusion, and psychotic behaviors are moderate complications
Respiratory depression, hypotension, and coma are the severe complications

questions.question:
Which of the following is NOT an appropriate preventative measure for
penicillin-induced anaphylaxis?

answers.B: Education in the use of epinephrine
answers.C: Pretreatment with diphenhydramine before administering penicillin
answers.D: Education of family members about the dangers of anaphylaxis

questions.printed_answer_heading: Pretreatment with diphenhydramine before administering penicillin
questions.explanation:
Patients with a history of anaphylaxis to penicillin should not be given the antibiotic, or related
antibiotics.
Penicillin induced anaphylaxis may be fatal.

questions.question:
A 65 year old with a neurological problem is found to have an extensor plantar
reflex when the calf muscle is squeezed. This indicates that he may have:
questions.explanation:
Gordon's sign occurs when one squeezes the calf muscles and elicits an extensor plantar reflex
Gordon's sign is positive in individual with pyramidal tract lesions and is often used as a
substitute babinski test

questions.question:
A 70 y/o with atrial fibrillation on warfarin presents to the ER with profound
neurological symptoms on the left side. CT scan shows no hematoma. The initial diagnosis is middle
cerebral infarct from emboli. Which of the following symptom(s) would be consistent with MCA
stroke?
questions.explanation:
Damage to the non-dominant hemisphere leads to neglect. A stroke of the dominant hemisphere
will lead to aphasia. Large strokes cause hemianopsia and deviation of eyes towards the lesion
Because the MCA is a straight offshoot of the ICA, it is more prone to emboli

questions.question: Which of the following is not an indication of transtentorial herniation?
questions.explanation:
Classic feature of transtentorial herniation include coma, fixed and dilated pupils, and
decerebrate posturing

questions.question: Which of the following nerves is involved with the patellar reflex?
questions.explanation:
The genitofemoral nerve completes the arch for cremasteric reflex
The femoral nerve is responsible for the patella reflects
The tibial nerve innervates plantar flexion of foot

questions.question: Which of the following is a narcotic antagonist?
questions.explanation:
Naloxone is a narcotic antagonist
Diazepam is a benzodiazepine
Atenolol is a beta blocker
Phenytoin is an anti-seizure medication

questions.question:
A patient has a CT of the brain after a motor vehicle accident-showing
incidental finding of a convexity arachnoid cyst. This may be secondary to hygroma, chronic
subdural/epidural hematoma, or epidermoid tumor. Which of the following is inaccurate?

answers.B: These lesions usually occur in the middle fossa
answers.C: This is the most common location for this lesion
answers.D: These lesions can rupture after head injury

questions.printed_answer_heading: This is the most common location for this lesion
questions.explanation:
This lesion is seen in 0.75% of the general population
Rupture of the cyst can lead to a subdural hygroma, which can increase intracranial pressure
Rupture of the cyst can cause acute and chronic subdural hematomas
The usual locations of these are sylvian fissure (54%), cerebellopontine angle (17.5%), and
parasellar or convexity (each 15%)

questions.question:
A patient has traumatic brain injury resulting in short term memory loss and
problems with perceiving sensory input. Select the part of the brain that was probably injured.
questions.explanation: The parietal lobe is involved in short term memory and is the primary sensory cortex

questions.question:
Why are patients who are bed ridden are asked to move their legs while in
bed?

answers.B: Takes their mind off of their medical condition
answers.C: Prevents deep vein thrombosis of the legs

questions.printed_answer_heading: Prevents deep vein thrombosis of the legs
questions.explanation:
This activity is taught to the patient to promote venous return. The muscular action aids in venous
return and prevents venous stasis in the lower extremities

questions.question:
A 36-year-old man comes to the physician with the chief complaint that he has
he has "spells" where he believes that he smells rotten eggs as well as feeling that he is hearing things
that are not there. During this time he also feels unaware of his surroundings. His wife no longer
wants him to be alone with the children due to these incidents that she finds bizarre. He has no prior
history of psychiatric illness. A brain tumor is found on MRI. In which of the following area of the
brain is this tumor most likely found on MRI?
questions.explanation:
Temporal lobe tumors can also present with complex partial seizures and psychiatric symptoms
of aggressive or labile behaviors and excessive anxiety

questions.question:
Which Medicare program is responsible for covering financial costs of
inpatient hospital care in people over the age of 65?
questions.explanation:
Medicare part A covers for inpatient hospital care
This is funded by social security tax
Medicare part A is automatically provided to all elderly patients
Medicare part B covers for physician services and durable medical equipment

questions.question:
A 40-year-old female is mugged and hit over the head. She has loss of
consciousness for 30 minutes but declines medical evaluation as she has only a headache. 2 days later
he is found unresponsive. Paramedics are called but she regains consciousness and asks for dinner.
The paramedic notes he patient is only oriented to person and has left-sided weakness. What is the
most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
After significant head trauma patients are at risk for seizures
Subdural hematoma is a consideration
An expanding subarachnoid hemorrhage would not have waxing and waning symptoms
Evaluation in the ED with CT and inpatient observation is indicated

questions.question: The terminal portion of the spinal cord is known as the:
questions.explanation:
The conus medullaris is the terminal end of the spinal cord
The conus medullaris occurs at lumbar vertebra L1-L2
The terminal nerve root tail is referred to as the filum terminale

questions.question: Which of the following is false about massive blood transfusions?
questions.explanation:
All except hypokalemia occur with blood transfusion
Citrate binds to calcium causing hypocalcemia
Occasionally platelets have to be administered after massive blood transfusions

questions.question: Morphine may be best characterized by which of the following statements?

answers.A: It is a pure opioid antagonist at the mu, kappa and delta receptors
answers.B: It has an addiction potential equal to that of codeine
answers.C: At high doses it causes death by respiratory depression
answers.D: It is classified as a mixed agonist -antagonist drug

questions.printed_answer_heading: At high doses it causes death by respiratory depression
questions.explanation:
Morphine is the prototype of many narcotic drugs that interact predominantly with the opioid mu-
receptor
These mu-binding sites are discretely distributed in the human brain, spinal cord and spinal
nucleus of trigeminal nerve.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a source of delirium?
questions.explanation:
Delirium or acute confusional state results from an underlying cause. It is a neuropsychiatric
syndrome with an acute onset and fluctuating course.
Symptoms involve perceptual deficits, mental confusion, severe disorganization of behavior,
cognitive deficiencies, delusions, and hallucinations
Causes include acute alcohol or pain medicine withdrawal, infection, medications, lack of sleep,
brain insult (hemorrhage, stroke, trauma and cancer), electrolyte imbalances, hypoglycemia, and
hypoxia

questions.question:
After a laparotomy in a 45 year old, the best method of managing postoperative
pain is:
questions.explanation:
In the hospital patient controlled analgesia is probably the best way to deliver pain medications
An infusion pump that delivers an intravenous analgesic is released when the patient pushes a
button
PCA reduces time to receive pain medication, reduces nursing work and reduces chances of
medication errors
PCA is useful in people who have good mentation and or are physically able to push the button.
However, the pumps often malfunction and are expensive

questions.question: Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are most commonly in the:
questions.explanation:
85% of AVMs are in the cerebral hemispheres
15% are in the posterior fossa

questions.question: In adults, naloxone doses can be repeated to a maximum of:
questions.explanation:
In adults, a dose between 0.4 mg to 2 mg can be given every 2-3 minutes for a maximum of 10
mg
Pediatric dosing for kids less than 5 years or 20 kg is 0.1 mg/kg
Pediatric dosing for kids greater than 5 years or 20 kg is a 2 mg dose is recommended

questions.question: In blunt trauma, which cervical disc is most like to herniate?
questions.explanation: The most common cervical herniations are C6 and C7

questions.question:
A patient complains of low back pain with radiation down the right leg. Select
the examination that is most specific for lumbar disc herniation.
questions.explanation:
Straight leg raise is performed with the patient supine
The leg on the affected side is passively extended at the hip and if radiating pain is elicited the
test is positive for L5, S1 nerve root entrapment
If performing this maneuver on the other leg causes this pain, this is more specific for disc
herniation and is a poor prognostic sign
The crossed straight leg raise is less sensitive but more specific

questions.question: What is the defect associated with Guillain-BarrÃ© syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Guillain-BarrÃ© is also known as idiopathic polyneuritis
It is associated with inflammatory demyelination of the peripheral nervous system
The etiology is thought to be exposure to a foreign antigen resulting in autoimmune destruction of
myelin
The most common foreign antigen is from Campylobacter jejuni

questions.question: Which of the following is the most common posterior fossa tumor in children?
questions.explanation:
Medulloblastomas are one of the common childhood tumors
Medulloblastomas are posterior fossa tumors typically occur at the midline

questions.question:
A client with Parkinson disease is experiencing increasing functional
impairment and is to be given carbidopa-levodopa (Sinemet). The caregiver explains that the
therapeutic action of this drug is to:

answers.A: Replace dopamine normally present in the central nervous system
answers.B: Suppress dopamine production in the central nervous system
answers.D: Slow nerve impulse transmission in the central nervous system

questions.printed_answer_heading: Replace dopamine normally present in the central nervous system
questions.explanation:
Carbidopa-levodopa (Sinemet) replaces dopamine, which is a neurotransmitter. Sinemet is
converted to dopamine in the central nervous system (CNS), where it functions as a
neurotransmitter
Carbidopa-levodopa (Sinemet) does not suppress production of dopamine. Carbidopa-levodopa
(Sinemet) reduces muscle rigidity and tremor
Spasticity is not associated with Parkinson's disease
Carbidopa-levodopa (Sinemet) does not slow nerve impulse transmission. It is a
neurotransmitter

questions.question: Which of the following is incorrect about lidocaine?

answers.C: It inhibits the passage of sodium through ion channels

questions.explanation:
Lidocaine has an amide bond that is hydrolyzed by the liver
Local anesthetics inhibit the passage of sodium through ion channels
Liver disease can reduce the metabolism of lidocaine

questions.question:
Select the pathway by which hormones from the hypothalamus travel to the
pars nervosa.

answers.A:
Secretory neurons to the extracellular space to hypophyseal port system to cells of the pars
nervosa
answers.B: Secretory neurons to axon terminals in the pars nervosa
answers.C: Secretory neurons to intermediate capillary plexus to cells of the pars nervosa
answers.D:
Secretory neurons to extracellular space to primary capillary plexus to hypophyseal port system
to secondary capillary plexus to cells of pars nervosa

questions.printed_answer_heading: Secretory neurons to axon terminals in the pars nervosa
questions.explanation:
The neurosecretory neurons are located in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the
hypothalamus
The axons of these neurons pass through the infundibular stalk to the to the pars nervosa
Here they release vesicles into the extracellular space
It then diffuses into the bloodstream

questions.question: The best agent used to treat SIADH is:
questions.explanation:
Sometimes cancers can prodce SIADH and cause significant water retention and dangerous
hyponatremia
The syndrome of SIADH is best treated with Demeclocycline
Lithium can also be used but has more side effects

questions.question:
For an asymptomatic patient with rheumatoid arthritis and a posterior
atlantodental interval (PADI) of 14 mm, which of the following is appropriate?

answers.B: An open-mouth odontoid radiograph to determine if surgery is indicated
answers.C: MRI to evaluate the true space available for the cord
answers.D: Spinal canal evaluated by CT scan

questions.printed_answer_heading: MRI to evaluate the true space available for the cord
questions.explanation:
An asymptomatic patient with rheumatoid arthritis who has a PADI of 14 mm should undergo
MRI to evaluate the true space available for the cord, since synovial pannus may result in more
substantial narrowing than is detectable by plain films or CT
Surgery generally is indicated if the true space available for the cord is less than 13 mm, the
cervicomedullary angle is less than 135°, or both

questions.question:
Which of the following MRV finding is associated with intracranial
hypotension?

answers.B: White matter lesions (WMLs) primarily in deep structures

questions.explanation:
Post-dural headache causing intracranial hypotension typically results in MRI findings of
enhancement of the dural and pial layers of the meninges (pachymeninges)
Deep white matter lesions (WMLs) may be seen in headache patients due to migraine with aura
Headache due to IIH can show an empty sella sign on MRI
Headache due to congenital Chiari type 1 malformation, would show cerebellar tonsils hanging
>5 cm below the foramen magnum on MRI

questions.question:
Based on the Henneman nerve size principle, which of the following motor
units is the first to be recruited?
questions.explanation:
Small and slow twitch motor units are first to be recruited
Large and fast twitch motor units are last to be recruited
Reticulospinal tracts carry extrapyramidal information and spinocerebellar tracts provide
sensory and motor feedback for cerebellar inputs
The motor neurons and their axons are primary targets for ALS and secondary demyelinization
occurs after axons

questions.question: A sign of increasing intracranial pressure (ICP) is:
questions.explanation:
Cushing reflex is a sign of increasing ICP
Patients experience a widening pulse pressure, irregular breathing and decreased heart rate-
Cushing's triad
Babinski reflex is elicited by stroking the sole of the foot-the great toe undergoes dorsiflexion
and the rest of toes fan out
A barotrauma reflex does not exist

questions.question: Neuraxial neurolysis provides pain relief in what percent of cases?
questions.explanation:
Neuraxial neurolysis can last up to four months
Pain relief reported in 60 percent of patients
Common side effects include bladder and motor paresis

questions.question:
The true statement about the physiology of an action potential is which of the
following?

answers.A: Na+ efflux from a cell causes depolarization
answers.B: Voltage-gated potassium channel closing is both time and voltage dependent
answers.C: K+ influx into a cell causes depolarization
answers.D: Voltage-gated potassium channels have an immediate response

questions.printed_answer_heading: Voltage-gated potassium channel closing is both time and voltage dependent
questions.explanation:
Delayed rectifier potassium channels, also known as voltage gated potassium channels, have a
delayed response so that potassium continues to flow even after repolarization
Na+ influx into a cell causes depolarization
K+ efflux from a cell causes hyperpolarization

questions.question:
A normal serum value for which of the following is most indicative of
adequate treatment of a patient with diabetes insipidus?
questions.explanation:
Diabetes insipidus is a condition characterized by inadequate arginine vasopressin activity
This causes increased urinary free water excretion and increased serum osmolality

questions.question:
A patient is admitted to the ER with severe headache, nuchal rigidity, and
fever. The CT scan is unremarkable. A spinal tap is planned. Which of the following facts is incorrect
concerning this procedure?

answers.A: Xanthochromia is a yellowish breakdown product of RBCs
answers.B: A traumatic tap will have decreasing number of RBCs in tubes 1-4
answers.C: A negative Gram stain means no infection
answers.D: CSF glucose is normally 60% of blood glucose

questions.printed_answer_heading: A negative Gram stain means no infection
questions.explanation:
A negative Gram stain does not rule out meningitis. This requires evaluating CSF glucose,
protein, cell count, and culture & sensitivity. A presumptive diagnosis requires starting
antibiotics before the culture results are ready.
With a subarachnoid hemorrhage the amount of RBCs remain the same in tubes 1 through 4.
A patient with papilledema and a brain lesion causing mass effect cannot have a lumbar tap due
to the risk of herniation.
If CSF is necessary for treatment, the patient will require a burr hole and ventricular tap.

questions.question: Which condition is not associated with iron deficiency anemia?
questions.explanation:
Iron deficiency anemia is a microcytic anemia
Characterized by low ferritin and high iron binding

questions.question:
A patient with AIDS develop symptoms of dementia. Which of the following
conditions is the most likely etiology?
questions.explanation:
AIDs dementia complex is a metabolic encephalopathy induced by the HIV infection and fueled
by immune activation of microglia and macrophages
Two of the other three diseases are opportunistic infections while lymphoma is cancer
This is a non-opportunistic infection and most common cause of dementia in AIDs patients

questions.question: Excessive bleeding caused by heparin overdose can be reversed by:
questions.explanation:
Protamine binds to heparin and reverses the bleeding caused by it
Dipyridamole is antiplatelet medication
Aminocaproic acid can antagonize the effects of thrombolytic medications

questions.question:
In the operating room, what is one of the best ways to get control of a bleeding
vessel?
questions.explanation:
There are many types and sizes of intraluminal shunts available today. While not widely used,
shunts can be very helpful in managing troublesome bleeding. These shunts can even be left in
place for several days
Packing may help tamponade the bleeding but with active vessel bleeding more aggressive
maneuvers are needed
Ligation alone always risks the possibility of developing ischemia

questions.question: Which of the following is consistent with presentation of a cerebellar tumor?

answers.A: Unilateral hearing loss and tinnitus and facial weakness
answers.B: Acute onset of severe vertigo lasting days, and improving over weeks

questions.explanation:
Cerebellar tumors commonly present with dysequilibrium.
Meniere disease consists of discrete vertiginal attacks lasting hours, associated with nausea and
vomiting, tinnitus, and hearing loss.
Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo typically generally causes vertigo only with changes in
position.
Vestibular neuronitis causes the acute onset of severe vertigo lasting days, and improving over
weeks.

questions.question: Which nerve root is part of the stellate ganglion?
questions.explanation: Stellate ganglion is composed of C7 to T1

questions.question:
What is the condition called concerning a worsening of multiple sclerosis
symptoms with heat?
questions.explanation: MS symptoms worsen with heat and is called Uhthoff phenomenon.

questions.question:
If the pupils remain constricted in a dim light, it indicates damage to which of
the following structures?
questions.explanation:
The superior cervical ganglion is the largest cervical ganglia.
It has the neurons that provide sympathetic innervation to the face.
Dilation of the pupils requires sympathetic innervation.
Damage to the superior cervical ganglion would prevent pupillary dilation.

questions.question:
A 58 y/o woman has been place on L-dopa for Parkinson disease. What drug is
routinely added to improve the effectiveness of L-dopa?
questions.explanation:
Only approx. 10% of L-dopa crosses the blood-brain barrier to become dopamine. Carbidopa is
a peripheral dopa decarboxylase inhibitor which prevents L-dopa from transforming into
dopamine.
This reduces the peripheral side effects of dopamine while augmenting the concentration of L-
dopa allowing for more to cross the blood brain barrier (BBB).
Entacapone inhibits the enzyme catechol-O-methyl transferase, COMT, which breaks down L-
dopa. It acts in the periphery increasing the concentration of L-dopa which can than cross the
BBB
Pramipexole and ropinirole are D2 receptor agonists used for PD. Selegiline is a MAO-B
inhibitor that prevents deactivation of dopamine

questions.question:
Which of the following conditions is most likely to produce unilateral loss of
smell?
questions.explanation:
Frontal lobe lesions can cause unilateral loss of smell
The lesion could be secondary to infection, tumor, intracranial hemorrhage, or trauma
Many times head trauma, particularly a significant acceleration-deceleration insult, will transect
the olfactory epithelium that pierces the cribriform plate to join the olfactory bulb. This leads to
anosmia.
Head trauma that causes a frontal lobe injury while sparing the olfactory epithelium can cause
unilateral loss of smell.

questions.question:
A patient developed an ischemic stroke after long periods of sitting. Which of
the following is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation:
Atrial septal defect results in a shunt between the venous and arterial systems without the
pulmonary vasculature to screen out emboli.
Emboli can bypass the lungs and end up in the arterial system, causing strokes.
The paradoxical embolus originated in the lower extremities and become lodged in the cerebral
vasculature.
ASD can result in right sided heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, atrial fibrillation, atrial
flutter, and Eisenmenger syndrome.

questions.question:
Which of the following signs is very specific for deep venous thrombosis
(DVT)?

answers.D: There are no signs that have more than a 70% specificity for deep venous thrombosis.

questions.printed_answer_heading:
There are no signs that have more than a 70% specificity for deep venous
thrombosis.
questions.explanation:
Since no combination of signs and symptoms can reliably predict the presence of a DVT, more
extensive evaluation must be done since it is a potentially life-threatening disease.

questions.question: What effect would normal aging have on the complete blood count?
questions.explanation: No changes in the complete blood account are expected with normal aging

questions.question:
A 35-year-old female with multiple sclerosis has clonus of her lower
extremities and bladder spasticity. What symptom is she likely to report if her neck is flexed briskly?

answers.C: An electric shock-like sensation down the spine or to the legs

questions.printed_answer_heading: An electric shock-like sensation down the spine or to the legs
questions.explanation:
Lhermitte sign is elicited by sudden passive flexion of the neck
The patient reports an electric shock-like sensation radiating down the spine that probably
indicates disease of the spinal cord
It can be seen in those with isolated optic atrophy and no signs of spinal cord involvement
Spontaneous urinary incontinence and exaggerated Babinski response can be seen with some
patients secondary to stimuli to the lower extremity

questions.question:
Which cause of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage is the least likely to close
spontaneously?
questions.explanation:
Normal-pressure CSF leaks, of which idiopathic leaks are a subset, close spontaneously in only
one third of patients
They can persist for years
In contrast, traumatic leaks close within a few months in almost all patients

questions.question:
A 16 year old is playing football and is knocked out for 2 minutes but recovers
quickly and is awake and alert with normal exam. CT of the head is normal. How soon can he return
to play?
questions.explanation:
The patient had LOC for less than 5 minutes and no amnesia, which is a grade 2 concussion
Provided there were no prior injuries, and there are no symptoms, the patient should be allowed
to return to play in 1 week
CT of the head should be done for every patient with LOC from trauma
An often neglected element is cognitive rest during recovery

questions.question: Enhancement patterns on contrast-CT done for acute infarction:

answers.A: Show cortical vessels due to slow antegrade flow
answers.B: Show a cortical gyral pattern after about 2 weeks
answers.C: Show cortical vessels due to retrograde collateral flow
answers.D: Show disappearance of gyral enhancement after about 2 months

questions.printed_answer_heading: Show a cortical gyral pattern after about 2 weeks
questions.explanation:
The cortical gyral enhancement pattern shows up about 1 week post infarct, peaks at 10-14 days,
and resolves by 4 months
Vessel enhancement in stroke is better seen on MR than CT
On CT, hyperdense vessels may be from acute thrombus, not enhancement
Gyral enhancement is thought due to BBB breakdown

questions.question:
A male was involved in a car accident and had sudden loss of consciousness.
He is evaluated in the ER and an urgent CT scan reveals that he has cerebral edema. His present GCS
is 9 and you decide to treat him with a drug to reduce the brain swelling. The drug of choice is:
questions.explanation:
Mannitol is used to promote diuresis in acute oliguric renal failure, reduce intraocular and
intracerebral pressure, enhance urinary excretion of some medications like Aspirin,
Barbiturates, Bromides and Ethylene glycol
Mannitol is used in conjunction with other diuretics to rapidly reduce edema or ascites when
appropriate
In humans, it is also used as an irrigating solution during transurethral prostatic resections

questions.question: What is best initial treatment of temporal arteritis?
questions.explanation:
The average age onset of temporal arteritis is around 70
Treatment is corticosteroids that prevent blindness

questions.question: What is brain herniation through a skull defect called?
questions.explanation:
Fungating herniation is a brain herniation through a defect in the skull secondary to surgery or
trauma
It is caused by increased intracranial pressure and may be fatal

questions.question:
Which of the following groups is not an absolute contraindication for use of a
thrombolytic agent?

answers.D: Patients with a known AV malformation

questions.explanation:
Thrombolic therapy of acute MI is most beneficial if initiated within the first hour of onset
Common absolute contraindications include CVA less than 6 months, high risk for internal
bleeding, recent surgery, pregnancy, and known bleeding disorder

questions.question:
A 56-year-old male has a 3-year history of spastic paraparesis that is
progressive. Over the past month he has developed urinary urge incontinence. He has pain at his back
and thighs with numbness of his left toes. He denies visual changes, upper extremity motor symptoms,
or problems with eye movements. 3 months ago he had clipping of a basilar tip aneurysm without
improvement. Select the next step in management.
questions.explanation:
The findings are consistent with a progressive myelopathy
There are multiple possible causes but the most likely is MS
One group of patients that have a poor prognosis is middle-aged males with progressive MS
MRI of the spinal cord could show demyelination or vascular malformations of the cord

questions.question:
A young female suffers a subarachnoid bleed. The consultant wants to study
one other organ system besides the brain to find the cause. The organ is:
questions.explanation:
There are some congenital causes that have an association with subarachnoid hemorrhage.
These congenital causes may reveal a familial occurrence and are associatd with certain
systemic disorders.
Patients who have Ehlers Danlos Syndrome, Marfan syndrome or polycystic kidney disease are
quite prone to form aneurysms of the brain vessels.

questions.question:
What is the most common cause of reduction in urine output in a postoperative
patient?
questions.explanation:
Normal urine output is about 1-2ml/kg/hr
Signs of hypovolemia should be checked in all patients

questions.question: A patient with neurogenic claudication can improve his symptoms by:
questions.explanation:
Neurogenic claudication improves with the supine position
Symptoms are worse with physical exercise and flexion of lumbar spine

questions.question: In an epidural hematoma, the blood collected is usually?
questions.explanation:
Epidural hematoma is an arterial hemorrhage.
It may present with headache and neurological signs.
CT scan is the best initial study.

questions.question:
When investigating a patient that has dropping hemoglobin levels it would be
important to:

answers.B: CT scan all indwelling lines to assess for leaks

questions.explanation:
Patients showing a drop in hemoglobin need to be evaluated for the source of blood loss
Checking stool for presence of occult blood or gastric secretions for GI bleeding can be a cause
of loss of hemoglobin

questions.question: The drug of choice required to reverse heparin is:
questions.explanation:
Protamine antagonizes the anticoagulant effects of heparin
Protamine is derived from fish sperm and is high in arginine content
The positively charged protein particles in protamine interact with the negatively charged
heparin
Adverse effects of protamine include hypersensitivity, bronchoconstriction, flushing and
hypotension.

questions.question: A competitive antagonist will:

answers.A: Bind to the receptor and produce no reaction
answers.C: Bind to the receptor and mimic the agonist
answers.D: Not require a receptor and diffuse easily across the lipid bilayer

questions.printed_answer_heading: Bind to the receptor and produce no reaction
questions.explanation:
An agonist is receptor specific, it binds then creates a reaction
An antagonist will bind, not cause a reaction and prevent the agonist from binding

questions.question:
How many days should a 70 year old patient be hospitalized in order for the
costs to be covered by Medicare?
questions.explanation:
The Medicare covers for hospital stay in all eligible elderly patients
But the hospital stay should be at least 3 days in order to be covered by Medicare

questions.question: Patients who are known to have an allergy to procaine should not be given:
questions.explanation:
Local anesthetics are classified into esters and amides
Esters have no "I" before the "caine": e.g. Procaine
Patients who are allergic to esters should not be given other esters
The only amide in the choices given is benzocaine

questions.question: Which of the following would not increase intracranial pressure (ICP)?
questions.explanation:
Coughing increases ICP

not treated?
questions.explanation:
An ependymoma in the posterior fossa is most likely to cause complications via mass effect and
local expansion
Of the choices listed, transforaminal herniation would be the most likely complication
These rarely hemorrhage and would not likely occlude the basilar artery

questions.question: Select the true statement about syringomyelia.

answers.A: Patients become symptomatic in their 30s or 40s
answers.B: Chiari malformations are associated in about half of patients
answers.C: Symptoms can usually be relieved by surgical decompression
answers.D: Symptoms include loss of position and vibration sense

questions.printed_answer_heading: Chiari malformations are associated in about half of patients
questions.explanation:
Syringomyelia is a slowly enlarging cavitary expansion of the cervical spinal cord that is usually
developmental but can be secondary to trauma or infection
Symptoms include loss of pain and temperature sense with upper extremity weakness but can
progress to lower extremity symptoms and bowel or bladder problems
Chiari malformations are seen in about half of patients and may require extensive decompression
of the posterior fossa
Surgical therapy of the cavity is rarely effective and recurrence is common

questions.question: Which muscle is the least affected in the facioscapulohumeral syndrome?
questions.explanation:
The facioscapulohumeral syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder in most patients
Affects mainly of upper body muscles
It is associated with chromosome band 4q35 in most patients

questions.question: What is the most common acquired paralysis in a healthy child?
questions.explanation:
About 25 percent of Guillain Barre cases do not present with antecedent infection
Most cases present with extremity pain
It is the most common cause of acquired paralysis

questions.question: Which of the following fact(s) is consistent with multi-infarct dementia?

answers.A: Condition can occur from multiple small strokes
answers.B: Condition can occur from a large infarct of frontal lobe
answers.C: Hypertension 80% of the time causes lacunar infarcts

questions.explanation:
Multi-infarct dementia occurs from an accumulation of small and large strokes that cause
progressive loss and damage to ever greater areas of functional brain. This leads to increasing
cognitive impairment, affective dysfunction, loss of motor functioning, and behavioral decline
Small vessel disease, lacunar infarcts, peaks in the 4th-7th decades, is primarily due to
hypertension, and takes 5-10 years to develop. A large single stroke to the thalamus and
cingulate can result in appreciable mental deterioration
The underlying etiologies are cardiovascular disease, DM, hypertension, elevated cholesterol,
smoking, familial predisposition, and traumatic injuries from hemorrhagic infarcts
Therapy basically is oriented towards treating the underlying conditions.

questions.question: Which spinal nerve does not contribute to the upper extremity muscles?
questions.explanation: T4 spinal nerve does not contribute to the upper extremity muscles

questions.question: Patient with documented contrast allergy can be give IV contrast along with:
questions.explanation: Patient can be premedicated with antihistamines and corticosteroids

questions.question: Select the choice which LEAST applies to Disease Management:

answers.A: Reducing the complications of chronic illness is one goal
answers.B: Disease Management focuses on chronic diseases
answers.C: Disease Management can be used with every patient
answers.D: Improved outcomes is a primary goal

questions.printed_answer_heading: Disease Management can be used with every patient
questions.explanation:
Disease Management focuses on specific chronic diseases.
Reducing the complications is of chronic illness is one goal of Disease Management.
Disease Management may include eating disorders, chronic heart disease, chronic obstructive
pulmonary disease (COPD), kidney disease, diabetes mellitus, cancer and many other chronic
disorders, but it is not intended to be used with every patient.
Disease Management like managed care has improved outcomes as a primary goal.

questions.question: All of the following are appropriate uses of vancomycin except:

answers.A:
Treatment of serious infections secondary to Gram-positive bacteria that are beta-lactam-
resistant
answers.B:
Treatment of infections secondary to Gram-positive bacteria in those with anaphylaxis to beta-
lactam antibiotics
answers.C: Empiric antimicrobial therapy for a febrile neutropenic patient
answers.D:
Antibiotic prophylaxis for implantation of devices or prosthetic materials at hospitals with high
incidence of MRSA infections

questions.printed_answer_heading: Empiric antimicrobial therapy for a febrile neutropenic patient
questions.explanation:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have established guidelines for situations in
which the use of vancomycin is appropriate as well as situations in which the use of vancomycin
is discouraged
"Empiric antimicrobial therapy for a febrile neutropenic patient, unless initial evidence
indicates that the patient has an infection caused by gram-positive microorganisms (e.g., at an
inflamed exit site of Hickman catheter) and the prevalence of infections caused by MRSA in the
hospital is substantial"

questions.question: Which is true regarding cervical spine fractures?

answers.A: Seen most commonly in elderly females
answers.B: Athletic activities are the most common cause
answers.C: Falls are the most common cause
answers.D: Methylprednisolone may be used in associated spinal cord injury

questions.printed_answer_heading: Methylprednisolone may be used in associated spinal cord injury
questions.explanation:
Males 16-24 have the most C-spines fractures
Motor vehicle accidents account for at least 50% of C-spine fractures
Although controversial, methylprednisolone may be used within 8 hours of spinal cord injury

questions.question: What is the source of blood in a subdural hematoma?
questions.explanation:
Subdural hematoma is a venous hemorrhage
May present with headache and neurological signs
CT scan is the best initial study

questions.question: The brachioradialis reflex involves what spinal nerve?
questions.explanation:
The brachIoradialis reflex is also known as the supinator reflex
The reflex is caused by the C6 spinal nerve and causes supination

questions.question:
A certain investigational drug, with a half-life of 4 hours, is given at a dose of
800 mg intravenously. How much of the drug is left in the serum after 12 hours?
questions.explanation:
After 12 hours the drug would have undergone three half lives
After three half lives there would be 100 mg
After one half life there would be 400 mg
After 2 half lives there would be 200 mg

questions.question: Select the correct statement about substance P.

answers.A: Substance P is only involved with the basal ganglia direct pathway
answers.B: Substance P is only involved with the basal ganglia indirect pathway
answers.C: Substance P is involved with both the direct and indirect pathways of the basal ganglia
answers.D: Substance P is not involved with either the direct or the indirect pathways of the basal ganglia

questions.printed_answer_heading: Substance P is only involved with the basal ganglia direct pathway
questions.explanation:
The putamen has spiny neurons that use substance P and GABA in the direct pathway to the
substantia nigra pars reticulate and the internal segment of the globus pallidus
It is theorized that the direct and indirect pathways of the basal ganglia form equilibrium with the
indirect pathway increasing output from the substantia nigra internal segment of the globus
pallidus

questions.question: Regarding the appearance of an infarct on MRI, which of the following is true?

answers.A: A hyperacute infarct will appear hyperintense on DWI, T2WI and hypointense on ADC
answers.B: A chronic infarct will appear hypointense on T2WI and hyperintense on DWI and ADC
answers.C: A subacute infarct will appear hypointense on T1WI and hyperintense on T2WI and ADC
answers.D: An acute infarct will appear hyperintense on T1WI, T2WI and DWI

questions.printed_answer_heading:
A subacute infarct will appear hypointense on T1WI and hyperintense on T2WI and
ADC
questions.explanation:
Areas of infarct express cytotoxic edema (shift of water into cells), which leads to restricted
diffusion of water molecules primarily due to dysfunction of membrane pumps and damage to
intracellular structures.
During the hyperacute and acute stages of ischemic stroke DWI should demonstrate a focal area
of restricted diffusion (area of high signal) and the ADC should demonstrate a focal area of low
intensity.
In the subacute and chronic stages there is hyperintense signal on DWI primarily due to T2 shine
through.

questions.question: Which of the following is false in regards to acute infarction?

answers.A: Noncontrast CT is relatively insensitive during the first 24 hours following symptom onset
answers.B: A hyperdense vessel seen on noncontrast CT is highly specific for thrombus
answers.C: Loss of gray matter-white matter distinction is can be seen within 1-3 hours of symptom onset
answers.D: Hemorrhagic transformation is most often seen within 24 hours following symptom onset

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Hemorrhagic transformation is most often seen within 24 hours following symptom
onset
questions.explanation:
Hemorrhagic transformation has a delayed onset, typically seen 24-48 hours after the insult.
The finding of a hyperdense vessel (commonly a hyperdense M1 MCA) may be highly specific
but it has a low sensitivity.
The role of noncontrast CT in evaluation of acute ischemic infarct is primarily to rule out
hemorrhage and /or mass.

questions.question:
A 57 year old male presents with worsening headaches that awaken him at
night. MRI shows a right frontal mass removed surgically. Pathologic analysis showed a hemorrhagic,
necrotic tumor with frequent mitoses and highly pleomorphic cells. Despite radiation and
chemotherapy the patient dies 8 months later. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Glioblastoma multiforme is the most aggressive of the astrocytomas
It is the most common primary intracranial neoplasm
Pilocytic astrocytoma and oligodendrogliomas are malignant but grow slowly
Meningiomas are benign

questions.question:
Which of the following signs is not indicative of upper motor neuron
pathology?
questions.explanation:
Moniz sign is seen when there is forceful passive plantar flexion of the ankle, which elicits an
extensor plantar reflex.
Chaddock sign is performed by stimulation of the skin over the lateral malleolus.
Oppenheim sign is dorsiflexion of the big toe when there is irritation downwards along the
medial aspect of the tibia.
Tinel sign is performed by tapping the nerve to elicit a sensation of pins and needle. It is used to
test the median nerve for compression at the wrist.

questions.question: Which of the following drugs is most likely to induce thrombocytopenia?
questions.explanation:
Heparin can induce thrombocytopenia
Lepirudin and argatroban are direct thrombin inhibitors used to treat HIT
It is important to discontinue heparin and heparin flushes.

questions.question: What part of the SOAP note does disease severity fall under?
questions.explanation:
The subjective portion (S), records patients complain
The objective portion (O), records physical examination
The assessment portion (A), is where the severity of the disease is evaluated
The plan portion (P), is where the proper treatment is recorded

questions.question:
Carotid-cavernous fistula can be categorized by the Barrow classification.
Which types are supplied by the ICA?
questions.explanation:
Type A CCF describes direct communication between ICA and cavernous sinus. Type B CCF
describes a communication between dural ICA branches and cavernous sinus.
Type C CCF is a communication between dural EXTERNAL carotid artery branch and
cavernous sinus
Type D is a communication from dural branches of ICA and external carotid artery branches to
cavernous sinus.
Retrieved from "Classification and treatment of spontaneous carotid-cavernous sinus fistulas"
Barrow J Neurosurg. 1985 Feb;62(2):248-56

questions.question: A positive Lasegue sign indicates presence of:
questions.explanation:
Lasegue sign is also caused the straight leg raise sign and is used to diagnose lumbosacral
radiculopathy.
