The test is best performed with the patient supine. The leg on the affected side is raised with the
knee fully extended.
Pain radiating down the leg indicates lumbar nerve root irritation. Some dorsiflex the foot at the
ankle to increase sensitivity.
Raising the leg that is contralateral to the pain is called the crossed straight leg test and is more
specific but less sensitive.

questions.question: How does shivering affect body temperature?

answers.C: It has no effect on body temperature
answers.D: It increases body temperature only if accompanied by sweating

questions.explanation:
Shivering results from muscle contraction and it increases body temperature
Sweating is a mechanism to lower body temperature

questions.question: The total possible score for the motor component of the Glasgow Coma Scale?
questions.explanation:
The maximum score of GCS is 15
Four for eye movement
Five for verbal response
Six for motor moment

questions.question: A patient with Biot respiration may have:
questions.explanation:
Biot respiration is an abnormal breathing pattern characterized by shallow gasps with irregular
periods of apnea
Biot respiration usually occurs after brain herniation, stroke or trauma to the brain
Biot respiration indicates extremely poor prognosis
Bitot respiration is clinically the same as Cheynes Stokes respiration

questions.question: Alkalosis will cause the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve to shift to the:
questions.explanation:
Alkalosis will cause the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve to shift to the left
Other causes of a left shift include hypocarbia, hypothermia and decreased 2,3-
diphosphoglycerate (2,3-DPG)
A right shift of the curve may due to acidosis, hypercarbia, hyperthermia and increased 2,3-DPG

questions.question:
A 70 year old man with memory loss, gait imbalance and incontinence
undergoes a CSF shunt procedure for normal pressure hydrocephalus. Post-operatively he is feeling
well, but the following day he is confused, afebrile and complaining of a headache. The most likely
complication in this patient is:
questions.explanation:
Approximately a quarter of elderly patients undergoing CSF shunting for NPH may suffer some
type of complication
Subdural hematoma occurs because the reduction in intracranial pressure brought on by the
reduction in CSF volume may cause the brain to pull away from the covering meninges stretching
and potentially rupturing the bridging veins
Meningitis would also be possible and does not necessarily have to be accompanied by a fever
in an elderly patient

questions.question: OU means:
questions.explanation: OU means both eyes

questions.question: In adults, which bacteria most commonly causes acute pyogenic meningitis?
questions.explanation:
Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most common etiology for bacterial meningitis in adults
Neisseria meningitides is the most common etiology for bacterial meningitis in infants and
children

questions.question: Which of the following has effect on distribution of intrathecal medication?
questions.explanation:
Patient factors that have the most effect on distribution of intrathecal medications are height, age,
weight, spinal anatomy, intraabdominal pressure, and pregnancy
Injected solution characteristics such as volume, concentration, viscosity, and temperature effect
distribution
Clinical technique such as level of injection, patient position, needle type, and intrathecal
catheter type all effect distribution

questions.question: Where is the location of the Wernicke's area?
questions.explanation:
The Broca's area is located in the left hemisphere
A lesion in the Broca's area results in speech deficit
The Wernicke's area is also located in the left hemisphere
A lesion in this area results in a speech receptive defect

questions.question: Which nerve is not involved with sensory supply to the 5th toe?
questions.explanation:
Sensation to the fifth digit is supplied by the sural nerve laterally, the superficial perineal nerve
dorsally, and the posterior tibial nerve to the rest

questions.question: What is false about diabetes insipidus findings?
questions.explanation: Diabetes insipidus is associated with dilute urine

questions.question:
A 65 year old male is brought to the emergency room with right sided
weakness and facial droop. She has an expressive aphasia and decreased sensation on the right side.
Which of the following is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation:
Contralateral motor weakness and sensory deficit is characteristic of a middle cerebral artery
infarct
Pure motor or sensory deficits are seen with a lacunar infarct
Receptive or expressive aphasia is seen when the dominant hemisphere is involved

questions.question:
All of the following is true about spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH)
except which of the following?

answers.A: Fibrin glue injected into the epidural space can treat SIH
answers.B:
The headache of SIH usually lasts more than 6 weeks and infrequently resolves with
conservative treatment
answers.C: Cisternography can be used to study the leak
answers.D: Cerebral MRI may show pachymeningeal enhancement

questions.printed_answer_heading:
The headache of SIH usually lasts more than 6 weeks and infrequently resolves with
conservative treatment
questions.explanation:
Spontaneous intracranial hypotension usually resolves in 2 weeks with bedrest and conservative
management
The supine position may reduce CSF pressure at the site of leakage and allows meningeal
defects to heal. Caffeine is also used
Localization of such leaks is best done with CT myelography
The existence of the leak can be proved by radionuclide cisternography. Either the radioactivity
will accumulate outside the subarachnoid space or fail to ascend to the cerebral convexities

questions.question: What is the average head circumference at 1 year of age?
questions.explanation:
The normal head circumference at birth is between 35-37 cm
Head circumference is expected to increase to 50 cm by 1 year of age
Preterm infants may have lower head circumferences
Infants with hydrocephalus will have larger head circumferences

questions.question:
Which of the following patients is the best candidate for discontinuation of
antiseizure medications?

answers.A: A patient with absence seizures with normal MRI and EEG in remission for 9 months
answers.B:
A patient 6 months after resection of an arteriovenous malformation that had caused seizures
only before the surgery
answers.C:
A patient with history of generalized tonic-clonic seizures with normal MRI and EEG who has
been seizure free for 3 years
answers.D: A patient with cerebral palsy and seizures who has been seizure free for 2 years

questions.printed_answer_heading:
A patient with history of generalized tonic-clonic seizures with normal MRI and
EEG who has been seizure free for 3 years
questions.explanation:
Most authorities would agree to a trial without medication for a patient with normal MRI and
EEG who has been seizure free for 2 years
Patients with permanent brain damage such as AVM resection or CP should be treated for life

questions.question: Which spinal nerve is involved with the hip flexion?
questions.explanation:
Elbow flexion involves C5 and C6
Wrist extension involves C6, C7, and C8
Finger abduction involves C8 and T1
Flexion of the hip involves L2, L3, and L4

questions.question: In a patient with gonococcal arthritis, treatment protocol is:

answers.B: IV antibiotic therapy until 2 days after clinical improvement

questions.printed_answer_heading: IV antibiotic therapy until 2 days after clinical improvement
questions.explanation:
Gonococcal infected joints require IV antibiotics until 48 hours after clinical improvement
based on daily aspiration.
The patient is then switched to oral antibiotics.
S. aureus infected joints usually require at least 4 weeks of IV antibiotics.

questions.question:
A 44 year old is undergoing transsphenoidal hypophysectomy. The surgeon
will make an incision posterior to the:
questions.explanation:
Transsphenoidal hypophysectomy is performed with incision between the upper lip and gum
It transverses through the sphenoid sinus

questions.question: What is a consequence of an extensive obstetrical vaginal hemorrhage?
questions.explanation:
Hemochromatosis would not be expected to occur in this healthy young woman, especially since
she did not receive prolonged transfusions
Sheehan's syndrome is a syndrome of necrosis of the anterior pituitary related to obstetric
hemorrhage which can be diagnosed by 1 week postpartum, as lactation fails to commence
normal
Other symptoms of Sheehan syndrome include amenorrhea, atrophy of the breasts, and loss of
thyroid and adrenal function
Cushing, Simmonds, and Stein-Leventhal syndromes are not known to be related to postpartum
hemorrhage

questions.question: In myelography, the injection of contrast is usually at which level?
questions.explanation: L4-L5 below the spinal cord

questions.question:
An elderly patient over 80 takes the MMSE (mini-mental status exam) scoring
25. What does this mean?
questions.explanation:
A score of 25 indicates acceptable functioning of an elderly individual
Values below 25 suggest cognitive decline and the lower the score the more severe the mental
deterioration
The etiology may be dementia which has several etiologies to include Alzheimer's
30 is the top score. From 18-59 years, 29 is the median score, and at 80 years and older, 25 is
the median score.

questions.question:
A 65 y/o male recently diagnosed with small cell lung cancer has developed
weakness in his legs and arms. There are no sensory abnormalities. Exam reveals weakness not as
bad as patient's complaint and strength improves with repeated movement. What is the most likely
diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
LEMS is a paraneoplastic syndrome commonly associated with small cell lung cancer. Other
implicated cancers are thymoma, leukemia, Hodgkin lymphoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and
prostate. 50-60% of time this diagnosis is secondary to cancer
Autoimmune antibodies are produced against calcium voltage gated channel
Diagnosis is predicated on EMG of single fiber and compound motor action potentials (CAMP)
examination
Strengthening of muscle with repeated movement is called Lambert sign due to delayed
outpouring of acetylcholine

questions.question: For pelvic pain, the spinal cord stimulator implant needle should be placed at?
questions.explanation: Pelvic pain is controlled by SCS implant at T12

questions.question: The most common cause of cerebellar disease is which of the following?

answers.B: Use of drugs such as 5-fluorouracil or phenytoin

questions.explanation:
Alcoholism is the most common cause of cerebellar disease.
Hypothyroidism, use of drugs such as 5-fluorouracil and phenytoin, cerebellar neoplasms,
hemorrhages, and infarcts also cause cerebellar disease, but alcoholism is the most frequent
offender.

questions.question:
What is the likely diagnosis for an 18-year-old female with complaint of 1
week of diplopia and lower extremity weakness who shows optic nerve edema on funduscopic exam
and hyperreflexia in her legs with decreased pain, temperature, and vibration sense?
questions.explanation:
Multiple sclerosis is a demyelination disorder often associated with visual changes, weakness,
spasticity or numbness in the extremities, ataxia, dysarthria, vertigo, bladder or bowel
dysfunction, and cognitive and emotional changes
Visual changes may include diplopia, nystagmus, unilateral eye pain, vision loss, and an afferent
papillary defect (Marcus-Gunn pupil)
Diagnosis of MS is clinical, confirmed by CSF studies and MRI

questions.question:
A patient has intermittent double vision with sagging eyelid, dysphagia and
mildly weak upper extremities. Blood test reveals antibodies to acetylcholine receptors at the
neuromuscular junction. IV edrophonium test is positive due to patient's improvement. What is the
most likely disease?
questions.explanation:
Myasthenia gravis is a disease with fluctuating muscle weakness and fatigability. It is an
autoimmune disease producing antibodies against the post synaptic acetylcholine receptors
It may require more than one test to make the diagnosis. Discovery of antibodies to acetylcholine
is specific and 80-90% sensitive except with ocular myasthenia gravis in which that test is
positive only 50% of the time
Treatment involves cholinesterase inhibitors, neostigmine, and immunosuppressants. In an
emergency situation when the respiratory muscles are affected, plasmapheresis or IVIG (IV
immunoglobulins) may be required

questions.question: What is the first step in hand washing?

answers.A: Make sure paper towels are available

questions.printed_answer_heading: Make sure paper towels are available
questions.explanation:
Before turning on the water make sure that a length of towel is available.
Remove rings and watches.
Wash the hands for at least 20 seconds.
Dry the hands and turn off the water with the paper towel.

questions.question:
A patient has a stroke. His exam reveals a left homonymous hemianopsia
which is congruent and with macular sparring. There are no motor or sensory deficits. Where has the
stroke most likely occurred?

answers.A: Thalamus particularly the lateral geniculate nucleus

questions.explanation:
The visual system starts as the optic nerves. Half of fibers from both nerves that innervate the
medial retinal field cross as the optic chiasm at the pituitary
The fibers are now called optic tract and curve around the midbrain ending on the lateral
geniculate nucleus of the thalamus near the posterior limb of the internal capsule. The fibers
become the optic radiation or geniculocalcarine tract that connects at the visual cortex of
occipital lobe
Infarctions of the occipital lobe produce a congruent homonymous hemianopsia. Macular sparing
can occur because there is a branch of the middle cerebral artery that provides blood supply to
the large number of fibers involved with central vision
Stroke of the occipital lobe involves the posterior cerebral artery

questions.question:
A patient undergoes general anesthesia with sevoflurane and a weak,
nonflammable inhalation agent used to potentiate sevoflurane. This agent results in high blood partial
pressure and can cause:
questions.explanation:
Nitrous oxide is used to potentiate many inhalational agents
It has a high blood partial pressure and should not be used if the patient has pneumothorax,
closed loop bowel obstruction, or pneumoperitoneum
It enters air filled cavities 34x faster than nitrogen and causes expansion
It can thus cause air emboli, rupture of pulmonary blebs, rupture of obstructed bowel, and
pneumothorax

questions.question:
All of the following statements about determining if a lower motor neuron
lesion is at the nerve root level or more distant, at the peripheral nerve are correct EXCEPT:

answers.A: Nerve root pathology will reveal a dermatomal loss of sensation
answers.B: Peripheral nerve pathology will reveal a loss of sensation specific to the nerve root(s) suspected
answers.C: Complete nerve root pathology always results in total muscle(s) paralysis
answers.D:
Peripheral nerve pathology can result in mild paresis to complete paralysis of muscle(s)
depending on the extent of the disease process

questions.printed_answer_heading: Complete nerve root pathology always results in total muscle(s) paralysis
questions.explanation:
Even with a complete nerve root injury, there is generally still some muscle strength and
movement
For example, a complete femoral nerve injury will result in loss of quadriceps but a complete
L1 nerve root injury will not result in complete quadriceps loss
This is because the femoral nerve is formed from L1 and L2

questions.question: Which type of pain is not managed with a spinal cord stimulator implant?
questions.explanation: Nociceptive pain is not amenable to SCS injection treatment

questions.question: How long should surgery be delayed for if a patient has eaten food?
questions.explanation: It is considered safe to proceed with surgery eight hours after solid food

questions.question: The most common type of cervical spine subluxation is:
questions.explanation: Anterior subluxation is the most common type of cervical spine derangement.

questions.question:
A certain agent added to a penicillin drug made the penicillin resistant to beta-
lactamase producing microbes. The agent added most likely is:
questions.explanation:
Clavulanic acid has a beta lactam ring similar to penicillin
The similarity in chemical structure allows the molecule to act as a competitive inhibitor of
beta-lactamases
Clavulanate has no antibacterial effect of its own
Probenecid prolongs the half-life of penicillin

questions.question: What structure secretes growth hormone?
questions.explanation:
The cells of the pars distalis are the majority of the anterior pituitary, and secrete growth
hormone and this is under control of the hypothalamus
The pars intermedia is the boundary between the anterior and posterior lobes of the pituitary and
in human fetal life, this area produces melanocyte stimulating hormone
The pars nervosa is the posterior pituitary gland and is largely a collection of axonal projections
from the hypothalamus the secrete vasopressin an oxytocin

questions.question:
Which population has the highest rate for the acute pancreatitis with valproic
acid?
questions.explanation: Valproic acid induced pancreatitis is most common in children

questions.question: The most common complication after a lumbar puncture is:
questions.explanation:
Post spinal headache is common and occurs in 30-70 percent of patients.
The headache usually begins after 24-48 hours and is common in young people.
The headache is often on the frontal aspects and improves with lying down.
The headache is self-limited but can be treated with an epidural blood patch.

questions.question: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) fluid is found in-between the:
questions.explanation:
CSF is usually found in the space between the middle layer (Arachnoid matter) and the pia
matter
CSF acts as a cushion or buffer for the cortex and protects the brain
CSF is produced by the choroid plexus
CSF enters the vascular system by first entering the dural venous sinuses

questions.question: Which lesion can be associated with mutism?
questions.explanation:
Frontal lobe lesions can be associated with mutism, urinary incontinence, or gait disturbance
Also associated with gait disturbance

questions.question:
All of the following medications can be used for treatment of status
epilepticus, except:
questions.explanation:
The major drugs used in status epileptics are benzodiazepines, phenytoin or fosphenytoin,
barbiturates, and propofol
Airway should be given priority and dextrose infusion is also beneficial
Carbamazepine is not used for treatment of status epileptics

questions.question: Which cranial nerve is most commonly affected by carotid dissection?
questions.explanation:
12% of patients with carotid artery dissection have cranial nerve involvement
The most commonly affected cranial nerve is the hypoglossal
The lower cranial nerves are more often affected than the facial, oculomotor, and trigeminal
nerves

questions.question:
Cavernous malformations (angiomas) are most commonly associated with what
other malformation?
questions.explanation:
The association of cavernous angiomas and developmental venous anomalies is common, more
than 10%
Cavernous angiomas are also associated with cherry angiomas and cafÃ© au lait spots, though
not as frequently
Cherry angiomas, also known as Campbell De Morgan spots or senile angiomas, are cherry red
papules on the skin

questions.question:
A 32-year-old female presents with a few month history of worsening
intermittent headaches associated with dizziness. Exam between headaches is normal. MRI shows a
probable ependymoma at the posterior fossa. What is the most serious complication?

answers.A: Vascular occlusion caused by the tumor

questions.explanation:
Enlargement of the tumor could cause compression of the posterior fossa and herniation
There could be transtentorial herniation if it is upward or transforaminal if it is downward
Posterior fossa tumors usually do not cause seizures
Anaplastic ependymomas may metastasize or seed other parts of the CNS

questions.question:
A patient complains of leg weakness and tingling of her hands and feet. Exam
show positive Romberg and Babinski, loss of vibratory and position sense in both lower extremities,
and hypotonia. CBC shows a macrocytic anemia and Schillings test shows decreased absorption of
vitamin B12. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Pernicious anemia results from anti-parietal cell antibodies preventing secretion of intrinsic
factor
The deficiency of vitamin B12 causes ineffective erythropoiesis
The synthesis of fatty acids requires vitamin B12 as a co-factor
The fatty acids are needed for the synthesis of myelin, without which the neurologic signs
develop

questions.question:
In a patient with head trauma and raised intracranial pressure, which of the
following treatment is not utilized?
questions.explanation:
Diuretics are widely used to treat elevated ICP but their use must be used with caution. The
patient must be sufficiently hydrated because these drugs can cause alterations in electrolytes
and serum osmolality
Sedation is necessary in patients with severe brain trauma. Some patients may even require
mechanical ventilation. Steroids have not been show to be of much benefit in head trauma
Head of bed elevation improves venous flow from the brain and reduces ICP. If patient is
hypovolemic and the head of bed is elevated, there may be a drop in cerebral blood flow
Fluid restriction is contraindicated in patients with head trauma. Fluid restriction reduces
cerebral blood flow, which results in decreased brain perfusion and causes an increase in
cerebral edema. One should maintain euvolemia or slightly less as long as CPP is 60 or greater.

questions.question: Injury to the cranial tentorium will most likely lead to:
questions.explanation:
Subarachnoid hemorrhage is most often due to tearing of bridge veins
Subdural hemorrhage is often due to tearing of tentorium
Epidural hemorrhage is common in middle meningeal artery injury

questions.question: A healthcare provider acting as an expert witness is required to:

answers.A: Have held their position for at least 5 years
answers.B: Provide their testimony free of charge
answers.C: Discuss their testimony with the claimant
answers.D: Review all pertinent information and records

questions.printed_answer_heading: Review all pertinent information and records
questions.explanation:
Expert witnesses provide opinions on information they have reviewed about the claimants case
They do not discuss the case with the claimant and in some instances are paid for their time

questions.question:
A 62 year old female smoker with a history of hypertension is brought to the
emergency department with sudden onset of dizziness, nausea, vomiting, and a bifrontal headache.
The basic CT of the brain is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The most common symptom of cerebellar infarct is vertigo or dizziness
More than half of patients have nausea and vomiting while 1/3rd have headache
Hemiparesis, nystagmus, dysarthria, and ataxia are common
Most patients present when alert but cerebellar edema can result in compression of the 4th
ventricle and produce brainstem compression and hydrocephalus

questions.question: Which one of these is not a dimension of managed care?
questions.explanation:
Health policy is at the heart of managed care, in that, it serves to direct and guide the systems
and disease management of the organization.
Systems management is the strategic, systematic and coordinated effort to maximize the
relationships and resources of the managed care organization.
Disease management is the most substantial aspect of effective managed care.
Foundations and grants serve non for profit organizations to enhance their budgetary needs, but
are not a dimension of managed care.

questions.question: Pituitary hypocortisolism is characterized by all of the following, except:
questions.explanation:
Pituitary hypocortisolism is caused by failure of the anterior pituitary to secrete ACTH
This results in low cortisol and 17-ketosteroids
Corticotrophin releasing hormone is released from the hypothalamus and is usually normal or
high in pituitary hypocortisolism

questions.question:
A tendency for study subjects to change behavior simply because they are
being studied is:
questions.explanation:
The Hawthorne effect refers to a tendency for study subjects to change behavior simply because
they are being studied
It gets its name from a factory called the Hawthorne Works, where a series of experiments was
carried out between 1924 and 1932
The effect continues in the present day and must be accounted for in some experiments

questions.question: In an adult with mild myelopathy, the ideal treatment is?
questions.explanation:
Spinal stenosis is the most common cause of myelopathy
Affects the entire spinal cord and manifests with muscle weakness
Surgical compression is the best option for severe spinal stenosis
Physical therapy is the treatment for most patients with myelopathy

questions.question:
Rifampin is the prophylactic drug of choice for individuals who have come in
contact with a patient with what infection?
questions.explanation:
Rifampin is the drug of choice for anybody who has come in close contact with a person who
has developed meningococcal meningitis
Alternative medications if unable to take rifampin would be ciprofloxacin or ceftriaxone

questions.question:
Short half-life NSAIDs other than aspirin should be stopped how many days
prior to elective surgery?
questions.explanation:
Patients are advised to stop short acting NSAIDs three days before surgery
Long acting NSAIDs should be stopped one week before surgery

questions.question:
Postoperative retention of urine can be treated with which of the following
drugs?
questions.explanation:
Urinary retention is a common complication during the post operative period
Cholinergic stimulation helps to contract the detrusor muscle and relieve the retention
Bethanechol is a cholinergic agent that is selective for M3 muscarinic receptors
Oxybutynin is an anticholinergic used for treatment of urge incontinence

questions.question:
When utilized for neurolytic pain relief, alcohol has which of the following
properties when compared to phenol?

answers.B: Less distribution from site of injection

questions.explanation:
Severe pain, lasting less than one minute, occurs along the distribution of the nerve(s)
immediately after injection of alcohol
Alcohol exhibits more diffusion from its injection site than phenol
The risk of neuritis is greater with alcohol
The duration of blockade is longer with alcohol

questions.question:
Which neurosurgical procedure is associated with a high incidence of diabetes
insipidus?
questions.explanation:
Some neurosurgical procedures are a common cause of DI.
Transsphenoidal surgery is often associated with DI following removal of an adenoma.
Most cases of DI following transphenoidal surgery are said to be temporary.

questions.question:
An 8 year old male is brought in with daily headaches occurring each morning
and it is associated with emesis before breakfast. The headaches are getting progressively worse and
have awoken him at night. Select the most likely diagnosis.
questions.explanation:
The patient may have an intracranial mass
Warning signs include awakening secondary to the headache, progression of symptoms, and
emesis
Complete history and physical would be appropriate
An MRI would be indicated as most tumors in this age group are in the posterior fossa

questions.question:
All of the following statements about hemorrhagic strokes are correct
EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Hemorrhagic strokes can occur from both embolic and thrombotic cerebrovascular accidents
Contributing causes are severe hypertension, anticoagulation, coagulopathy, vasculitis, and
thrombolytic therapy for MI and stroke
Additional symptoms include nausea, vomiting, seizures, and altered mental status

questions.question:
When a lumbar sympathetic block is successful, this can be determined by
change in:
questions.explanation: Proper lumbar sympathetic block is determined by change in body temperature

questions.question: Which is not a risk factor for nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH)?
questions.explanation:
Risk factors, include connective tissue disorders, long-term analgesia use, BCP's, SLE, moya-
moya, metastatic tumors, infections, aortic coarctation, persistent fetal circulation (PFC)
Reactive arthrits is not a risk factor

questions.question: Select the virus that is not in the herpes virus group.
questions.explanation:
Herpes viruses are enveloped DNA viruses
It contains EBV, HSV I, HSV II, Varicella zoster, and CMV
The hepatitis B virus is not a herpes virus

questions.question: Which of the following is a common cause of tonic-clonic seizures in adults?
questions.explanation:
Causes of seizures in the adult population include tumors, trauma, drug withdrawal, and vascular
disease

questions.question:
Brain MRI of a 1-year-old boy presenting with ataxia and vomiting shows an
enhancing mass in the cerebellar vermis. 4th ventricular extension. Most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The patient age, imaging appearance, and anatomic location all fit best with medulloblastoma
Ependymomas are the second most likely posterior fossa lesion in this age group
Medulloblastomas tend to appear homogeneous while ependymomas usually appear
heterogeneous, due to internal cysts, calcifications, and hemorrhage

questions.question:
Morphine should not be used in the following group of patients except those
with:
questions.explanation:
Morphine can cause respiratory depression requiring its avoidance in patients with asthma,
COPD and emphysema.
Morphine could cause an elevation of CO2 which can increase intracranial pressure in head
trauma patients a dangerous condition
In prostatic hypertrophy, morphine can cause urine retention

questions.question: Which is not associated with electroconvulsive therapy?
questions.explanation: ECT increases cerebral metabolic activity but can cause herniation

questions.question: Which is least likely to occur after bilateral adrenalectomy?
questions.explanation:
Bilateral adrenalectomy causes permanent glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid deficiency
It may also lead to Nelson syndrome, which is caused by a rapidly enlarging ACTH-producing
pituitary adenoma
Empty sella syndrome is characterized by an inability to visualize the pituitary gland on MRI
scanning, due to a shrunken, flattened, or absent gland
It does not occur after adrenalectomy

questions.question:
What would be the effect of a lacunar stroke involving the internal capsule's
posterior limb?
questions.explanation:
Lacunar strokes affect non-cortical parts of the brain stem and cerebellum and are caused by
occlusion of the penetrating branches of cerebral arteries
Obstruction can be embolic or secondary to lipohyalinosis
The posterior limb of the internal capsule has corticospinal fibers
The leg, arm, and face are affected by pure motor hemiparesis

questions.question:
A 44 year old on heparin requires urgent surgery. How long must be heparin be
discontinued before one can safely undergo surgery?
questions.explanation:
Heparin should be discontinued 6 hours prior to surgery
The heparin can be restarted within 12-24 hours after surgery if postoperative hemorrhage is no
longer a threat
Heparin can be reversed with protamine

questions.question:
When performing a cervical transforaminal epidural injection, the correct
needle position in relation to the neural foramina should be?
questions.explanation: The needle should be position posteriorly in relation to the foramina

questions.question: Medicare covers what patient population?
questions.explanation:
Medicaid is designed to help low income families
It is funded by the state
Medicare is for elderly population

questions.question:
A male complains of intermittent, severe, brief episodes of lancinating pain of
the cheek, gums and lips. These are often produced by chewing. Exam and MRI are normal. What is
the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Tic douloureux, or trigeminal neuralgia is a clinical diagnosis
Classically it is a severe, lancinating, and brief
Impingement on the fifth cranial nerve would also cause weakness of chewing
Treatment is initially carbamazepine and phenytoin if the first is not tolerated

questions.question:
Peri-ventricular calcifications are characteristic of which of the following
infections?
questions.explanation:
Congenital infections are often given the term TORCH syndrome
Peri-ventricular calcifications are common with congenital CMV infection
Sensorineural deafness or other cranial nerve abnormalities are common
Hydrocephalus is commonly seen with congenital infections

questions.question:
Which of the following conditions does not prevent magnetic resonance
cerebral venography?

answers.D: Ferromagnetic hemostatic clips in the brain

questions.explanation:
Implanted electronic devices, ferromagnetic foreign bodies, severe renal disease, and some
cardiac valves are contraindications to MRV using gadolinium
MRV can be done without gadolinium but images are not as good
This would allow patients with severe renal disease to be scanned

questions.question:
Which of the following patients with an ischemic stroke are not eligible for
tPA therapy?

answers.A: Uncontrolled hypertension at time of admission
answers.B: Patient on anticoagulation even with a normal INR

questions.explanation:
Certain patients are not eligible for tPA therapy
Patients with a NIHSS>22 are at increased risk of hemorrhage
All patients who take oral anticoagulants regardless of INR are excluded

questions.question:
The otolaryngologist-head and neck surgeon is consulted by the neurosurgeon
to assist in the transseptal-sublabial approach to the sphenoid sinus. During the preoperative
interview, the patient reports that she has had previous sinus surgery and had her nose straightened
from the inside. Nasal endoscopy performed in the office determines that she has had a septoplasty
and reveals that the septal mucoperichondrial flaps are densely adherent to one another. Recognizing
that this may result in a difficult dissection, which of the following approaches to the sphenoid should
be avoided?

answers.A: Meticulous dissection through the previous cicatrix
answers.B: Dissection above or below the previous cicatrix

questions.printed_answer_heading: Meticulous dissection through the previous cicatrix
questions.explanation:
The lateral rhinoplasty approach results in some cosmetic defect but the sphenoid can be
adequately exposed.

questions.question: Which is least consistent with the diagnosis of Cushing syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Patients with Cushing syndrome typically have hypernatremia, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia,
hypervolemia, hypertension, and peripheral edema

questions.question:
A patient, who is undergoing a lumbar puncture for further evaluation of
possible multiple sclerosis. She is very afraid of a post-LP headache. You tell her you will be using a
small needle, with the bevel inserted parallel to the dural fibers, and that the stylet will be replaced
before the needle is removed. She continues to fear the procedure. What else can you offer to
minimize the risk of developing a post-LP headache?

answers.A: Advise her to drink coffee prior to the LP
answers.B: Prescribe subcutaneous sumatriptan to be taken BID on the day prior to the LP
answers.C: Encourage her to drink caffeinated beverages for at least 2 days prior to the LP
answers.D: Prescribe frovatriptan 2.5 mg once daily for 5 days prior to the LP

questions.printed_answer_heading: Prescribe frovatriptan 2.5 mg once daily for 5 days prior to the LP
questions.explanation:
Frovatriptan use for 5 days prior to a LP has been shown to reduce the incidence of post-LP
headaches, while there was no benefit observed when sumatriptan was given for just 1 day prior
to the LP
There was no pharmacologic benefit seen with caffeine when used as a nociceptive agent for
post-LP headaches
Since aspirin is an anti-platelet agent, it would not be recommended prior to a LP, with no
nociceptive benefits observed

questions.question: Levetiracetam is eliminated by:
questions.explanation:
Levetiracetam is eliminated via renal as unchanged form
It is an antiseizure medication

questions.question:
A newborn has a lumbar meningomyelocele. The neonate's weight is
appropriate for gestational age and has a vigorous cry. He has a good urine stream, clubfeet, and
spontaneous flexion and extension at the knees. A sterile dressing has been placed over the defect.
What should be communicated to the parents?

answers.A: Nothing. Allow the neurosurgeon to provide counseling
answers.B: Convey concerns about the newborn's brain
answers.C:
Explain that the newborn has a spinal cord defect and that a pediatric neurosurgeon will be
asked to assist in treatment and management
answers.D: Ask if the mother took prenatal vitamins for the whole pregnancy

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Explain that the newborn has a spinal cord defect and that a pediatric neurosurgeon
will be asked to assist in treatment and management
questions.explanation:
The initial management of a meningomyelocele is a sterile dressing
Closure will be done by a neurosurgeon
Reassurance should be provided by the primary care physician
Although many such cases are associated with folate deficiency, it could cause great harm to
raise this issue at this time

questions.question:
A patient has mesial temporal lobe epilepsy syndrome with intractable
complex partial seizures. He has an aura followed by complex automatisms, unilateral posturing, and
behavioral arrests. MRI shows a small hippocampus with increased T2-weighted sequences and
small temporal lobes. Select the other feature that is likely to be present in this patient.
questions.explanation:
Most complex partial seizures are secondary to mesial temporal lobe epilepsy
There is usually and aura followed by complex posturing or complex automatisms
There is usually hippocampal sclerosis, small temporal lobes, or enlarged temporal horn
Hypothyroidism, herpes, and tuberous sclerosis are not associated with this disease

questions.question:
All of the following are utilized in the treatment of pulmonary embolus (PE)
EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Heparin and thrombolytics are routinely used in the treatment of PE
IVC filter placement is considered when contraindications to heparin or in the setting of
recurrent DVT/PE
Aspirin has no place in the treatment of PE

questions.question: At what point should discharge planning begin?

answers.B: Once the patient is medically stable

questions.explanation: The most effective time to start discharge planning is at admission

questions.question: Which is false about brain trauma?

answers.A: Subdural hematomas can be caused by a lumbar puncture
answers.B: Epidural hematomas are usually associated with underlying brain injury
answers.C: Subdural hematomas usually occur from tearing of venous bridging veins
answers.D: Subdural hygromas are late developments after head trauma

questions.printed_answer_heading: Epidural hematomas are usually associated with underlying brain injury
questions.explanation:
Acute subdural hematomas are commonly associated with extensive primary injury
Chronic subdural hematoma is a common reversible cause of dementia. Some chronic fluid
collections are subdural hygromas
Risk factors for subdural hematomas include chronic alcoholism, epilepsy, coagulopathy,
anticoagulant therapy, hypertension, diabetes and thrombocytopenia
Acute subdural hematomas most often occur over the cerebral hemispheres but can also be found
in between the hemispheres along the tentorium or in the posterior fossa

questions.question:
What is the term for the potential maximum therapeutic response that a drug can
produce?
questions.explanation:
Efficacy refers to the potential maximum therapeutic response that a drug can produce
Potency refers to the amount of drug needed to produce an effect
Affinity refers to the ability of a drug to bind to receptors and form drug receptor complex

questions.question:
Which of the following structures is most likely to be compressed by a mass on
the pelvic brim?
questions.explanation:
The lumbosacral trunk is nervous tissue that connects the lumbar plexus with the sacral plexus.
The pelvis is divided by an plane that passes through the prominence of the sacrum, the pectineal
and arcuate lines, and the upper margin of the symphysis pubis.
The circumference of this plane is termed the pelvic opening or brim.
A mass on the pelvic brim can compress the lumbosacral trunk.

questions.question:
Which one of the following medications can increase the bioavailability of
valproate?
questions.explanation:
Only Cimetidine is able to inhibit liver enzymes
Valproate levels might be dangerously increased since it is metabolized by the liver
Phenobarb, Phenytoin and Rifampin are potent liver enzyme inducers
Hepatotoxicity is a feared side effect of valproic acid

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding Huntington disease (HD)?

answers.B: Children with a parent with HD have 25% likelihood of inheriting it
answers.C: Can be prevented by following a diet low in specific amino acids
answers.D: Is an incurable degenerative disease of the brain

questions.printed_answer_heading: Is an incurable degenerative disease of the brain
questions.explanation:
HD is autosomal dominant
Children of a parent with HD have 50% chance of inheriting it
Genetic testing and avoiding pregnancy is the only prevention

questions.question: Lidocaine is metabolized by:
questions.explanation: Lidocaine is metabolized in the liver

questions.question: Select the medication that can cause drug induced Parkinsonism.
questions.explanation:
Drug induced Parkinsonism most often is secondary to dopamine (D2) receptor antagonists
Antinausea medications including prochlorperazine and metoclopramide can cause this
condition
First generation antipsychotic medications such as haloperidol are also causes
Pantoprazole, famotidine, and fluoxetine do not have this side effect

questions.question: Which third generation cephalosporin does not cross the blood brain barrier?
questions.explanation:
Levels of cefotaxime, cefazolin, ceftriaxone, and ceftazidime in the central nervous system are
adequate to treat meningitis caused by highly susceptible organisms.
Meningitis secondary to N. meningitidis, H. influenzae, and Enterobacteriaceae can generally be
treated with these antibiotics.
Cefoperazone does not cross the blood brain barrier in sufficient concentration to treat
meningitis.

questions.question:
Which of the following sports may a patient with instability of the atlantoaxial
joint participate in?
questions.explanation:
Patients with atlantoaxial instability should be advised to avoid all contact sports and diving.
Noncontact sports other than diving are acceptable.

questions.question:
A 69 y/o male goes to his doctor because of recent onset of extreme difficulty
urinating with suprapubic pain and hematuria. He has over the last 3-4 months been experiencing
increasing mid-back pain which is constant, quite painful, occasionally debilitating and not relieved
by any change in position. There has also been numbness of the legs with intermittent weakness. He
has felt weak and lost about 20 pounds over the last 4 weeks. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The most likely diagnosis is metastatic prostate cancer to the spine. Other tumors that tend to
metastasize to the spine are breast, melanoma, kidney, lung, cervix, and pancreatic.
Thoracic meningioma does not usually cause spine pain.
Spinal stenosis normally produces only mild discomfort consistent with spondylosis in which
posture changes can reduce the back discomfort
Osteomyelitis can result in severe back pain. These conditions could lead to spinal cord
compression with lower extremity and bladder involvement but would not cause hematuria

questions.question:
Which of the following types of multiple sclerosis is most commonly
diagnosed?
questions.explanation:
80-85% of patients are diagnosed as have relapsing-remitting MS.
Some patients initially have relapsing-remitting disease but go on to have secondary progressive
MS.
Only 10% of patients have primary progressive MS.
Progressive/relapsing MS is characterized by a intermittant downhill progression.

questions.question:
A 25 year old female has intractable epistaxis and while undergoing arterial
embolization develops right sided weakness and a severe headache. Her pre-procedure skin exam
showed many tiny red lesions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia is also known as Osler-Weber-Rendu disease and can
cause epistaxis, GI bleeding, intracerebral hemorrhage, and cerebral abscesses
AVMs can be found in the lung, liver, and brain
This patient had an intracerebral hemorrhage
Pulmonary AVMs can cause shunting leading to cerebral and systemic abscesses

questions.question:
The most common cause of convergence-retraction nystagmus in a 10-year-
old?
questions.explanation:
Convergence-retraction nystagmus is a jerk convergence-retraction movement due to
cocontraction of the extraocular muscles, especially on attempted convergence or upward gaze
The etiology varies with age
In the newborn, congenital aqueductal stenosis is the most common cause; at age 10, pinealoma
is the most likely cause
Brain stem vascular malformations and head trauma and may be the cause in those 20 to 40,
while multiple sclerosis and basilar artery stroke are the most likely causes above the age of 40

questions.question: Which of the following does not apply to Protected Health Information?

answers.C: The patient decides what is private and what can be made public
answers.D: HIPAA defines as "any information, whether oral or recorded in any form or medium"

questions.printed_answer_heading: The patient decides what is private and what can be made public
questions.explanation:
The acronym for Protected Health Information is PHI.
Protected Health Information (PHI) is protected by HIPAA regulations.
The patient decides what information can be disclosed, however patient information is not for
public disclosure.
HIPAA defines as Protected Health Information (PHI) as "any information, whether oral or
recorded in any form or medium." Retrieved from:
http://dx.doi.org/10.1201/9780203501283.ch14

questions.question: Which of the following statements about tick paralysis is true?

answers.B: Removal of the tick is curative
answers.C: CT scan of the brain is imperative

questions.printed_answer_heading: Removal of the tick is curative
questions.explanation:
Tick paralysis is caused by a neurotoxin released in the saliva of an attached female tick
Onset of symptoms is within a few days after tick attachment and begins with irritability,
restlessness, and an ascending flaccid paralysis and possibly ataxia
Deep tendon reflexes are lost and the disease may rapidly progress causing bulbar paralysis and
respiratory depression
Death may result if the tick is not removed; removal of the tick is curative

questions.question:
Which of the following is the safest positioning to preserve neurologic function
prior to reduction and stabilization of a T12-L1 dislocation fracture with an incomplete neurologic
deficit?

answers.B: Lateral decubitus with lower extremities extended
answers.D: Prone with rolls under chest and thighs

questions.explanation:
Patients in the supine position have extension of the thoracolumbar spine at the level of a fixed
kyphosis secondary to the dislocation fracture
This causes further narrowing of an already compromised spinal canal
Placing the patient in the lateral decubitus position with the knees flexed may provide enough
decompression to allow improvement in an individual who is neurologically incomplete

questions.question:
The thoracolumbar spine is described by Denis classification. Which of the
following is correct about Denis classification?
questions.explanation:
The 3 columns are as follows
Anterior longitudinal ligament, anterior half of vertebral body, and anterior portion of annulus
fibrosis are the anterior column
Posterior longitudinal ligament, posterior half of vertebral body, and posterior aspect of annulus
fibrosis are the middle column
Neural arch, ligamentum flavum, facet capsule, and interspinous ligament are the posterior
column

questions.question:
You are to administer bethanechol chloride (Urecholine) to a client
experiencing acute postoperative nonobstructive urine retention. Prior to administering this drug, you
will:

answers.A: Gather and prepare the necessary IV equipment
answers.B: Have acetylcholine injectable available and ready to administer
answers.C: Administer a SQ test dose of the medication
answers.D: Teach the client that the drug's effects are usually felt within 3 to 4 hours of administration

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Teach the client that the drug's effects are usually felt within 3 to 4 hours of
administration
questions.explanation:
A test dose of bethanechol chloride (Urecholine) will always be given SQ to determine the
minimal effective dose. A 2.5-mg SQ dose is given and then repeated every 15 to 30 minutes for
a total of 4 doses
Bethanechol chloride should never be given IV or IM since it could cause circulatory collapse
Injectable atropine (an anticholinergic) should be available to provide circulatory support if
needed.
The effects of bethanechol chloride (Urecholine) are felt within 30 to 90 minutes

questions.question:
Optic nerve glioma occurs in what percent of patients with neurofibromatosis
type 1:
questions.explanation:
Optic nerve glioma is the most common intracranial tumor associated with neurofibromatosis
It occurs in about 10 to 15 percent patients with neurofibromatosis type 1
It is associated with chromosomal 17q11.2 defect

questions.question:
Which of the following is least important in a bowel program of patients with
spinal cord injury (SCI)?
questions.explanation:
The most important factors in a bowel program for patients with SCI are a regular schedule, hot
fluid intake, and rectal stimulation with suppository or manually
A high fiber diet is recommended

questions.question:
Exam of a patient for a gait disturbance is in progress. While the patient is
supine, the examiner places a hand behind one knee and rapidly raises it. The foot initially is also
raised off the exam table. On repetition of the maneuver, the foot drags across the table. This is not
repeated on the other leg or at the forearm-wrist area. Select the true statement about his patient.

answers.A: The patient has musculoskeletal injury resulting in decreased muscle tone
answers.B: The patient has paratonia that may be normal
answers.C: The patient exhibits rigidity and may have Parkinsonism
answers.D: The patient may have motor neuron disease causing decreased muscle tone

questions.printed_answer_heading: The patient has paratonia that may be normal
questions.explanation:
Fluctuating changes in resistance during testing of motor tone is called paratonia
It may be secondary to difficulty relaxing during an exam or with aberrant frontal lobe pathways
Increased tone, as seen in this patient, makes muscle injury unlikely
Cogwheel rigidity with jerky resistance found in Parkinsonism is not present and would not be
focal

questions.question: What muscle grade is characterized by full range of motion against gravity?
questions.explanation:
Muscle grade 5 is characterized by full normal range of motion against resistance and gravity
Muscle grade 4 is characterized by full normal range of motion against gravity and minimal
resistance
Muscle grade 3 is characterized by full normal range of motion against only gravity
Muscle grade 2 is characterized by full range of motion without gravity

questions.question: Which of the following is a positive Homan sign?

answers.C: Dorsiflexion of the ankle resulting in pain in the calf

questions.printed_answer_heading: Dorsiflexion of the ankle resulting in pain in the calf
questions.explanation:
Calf pain experienced upon dorsiflexion of the ankle is a positive Homan sign may indicate
deep-vein thrombosis.
Homan sign is not diagnostic of DVT.
It is 30 to 72% specific and 60-88% sensitive if seen with pain and erythema.
Venous duplex is generally used for diagnosis.

questions.question:
A 40 y/o male is referred to a neurologist because of increasing weakness in
the arms with loss of manual dexterity in hands, cramping and twitching. He has occasional trouble
swallowing and enunciating words. Neuro exam reveals weakness in arms, relatively normal strength
in legs, slight hyperactivity in leg reflexes and fasciculations of tongue. Sensory exam is normal. What
is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
75% of ALS begins in the limbs. It is a disease that involves a combination of loss of neurons of
ventral horn of spinal cord and cerebral cortex.
That is why there may be a combination of muscle weakness with atrophy and some findings of
rigidity and spasticity. 25% of patients begin with bulbar findings.
Multiple sclerosis would be expected to have some sensory findings. Guillain-Barre usually
begins as numbness and weakness in the legs that spreads superiorly.
A foramen magnum meningioma would be expected to produce weakness in all extremities with
hyperreflexia throughout.

questions.question:
The highest incidence of cerebrospinal fluid leak occurs with which approach
when resecting an acoustic neuroma?
questions.explanation:
The retro sigmoid approach provides good exposure to all acoustic neuromas but also leads to
several complications
The incidence of CSF leak is highest with this approach
Moreover, the highest incidence of tumor recurrence is also common with this approach

questions.question: Amyloid protein is usually stained with:
questions.explanation:
Amyloid is a proteinaceous material, which is easily identified by Congo red
The protein can appear apple green and birefringent under polarized light

questions.question:
A 68 year old has been hit in the head and his GCS is 12. In the ER, his pupils
are equal and reactive and his hemodynamics are stable. 1 hr later his BP is 190/100 and right pupil
is larger than the left. All of the following are important in the immediate management except?
questions.explanation:
In a patient with elevated ICP, the first step is to ensure airway and oxygenation
Hyperventilation to a PCO2 of 30 can help constrict cerebral blood vessels and lower
intracranial pressure
Mannitol can be used to remove excess fluid and also relieve ICP
A patient with rising intracranial pressure should never be sent to the CT scan suite without first
being stabilized. Irrespective of the cause, the treatment for elevated ICP is the same

questions.question: Methylparaben allergy prohibits the use of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Methylparaben is the preservative found in lidocaine

questions.question:
Whichof the following muscle innervations is intact with C5 spinal cord
lesion?
questions.explanation:
A C5 spinal cord lesion is characterized by the innervations of the rotator cuff, biceps, and
deltoid muscles remaining intact

questions.question: What imaging modalities is best to diagnose Chiari type 1 malformations?

answers.B: Magnetic resonance image of the brain
answers.D: Magnetic resonance image of the lumbar spine

questions.printed_answer_heading: Magnetic resonance image of the brain
questions.explanation:
The best imaging to detect Chiari type 1 malformation is the sagittal image of an MRI of the
brain.
It would show triangular or pointed cerebellar tonsils that descend 5 mm or more below the
foramen magnum. This results in obliteration of the CSF space at the cervicomedullary junction.
A CT might show a crowded foramen magnum.
The lower brainstem and bulbomedullary junction are not adequately visualized on CT
myelogram.

questions.question: What percent of population have anisocoria?
questions.explanation: Around 20 percent of population have unequal size pupils

questions.question: MRI signal with traumatic cord injury has what appearance?

answers.A: Both T1 and T2 signal is increased
answers.B: T1 signal is isointense to cord; T2 signal is increased
answers.C: T1 signal is hypointense; T2 signal is hyperintense
answers.D: The earliest finding is cord swelling but no signal change

questions.printed_answer_heading: T1 signal is isointense to cord; T2 signal is increased
questions.explanation:
The signal changes are due to cord edema, not hematomyelia, which is not commonly present
As the edema resolves, the cord appearance improves
Cord swelling may also be present

questions.question: Where is the location of the Broca's area?
questions.explanation:
The Broca's area is located the left hemisphere
Lesion in the Broca's area results in speech deficit
The Wernicke's area is also located in the left hemisphere
Lesion in this area results in speech receptive defect

questions.question: Brain abscess is least likely after:
questions.explanation:
It is very rare for meningitis causes an abscess.
The most common causes of brain abscess are infections from contiguous sites like the ear,
mastoid and sinuses.
Congenital heart disease and skull trauma are other common causes of brain abscess.

questions.question:
Patient has reduction in factor VIII and has bleeding after tooth extraction.
Ristocetin fails to cause platelet aggregation. The next treatment is:
questions.explanation:
The patient with hemophilia A is often pretreated before surgery.
DDAVP will raise the levels of von Willebrand factor and may lower risk of bleeding.
This patient should be treated with recombinant factor VIII.
This is less likely to result in viral transmission than cryoprecipitate or fresh frozen plasma.

questions.question: Epinephrine increases the effectiveness of lidocaine by:
questions.explanation: Epinephrine reduces absorption of lidocaine by vasoconstriction

questions.question:
If a trauma patient has clear fluid draining from the nose the provider should
do which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Clear drainage following head trauma is indicative if a cerebrospinal fluid leak so it needs to be
analyzed
The other interventions are inappropriate in this case

questions.question: Which is not a presentation of familial hemiplegic migraine?
questions.explanation:
Familial hemiplegic migraine is an autosomal dominant disease
Characterized by hemiplegia followed by a migraine headache
Gene is located on chromosome nineteen

questions.question: An Oppenheim reflex is accomplished by downward irritation of the the:
questions.explanation:
Rossolimo reflex is accomplished by tapping the foot
Mayers reflex is performed by flexion of the digits
Oppenheim reflex is performed by stroking the tibia eliciting dorsiflexion of the great toe
indicating pyramidal tract pathology
Ciliospinal reflex is accomplished by pinching the neck

questions.question: Which of the following substances has a role in pain perception?
questions.explanation:
Endorphins are released by stress and have a marked role in pain perception
Another substance that has a role in pain perception is substance-P
Dopamine is implicated in psychotic problems
Serotonin is implicated in mood disorders

questions.question: What is homonymous hemianopia?

answers.A: A visual defect involving half of the field of vision in both eyes on the same side
answers.B: A visual defect involving half of the field of vision in one eye
answers.C: A visual defect involving half of the field of vision in one eye and the other half in the other eye
answers.D: A visual defect involving the peripheral vision

questions.printed_answer_heading: A visual defect involving half of the field of vision in both eyes on the same side
questions.explanation:
Homonymous hemianopia is loss of the same half of the field of vision in both eyes tunnel vision
Loss of peripheral vision is called
Hemianopia is loss of half of the field of vision and can affect only one eye
When half the field of vision is lost, the division is a vertical line

questions.question: Which is false about phenytoin?

answers.B: Blood levels can be affected by other medications
answers.C: Gingival hyperplasia is a troubling side effect

questions.explanation:
Phenytoin is used to treat epilepsy, most commonly the tonic-clonic type
Phenytoin is not used for absence seizures and may exacerbate the condition.
It can cause nystagmus especially if levels are toxic. It can cause folate not thiamine
deficiencies.
Other adverse effects include gingival hyperplasia, ataxia, drowsiness, vertigo, and pruritis.

questions.question:
A transsphenoidal hypophysectomy is done with an incision through which
structure?
questions.explanation:
Transsphenoidal hypophysectomy is performed with incision between the upper lip and gum
It transverses through the sphenoid sinus

questions.question:
The initial treatment for a patient with a hemolytic transfusion reaction is
which of the following?
questions.explanation: The immediate treatment of hemolytic reaction is to stop the transfusion

questions.question:
A patient has an MRI showing deposition of iron in the globus pallidus and
retina. Which symptom is least likely initially?
questions.explanation:
The patient has Hallervorden-Spatz syndrome
Onset is most commonly in late childhood or early adolescence but may be later in life with a
persistent downhill course with death in 10 to 12 years with few exceptions
Dementia is a common finding
Treatment of symptoms is all that is available include anti-Parkinson and anticholinergic
medications

questions.question:
Pupils that are bilaterally small and constrict when the patient focuses but do
not constrict in the presence of light are due to?
questions.explanation:
Argyll Robertson pupils are bilateral small and constrict when one focuses. However, the pupils
do not constrict when exposed to light

questions.question: A bloody tap during lumbar puncture is usually due to?
questions.explanation:
Intracerebral hemorrhage generally does not present with blood in the CSF
If the aorta is accidently injured, the blood flow can be spurting but it is very rare unless the
needle was not in the midline
Blood observed initially after a LP is usually traumatic and may be due to injury to the spinal
venous plexus
Often the fluid will clear as succeeding tubes are filled. If the red blood cells have been in the
spinal fluid for some time, xanthochromia will be present

questions.question:
Endoscopic transsphenoidal hypophysectomy is characterized by which of the
following?

answers.A: A large incision at the junction of the gum and upper lip
answers.B: A panoramic view of the surgical field
answers.C: An excellent three-dimensional view of the surgical field
answers.D: Greater risk of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak than traditional transsphenoidal hypophysectomy

questions.printed_answer_heading: A panoramic view of the surgical field
questions.explanation:
Endoscopic transsphenoidal hypophysectomy requires no external incision
Unlike traditional transsphenoidal hypophysectomy, it does not provide a three-dimensional
view of the surgical field, but it does provide a panoramic view
The risk of CSF leak is generally less with endoscopic than traditional transsphenoidal
hypophysectomy

questions.question: Which hormone is responsible for lactation?
questions.explanation:
Prolactin is produced in the anterior pituitary gland
It is responsible for lactation

questions.question: The most important stimulus for cerebral blood flow is?
questions.explanation: Autoregulation of cerebral blood flow is mostly regulated by carbon dioxide

questions.question:
A female has atrophy and flaccid paralysis of the right ankle muscles.
Blockage of which artery would cause the findings?
questions.explanation:
Lumbosacral anterior spinal arteries blockage would affect the anterior portion of the spinal
cord, including the anterior horns
This would cause the motor deficits and atrophy
The middle cerebral artery supplies the lateral cortex and would cause paralysis but not atrophy
The posterior spinal arteries supply the dorsal cord

questions.question: What type of inheritance pattern is followed by Rett syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Rett syndrome is an X linked dominant disease
Symptoms presents after one year of age

questions.question: Select the true statement about epidural anesthesia.

answers.A: It can be used in patients with a hemorrhagic diathesis
answers.B: It can be associated with hypotension
answers.C: It provides anesthesia for the sacral and lumbar nerve roots only
answers.D: The catheter should be placed at the L2-L3 level

questions.printed_answer_heading: It can be associated with hypotension
questions.explanation:
The catheter is placed at the L3-L4 interspace
A full dose provides anesthesia to nerve roots T10 to S5
Drug reaction, hypotension, and rare neurologic complications can occur
Adverse affects to anesthesia, bleeding tendency, infection of the lumbar area, or underlying
neurologic defects are all contraindications

questions.question:
A 16 year old male is brought in for recurrent unilateral throbbing headaches
with associated visual aura, nausea, vomiting, and photophonophobia. MRI is done and the patient is
referred for a cerebral angiogram. What is the most likely incidental finding prompting the referral?
questions.explanation:
The history is classic for migraine headache.
The most common incidental finding would be an arteriovenous malformation that can cause
intracranial hemorrhage.
An angiogram will be needed to evaluate the lesions.
An arachnoid cyst would not require treatment.

questions.question: Which of the following about hemorrhoids is false?
questions.explanation:
Shoulder pain is related to C5 spinal nerve injury
C5 controls muscle innervation to the biceps and brachioradialis
C6 injury relates to numbness of lateral forearm and hand
C7 controls medial two fingers

questions.question: The blood supply to the spinal cord does not come from which artery?
questions.explanation: Spinal cord is supplied by one anterior and two posterior spinal arteries

questions.question: White rami communicantes contain which of the following fibers?

answers.A: Preganglionic general efferent and visceral fibers

questions.printed_answer_heading: Preganglionic general efferent and visceral fibers
questions.explanation:
The white rami communicantes contains visceral and preganglionic general efferent fibers.
All the thoracic and the first 2 lumbar nerves contribute to the adjoining sympathetic ganglion.
The preganglionic sympathetic fibers are myelinated.
The white rami communicantes is not present below L2.

questions.question:
A 65 y/o male is admitted to the ER with left hemiparesis but is awake and
alert. CT scan shows no intracranial hemorrhage or tumor and the infarct area is not well visualized
at this time. The patientâ€™s symptoms developed approximately 2 hours ago. There is no past
history of stroke. He had recent arthroscopic knee surgery. He is given TPA. Which of the following
would not be a contraindication to this therapy?

answers.A: Seizure at the time of stroke
answers.C: Systolic blood pressure greater than 175 mm Hg

questions.explanation:
Many institutions follow the NINDS (National institute of neurological disorders and stroke)
criteria which is the gold standard. Additional exclusionary criteria are platelet count <100,000,
greater than 3 hours from onset of symptoms to therapy, heparin within 48 hours, elevated PTT,
known history of intracranial hemorrhage, history of CVA within 3 months, and glucose >400 or
<50
NIHSS (national institute of health stroke scale) measures 11 areas and the score can range from
0-42. Some institutions use a score of >22 as a relative reason to not use thrombolytics
The criteria is being challenged and liberalized with other studies. SMART (simplified
management of acute stroke using revised treatment criteria) has increased the time period to
start therapy from 3 hours to 4.5 hours. With this new timeframe comes some new restrictions to
using TPA followed by some centers such as NIHSS >25 and >80 years

questions.question: Jugular foramen syndrome includes all the following signs except?
questions.explanation:
Glomus jugulare tun ors or basal skull fractures may cause jugular foramen syndrome
The vagus nerve, the glossopharyngeal nerve, and the spinal accessory nerve can be injured in
this syndrome
Clinical signs include ipsilateral sternocleidomastoid and trapezius weakness, dysphagia,
dysphonia, depressed gag reflex, ipsilateral loss of taste in the ipsilateral posterior third of the
tongue, ipsilateral vocal cord paresis, and anesthesia of the posterior third of the tongue
Because the twelfth cranial nerve is not involved, the tongue does not deviate

questions.question:
A construction worker fell 2 stories suffering a head injury. In the ER, he is
unresponsive and posturing with his forearms flexed close to his body and legs rigidly extended with
internal rotation and plantar flexion. What is this condition called?
questions.explanation:
It indicates an injury above the red nucleus in the midbrain
Decerebrate posturing involves the arms rigidly extended close to the body with internal rotation
and the legs stiffly extended.
Diffuse hyperreflexia may indicate spinal cord compression in the cervical region.

questions.question: Which of the following is the feared side effect of phenytoin?
questions.explanation:
Gingival hyperplasia occurs with long term use of phenytoin
Hirsutism and acne may also occur as well
Rare side effects include ataxia, Stevens Johnson syndrome, and diplopia

questions.question:
Signs and symptoms of cervical radiculopathy include all of the following
except:

answers.C: Pain that is worse at night
answers.D: Pain with active but not passive movement

questions.printed_answer_heading: Pain with active but not passive movement
questions.explanation:
Cervical radiculopathy is a problem with the roots of the cervical nerves, most commonly C6
and C7 and can be caused by injury, disc herniation, osteophytes, and degenerative changes
Findings on physical exam may include head tilting away from injured size, limitation of active
range of motion of affected shoulder, tenderness of paraspinal muscles, weakness of elbow
flexion and wrist extension (C6), weakness of elbow extension and wrist flexion (C7), and a
positive Spurling test (pain with downward pressure on the head when it is rotated with the neck
extended)
Choice 4 occurs with rotator cuff tendonitis

questions.question: Which of the following is true about central cord syndrome?

answers.A: Proprioception is lost but motor function is intact
answers.B: There is loss of motor function but vibration and temperature sensations are intact
answers.C: There is greater involvement of the upper extremities
answers.D: There is greater loss of pain sensation than other sensory deficits

questions.printed_answer_heading: There is greater involvement of the upper extremities
questions.explanation:
Central cord syndrome is secondary to acute injury to the cervical spine
The upper extremities are more affected than the lower extremities
There can be sensory loss distal to the injury
There can be urinary retention

questions.question:
A patient presents to the emergency room with a headache in is suspected to
have either an intracranial bleed or mass lesion. Which of the following is the diagnostic procedure
of choice?

answers.B: CT of the brain with contrast
answers.C: CT of the brain without contrast

questions.printed_answer_heading: CT of the brain without contrast
questions.explanation:
CT of the brain is the procedure of choice as it is more sensitive than MRI for an acute bleed
Contrast may interfere with visualization of subarachnoid blood
CT is generally more available on emergent basis; MRI takes longer and limits access to the
patient who may be unstable
LP should never be done without ruling out mass lesions

questions.question:
A patient developed acute dystonia just before he was about to undergo
surgery. Which one of the following preoperative medications could have caused this?
questions.explanation:
It is caused by drug-induced alteration of dopaminergic-cholinergic balance
Antipsychotic medication that act on dopamine receptors are commonly implicated
Metoclopramide is an antiemetic that can be helpful as a preoperative medication
Acute dystonia can occur with Metoclopramide administration

questions.question: The second most common site of cervical herniation in adults is?
questions.explanation:
C6-C7 is the most common level for cervical herniation accounting for 50%
C5-C6 is the next most common level accounting for 30%

questions.question: Which is the most common type of stroke with a gradual onset?
questions.explanation:
Thrombotic strokes comprise 40% of all strokes, followed by embolic strokes (30%), lacunar
strokes (20%), and hemorrhagic strokes (10%).
Thrombotic and lacunar strokes usually have a gradual onset, whereas embolic and hemorrhagic
strokes usually have a sudden onset.

questions.question:
A 59 year old man with advanced Parkinson disease has progressively lost
effective response to multiple Parkinson's medications and has begun to develop adverse effects.
Functional activities of daily living are impaired. In considering surgical options, all the following
are accepted surgical interventions for advanced Parkinson currently except:
questions.explanation:
Unilateral pallidotomy is standard but bilateral pallidotomy is rarely performed at this time
Unilateral pallidotomy is used for advanced dyskinesias and fluctuating response to L-dopa
Deep brain stimulation is effective for advanced patients with rigidity, akinesia and postural
disturbances

questions.question: Which of the following medications is a known enzyme inducer?
questions.explanation:
Many drugs can induce liver enzymes and result in reduced bioavailability of medications
Phenobarb is among the commonly used medications that induces liver metabolism
Ritonavir, Cimetidine and Erythromycin are all liver enzyme inhibitors

questions.question:
After a transsphenoidal hypophysectomy, a patient develops a cerebrospinal
fluid (CSF) leak. Which is the most appropriate initial management?

answers.B: Application of topical thrombin to the leakage site
answers.C: Insertion of a lumbar CSF drain
answers.D: Urgent surgery to repair the leak

questions.explanation:
The initial management of a CSF leak should include bed rest with head elevation to lower the
intracranial pressure
Many leaks will heal spontaneously
Topical thrombin is not helpful because the primary problem is a hole in the dura, not a blood
coagulation defect

questions.question:
A pharmaceutical representative offers a "drug dinner" or an opportunity to
have a gourmet meal with an accompanying lecture. Which of the following is the best option?

answers.C: Discuss the offer with legal counsel
answers.D: Report the pharmaceutical representative to the FDA

questions.explanation:
Pharmaceutical companies have been severely limited in their abilities to provide compensation
to caregivers
"Drug dinners" are still allowed but of somewhat questionable value educationally
The money would be better spent subsidizing traditional conferences
review_required: Question text and options repeated elsewhere in source PDF

questions.question:
A nurse is taking care of a patient who is being treated for elevated ICP
following a head injury. An ICP monitor has been inserted into the brain. All of the following
statements about hyperventilation are correct EXCEPT:

answers.C: Brain will readjust to PCO2 in 48-72 hours
answers.D: Increasing hyperventilation is not recommended for ICP spikes

questions.printed_answer_heading: Increasing hyperventilation is not recommended for ICP spikes
questions.explanation:
In a normal brain a 1 mm change in PCO2 will change CBF 2.5% in the 30-60 range
In using hyperventilation for ICP, one must weigh the advantage of decreasing elevations vs.
causing vasoconstriction which reduces blood flow to the brain
In addition, PCO2 of 25-30 will also contribute to hypotension from a reduction of venous return
When confronted with a dangerous spike in ICP, it is appropriate to increase the
hyperventilation temporarily

questions.question:
Which is a predictor of a poorer prognosis with subarachnoid hemorrhage
(SAH)?

answers.C: Younger age at time of SAH

questions.explanation:
History of cigarette smoking, a higher grade of SAH, and complications predict a poorer
prognosis for SAH

questions.question:
All of the following statements about syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic
hormone, SIADH, is correct EXCEPT?

answers.A: The urine output should be diminished
answers.B: The urine specific gravity should be decreased
answers.C: The serum sodium will be decreased

questions.explanation:
The SIADH can result from head trauma, brain tumors, non-cerebral cancers, meningitis, and
encephalitis
ADH is released to stimulate the kidneys to absorb water when the body's serum osmolality is
increased and prior to becoming dehydrated
Normal serum osmolality is 275-299 mOsm/kg
The urine specific gravity is increased. Normal serum sodium is 135-145 mEq/L. Sodium of
120-125 will cause lethargy, confusion, nausea, and vomiting. A level of 110 could lead to
seizures and death

questions.question:
A true statement about aneurysms in a parasellar/cavernous sinus distribution
include:

answers.B: Aneurysm rupture within the cavernous sinus leads to tamponade
answers.C: CN III, IV, V1, V2, and VI can be damaged by such aneurysms
answers.D: Anisocoria can be caused by pressure from an aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery

questions.printed_answer_heading: CN III, IV, V1, V2, and VI can be damaged by such aneurysms
questions.explanation:
If a carotid aneurysm ruptures in the cavernous sinus, a C-C fistula is formed
The only complaints may be ophthalmic
All CNs traveling in the cavernous sinus may be involved/compressed by aneurysms
Anisocoria can be due to impingement of the peripheral pupillary nerve fibers in CN III due to
an adjacent POSTERIOR communicating artery

questions.question:
All of the following statements about complications of ventriculoperitoneal
shunt placement are correct EXCEPT:

answers.C: Subdural hematoma from perforating the dura

questions.printed_answer_heading: Subdural hematoma from perforating the dura
questions.explanation:
Other complications include bowel and urinary bladder perforation, infection, and shunt
malfunction.
Subdural hematoma could result from over drainage
This is particularly likely in the elderly in which the dura tends to be adhered to the underlying
bone. If too much CSF is drained, the brain will shrink away from the dura tearing a bridging
vein
Slit ventricle syndrome is a subcategory of over drainage condition

questions.question:
A patient is brought in by family for memory problems. The physical exam is
normal but the mini mental exam score is 19 and the clinical diagnosis is dementia. CT of the brain
and labs are normal. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation:
