Most patients with Alzheimer disease have a gradual decline of function first losing instrumental
activities of daily living and then ADLs
The most common cause of dementia is Alzheimer disease
Lewy body disease would more likely show movement difficulties
Vascular dementia would likely have abnormalities on CT and Pick disease would show loss of
inhibition and personality changes

questions.question:
A 55-year-old male complains of left sided facial pain. The pain is a shooting,
severe, and occurs several times a day. First line treatment would be which of the following
medications?
questions.explanation:
The patient most likely has trigeminal neuralgia, which is neuropathy of CN 5
The drug of choice is carbamazepine, which is structurally related to tricyclic antidepressants
The medication's mechanism of action is related to the inhibition of voltage

questions.question:
Which of the following incontinence care methods is recommended for
paraplegic patients?
questions.explanation:
Patients can be thought to self catheterize themselves.
Indwelling catheters puts patients at high risk of infection.
Using strict aseptic methods is very important to avoid infection.
Most laxatives should not be used on a daily basis.

questions.question: In adults, normal physiological rate of cerebral blood flow is:
questions.explanation: Under normal physiologic condition, the cerebral blood flow at a rate of 35 mL per minute

questions.question:
Which of the following reason(s) would make it advantageous to evaluate a
patient with a suspected stroke using MRI vs. CT scan?

answers.A: Ability to visualize early brainstem strokes and small infarcts
answers.B: Ability to ascertain ischemic stroke damage

questions.explanation:
Diffusion weighted MRI can show early stroke changes while perfusion weighted MRI can
assess cerebral blood flow and blood volume
Research is ongoing on determining and quantifying salvageable brain. Some neuroradiologists
advocate the potential of CT perfusion scan to be a better predictor but this remains
controversial
MRI can show blood and determine the age of the bleed. This is because blood breaks down
through stages: oxyhemoglobin to deoxyhemoglobin to methemoglobin to ferritin and
hemosiderin

questions.question:
Anticonvulsants such as phenobarbital and benzodiazepines such as lorazepam
exert their influence through which of the following types of receptors?
questions.explanation:
Many anticonvulsants and benzodiazepines exert their action with affinity for the GABA
receptors

questions.question: Patients taking furosemide should also be given:
questions.explanation:
Potassium supplementation is needed in patients taking loop diuretics
Loop diuretics commonly result in electrolyte disturbances
This is particularly dangerous for patients who are also taking digoxin
KCl oral tablets are used to supplement the potassium lost during diuretic therapy

questions.question:
A patient is involved in a MVA and suffers multi organ trauma. He is brought
to the ER by EMS and found to be hypotensive, tachycardic and his abdomen is distended. He is
disoriented and confused. He has a GCS of 9 and his legs are warm and the pulses thready. The most
likely cause of his shock state is due to?
questions.explanation:
When the peripheral circulation vasodilates it causes the SVR to drop. The cardiac output in
neurogenic shock is often increased because the BP is low. In neurogenic shock the body loses
its ability to regulate flow to other organs
In neurogenic shock, the cardiac output is usually normal but there is a low BP. The peripheries
are warm and the pulses are palpable
Individuals will show severely depressed mental findings or paralysis, oliguria and lactic
acidosis. Treatment requires combination of inotropes and vasopressors like dopamine.
Profound blood loss from trauma causes hypotension, tachycardia, low CVP, oliguria and weak
pulses.

questions.question: Select the finding that would not indicate aspiration.

answers.B: Clearing the throat while drinking or eating
answers.C: A wet quality to the voice while drinking

questions.explanation:
Emesis would not indicate aspiration
Coughing, clearing the throat, or a change in speech can indicate aspiration

questions.question: A prophylactic antibiotic is indicated:

answers.A: Prior to a foley catheter placement
answers.C: Prior to insertion of a central line
answers.D: To decrease incidence of surgical site infection prior to elective surgery

questions.printed_answer_heading: To decrease incidence of surgical site infection prior to elective surgery
questions.explanation:
Prophylactic antibiotics do not prevent many types of infections such as urinary tract infections,
ventilator-associated pneumonia, or intravenous line sepsis
Prophylactic antibiotics are able to decrease the risk of infection in certain elective surgery
procedures
Prophylactic antibiotics are not recommended for all surgery and misuse can lead to
development of resistance

questions.question: A patient with spinal cord injury can best be treated for his pain with:
questions.explanation: PCA allows titration of drug by the patient

questions.question: Which is not associated with Guillain Barre syndrome?

answers.C: Autonomic dysfunction, such as fluctuations in heart rate and blood pressure

questions.explanation: About 20% require mechanical ventilation

questions.question: Bamboo spine is commonly seen in:
questions.explanation:
The diagnosis of ankylosing spondylitis is made by a combination of clinical features and x-ray
signs
The radiographic feature of ankylosing spondylitis is enthesitis of the annulus fibrosis
Ossification of the annulus fibrosis leads to a bamboo spine
Peripheral joint involvement is most common in the hips and shoulders in ankylosing spondylitis

questions.question:
A 67 year old female is brought to the emergency department with a 1 hour
history of right sided weakness and aphasia. She has a history of atrial fibrillation on aspirin only.
The patient is alert and able to follow one step commands. There is impairment of rightward gaze and
left gaze deviation. Right face and arm flaccid paresis is present but she can lift her right leg up.
There are decreased reflexes on the right side. What is the diagnostic study of choice?
questions.explanation:
The patient has had an acute cerebrovascular accident
A CT scan will determine if the CVA is ischemic or hemorrhagic
If ischemic, treatment with TPA is indicated as symptoms have been present for less than 3 hours
The other tests will take longer perhaps delaying treatment

questions.question: In a patient with tabes dorsalis, you would suspect?
questions.explanation:
Tabes dorsalis is a myeloneuropathy that involves dorsal root ganglion
It is associated with syphilis infection
Characterized by sensory pain, ataxia, and urinary incontinence

questions.question:
A one-month-old infant is brought to the emergency department after a seizure.
The patient has had a fever to 102.2°F and vomiting. The infant had hepatitis B vaccine at birth.
Lumbar puncture is preformed and the CSF is cloudy. CSF glucose is 30 mg/dL, protein is 50 mg/dL,
and opening pressure is 150 mm H2O. Gram stain shows gram-negative coccobacilli. What antibiotic
should be started?
questions.explanation:
The gram stain most likely shows Haemophilus B (HIB)
The HIB vaccine has reduced the incidence but this child has not received the first dose
Ceftriaxone is a 3rd generation cephalosporin, which will cover HIB
Vancomycin is for gram-positive organisms, Moxifloxacin is a quinolone and not appropriate for
infants

questions.question:
How long should an isolated calf deep venous thrombosis be treated with
anticoagulation?
questions.explanation:
Deep venous thrombosis below the knee should be treated with anticoagulation for 3 to 6 months
provided the etiology was of transient nature and there is no evidence of long term
hypercoagulability
Most patients are started on low molecular weight heparin and transitioned to warfarin.

questions.question: The most frequent complication of cordotomy is:
questions.explanation:
Cordotomy has about 6 percent complication rate.
Almost all patients develop numbness and tingling.
Horner syndrome is also very common after cordotomy.
Ipsilateral leg weakness is the 3rd most common complication.

questions.question:
What muscle grade is characterized by full range of motion against full
resistance?
questions.explanation:
Muscle grade 5 is characterized by full normal range of motion against resistance and gravity
Muscle grade 4 is characterized by full normal range of motion against gravity and minimal
resistance
Muscle grade 3 is characterized by full normal range of motion against only gravity
Muscle grade 2 is characterized by full range of motion without gravity

questions.question: Characteristics of autonomic hyperreflexia include which of the following?

answers.B: Neurologic level of injury below T7

questions.explanation:
Autonomic hyperreflexia is seen in patients with spinal cord injuries with neurologic levels of
T6 and above
Headache and hypertension, often with bradycardia, are hallmarks of the syndrome

questions.question: Which of the following findings defines Scheuermann kyphosis?

answers.A: Thoracic rigidity on hyperextension lateral radiographs
answers.B: The presence of thoracic disk space narrowing
answers.C: Three adjacent vertebral bodies with at least 5° of anterior wedging

questions.printed_answer_heading: Three adjacent vertebral bodies with at least 5° of anterior wedging
questions.explanation:
All of the above are findings associated with Scheuermann kyphosis; however it is defined by
the anterior wedging of 3 consecutive vertebral bodies of at least 5°

questions.question:
A preferable type of liability insurance policy which provides coverage for the
insured for all acts occurring during the period the policy was in effect, regardless of when the
lawsuit is filed:
questions.explanation:
Occurrence policies are difficult for the company that provides the coverage due to the inability
to plan long range and liability coverage
With a claims made policy coverage must be at the time of the incident through the time the
lawsuit is filed

questions.question: What is the most common cause of death in patients with spinal cord injuries?
questions.explanation:
Cardiovascular disease is the major cause of mortality in the general population and in SCI
patients
The other conditions are more common in SCI but are less frequently cause of death

questions.question: Which neuropathway controls pressure and vibration?
questions.explanation:
Pain and temperature sensation travels via the spinothalamic tract
Vibration and pressure travels via the posterior columns
The corticospinal tract transmits neural signals to skeletal muscle

questions.question:
Which of the following can be added to lidocaine to reduce the burning
sensation when it is administered?
questions.explanation:
In some cases it is appropriate to add sodium bicarbonate to acid lidocaine to reduce discomfort
with injection.
Epinephrine is added as a vasoconstrictor to keep the lidocaine in the area and to decrease
bleeding.

questions.question: Where is the substantia gelatinosa of the spinal cord?
questions.explanation:
The spinal cordâ€™s grey matter is divided into the 10 laminae of Rexed.
This provides a cytoarchitectonic map of the spinal cord that assists in interpretation of
neurophysiological data and synaptic connections.
Laminae I through IV comprise most of the dorsal horn.
Lamina I is the nucleus postmarginalis, lamina II is the substantia gelatinosa, and laminae III and
IV are the nucleus proprius dorsalis.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a symptom associated with diabetes insipidus?
questions.explanation:
Diabetes insipidus is suggested by high urine output with low osmolality and hypernatremia
Psychogenic polydipsia usually has an almost normal sodium level

questions.question:
In a 45-year-old female with a pituitary mass, the most common hormone
secreted is:
questions.explanation:
The most common tumor secreted by pituitary gland is prolactin
Prolactinomas generally are asymptomatic

questions.question:
All of the following statements about cardiovascular risks of sumatriptan are
correct EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Sumatriptan (Imitrex) is a triptan sulfa drug that is structurally similar to serotonin (5HT)
As a 5HT agonist it activates receptors that cause vasoconstriction
Other risks include ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation. It should not be given to
patients with coronary artery disease
Dihydroergotamine has similar complications

questions.question: The average turnover time of cerebrospinal fluid is?
questions.explanation: Complete turnover of cerebrospinal fluid occurs in about 8 hours

questions.question:
A patient develops meningitis after head trauma. The patient expires and the
autopsy reveals softening of brain and diffuse edema. The type of necrosis is defined as:
questions.explanation:
Liquefaction necrosis is transformation of solid tissue into fluid
Liquefactive necrosis is tyoical of bactareial or fungal infections
The necrosis is due to release of hydrolytic enzymes
Liquefactive necrosis often results in abscess fromation

questions.question: Normal levels of glucose in the CSF are usually associated with:
questions.explanation:
CSF glucose levels usually are 60 percent of the peripheral blood glucose levels
Low levels of glucose in CSF are usually associated with bacterial, fungal and mycobacterial
infections
High CSF glucose levels have no diagnostic significance

questions.question: Primidone is used to treat:
questions.explanation: Primidone treats grand mal seizures

questions.question: Which of the following describes the term credentialing?

answers.B:
The process and verification assuring the practitioner meets pre-established criteria for practice
in a network or organization
answers.C: The broad term used for those who are licensed to practice
answers.D:
The review and verification process used to determine the current clinical competence of a
practitioner

questions.explanation:
Credentialing is the process and verification assuring the practitioner meets pre-established
criteria for practice in a network or organization.
Credentialing is also the review and verification process used to determine the current clinical
competence of a practitioner.
Each organization has pre-established criteria for practice within the organization or network.

questions.question: Which of the following drugs is an antidote for heparin overdose?
questions.explanation:
Protamine sulfate quickly terminates the action of heparin on a 1:1 mole basis
Vitamin K is an antidote for warfarin poisoning
Flumazenil is an antidote for diazepam overdose

questions.question: Which is not correct regarding the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)?

answers.D: Tests eye opening response to stimuli

questions.explanation:
GCS is not very reliable between evaluators
GCS tests verbal, motor, eye-opening response to stimuli

questions.question:
What is the best feeding equipment for a patient with limited range of motion
(ROM) of the shoulder?
questions.explanation:
Swivel utensils are beneficial for patient with limited ROM in the forearm
Long handle utensils are beneficial for patient with limited ROM in the shoulder

questions.question: What gestation age does the neural tube closes?
questions.explanation: The neural tube closes around 18 weeks

questions.question: Which of the following are symptoms associated with central hypothyroidism?
questions.explanation:
Central hypothyroidism can present with symptoms of bradycardia, weight gain, normal blood
pressure
Surgical intervention or radiation to the pituitary gland can also cause altered levels of TSH and
hypothyroid symptoms

questions.question: Which is not true regarding seizures?

answers.A: Morbidity and mortality increase the longer the patient is in status epilepticus
answers.B: Adult onset seizures in patients from Mexico or Latin America may suggest neurocysticercosis
answers.C: EEG is no longer useful in diagnosis of seizures
answers.D: Anoxia is a dangerous complication of status epilepticus

questions.printed_answer_heading: EEG is no longer useful in diagnosis of seizures
questions.explanation: EEG continues to be diagnostic for seizures

questions.question: How many thoracic spinal nerves are there in a human body?
questions.explanation:
There are seven cervical vertebrae
There are eight cervical spinal nerves
There are twelve thoracic vertebrae
There are five lumbar vertebrae

questions.question: Which of the following is not true about the thoracic duct?

answers.A: It can be injured during neonatal shunt procedures
answers.B: It crosses over from right to left at T6
answers.C: It contains valves only in the abdominal segment
answers.D: It may terminate at the junction of either the right or left subclavian veins

questions.printed_answer_heading: It contains valves only in the abdominal segment
questions.explanation: The thoracic duct also contains one-way valves in the thoracic portion.

questions.question:
Although newer and more effective drugs are available, phenobarbital is still
considered an appropriate long-term therapy for which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
Phenobarbital has been mostly replaced with newer drugs except in the case of certain seizure
disorders: status epilepticus, febrile seizures, seizures in term neonates and seizures that have
failed to respond to phenytoin or fosphenytoin.
Zolpidem or zaleplon (benzodiazepine-like agents) or benzodiazepines are considered the
current drugs of choice for the treatment of insomnia.
Benzodiazepines are the drug of choice for both anxiety and alcohol withdrawal therapy.
Although benzodiazepines have a higher safety margin and are less likely to be as addictive as
phenobarbital, they should be used cautiously. Benzodiazepines do carry a risk of dependency;
conditions such as anxiety and insomnia should be treated in as short a period as possible.

questions.question:
The pupillary light reflex can be eliminated by cutting the any following nerves
or structures except:
questions.explanation:
The pupillary light reflex controls the diameter of the pupil.
This is in response to light intensity on the retina.
The afferent limb is the optic nerve and the efferent limb is the oculomotor nerve.
The short ciliary nerves are not involved.

questions.question:
Increased cerebral blood flow as measure by transcranial Doppler is
associated with clinical complication if greater than:
questions.explanation:
Elevated cerebral blood flow beyond 50 cm/second can result in hemorrhagic stroke,
intracranial aneurysmal rupture, cerebral edema, increased intracranial pressure, and thrombosis

questions.question:
Which of the following in false concerning acute nontraumatic intracranial
hemorrhage (ICH)?

answers.A: 70-90% of cases of intracranial hemorrhage in adults are nontraumatic
answers.B: ICH is the cause of 15-20% of acute infarcts
answers.C:
Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) typically results in brainstem and deep gray nuclei
hemorrhages
answers.D: Hypertensive intracranial hemorrhage most commonly affects the striatocapsular region

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) typically results in brainstem and deep gray
nuclei hemorrhages
questions.explanation:
Amyloidosis refers to the deposition of B-amyloid (insoluble fibrillar proteins) in the
extracellular space.
CAA typically results in lobar hemorrhage and is typically multifocal at the subcortical white
matter.
Alzheimer's disease and the APOE4 allele are associated with CAA hemorrhages.

questions.question: During a spinal tap, which structure is not penetrated by the needle:
questions.explanation:
During a middle tap for CSF, one will penetrated the interspinous, supraspinous ligaments and
the dura
The pia matter is not penetrated during a spinal tap

questions.question:
Facial palsy is present in a patient with a probable temporal bone fracture.
What type of fracture is most likely?
questions.explanation:
Although fewer patients with longitudinal fractures have facial palsy than patients with
transverse fractures, longitudinal fractures are significantly more common
Therefore, the likelihood of a longitudinal fracture in this case is high

questions.question: Which spinal nerve provides sympathetic innervation to the eye?
questions.explanation: The sympathetic innervation arises from C8 and T1 spinal nerves

questions.question:
A 42-year-old has developed a disease that has left her unable to care for
herself. She suffers from irregular, purposeless, and asymmetrical movements of limbs which are
worse if she is irritated. Her MRI showed atrophy of the putamen and caudate nucleus. Diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Huntington disease is a neurodegenerative disorder which involves choreiform movements of
the limbs
Mood disorders are commonly presenting symptoms of the disease

questions.question: A patient controlled analgesia device is often used in hospitals to deliver:
questions.explanation:
PCA stands for patient controlled analgesic machine
Patient has control of the administration of the drug

questions.question: Planning and learning of movements is controlled by which nuclei in the brain?
questions.explanation:
The VL nucleus is a part of the thalamus
It receives neuronal input from substantia nigra, globus pallidus and cerebellum
It send neurons to the primary motor cortex
The nucleus plays a vital role in coordination and learning of movement

questions.question: What is the action of mechanism of clonazepam?
questions.explanation:
Clonazepam is a benzodiazepine used for panic disorder, seizure disorders and other indications
Benzodiazepines enhance the action of GABA

questions.question:
A patient with transection of the spinal cord at C5 is expected to have
spastic/reflexive bladder. Which of the following would be most appropriate bladder management?

answers.A: The patient will regain voluntary control of the bladder
answers.B:
The patient should be taught Crede's maneuver of application of external pressure over the
bladder to initiate voiding
answers.C: The patient should have formal schedule for intermittent self-catheterization
answers.D: The patient will need an indwelling catheter

questions.printed_answer_heading: The patient should have formal schedule for intermittent self-catheterization
questions.explanation:
Self-catheterization is less likely result in infection than and indwelling catheter
The Crede maneuver is not used with a spastic bladder
The patient will not regain bladder control

questions.question:
A patient with tuberous sclerosis is found to have a uniform calcified series of
lesions on head CT. These lesions most likely represent:
questions.explanation:
More than 50 percent of tuberous sclerosis patients by the age of 5 years have calcified
subependymal nodules most commonly located in the periventricular regions
These do not cause problems unless they obstruct CSF flow which then can lead to
hydrocephalus
Calcified meningiomas uniformly calcify but are most common in elderly patients

questions.question: The most common presentation of a cerebral abscess is:
questions.explanation:
Headache is the most common presentation of a brain abscess
Focal defects are next most common, followed by a fever
Fever, nausea, vomiting and stiff neck also occur in some patients

questions.question:
A patient has been on valproic acid for partial seizures that have intermittently
been complicated with secondary tonic clonic spells. Recently, he has had two episodes of status
epilepticus. The next best drug which may be useful in this patient is:
questions.explanation:
Lamotrigine a sodium channel blocker that is an anticonvulsant.
Lamotrigine is used in patient that do not tolerate or respond to valproic acid. It is used for
partial seizures and for bipolar disorder.
It is also one of the medications that may be effective for Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.
The adverse reaction of greatest concern is Stevens-Johnson syndrome, especially if used with
carbemazepine.

questions.question:
Which type of nystagmus is commonly associated with suprasellar mass
lesions?
questions.explanation:
See-saw nystagmus is a nystagmus with one eye elevated and intorted and the other depressed
and extorted
It is frequently associated with suprasellar mass lesions

questions.question:
Which of the following studies is most likely to be helpful in the diagnosis of
idiopathic intracranial hypertension?
questions.explanation:
Idiopathic intracranial hypertension can be diagnosed with MRI/MRV
Positive findings include enlarged optic nerve sheathes, cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, and
small slit-like ventricles
Orbital ultrasound can measure the diameter of the optic nerve sheath and determine if there is
increase in fluid with eccentric gaze
Unfortunately, this noninvasive and inexpensive test requires an experienced, highly skilled
technician

questions.question: Thrombolytic agents are contraindicated in patients with?
questions.explanation: Hemothorax is a contraindication to anticoagulant use

questions.question: Meningitis caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae is best treated with:
questions.explanation: Vancomycin with ceftriaxone is the treatment of choice for streptococcal meningitis

questions.question:
Moving a patient from the supine to Trendelenburg position is least likely to
increase which of the following?
questions.explanation:
The Trendelenburg position increases venous return
This often increases the cardiac output, central venous pressure, and systemic arterial blood
pressure
The heart rate generally does not increase; if it does change, it tends to decrease

questions.question:
Which of the following tests permits rapid confirmation of the identity of
Cryptococcus in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)?

answers.A: Detection of polysaccharide in the CSF
answers.B: Detection of specific antibodies in the CSF
answers.C: Detection of lipo-oligosaccharides in the CSF
answers.D: Detection of cell-wall antigens in the CSF

questions.printed_answer_heading: Detection of polysaccharide in the CSF
questions.explanation:
Cryptococcus is the only medically important encapsulated yeast
The capsule consists of polysaccharide, which is antigenic and diffuses away from the cell in the
CSF
Antigenic tests used to detect capsular polysaccharide are twice as sensitive for the rapid
diagnosis of cryptococcal meningitis as is microscopic examination with India ink
Antibodies are never used because it takes too long for them to form

questions.question:
A 6 year old female has nausea and vomiting. MRI shows pineal recess mass
with compression of the tectal plate. There is triventricular hydrocephalus. Which of the following is
most likely to be elevated?
questions.explanation:
Pineal tumors can be germ cell or non-germ cell
The most common tumor marker found is beta hCG
These tumors often cause hydrocephalus
Endocrine abnormalities include diabetes insipidus, growth arrest, or amenorrhea

questions.question: Which of the following is least likely to increase a patient's risk of falling?
questions.explanation:
Diuretics increase the risk of falling because of hypovolemia
All sedative-hypnotics increase the risk of falling
Epidural anesthesia increases the risk of falling because of altered sensory and motor function in
the lower extremities

questions.question: In which scenario is a Glasgow Coma Scale not very valid?

answers.C: 45 year old with a femur fracture and flail chest
answers.D: 22 year old who was thrown off his motor bike

questions.explanation:
The GCS is only valid in children over the age of 36 months
Under the age of 36 months, the validity of verbal performance is not accurate
Other people in whom the GCS is not valid are those who are intubated and others who have
severe facial and eye injuries where the verbal and eyes responses cannot be assessed

questions.question:
What is the most common cause of metastasis causing epidural spinal cord
compression?
questions.explanation:
The most frequent origin of metastasis resulting in epidural spinal cord compression is the
breast, which causes about a fourth of epidural metastasis
Other origins include prostate, lung, and malignant lymphoma which each result in about 10 to
15% of cases of epidural spinal cord compression

questions.question:
Preganglionic neurons of the parasympathetic nervous system are located in
which of the following structures?
questions.explanation:
The autonomic nervous system has fibers from the CNS that terminate in the ganglia.
These are preganglionic fibers.
The nerves from the ganglia to organs are postganglionic fibers.
Parasympathetic preganglionic neurons are found in the brainstem.

questions.question:
A male patient has had burning pain, allodynia, swelling, and intermittent
bluish discoloration of his hand for past two months. Which is the most appropriate diagnostic block?
questions.explanation:
The symptoms are classic for complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS)
CRPS is believed to be mediated by sympathetic mechanisms
Improvement with a stellate ganglion block, which interrupts sympathetic input into the
ipsilateral upper extremity, provides strong supports for diagnosis of CRPS

questions.question: What is not a clinical presentation of Ramsay Hunt syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Ramsay Hunt syndrome presents with facial paresis, hyperacusia, and unilateral ageusia
It presents with facial paresis, hyperacusia, and unilateral ageusia and usually is associated with
varicella zoster reactivation

questions.question: In a patient with acute radiculopathy, the most common presentation is?
questions.explanation:
Acute low back pain is the most common presentation of acute radiculopathy
Distal polyneuropathy is most common in diabetic neuropathy

questions.question: When physicians burnout, it can result in which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Physician burnout may lead to more severe impairment such as alcohol abuse, suicidal ideation,
and drug use.
Physical, mental, and emotional exhaustion are symptoms of burnout.
Symptoms include feelings of helplessness, negative attitudes, irritability, anger, frustration,
isolation, hopelessness, and fatigue.

questions.question: All of the following statements are TRUE regarding achondroplasia, EXCEPT:

answers.A: The disorder is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait
answers.C: Hydrocephalus is not a common complication of this disorder
answers.D: It can be diagnosed before birth

questions.printed_answer_heading: Hydrocephalus is not a common complication of this disorder
questions.explanation:
Achondroplasia is caused by mutation of fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) gene
It results in short arms and legs while head growth is not affected
Hydrocephalus is a common complication of this disorder
Lumbar stenosis may occur later in life

questions.question: Neurocysticercosis is caused by an infection with:
questions.explanation:
Neurocysticercosis is caused by Taenia solium, the most common parasitic cause of central
nervous system in the world
It is spread by fecal oral contamination
Prognosis is good with treatment but surgery is needed if there is resulting hydrocephalus
secondary to an interventricular cyst

questions.question: Which of the following is common in spinal stenosis?

answers.A: Increase in back pain with standing
answers.B: Increase in back pain with sitting

questions.printed_answer_heading: Increase in back pain with standing
questions.explanation:
Spinal stenosis often presents with paresthesias and back pain that increase with standing but
decrease with sitting

questions.question:
Which of the following is not an absolute contraindication for epidural steroid
injection?
questions.explanation: Paralysis is a relative contraindication for epidural steroid injection

questions.question:
A 2 week old infant has fever, poor feeding, irritability, and a bulging
fontanelle. Lumbar puncture yields cloudy CSF and the gram stain shows Gram positive cocci. Select
the most likely organism.
questions.explanation:
The most likely cause of infection in this patient is group B Streptococcus
Early infection with this organism is from the mother but late infection (after 7 days) is
secondary to environmental exposure
Other common causes of meningitis in the neonate are E. coli, H. Influenzae, L. monocytogenes,
group D streptococci, Staphylococcus, and gram negative rods
Treatment is usually with an extended spectrum beta lactam and an aminoglycoside

questions.question:
Significant cerebral edema can be indicated by the rate of change of pupillary
diameter. What is the lowest rates of change should be concerning?
questions.explanation:
Increase of pupillary diameter greater than 0.6 mm/sec is highly suggestive of significant
cerebral edema

questions.question: What is not a common symptom of migraine in children?
questions.explanation:
The estimated incidence of migraine in prepubertal children is about four percent
This rate increases to fifteen percent by age of twenty
Migraine is characterized by bilateral, throbbing, sensorimotor deficit, and speech impairment
About 70 percent of children with migraine also have abdominal discomfort

questions.question: What area of the basal ganglia is damaged by MPTP?
questions.explanation:
Parkinsonism is caused by MPTP induced damage to the substantia nigra
MPTP is a contaminant of street made MPPP, a synthetic opioid
It is converted to MPDP+ and then MPP+ by glial cells, taken up by the dopamine uptake system,
and causes mitochondrial damage resulting in cell death

questions.question: Laceration of the middle meningeal artery can result in:
questions.explanation:
Epidural hematoma is due to traumatic collection of blood in between the inner table of skull
and dural membrane.
The majority of epidural hematomas occur in the temporal parietal region where the skull
fracture crosses the path of the middle meningeal artery'
Epidural hematoma is usually due to arterial bleeding but can also occur from torn venous
sinuses'
Expanding epidural hematomas can also produce a midline shift and cause a brain herniation.

questions.question: Patients with Parkinson disease generally develop which symptom first?
questions.explanation:
Approximately 30% do not develop the shaking early in the disease
This tremor is maximal at rest disappearing with movement
It involves the more distal part of the limbs
The pill-rolling tremor is a classic finding in which the thumb and index finger are in contact as
the hand moves in a circular fashion

questions.question:
The most common presenting symptom in a patient with an acoustic neuroma
is?
questions.explanation:
The majority of patients with an acoustic neuroma presents with unilateral hearing loss
The hearing loss is either due to damage to the cochlear nerve or interruption of cochlear blood
supply

questions.question: A surgical procedure must explained to a patient by the?
questions.explanation: Only the surgeon is qualified to explain the surgical procedure

questions.question: The pH of cerebrospinal fluid is:

answers.D: More basic than plasma only with meningitis

questions.explanation: The pH of cerebrospinal fluid is more basic than plasma pH

questions.question:
What percentage of patients allergic to penicillins have a cross over allergy to
cephalosporins?
questions.explanation:
There is about a 10-15% cross reactivity in allergy from penicillin to cephalosporins.
To be safe, it is better to avoid both agents if there is an allergy to one class of antibiotics.

questions.question: The majority of primary CNS tumors in children are:
questions.explanation:
Astrocytomas and medulloblastomas are the most common primary CNS tumors in childhood.
Adenomas, including those of pituitary origin, occur but are much less common.
Meningiomas are more common in adults and neurofibromas are not considered primary CNS
tumors.

questions.question:
All of the following facts about alcoholic withdrawal seizures are correct
EXCEPT?
questions.explanation:
These seizures generally last 1-3 minutes
They tend to be grand mal seizures

questions.question: Which of the following is not an inhibitory neurotransmitter?
questions.explanation:
Excitatory amino acids depolarize neurons and include cysteic acid, aspartic acid, homocysteic
acid, and glutamic acid
Inhibitory amino acids hyperpolarize neurons and include GABA, taurine, glycine, and beta-
alanine

questions.question: Subfalcine herniation causes mass effect in what location?
questions.explanation:
The most common type of intracranial herniation is subfalcine, causing mass effect on the frontal
lobe due to a space-occupying lesion
Descending transtentorial herniation is the second most common form, caused by temporal lobe
mass effect
Ascending transtentorial herniation is due to a space-occupying lesion in the posterior fossa
causing upward herniation of cerebellar hemisphere and vermis
Tonsillar herniation is also due to a space-occupying lesion in the posterior fossa, causing
downward herniation of the tonsils through the foramen magnum

questions.question: What is the best initial measure for postoperative urinary retention?

answers.B: Advise the paient to sit up
answers.C: Pouring warm water over the perineum

questions.printed_answer_heading: Advise the paient to sit up
questions.explanation:
The simplest initial management is to let patients sit up
Pouring warm water over the perineum can also be tried
Catheterization should be tried if no improvement with simple measures
Bethanechol is a parasympathomimetic drug useful in post operative urinary retention

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct statement about cranial abnormalities?

answers.A: Scaphocephaly results from early closure of the sagittal sutures
answers.B: A large defect in the skull results in cranial meningocele or encephalocele
answers.C: Bilateral closure of the coronal and lambdoid suture results in plagiocephaly
answers.D: Premature closure of the parietal sutures causes acrocephaly

questions.printed_answer_heading: Scaphocephaly results from early closure of the sagittal sutures
questions.explanation:
Small defects in the skull cause encephalocele or meningocele
Premature closure of the coronal suture causes acrocephaly
Unilateral closure of the coronal and lambdoid sutures causes plagiocephaly

questions.question: What is the predominant finding in Alzheimer disease?

answers.D: Loss of pigmented cells in the substantia nigra

questions.explanation:
Alzheimer disease shows neuronal loss, loss of synapses, amyloid plaques, and fibrillary
tangles
These changes are present in all areas of the cerebral cortex but most evident at the hippocampus
and adjacent areas in the temporal lobe
Neuronal loss can lead to ventricular enlargement

questions.question: Why is carbidopa given with levodopa for the treatment of Parkinson disease?

answers.A: It crosses the blood brain barrier and is a dopamine agonist
answers.B: It decreased nausea and vomiting associated with levodopa
answers.C: It prevents peripheral conversion of levodopa to dopamine
answers.D: It has anticholinergic activity that decreases tremor

questions.printed_answer_heading: It prevents peripheral conversion of levodopa to dopamine
questions.explanation:
Carbidopa is a dopa decarboxylase inhibitor
It crosses the blood brain barrier poorly so its actions are in the periphery to prevent peripheral
conversion of levodopa to dopamine
Levodopa can cross the blood brain barrier but dopamine does not
Levodopa is converted in the CNS to dopamine

questions.question:
In the treatment of low back pain, warm compresses will most likely reduce
which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Warm compresses will often reduce muscle tone and alleviate muscle spasm
They may also increase muscle blood flow

questions.question:
A 40 year old male complains of a hand tremor that is most noticeable when
trying to perform a task. It started a few years ago but is gradually getting worse. This type of tremor
is most likely due to pathology at which structure?
questions.explanation:
The patient has a kinetic or intention tremor that is usually due to cerebellar damage
Rarely intention tremors can be secondary to spinocerebellar tract damage
Parkinson disease is due to disease of the substantia nigra and is characterized by a resting
tremor that improves with intentional movements
Lesions of the internal capsule result in weakness

questions.question:
Select the incorrect statement about the 9th cranial nerve, the glossopharyngeal
nerve.

answers.A: It supplies parasympathetic fibers via the otic ganglion to the parotid gland
answers.B: It provides taste sensation on anterior two thirds of tongue
answers.C: It provides sensation to the tonsils, pharynx, and middle ear
answers.D: It carries visceral sensory output from carotid body

questions.printed_answer_heading: It provides taste sensation on anterior two thirds of tongue
questions.explanation:
The 9th cranial nerve supplies taste to the posterior 1/3 of the tongue
The facial nerve (CN VII) provides taste to anterior 2/3d of tongue
CN IX supplies motor fibers to stylopharyngeus which controls gagging and swallowing

questions.question: In a 55 year old, which of the following treatments can induce arrhythmia?
questions.explanation:
Phenol delivery is a painless process
It can be associated with arrhythmia

questions.question:
A patient is under treatment for lung cancer and complains of a backache for a
2 weeks that has somewhat responded to ibuprofen. He now has right lower quadrant abdominal pain
and inguinal pain. He is tender over the lower thoracic spine and symmetrical weakness of the lower
extremities with hyperreflexia. There is symmetrical decreased sensation below T11. What is the next
step?
questions.explanation:
The patient is having cord compression from a metastatic tumor
High dose glucocorticoids should be started urgently
MRI of the thoracic spine is needed not plain films
Local radiation therapy will most likely be needed

questions.question: What is the most beneficial activity for a patient with visual field deficit?
questions.explanation: Balloon batting is the best activity for a patient with visual field defect

questions.question: Which of these expresses the acronym PHI?
questions.explanation:
Protected Health Information expresses the acronym PHI.
PHI includes individual records of health status, provision of care, and payment information for
health care.
PHI is includes an individual's medical record and payment history.
PHI is protected and only by exception may patient information be disclosed.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not a secondary cause of craniosynostosis?
questions.explanation:
Primary craniosynostosis is idiopathic and more common than the secondary form.
It is theorized that there is a primary defect in the mesenchymal layer that causes ossification.
Secondary craniosynostosis is caused by hyperthyroidism, vitamin D deficiency,
hypophosphatemia, rickets, hypercalcemia, and renal osteodystrophy.

questions.question: Which is false about the latissimus dorsi muscle?

answers.A: It is a broad flat muscle on the posterior trunk and covered by trapezius
answers.B: The muscle causes extension, adduction and horizontal abduction
answers.C: The muscle is supplied by the thoracodorsal nerve
answers.D: When the nerve to it is injured it causes winging of the scapula

questions.printed_answer_heading: When the nerve to it is injured it causes winging of the scapula
questions.explanation:
The latissimus dorsi is a large muscle in the back that is responsible for extension, adduction
and transverse extension
The muscle is supplied by the thoracodorsal nerve and the muscle is chiefly used to lift weights,
pull down, or perform dead lifts
It was also used as a muscle to perform cardiomyoplasty
Injury to the serratus anterior muscle nerve is the cause of winging of the scapula

questions.question:
A patient sustains blunt force trauma to the right side of his neck and later
presents with Horner syndrome and left sided upper extremity weakness, what has most likely
occurred?

answers.B: Vertebral artery dissection with partial occlusion
answers.D: Internal carotid artery dissection with partial occlusion

questions.printed_answer_heading: Internal carotid artery dissection with partial occlusion
questions.explanation:
Internal carotid dissection commonly presents with Horner's syndrome because the sympathetic
nerves, which innervate ocular muscles, travel in close proximity to the ICA.
Partial occlusion is evident due the patient's symptoms of left sided upper extremity weakness,
which is likely due to reduced blood flow to the middle cerebral artery.

questions.question:
Acute rise in intracranial pressure in a 13 year old patient causes multiple
symptoms. Which of the following would be the latest symptom or sign to manifest?
questions.explanation:
Critically increased intracranial pressure initially will show decreased consciousness
Other signs and symptoms are likely to occur in the following sequence: headache, nausea,
vomiting, irritability, and abducens nerve palsy
Papilledema is not present in all patients with increased intracranial pressure
Symptomatic papilledema with vision loss only occurs with chronic or advanced increased
intracranial pressure

questions.question:
What is the most likely reason for failure of regeneration of an axon in the
CNS?

answers.A: The soma degenerates if the axon is damaged
answers.B: The axon is not able to sprout and grow
answers.C: Axonal growth is blocked by scarring from astrocytes

questions.printed_answer_heading: Axonal growth is blocked by scarring from astrocytes
questions.explanation:
Axon regeneration in the CNS is prevented by lack of growth factors and an environment hostile
to axon growth
This includes myelin-associated inhibitors, oligodendrocytes, oligodendrocyte precursors,
astrocytes, and microglia

questions.question: Which of the following medications is indicated in central diabetes insipidus?
questions.explanation:
Intranasal desmopressin helps to control hypotonic water loss in cases of central DI
Nephrogenic DI is difficult to treat and diuretics can be tried to increase proximal water
absorption

questions.question:
Which of the following metastatic tumors to the brain is most likely to result in
an intracranial bleed?
questions.explanation:
Brain tumors from the lung, breast, melanoma, renal and colon are common
The most common source of brain metastases is lung cancer in males and breast cancer in
females
Melanoma is most commonly associated with brain metastases with often presents with
hemorrhage
However, since there are a greater incidence of lung cancer with metastases, overall these
lesions are the most common source of a hemorrhagic lesions

questions.question:
A 19 year old is involved in a severe head trauma and has a GCS of 7. It is
believed that he has elevated intracranial pressure. Which of the following findings would go along
with your suspicion?
questions.explanation:
Cushing reflex is a nervous system response to increased intracranial pressure
It results in widen pulse pressure, irregular breathing and bradycardia
Cushing reflex is seen at the end stages of head injury and may indicate imminent herniation
Other features of Cushing reflex include hypertension and increased peripheral vascular
resistance

questions.question: Which of the following antibiotics is effective against L. monocytogenes?
questions.explanation:
Ampicillin is effective against L. monocytogenes infection
Neonates who have culture negative meningitis should be treated with a regimen containing
ampicillin
Third generationcCephalosporin are not effective against Listeria species

questions.question: Which of the following treatment is not used to treat high intracranial pressure?
questions.explanation:
The least invasive means of lowering ICP is elevating head of the patient. Trendelenberg
position lowers the head and should not be used
Hyperventilation can reduce C02 and leads to vasoconstriction of blood vessels; it should only
be used for short term
Mannitol or diuretics draws fluid and increased diuresis; mannitol also acts as a free radical
scavenger
Hyperglycemia is detrimental to the brain in trauma, so euglycemia should be maintained

questions.question: Cranial nerve IX is also known as:
questions.explanation:
CN IX is known glossopharyngeal nerve
CN X is known as vagus nerve
CN XI is known as accessory nerve
CN XII is known as hypoglossal nerve

questions.question:
All of the following findings can be present in children with
craniopharyngioma, except:
questions.explanation:
Craniopharyngioma is a tumor of the anterior pituitary gland and it can lead to hypopituitarism
Since the tumor is locate just above the optic chiasm the resultant lesion is bitemporal
hemianopsia
Galactorrhea can occur as a side effect of antipsychotic drugs or by hyper-functioning pituitary
tumors

questions.question: Body positioning is usually sensed by which nerve fibers?
questions.explanation: Pressure and body position are controlled by the posterior column

questions.question: A cervical rib generally causes compression of:

answers.C: C8 T1 which primarily forms the lower trunk of brachial plexus

questions.printed_answer_heading: C8 T1 which primarily forms the lower trunk of brachial plexus
questions.explanation:
Cervical rib usually compresses the lower trunk of brachial plexus
Segments C8 and T1 are most commonly affected
Individuals may complain of pain, paresthesia along the ulnar nerve course
The hand may develop weakness, becomes numb and clumsy

questions.question:
Which of the following are not involved in the development of the midbrain
and cerebellum?
questions.explanation:
Just before the closure of the neural tube, pax proteins are found on it and are needed for closure
The amounts of the wnt-1 and engrailed gene are reduced
If there is absence of engrailed and wnt-1 genes in mice, there is no midbrain or cerebellum

questions.question: Which of the following statements about West Nile virus is not true?

answers.A: Mosquito bites cause nearly all West Nile infections in humans
answers.B: The primary amplifying hosts are birds
answers.D: Disease can be transmitted from human contacts

questions.printed_answer_heading: Disease can be transmitted from human contacts
questions.explanation:
Mosquito bites cause nearly all West Nile infections in humans.
Much less rarely it can be transfusion related.
The virus has a bird-mosquito-bird cycle with birds being the primary amplifying host.
Horses, humans, and other animals are incidental hosts. It is not directly transmitted from person
to person.

questions.question:
The most common fungal infection to cause central nervous infections in HIV
patients is:
questions.explanation: The most common central nervous system fungal infection in HIV is cryptococcus.

questions.question: Which of the following is a contraindication for use of thrombolytics?
questions.explanation:
A history of cerebral hemorrhage or a hemorrhagic stroke is a contraindication to administration
of thrombolytics
In such scenarios the risk of hemorrhage may be further increased

questions.question:
A 7 year old male presents with nuchal rigidity, fever, and intermittent stupor
is evaluated with a CT scan showing enhancement of the basal cisterns after contrast injection.
Lumbar puncture showed CSF with WBCs 100/µL with 100% lymphocytes, protein 160 mg/dL,
glucose 20 mg/dL, and negative gram stain. Select the most likely diagnosis.
questions.explanation:
The differential for the clinical presentation includes Medulloblastoma, meningeal leukemia,
viral meningitis, and tuberculous meningitis
The extremely low glucose makes tuberculosis the most likely
The CT finding would be secondary to basal cistern exudate
AFB smear and culture are needed

questions.question: Saccular aneurysm rupture likelihood is NOT associated with:
questions.explanation:
Increasing aneurysm size increases rupture incidence
Patient age has no association with rupture risk

questions.question: The drug used to prevent strokes by inhibiting platelet aggregation is:
questions.explanation:
Clopidogrel, antiplatelet drug, is used to prevent strokes and coronary restenosis by inhibiting
platelet aggregation

questions.question: Respiratory depression caused by morphine overdose should be treated with:
questions.explanation:
Naloxone can reverse the effects of morphine and other narcotics
Flumazenil reverses the effects of benzodiazepines
Phenobarbital can worsen respiratory depression
Naltrexone is used for alcohol addiction

questions.question:
In a patient with septic arthritis of the joints, the most common finding on x
rays is?
questions.explanation:
Though plain x-rays have very limited usefulness in assessing joint septic arthritis, several
findings help in suggesting the diagnosis in which the most common finding is periarticular soft
tissue swelling
CT scans and MRI are better for evaluating a septic joint and its sequelae: effusions,
osteomyelitis and abscesses

questions.question: Which of the following structures is located in the spinal epidural space?
questions.explanation:
The internal vertebral venous plexuses are in the vertebral canal between the vertebrae and the
dura mater in the epidural space.
There are tributaries from the spinal cord and the bones.
The intricate network forms around the foramen magnum and is connected to the vertebral veins.
It is connected above with the occipital sinus, the condyloid emissary vein, the basilar plexus,
and the rete canalis hypoglossi.

questions.question:
A 7 y/o is noticed by the teacher to be unresponsive with a blank stare and
some lip licking. What is the condition?
questions.explanation:
Absence seizure also called petit mal seizure is of short duration mostly affecting children
It involves the impairment of consciousness and interruption of activities with development of a
blank stare and possible presentation of automatisms such as lip smacking
The diagnosis is made by showing the classic spike and slow wave discharge on EEG

questions.question: What occurs in patients developing a central herniation of the brain?
questions.explanation: Central herniation of the brain will cause bilateral deterioration of function, posturing and coma

questions.question:
Which of following presenting features is not a contraindication for home
discharge after general anesthesia?
questions.explanation: Isolated nausea after general anesthesia is common

questions.question: One is likely to see Charcot-Bouchard aneurysms in a patient with:
questions.explanation:
Charcot-Bouchard aneurysms are a common cause of cerebrovascular disease
These are small aneurysms that occur in penetrating arteries of the mid brain and brainstem and
associated with hypertension
The most common vessel involved are the lenticulostriate branches of the middle cerebral
The hemorrhages occur in the putamen, caudate and thalamus area

questions.question: Which is not involved in the neural pathway of pain perception?
questions.explanation: Pain afferent starts at the dorsal horn and travel to brainstem via spinothalamic tract

questions.question: Which is true about aneurysms in the brain?

answers.A: Are the most common cause of subarachnoid hemorrhage in young people
answers.B: Majority of aneurysms occur posterior branches of the circle of Willis
answers.C: The rate of rebleed tends to decrease after 48 hours of the initial rupture.
answers.D: Ligation of the middle cerebral artery is a normal accepted mode of surgical treatment.

questions.printed_answer_heading: The rate of rebleed tends to decrease after 48 hours of the initial rupture.
questions.explanation:
Brain aneurysms occur in about 1% of the population based on short studies but this number is
felt to be too high. Factors that cause subarachnoid hemorrhage include aneurysm, AV
malformations, hypertension, trauma and anticoagulant therapy
The majority of aneurysms occur in the first and second order vessels originating from the
arterial circle of Willis. Multiple aneurysms are common in 30%.
Typical presentation is a severe headache, loss of consciousness, nausea, vomiting or
meningismus. Many aneurysms have a tendency to rebleed within the first 48 hours
Surgical and endovascular techniques are used to repair their aneurysm. The neck of the
aneurysm has to be clipped and not the major blood vessel. Clipping any major blood vessel in
the brain can have serious consequences

questions.question: Which symptom is not consistent with spinal shock?

answers.C: Loss of anal sphincter tone or fecal incontinence

questions.explanation:
Aflexia, flaccidity, loss of anal sphincter tone and bulbocavernous reflex, fecal incontinence,
priapism are seen in spinal shock

questions.question: Flumazenil is used for overdose of which of the following medications?
questions.explanation:
Flumazenil is a benzodiazepine receptor antagonist
It is used in a benzodiazepine overdose such as diazepam
Meperidine is an opioid drug

questions.question:
Dressing that adheres to the incisional site may be removed by which of the
following methods?

answers.A: Moistening the dressing with sterile saline
answers.C: Placing a warm compress over the dressing
answers.D: Finding an edge and slowly working the dressing free

questions.printed_answer_heading: Moistening the dressing with sterile saline
questions.explanation:
Moistening the dressing softens the adhesion and aids in removal, thus preventing damage to the
incision and the surrounding tissue

questions.question:
An adult male patient presents with intense unilateral headaches. They occur at
the right periorbital area and are often associated with rhinorrhea and lacrimation. This is most
likely?
questions.explanation:
Cluster headaches are vascular and are recurrent like migraines.
Cluster headaches are seen more often in men than women.
It does not generalize and stays unilateral.
1/3 of patients present with Horner's syndrome.

questions.question: Which of the following agencies is responsible for workplace safety?
questions.explanation:
OSHA is the agency responsible for workplace safety
It is part of the Department of Labor
FDA enforces the laws that regulate interstate transport and quality of drugs and food
NIH is the nation's medical research agency

questions.question:
All of the following statements about cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) are correct
EXCEPT?

answers.A: 10% of the intracranial content is CSF
answers.B: The CSF turns over 3.7 times a day
answers.C: CSF is covered by the pia mater
answers.D: CSF is produced by ependymal cells of the choroid plexus

questions.printed_answer_heading: CSF is covered by the pia mater
questions.explanation:
500 ml of CSF is produced daily in an adult. CSF lies between the pia mater and arachnoid
mater. The choroids plexus is present in all 4 ventricles
CSF has several functions which include buoyancy, protection, chemical stability, and
prevention of brain ischemia
CSF is reabsorbed into the dural venous sinuses by the arachnoid granulations or villi.
It may be that CSF which bathes the cranial and spinal nerves actually enters the lymphatic
system

questions.question:
A patient with a left cerebrovascular accident is receiving therapy. She has a
motorized wheelchair but repeated runs into objects on the right side. She needs to be reminded to
advance the right leg during gait training. There is no sensation of this leg. Select the correct
description that explains these findings.
questions.explanation:
The patient is exhibiting neglect of the right side
It can be seen after stroke, brain surgery, or TBI

questions.question:
Subarachnoid hemorrhage is most commonly caused by which of the
following?
questions.explanation:
The most common cause of subarachnoid hemorrhage is trauma
In young adults the most common cause is ruptured cerebral aneurysm
5 to 10% of cerebrovascular accidents are due to subarachnoid hemorrhage
In the US, the annual incidence of SAH secondary to aneurysm is 6 to 16 per 100,000

questions.question: Intraoperative thrombocytopenia is most commonly due to?
questions.explanation: Dilutional thrombocytopenia is the most common cause of intraoperative thrombocytopenia

questions.question:
A post-op patient develops acute confusional state with hallucinations, marked
agitation and altered sleep-wake cycle. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Delirium is the single most common acute mental disorder affecting adults in the hospital
It occurs in 10-20% of hospitalized adults, 30-40% of elderly patients, and 80% of ICU patients

questions.question:
An 81 year old male has been hospitalized and is ready for discharge. His
daughter has durable power of attorney for health care. The patient's mini-mental status score is
22/30. What should be done?

answers.A: The patient might be able to make his own decisions
answers.B: The patient's daughter should make the decisions
answers.C: The daughter should go to court and request guardianship
answers.D: The physician is responsible for making decisions

questions.printed_answer_heading: The patient might be able to make his own decisions
questions.explanation:
The patient's mini-mental status indicates that he has mild dementia but may well be able to
make his own decisions
If the patient is not making rational decisions, the daughter should exercise power of attorney
The patient should be reevaluated once he has returned to his baseline
The daughter may need to go to court to be assigned as his guardian

questions.question: Which of the following drugs can cause constipation?
questions.explanation:
Opioids are known to cause constipation.
Constipation and meiosis do not disappear with long-term use of opioids.
Senna is a laxative, ketorolac is an NSAID, and sumatriptan is used for migraines.
They generally do not cause constipation.

questions.question:
In a patient with an automatic implantable defibrillator undergoing surgery, the
doctor should?
questions.explanation: The ICD usually can be deactivated by magnets

questions.question: Which is true regarding Guillain Barre syndrome?

answers.B: IVIG and plasmapheresis are recommended treatments
answers.C:
Ascending asymmetric progressive motor weakness with increased deep tendon reflexes
(DTR's) is typical
answers.D: CSF shows a decrease in protein without cells

questions.printed_answer_heading: IVIG and plasmapheresis are recommended treatments
questions.explanation:
Neurological disability is usually transient
Ascending symmetrical progressive motor weakness with areflexia
CSF shows increased protein without cells

questions.question: Tongue movements are controlled by which cranial nerve?
questions.explanation:
CN VII is responsible for taste to anterior two thirds of the tongue.
CN IX controls taste to posterior one third of the tongue.
CN XII innervate the tongue muscle.

questions.question: What must be obtained prior information being released?
questions.explanation: An informed consent must be obtained for any information released

questions.question:
The diagnosis of a Chiari Type II malformation is made by MRI in an infant
presenting with bilateral CN VI palsies, tongue fasciculation and head lag. Which concurrent
anomalies may also be commonly present?
questions.explanation:
Type II Chiari malformations are often associated with spina bifida which may be quite severe
and contain meningeal and neural tissues as well
An evagination of meningeal tissue in spina bifida is called a meningocele where the
combination of meningeal and neural elements are termed meningomyelocele
Symptoms reflect compromise of the lower brainstem cranial nerves as a result of the downward
displacement caused by the type II malformation
Lumbar puncture is contraindicated if a spina bifida is suspected as needle insertion may
directly injure neural elements within the neural tube defect

questions.question:
A 28 year old suddenly complains of the worst headache of her life and
collapses. She may have:
questions.explanation:
Classic features of a ruptured berry aneurysm is the worst headache I have ever had
Sentinel headaches caused by slow leaks may occur days or weeks prior to a full rupture
Other symptoms of a berry aneurysm include double vision, loss of vision, or neck pain
Once suspected, the diagnosis is made by angiography, MRI or CT scan

questions.question:
Which of the following disease processes does not cause loss of vibratory
sense?
questions.explanation:
Vitamin E and B12 deficiencies can cause loss of vibratory sense
Conditions that cause peripheral neuropathy such as diabetes mellitus and dysfunction of the
posterior columns in the spinal cord such as multiple sclerosis can lead to diminished to loss of
vibratory sense
Other diseases include hereditary/genetic/familial disorders, spinal cord trauma, spinal
compressive lesions, certain strokes, and brain tumors

questions.question:
A provider is planning a presentation at a conference and had planned to
distribute a handout from an article but cannot find the name of the author. Select the best action.

answers.A: Use the information for the presentation but do not distribute the article
answers.B: Use the image during the presentation and apologize for not having a reference
answers.C: Provide the handout and apologize for not including the author
answers.D: Do not use the information from the handout

questions.printed_answer_heading: Use the information for the presentation but do not distribute the article
questions.explanation:
Professional presentations must include any references to any copyrighted material
Providing the handout or using the image would not be legal or professional
Including the information would be appropriate

questions.question:
An individual with facet arthritis can be diagnosed with what type of branch
block:
questions.explanation: Medial branch block is diagnostic for facet arthritis.

questions.question: The ideal test of choice to make a diagnosis of brain abscess is?
questions.explanation:
CT scan is the most reliable test to assess a patient for a cerebral abscess
Classically one will see a distinct ring-enhancing lesion
MRI is now being widely used to make the diagnosis and is more sensitive for cerebritis

questions.question:
A patient presents with a change in mental status. What is the first step in
management?
questions.explanation:
Hypoglycemia should be ruled out in a patient with a change in mental status
Other measures should include high flow oxygen and IV access
Glucose containing IV fluids should be administered if hypoglycemia discovered

questions.question: For a stage II pressure ulcer the best dressing is?
questions.explanation: Vapor permeable dressings are the best for the treatment of stage II ulcers

questions.question:
Treatment that most likely will not assist in attaining a positive outcome is
considered to be:
questions.explanation: Treatment unlikely to assist the patient in their care is considered futile

questions.question:
What is the correct muscle strength grading in a patient with muscle movement
only against gravity?
questions.explanation:
No muscle movement is a grade zero
Grade 3 motor strength is movement against only gravity
Normal motor strength is grade 5

questions.question: Pituitary tumors can cause which of the following eye movements?
questions.explanation:
Pendular see saw nystagmus consists of intorsion and elevation and of one eye with
simultaneous extorsion and depression of the other eye.
This is the first half of the cycle.
It is followed by change in direction during the next half.
It is seen in diseases affecting the crossing axons of the optic chiasm such as pituitary tumors.

questions.question:
A 75-year-old female presents to the emergency department with a myocardial
infarction. She develops asystole and resuscitation is achieved after a prolonged period. She remains
unconscious for 72 hours but gradually improves slightly. She breathes independently and will
swallow food placed in her mouth. She does not speak or interact. Painful stimuli results with
withdrawal. A feeding tube is placed and there is no change for a few months. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The patient has no evidence of cognitive function but has sustained autonomic activity
This can occur secondary to severe damage to the cerebral cortex and intact brainstem
MRI will reveal the ischemic damage to the cerebral cortex
Protracted hypoxemia or near drowning can cause this condition

questions.question:
Which of following ages most commonly has associated with REM
parasomnias?
questions.explanation:
REM parasomnias is commonly related to older population
Predominantly in males
Results from lack of normal atonia in REM cycle

questions.question: An unlicensed assistant may not perform which of the following?
questions.explanation: A surgical site must be assessed by a licensed member of the health care team

questions.question:
Which of the following findings would be indication of a VP shunt
malfunction?
questions.explanation:
Nausea, vomiting, and irritability are the most common signs of VP shunt malfunction
Other signs would be behavior changes, headache, visual perceptual difficulties, and pallor
Fever and neck stiffness are signs of infection

questions.question:
Damage to the precentral gyrus secondary to thrombosis of the branch of the
middle cerebral artery. Select the most probable result.
questions.explanation:
The primary motor cortex is at the precentral gyrus
A lesion would affect the contralateral side
The primary somatosensory cortex is at the postcentral gyrus

questions.question: The longest acting local anesthetic is:
questions.explanation:
Bupivacaine is indicated for local anesthetics and is used for epidural anesthesia. Sometimes
bupivacaine is combined with epinephrine to prolong action
Bupivacaine binds to sodium channels and block sodium channels into nerve cells, which
prevent depolarization
Bupivacaine is one of the longest acting local anesthetics and can often provide pain relief for
up to 20 hours
Compared to other local anesthetics, the drug is markedly cardiotoxic. Other cardiac effects
include hypotension, bradycardia, arrhythmias and cardiac arrest

questions.question:
Which of the following should be the first step in approaching a newly
admitted patient who is agitated?
questions.explanation: A friendly and professional approach is the best method to deal with agitated patients

questions.question: What is the ideal medication for intrathecal delivery system?
questions.explanation: Morphine is the first line for intrathecal delivery system

questions.question: Which of the following neurons are not found in the cerebral cortex?
questions.explanation:
Purkinje cells are found in the cerebellum
They constitute the sole output neurons of the cerebellar cortex
Their cell bodies are arranged in a single sheet at the border zone between the molecular and the
granule cell layers
Axons of purkinje cells project primarily to cerebellar nuclei, although some axons from the
vermis bypass the deep cerebellar nuclei to reach the vestibular nuclei directly

questions.question: Select the correct statement about post lumbar puncture headache (PLPH).

answers.A: The risk of headache is decreased by replacing the stylet before needle removal
answers.B: The headache is worse when lying flat

questions.printed_answer_heading: The risk of headache is decreased by replacing the stylet before needle removal
questions.explanation:
PLPH is characterized by a throbbing or dull pain decreased by lying flat
The MRI can show pachymeningeal enhancement, brain sagging, and basal cistern obliteration
Most PLPH resolve in a few days but rarely symptomatic subdural hematomas occur
Rarely CN VI palsy is seen

questions.question:
What special concern is there during a surgical procedure on a patient with
known alcoholism?

answers.B: The need for higher doses of anesthesia
answers.D: Longer period of time expected in recovery

questions.printed_answer_heading: The need for higher doses of anesthesia
questions.explanation:
Chronic alcohol intake increases production of liver enzymes.
Chronic alcoholics may need higher doses to achieve anesthesia.
Alcohol withdrawal usually occurs 2-3 days after the last drink.

questions.question: Which is false about deep tendon reflexes?

answers.A: Delayed deep tendon reflexes are seen with hypothyroidism
answers.B: Root and grasp reflexes indicate diffuse cortical dysfunction
answers.C:
Right upper and lower extremity reflexes of 3+/4 with left upper and lower extremity reflexes of
1+/4 indicate a spinal cord lesion
answers.D: Brisk upper and lower reflexes without other neurologic findings is a normal variant

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Right upper and lower extremity reflexes of 3+/4 with left upper and lower extremity
reflexes of 1+/4 indicate a spinal cord lesion
questions.explanation:
Disparity between right and left deep tendon reflexes is most likely a cortical lesion.
The deep tendon reflex will be increased on the side of cortical dysfunction due to the loss of
descending inhibition.
Brisk or weak deep tendon reflexes, as long as symmetric, are not pathologic.

questions.question:
Surgery for epilepsy is best indicated for a patient with which of the
following?

answers.A: Multiple areas involving the inferior cerebral cortex
answers.B: Localized area of the temporal cortex

questions.printed_answer_heading: Localized area of the temporal cortex
questions.explanation:
Surgical therapy for seizures is only used if medications fail or are not tolerated as the outcomes
are variable. Medical failure is defined as persistent seizures despite use of three medications.
Surgery has become less common due to the implimentation of vagal nerve stimulation.
Surgery is most successful if there is a localized area of the temporal cortex that is the cause.
Video-electroencephalographic monitoring with intracranial electrodes is generally used.

questions.question:
A patient recovering from a viral infection notices significant weakness in the
legs which is ascending. There is associated severe pain in muscles. Exam reveals no reflexes and
loss of position sense. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Guillain-Barre syndrome has 6 subtypes
This condition is an autoimmune response triggered usually by an acute infection
It presents with ascending paralysis that can involve the brainstem affecting cranial nerves and
respiration
Treatment involves IV immunoglobulins or plasmapheresis

questions.question:
The anticonvulsant that is used to treat tonic clonic seizures and requires
loading is:
questions.explanation:
Phenytoin is an old anticonvulsant used for tonic-clonic and partial seizures
Phenytoin blocks Na+ channels in neuronal membranes
The drug has to be loaded in the systemic circulation and it has dose-dependent nonlinear
elimination kinetics
Long-term use of phenytoin has been associated with sedation, diplopia, gingival hyperplasia,
hirsutism, respiratory depression in overdose and it has teratogenic potential

questions.question: Select the oldest headache treatment that is still used.
questions.explanation:
Trephination is placing a burr hole in the skull and has been done in Africa for thousands of
years and is still done
A skull that was thousands of years old showed bone growth, indicating that some patients
survived the procedure
Willow bark was first mentioned by Hippocrates about 400 B.C. and was made into aspirin in
1838
The skull of a catfish, boiled in oil, was used as a poultice in ancient Egypt but is no longer used

questions.question: After a fall in an elderly patient, the most likely complication is?
questions.explanation:
Chronic subdural hematomas are feared complication of fall in the elderly population
Because of cerebral degeneration the brain is hypermobile in its closed bony structure
Any sudden movement can lead to tearing of the big veins and lead to a subdural hematoma
Epidural hematoma usually results from temporal bone fracture

questions.question: What is the most common chronic compliant after spinal cord injury?
questions.explanation:
Due to increased mental and physical requirements fatigue is the most common long term issue
for SCI patients
Depression, bowel and bladder control, and spasticity can be treated with procedures or
medication

questions.question:
A 33-year-old male without past medical history collapses while at work. He
has a seizure lasting 2 minutes and is brought to the emergency department by paramedics. He is fully
recovered within 60 minutes and reports that he has been having early morning headaches for 3
weeks. MRI shows a left frontal lesion that is enhances and is thought to be a primary brain neoplasm.
What is the most common primary brain tumor in this age group?
questions.explanation:
In this age group the most common primary brain tumor is malignant astrocytoma
These are either grade 3 or 4
Grade 4 astrocytoma is called glioblastoma multiform and is very locally invasive
It is more common in males

questions.question:
Which of the following is least likely to preserve vision in idiopathic
intracranial hypertension (IIH)?

answers.B: Decompression of the optic nerve sheath

questions.explanation:
IIH can be medically treated with carbonic anhydrase inhibitors or loop diuretics but thiazide
diuretics are not used
If medical treatment fails, the surgical procedure that is most likely to preserve vision is
decompression of the optic nerve sheath
Other surgical procedures used include ventriculoperitoneal shunt, lumboperitoneal shunt, and
intracranial venous sinus stent placement

questions.question:
Which of the following is the most important measure for pressure ulcers in a
patient that is paralyzed?

answers.B: Repositioning and turning every two hours

questions.printed_answer_heading: Repositioning and turning every two hours
questions.explanation:
The most important intervention to prevent pressure ulcers is repositioning and turning the
patient

questions.question: The Hoffman-Tinel sign is often used for which of the following?

answers.C: Assess ability of patient to sense pain

questions.explanation:
In 1915, both Jules Tinel and Paul Hoffman separately described the phenomenon that
percussion over the distal end of a regenerating nerve produced a tingling sensation.
Progression of regeneration results in the location to move distal from the site of the injury.

questions.question:
A 56-year-old female presents to you with muscle weakness, cutaneous striae,
easy bruisability and osteoporosis. Further work up reveals that she has had a history of peptic ulcer
disease, a moon shaped face and fat deposition in the interscapular areas. You suspect that the patient
has Cushing disease. The most common cause of Cushing disease is:
questions.explanation:
Cushing disease is reserved for Cushing syndrome that is caused by excessive secretion of
ACTH from a pituitary tumor, usually an adenoma
Cushing disease is responsible for 70% of cases of endogenous Cushing syndrome. The rest of
the cases are caused by ectopic secretion of ACTH by a tumor or adrenal gland tumor.
The pituitary tumors in Cushing disease are microadenomas which measure 10mm or less. These
microadenomas do not cause mass effect and are often discovered after hypersecretion of ACTH
is determined.
Macroadenomas are uncommon in patients with Cushing disease. These tumors cause mass
effect like supra-sellar extension, optic chiasm compression and cavernous sinus compression
