questions.question: Which of the following drugs can be given for an acute seizure?
questions.explanation:
Diazepam can be given for an acute seizure
It works to suppress the brain's electrical activity
It also relaxes the muscles
Penicillin, atenolol and atorvastatin are not indicated in the treatment of acute seizures

questions.question:
Postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) can be treated with which of the following in a
patient who is intolerant of opiates?
questions.explanation:
Amitriptyline is a tricyclic antidepressant used as a pain modulator found to be effective in PHN
Transdermal fentanyl and oxycodone are narcotics
Aspirin and other NSAIDS are often not sufficient to treat this pain
Transdermal lidocaine, pregabalin, and gabapentin can also be used

questions.question: Which of the following is a common initial treatment for Parkinson disease is:
questions.explanation:
The best initial treatment for Parkinson is levodopa
Levodopa is converted to dopamine in the substantia nigra
Some authorities prefer to start with dopamine agonists or MAO-B inhibitors

questions.question:
Which of the following does not increase the infection rates in a clean
operative procedure?
questions.explanation:
Preoperative antibiotics do not increase the infection rate. All the other listed factors do
Systemic factors that increase risk of infection include malnutrition, poor tissue perfusion,
obesity, diabetes, use of steroids and immunosuppressants
Wound characteristics that increase infection include hematoma, foreign material, dead space,
poor skin preparation, shaving and use of drains
Surgery factors which increase infection include poor surgery technique, long surgery,
intraoperative contamination and inadequate theatre ventilation

questions.question:
Which of the following would be correct about MRI of a 70-year-old
unresponsive male?

answers.A: Acute anoxia would show hyper-sharp distinction between white and gray matter
answers.B: Subacute anoxia shows a more diffuse distinction between white and grey matter
answers.C: Diffusion-weighted imaging is the best method to detect diffuse anoxia

questions.explanation:
Cerebral infarctions may be evident by diffusion weighted imaging as early as 30 to 60 minutes
after infarction
The normal brain shows Brownian motion
Cytotoxic edema results in restriction of Brownian motion
Diffusion weighted imaging is more sensitive to early changes after a stroke than more
traditional MRI measurements

questions.question: In post-operative imaging of the sella/pituitary:

answers.A: Chiasmal tethering leads to visual defects
answers.B: Sinuses do not need to be in the FOV
answers.C: Delayed contrast enhanced T1 weighted fat-saturation imaging is necessary

questions.printed_answer_heading: Delayed contrast enhanced T1 weighted fat-saturation imaging is necessary
questions.explanation:
Post operatively, the sella is fat-packed. To see residual pituitary tissue, one needs contrast,
delayed imaging (due to portal venous supply) and fat saturation
Chiasmal tethering may be asymptomatic
Postoperative imaging should include the sinuses if the surgical approach was transsphenoidal
Dynamic contrast-enhanced T1WI is difficult post-operatively

questions.question:
Taste sensations to the posterior 1/3rd of the tongue are derived via which
cranial nerve?
questions.explanation:
CN VII is responsible for taste to anterior two thirds of the tongue.
CN IX controls taste to posterior one third of the tongue.
CN XII innervate the tongue muscle.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions contribute to the mortality after a stroke?
questions.explanation:
A serious CVA leads to significant immobility
As a result of this bedridden situation many patients develop DVT leading to pulmonary embolus
and battle pulmonary congestion leading to pneumonia, both conditions that result in death
Many stroke patients succumb from a fatal cardiac event
The same atherosclerosis that contributed to the CVA is also present in the coronary arteries
with varying degrees of DM, hypertension, and elevated cholesterol/triglycerides.

questions.question:
The drug of choice for the treatment of methicillin resistant staphylococcus
aureus:
questions.explanation:
Vancomycin is the drug of choice for methicillin resistant staphylococcus
Vancomycin is bactericidal and useful for MRSA
Vancomycin is excreted in the kidney and thus levels of the antibiotic need to be monitored

questions.question: The second most common organism cultured in infected intrathecal catheters?
questions.explanation:
Staphylococcus epidermidis is the most common organism found in infected intrathecal lines
Followed by a staphylococcus aureus infections

questions.question:
Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) should not be used in the
presence of?
questions.explanation:
TENS is a form of electroanalgesia involving the application of electrical stimuli to the skin.
TENS activates low-threshold myelinated nerve fibers which inhibits transmission of pain by
unmyelinated C pain fibers.
A demand pacemaker may be inhibited by the electrical stimuli.

questions.question:
A patient is scheduled to have a phrenic nerve stimulator implanted. What
condition would necessitate this procedure?
questions.explanation:
The diaphragm is innervated by the phrenic nerve that is formed by the C2-C4 nerve roots
A high spinal cord injury results in paralysis or significant paresis of the diaphragm that
contributes to respiratory effort
The stimulator is implanted in order to reestablish function of the diaphragm that may allow the
patient to be weaned off the respirator

questions.question:
Which of the following is critical information that must be conveyed to a
patient in the pre-operative period?

answers.B: What to bring to the hospital
answers.D: What kind of anesthesia will be used

questions.explanation: A patient must know not to eat or drink for at least eight hours before admission for surgery

questions.question: In patients suffering seizures, phenytoin's mechanism of action is:

answers.A: Enhancement of slow inactivation of sodium channels
answers.B: Blocking the repetitive activation of sodium channels

questions.printed_answer_heading: Blocking the repetitive activation of sodium channels
questions.explanation:
Phenytoin works in treatment of seizures by blocking the repetitive activation of sodium channels
Phenobarbital and benzodiazepines provide GABA-A receptor enhancement
Topiramate and lamotrogine are glutamate modulators

questions.question: Which of the following agents is not a beta lactamase inhibitor?
questions.explanation:
Amoxicillin and Clavulanate, Ampicillin and Sulbactam, Piperacillin and Tazobactam and
Ticarcillin and Clavulanate are combined to take advantage of the beta lactamase inhibitor
function inherent in the second drug of the four combinations.

questions.question: Gray rami communicans contain which of the following nerve fibers?
questions.explanation:
The gray rami communicans arises from ganglion of the sympathetic trunk.
They contain postganglionic sympathetic fibers and join each spinal nerve.
Cervical and thoracic fibers supply the heart, thoracic the body wall, lumbar the legs and
abdominal wall, and pelvic the pelvic wall and legs.

questions.question:
Which of the following does not increase intracranial pressure (ICP) after head
trauma?
questions.explanation:
Anytime there is a bleed in the brain, the ICP will generally increase.
Cerebral edema can occur soon after head injury and presents with a variety of signs like
headache, loss of consciousness, pupillary dilatation and visual impairment.
Otorrhea is a consequence of skull fracture and is not directly related to elevated ICP
In severe head injuries with open wounds, meningitis can occur and result in elevated ICP

questions.question: Which is not a common side effect of cholinesterase inhibitors?
questions.explanation:
Nausea, diarrhea, and vomiting are all common side effects associated with cholinesterase
inhibitors.
Anemia is an infrequent adverse effect of cholinesterase inhibitors.
Cholinesterase inhibitors are used to treat Alzheimer disease.

questions.question:
The most serious toxicity of Primaxin(imipenem/cilistatin) in patients with
renal failure is:
questions.explanation: Primaxin can cause myoclonic seizures and a confusional state.

questions.question: Which of the following is false about acupuncture?
questions.explanation: Acupuncture is a relative safe procedure the affects mainly the nervous and endocrine systems

questions.question: Which of these is not a result of implementing effective clinical pathways?

answers.C: Individual preferences for practice and care

questions.printed_answer_heading: Individual preferences for practice and care
questions.explanation:
Improvement in the efficiency of care is a result of implementing effective clinical pathways.
Reduced costs are another result of implementing effective clinical pathways.
Quality of care is a major result of implementing effective clinical pathways.

questions.question:
Which medication has protective effect against granuloma formation during
intrathecal administration?
questions.explanation: Clonidine has been shown to be granuloma protective

questions.question: Which of the following is not an advantage of MRI over CT scanning?

answers.A: Multiplanar imaging without repositioning the patient

questions.explanation: Imaging of solidly calcified structures (eg, bone, cartilage) is better with CT scanning

questions.question:
Temporary loss of nerve function without axonal injury is classified as which
of the following?
questions.explanation:
Neuropraxia is defined as temporary loss of nerve function without presence of axonal injury
Axonotemesis is the second grade of injury where there is disruption of the axon sheath. In this
injury, wallerian degeneration is seen in the distal nerve fragment
Neurotemesis is the most severe injury with disruption of both the axon and sheath. Regeneration
in such injuries is not always possible
Regeneration in peripheral nerves occurs at a rate of 1 mm/day or about 1 inch in a month

questions.question:
A 32-year-old female presents with complaint of diplopia and on rightward
gaze her left eye will not adduct past the midline, horizontal nystagmus is noted in the right eye, but
upward and downward gaze are normal--What is her diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Cranial nerve 3 palsy manifests as ipsilateral pupillary dilatation with inability to look up, down
or medially
Internuclear ophthalmoplegia results in diplopia, unilateral impairment of adduction and
contralateral nystagmus but intact adduction

questions.question: Epidural steroid injections only work for low back pain when?

answers.A: Pain has lasted more than 2 years
answers.B: Pain is not controlled with oral narcotics

questions.explanation:
Epidural steroid injections are most effective with radicular pain.
Radicular pain indicates nerve root inflammation which respond to steroids
Epidural steroids are most effective for pain less than 3 months and rarely beneficial for pain
greater than 12 months
They are not indicated for just low back pain

questions.question: Which of the following causes tremors?

answers.B: Certain drugs such as valproic acid

questions.explanation:
Other causes include TBI, stroke, chronic kidney failure, Parkinson disease, neurodegenerative
diseases, alcohol abuse, liver failure, hyperthyroidism, and mercury poisoning
Essential, hysterical, and familial tremors do not have a specific underlying pathological disease
process

questions.question:
Which of the following wound closure choices is not an adequate replacement
for suture technique?
questions.explanation:
While each method has its purpose, they are not interchangeable, and healing by secondary
intention is limited to distinct situations
In general, healing by secondary intention is not an alternative to suture techniques

questions.question: Motor vehicle accidents are:

answers.A: #1 cause of death in people >75 years

questions.explanation:
Motor vehicle accidents are responsible for the most spinal cord injuries
Head injury is most commonly caused by falls with MVA's being second

questions.question: Which of the following is not a role of social workers?

answers.A: Assess the needs patients during hospitalization and at home
answers.B: Manage financial matters on behalf of the patient
answers.C: Identify available resources and refer patient
answers.D: Work as a team with the physician in charge of care

questions.printed_answer_heading: Manage financial matters on behalf of the patient
questions.explanation:
Social workers are not expected to handle financial matters.
A representative payee can be assigned to manage financial matters.
Social workers should be aware of available resources for patients.
Social workers are essential members of a health care team.

questions.question:
The dorsal primary rami of spinal nerves innervate which of the following
group of muscles?
questions.explanation: The dorsal primary rami of the spinal nerves innervate the deep muscles of the back

questions.question:
Which of the following is characterized by progressive basal ganglia
calcification and encephalopathy?
questions.explanation:
Fahr syndrome is also known as idiopathic basal ganglia calcification
It is thought to have autosomal dominant inheritance but no specific gene location has been found
Age of onset is variable but in children there may be senile appearance, dwarfism, retinitis
pigmentosa, ataxia, mental retardation, seizures, dysarthria, and choreoathetotic movements
The calcification usually start in the pons and dentate followed by the basal ganglia and finally
at the corpus callosum

questions.question:
What should patient who develops high-grade fever and muscular rigidity after
receiving a general anesthesia be given?
questions.explanation:
Malignant hyperthermia is characterized by high grade fever, muscular rigidity, andhigh
metabolic rate.
Succinylcholine, halothane, and other anesthetic gases are implicated.
It is caused by mutations in raynodine receptors of sarcoplasmic reticulum.
The only antidote is dantrolene which blocks raynodine receptors.

questions.question:
Your client has been diagnosed with diabetes insipidus. In addition to accurate
fluid management and assessment of daily weight, you anticipate the administration of:
questions.explanation:
Vasopressin (Pitressin) is an antidiuretic hormone replacement and may be given
intramuscularly, subcutaneously, and nasally. Diabetes insipidus is a disorder of the pituitary
gland
Normally, the pituitary produces the antidiuretic hormone that helps to concentrate urine.
However, the pituitary gland of clients with diabetes insipidus does not produce the antidiuretic
hormone, and clients may have a urinary output of 2 to 10 liters per day
Glipizide is a therapy for diabetes mellitus, not diabetes insipidus
Vasopressin is not given intravenously. Client Need: Physiological Integrity

questions.question: Which of the following is often beneficial side effect of topiramate?
questions.explanation:
Weight loss has been reported as a side effect of topiramate therapy
It usually begins during the first few months of administration
Agranulocytosis and aplastic anemia are seen with carbamazepine therapy

questions.question: What is the best test to identify an intracerebral hemorrhage?
questions.explanation:
The best way to identify an intracerebral hemorrhage is a CT scan
With an MRI, hemorrhage is not always visible within the first few hours
Angiography can identify medium and large size vessels and is preferred in young patients with
suspected structural anomalies
LP may reveal xanthochromia and a profile similar to that seen in subarachnoid hemorrhage

questions.question: The mechanism of dantrolene involves:

answers.A: Blocking calcium release from sarcoplasmic reticulum

questions.printed_answer_heading: Blocking calcium release from sarcoplasmic reticulum
questions.explanation:
Dantrolene blocks calcium release from sarcoplasmic reticulum.
It is indicated for prevention and treatment of malignant hypertension and for spacticity
It is used off label for neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

questions.question: Which of the following is a contraindication to image-guided surgery (IGS)?

answers.A: The patient has a history of allergy to contrast products
answers.C: The procedure is revision endoscopic sinus surgery with distorted anatomy anticipated

questions.explanation:
IGS has virtually no contraindication
No contrast injection is required, no interference is to be feared with implantable devices or
prostheses, even by electromagnetic IGS systems
An up-to-date preoperative CT scan is always a prerequisite of IGS, regardless of the extent of
pre-existing anatomical distortion
The issue of head movements during surgery is also eliminated by the use of a specific headset
during image acquisition for automated registration

questions.question: Which cranial nerve is affected by Bell palsy?
questions.explanation:
Bell's palsy is idiopathic paralysis of the VII cranial nerve which is self limited. 1% of cases
are bilateral
It is due to inflammation which causes edema resulting in ischemic compression in the boney
canal generally near the geniculate ganglion

questions.question: What is the most common cause of meningitis in the elderly population?
questions.explanation: Streptococcus pneumonia is the most common organism for septicemia and pneumonia in elderly

questions.question:
Which of the following will be seen on MRI in patients with corpus callosum
agenesis?

answers.B: Deformity of the 3rd and lateral ventricles

questions.printed_answer_heading: Deformity of the 3rd and lateral ventricles
questions.explanation:
Corpus callosum agenesis can cause a batwing conformation of the lateral ventricles
There can be dilation of the 3rd ventricle and it may have an opening on the brain surface
The condition may be asymptomatic or can be associated with various cognitive disorders
Aicardi syndrome is characterized by corpus callosum agenesis, mental retardation, vertebral
anomalies, chorioretinitis, and epilepsy

questions.question:
Which is not true regarding vasospasm following subarachnoid hemorrhage
(SAH)?

answers.A: Normovolemia, normothermia, normal oxygenation are essential
answers.C: Calcium channel blockers have not been found to be helpful
answers.D: Bedside transcranial Doppler studies can demonstrate vasospasm

questions.printed_answer_heading: Calcium channel blockers have not been found to be helpful
questions.explanation:
Calcium channel blockers have been found to decrease the incidents of ischemic neurological
deficits
Nimodipine improves overall outcome with SAH 3 months after incident
Mechanism of calcium channel blockers is unknown

questions.question:
A 9-month-old child has a chronic cough and sputum production. He was
placed on an antibiotic and 5 days later, the mother noticed that his head was bulging. Examination
revealed that he has bulging anterior fontanels. The child was most likely given:
questions.explanation:
Tetracycline can cause bulging fontanels in infants. After fusion of the sutures it can pseudotumor
cerebri.
It should not be use in children <8 years as it can discolor teeth.
If used long term, tetracyclines may produce microscopic brown-black discoloration of the
thyroid.
Rarely abnormal thyroid function occur.

questions.question:
In a patient with tuberculous meningitis, which drugs may be used in addition
to the 4-drug regimen?
questions.explanation:
Steroid is added to the four drug regimen in patient with tubercular meningitis
Steroid reduces permanent neurological damage

questions.question: What is the organism responsible for encephalitis by the California subgroup?
questions.explanation: LaCrosse virus is the most common organism of encephalopathy by the California subgroup

questions.question:
Which of the following imaging methods is the preferred study for brain
structure in epilepsy?
questions.explanation:
MRI is the best imaging study for evaluating epilepsy.
It has the highest sensitivity and specificity for structural abnormalities and for identifying
intracranial lesions.

questions.question: The third leading cause of death in the USA is:
questions.explanation:
Stroke is the 3rd leading cause of death in the USA
Strokes kill more than 4 million people each year
Strokes are the leading cause of disability in USA

questions.question:
Which of the following can develop a therapeutic relationship in an
emergency?

answers.A: Question the individual as quickly and thoroughly as possible to determine the problem
answers.C: Calm the individual by telling him that everything is going to be fine
answers.D: Repeatedly question the individual about what led up to the accident

questions.explanation:
Using questions that are open-ended encourages the individual can provide detailed information
and helps develop a good therapeutic rapport.

questions.question:
A young patient presents three weeks after a concussion during a football
game. He did not loose consciousness but was confused for 10 minutes. CT of the brain was normal.
He complains about continuous headaches and occasional dizziness. He seems depressed and says he
has problems concentrating. Exam is normal. Select the true statement about the patient's condition.

answers.A: The patient should not participate in collision or contact sports for one month
answers.B: The patient needs a repeat CT
answers.D: He should be given weak narcotics for the headache

questions.explanation:
Blunt head trauma that causes anterior posterior movement of the brain within the skull can cause
a concussion
Confusion, amnesia, and transient loss of consciousness are all common
Fatigue, headache, dizziness, and difficulty concentrating are the symptoms of postconcussion
syndrome
Recovery will occur in 6 to 12 months so collision and contact sports should be avoided until
then

questions.question:
Which of the following is the most appropriate analgesic pharmacotherapy for
a patient in his second post op day?
questions.explanation:
Patient controlled analgesia has been shown to be effective in reducing pain and unnecessary
suffering
Oral diazepam is not used to reduce pain
Fentanyl administration is effective to reduce pain but it is not appropriate in the post op setting
Naloxone is not an analgesic

questions.question:
Which type of respiration may be seen with increased intracranial pressure
(ICP)?
questions.explanation:
When ICP progresses to the point of compressing the brain stem a patient's respirations become
slower and irregular with possible apneic episodes

questions.question:
Following a motorcycle accident, an adult is admitted to the ER alert and fully
oriented even though he was unconscious at the scene. He suddenly loses consciousness and dilates
his left pupil. MRI is done. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Epidural hematomas are typically caused by a tear of the middle meningeal artery from a
temporal skull fracture. It appears as a hyperdense biconvex mass between the skull and dura.
Clinical presentation is highly variable. Classical scenario is a lucid interval following a period
of altered consciousness from which the patient deteriorates developing a dilating pupil and
hemiparesis on the contralateral side
If treated promptly with craniotomy, the outcome is favorable in 85-90% of cases

questions.question:
Which of the following proteins binds to tissue factor and to initiate the
clotting?
questions.explanation:
The extrinsic pathway of the clotting cascade is initiated by the binding of tissue factor to factor
VII or factor VIIa.
All clotting factors need proteolytic cleavage for activity.
The exception is factor VII that has a low level of activity before cleavage.
This allows interaction with phospholipids and tissue factor to initiate the clotting cascade.

questions.question: Hyperphagia is caused by a lesion in the?
questions.explanation:
The hypothalamus plays a major role in regulating eating behavior
The ventromedial nucleus is found in the tuberal region of the hypothalamus
Bilateral lesions of the ventromedial nuclei of the hypothalamus cause hyperphagia, obesity, and
savage behavior, whereas lesions of the lateral hypothalamus produce loss of appetite

questions.question:
A patient with Parkinson disease receives levodopa. The peripheral side
effects of levodopa administration can be reduced by:
questions.explanation:
Carbidopa is a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor with little or no pharmacological activity
It inhibits the peripheral decarboxylation of levodopa to dopamine
Peripheral side effects usually arise from high levels of dopamine in the serum
Bromocriptine is a dopamine agonists

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding patient-controlled anesthesia (PCA)?

answers.B: Over sedation can usually be avoided
answers.C:
The delivery system can usually increase the time interval between patient demand and delivery
of the medication
answers.D: Basal infusion rates should be routinely delivered

questions.printed_answer_heading: Over sedation can usually be avoided
questions.explanation:
Opioid analgesics are used in managing severe acute postoperative pain. Injectable non-
steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (e.g., ketorolac) are also useful, and regional anesthetic
techniques (e.g., local spinal anesthetic) are used in some cases
An opioid may be administered epidurally, typically administered during surgery and continued
2 to 3 days postoperatively. In the recovery room, morphine sulfate or meperidine are
medication options. The dose of narcotics may have to be repeated at short intervals (e.g., every
15 to 30 minutes) until pain relief is established
On the hospital floor, parenteral morphine sulfate usually provides pain relief. Higher doses
provide greater analgesia and a longer duration of effect. PCA allows self-administration of
small opioid doses as needed. It has become the standard of care for the administration of
postoperative narcotic analgesics for pain control
Dosage (frequency and amount) should be modified according to the patient's response. By
limiting the number of doses of medication per hour, the physiciancan avoid oversedation of the
patient. PCA pumps avoid the lag period between when the patient senses pain and initiates the
call for medication and actual delivery by the nurse. It can also reduce the amount of work of
drawing up and delivering multiple doses of medication by the nursing staff. PCA pumps can
also deliver a constant rate of medication per hour whether or not the patient hits the demand
button

questions.question: Mast cells are involved in which of the following types of reaction?
questions.explanation:
Type I: Immediate in onset and mediated by IgE and mast cells and/or basophils
Type II: Delayed in onset and caused by antibody (usually IgG) mediated cell destruction
Type III: Delayed in onset and caused by IgG: drug immune complex deposition and complement
activation
Type IV: Delayed in onset and T cell-mediated

questions.question:
All the following statements about the spinothalamic tracts are correct
EXCEPT:

answers.A: Lateral spinothalamic tract assesses pain and temperature
answers.B:
Both lateral and anterior spinothalamic tracts enter the spinal cord and ascend 4-5 levels in
Issuer's tract before crossing in the white commissure.
answers.C: Anterior spinothalamic tract assesses crude touch, pressure, and itch
answers.D: These tract from the spinal cord enter the thalamus

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Both lateral and anterior spinothalamic tracts enter the spinal cord and ascend 4-5
levels in Issuer's tract before crossing in the white commissure.
questions.explanation:
The anterior and lateral spinothalamic tracts ascent only 2-3 levels before crossing over
The spinothalamic tract is divided into the direct and indirect subsystems
The direct subsystem is for conscious appreciation of sensation
The indirect subsystem is for arousal and affective impact of pain

questions.question: Which is the best knot to use when applying a patient restraint?

answers.D: Knots are not needed for patient restraints

questions.explanation:
A half bow knot is secure enough for restraints, but it can be quickly and easily released if
necessary

questions.question: Atropine is associated with all of the following side effects, except:
questions.explanation:
Atropine is an anticholinergic that is often used prior to surgery to dry up secretions
Pupillary dilation, tachycardia, and urinary retention are some side effects of atropine

questions.question:
During a posterior approach for a lumbar dissection a patient becomes
profoundly hypotensive. What should be done?

answers.B: Finish quickly and obtain an urgent CT
answers.D:
Pack the wound, place the patient in a supine position, and call vascular surgery for an
exploratory laparotomy

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Pack the wound, place the patient in a supine position, and call vascular surgery for
an exploratory laparotomy
questions.explanation:
A potentially fatal complication of the anterior longitudinal approach for lumbar surgery is
violation of the anterior longitudinal ligament damaging the great vessels

questions.question: Which of the following is characteristic of the bulbospongiosus reflex?

answers.A: It is a test for functional integrity of S1 to S3
answers.B: It is a test for functional integrity of S2 to S4
answers.C: It is a test for functional integrity of S3 to S5
answers.D: It is a test for functional integrity of S4 to S6

questions.printed_answer_heading: It is a test for functional integrity of S2 to S4
questions.explanation:
The test is elicited by pinching the glans penis
The bulbospongiosus muscle encircles the corpus spongiosum and corpus cavernosa at the root
of the penis then contracts

questions.question: Which one of the following is not the side effect of atropine?
questions.explanation:
Atropine is anticholinergic drug
It causes dry skin, dilated pupil, urinary retention, and tachycardia
Psychosis, flushed skin, and decrerased secretions are also seen
Excessive salivation occurs in cholinergic poisoning

questions.question: What is the most likely cause of postoperative fever within the first 48 hours?
questions.explanation:
In the first 24 to 48 hours post-op IL-1 and -6, and TNF are responsible for postoperative fever
The other options may cause fever but at later time points

questions.question: What is the least common complication of the spina bifida?
questions.explanation: Spina bifida is not normally associated with upper extremity weakness

questions.question:
What preoperative tests should be performed in an otherwise healthy 45 year
old woman undergoing elective surgery?
questions.explanation:
ECG should be performed on all patients over 40 to identify previous silent MI, arrhythmia
Preoperative tests should be ordered after preexisting conditions and a history and physical have
been performed

questions.question: What is the major aim of preoperative screening?

answers.A: To assess patient's physical and psychological readiness for surgery
answers.C: To provide explanation about the surgery

questions.printed_answer_heading: To assess patient's physical and psychological readiness for surgery
questions.explanation:
Identifying potential barriers for surgery is the major aim of preoperative screening.
Preoperative screening also helps in predicting surgery or anesthetic complication.
Informed consent should be obtained before screening.
Patient's concerns should be addressed before planning the operation.

questions.question:
After a thromboembolic event, elective surgery should ideally be postponed
for:
questions.explanation:
Elective surgery should be postponed at least one month but ideally it should be delayed three
months

questions.question:
You are most likely going to find the artery of Adamkiewicz located at the
level of:
questions.explanation:
The artery of Adamkiewicz is normally found between T8 and L3..
About fifteen percent of patients have the artery of Adamkiewicz above T8.

questions.question:
An epidural spinal cord stimulator to treat foot pain should be implanted at
what site?
questions.explanation: The SCS electrode should be placed between T11 and T12 for foot pain

questions.question:
A female notices discharge from her nipples and amenorrhea. The pregnancy
test is negative. Her exam otherwise is normal except suggestion of a possible slight left temporal
quadrantanopsia. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Prolactinoma causes amenorrhea and galactorrhea. A serum level should be elevated and MRI
will reveal a tumor
FSH tumors are non-functioning and only cause symptoms due to mass effect. Hypothyroidism
can cause hyperprolactinemia but no visual disturbances
ACTH tumors do not cause amenorrhea and galactorrhea
Cushing disease symptoms include hypertension, hirsutism, fatigue, and truncal obesity

questions.question:
42-year-old woman complains of the sudden onset of a severe headache after
brief period of unconsciousness. Exam reveals stiff neck, photophobia and dilated pupil. There was
no trauma. Which type of vascular event has most likely occurred?
questions.explanation:
Sudden onset of very severe headache with photophobia is classic presentation of SAH
(subarachnoid hemorrhage) in which 85% of the time cerebral angiography will reveal an
aneurysm(s). 15-20% of the time no obvious source of bleeding is determined in which a repeat
angiogram is sometime ordered.
Most neurosurgeons recommend immediate surgery to avoid complications of rebleeding and
treat vasospasm more aggressively.
SAH is graded on Hunt and Hess scale I-V with I being minimum symptoms and V being deep
coma with poor prognosis

questions.question: Which of these happens when physicians do not met managed care standards?

answers.B: There are state and federal fines
answers.C: There is an imbalance in quality and cost

questions.explanation:
Physicians who do not meet managed care standards are removed from the contract.
When physicians do not meet managed care standards there is an imbalance in quality and cost.
There are no current state or federal fines for not meeting managed care standards.

questions.question: The choice which is FALSE related to Medicare is:

answers.A: Paid by citizens through their taxes
answers.D: Set forth to pay the medical bills of those 65 and older

questions.explanation:
Medicare is funded by citizens through their employment or self-employment taxes.
Medicare is an entitlement program (for enrollees and their spouses).
Medicare is a federally funded program.
Medicare was set forth to pay the medical bills of those 65 and older.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best abortive treatment for cluster headaches?
questions.explanation:
The pharmacologic management of cluster headaches is divided into abortive (or symptomatic)
strategies and preventative (or prophylactic) strategies.
Cluster headaches generally are intensely painful, develop rapidly, achieve peak intensity in
about 10 minutes, and last about two hours untreated.
High flow concentrated oxygen via nasal cannula or mask is the most effective treatment.
Ergotamine sublingually or rectally may be helpful, and triptans have been used, but oral
medications generally are less helpful due to the time needed for absorption.

questions.question:
Which of the following describes the primary role of the nurse in the
healthcare system?

answers.A: Delivering the care ordered by physicians

questions.explanation:
The primary role of the nurse is to deliver the care ordered by physicians for patients.
Educating and providing information to patients is another of the primary roles of the nurse in the
healthcare system.

questions.question:
A 44 year old is robbed and is knocked unconscious for several minutes from a
blow to his head. Other than a mild headache, he is otherwise fine and returns home. The following
day he is found to be unresponsive by his wife, but by the time the ambulance arrives he regains
consciousness and is alert but has slight right sided weakness. Which is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.A: Cerebral herniation due to evolving epidural hematoma
answers.D: Narcotic encephalopathy due to medications taken for headache

questions.explanation:
The patient may well have an epidural hematoma but progressive obtundation would be
expected with cerebral herniation
With head trauma with loss of consciousness, post-traumatic epilepsy would be possible and
result in fluctuating levels of alertness from postictal states

questions.question: Which one of the following patients is at high risk of postoperative bleeding?
questions.explanation:
Many of the coagulation factors are made in the liver.
Patients with chronic liver disease are at high risk of bleeding after surgery.
Steroid therapy suppresses endogenous steroid secretion.

questions.question: A male with a prolactinoma is least likely to exhibit which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Prolactinomas tend to cause decreased libido, impotence, and infertility
As with any type of pituitary tumor, they may also cause visual changes

questions.question:
A patient with a left arm amputation complains of cramping and burning pain
of the left hand. What is the correct term for this?
questions.explanation:
60 to 80% of patients report phantom limb sensations after amputations
50 to 80% report pain

questions.question:
A patient's ICP is being monitored in the neurosurgical ICU due to a closed
head injury. His ICP measurements suddenly start to rise. An acute increase in ICP is characterized
by which of the following clinical findings?
questions.explanation:
Irregular respirations, bradycardia, and increased blood pressure result from high ICP increases
and are termed the Cushing response or triad.. Irregular respirations are due to hypoperfusion of
the brainstem. Cushing response is a terminal event of head trauma and usually indicates that
herniation is imminent. During the initial rise of ICP, there will be tachycardia.
Hypertension is a compensatory response to decreased cerebral perfusion which is the
difference between MAP and ICP. Blood pressure will rise due to vasoconstriction and
increased cardiac output to increase CPP
The resultant hypertension stimulates the baroreceptors in the carotid bodies causing
bradycardia.
Herniation of brain parenchyma through the tentorial incisura or foramen magnum causes
brainstem and third cranial nerve compression leading to a fixed and dilated pupil. Papilledema
is a finding of chronically elevated ICP.

questions.question:
What is the best treatment regimen for a postoperative deep vein thrombosis
(DVT)

answers.A: Heparin GTT and Plavix 75 mg qd
answers.B: Aspirin 325 mg PO qd with Coumadin titrated to INR of >3.0
answers.C: Plavix 75 mg qd PO with Coumadin titrated to INR of >2.0
answers.D: Enoxaparin at 1 mg/kg SC with warfarin titrated to INR of 2.0 to 2.5

questions.printed_answer_heading: Enoxaparin at 1 mg/kg SC with warfarin titrated to INR of 2.0 to 2.5
questions.explanation:
The patient needs to become therapeutic with a heparin drip or enoxaparin.
They are started on warfarin with an INR of 2.0 to 2.5 for 3-6 months.
The treatments must overlap for several days.
DVT prophylaxis is unfractionated heparin 5000 U SQ BID or TID, or enoxaparin 30 to 40 mg
Qday or BID

questions.question: Which of these is true of clinical pathways?

answers.A: Laboratory and radiographic diagnostics are recommended for each pathway
answers.B: Differential diagnoses are a central feature

questions.explanation:
Laboratory or radiographic diagnostics are recommended for each pathway.
Differential diagnoses are a central feature of clinical pathways.
Therapeutic treatment plans are presented in clinical pathways.
Pathways are guidelines and never replace the judgment of the practitioner who must consider
the patient in each case.

questions.question:
Select the correct statement about asymptomatic patients with MRI findings of
white matter lesions (WMLs).

answers.A: FLAIR or T2 weighted sequences on MRI are best to visualize WMLs
answers.B: WMLs in asymptomatic patients most often results in multiple sclerosis
answers.D: It is very rare for asymptomatic patients to have WMLs

questions.printed_answer_heading: FLAIR or T2 weighted sequences on MRI are best to visualize WMLs
questions.explanation:
WMLs are a nonspecific finding that can be associated with demyelination, ischemia, or gliosis
Deep WMLs are more likely associated with ischemia or demyelination than periventricular
WMLs
WMLs are best seen by MRI on FLAIR or T2 weighted sequences
Confluent and larger lesions probably indicate more extensive pathology

questions.question: Which of the following is the overall aim of rehabilitation?

answers.A:
Restoring the highest achievable level of personal independence in patients facing several
challenges
answers.B: A simplified referral system to support the recovery of patients in an outpatient setting
answers.C:
The utilization of objective and subjective indicators to measure and evaluate the quality and
safety of clinical services provided to members
answers.D: Teaching patients how to manage a chronic disease

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Restoring the highest achievable level of personal independence in patients facing
several challenges
questions.explanation:
Restoring the highest achievable level of personal independence in patients facing several
challenges is the overall aim of rehabilitation.
A simplified referral system to support the recovery of patients in an outpatient setting is the aim
of an outpatient clinical referral system.
The utilization of objective and subjective indicators to measure and evaluate the quality and
safety of clinical services provided to members is the definition of quality improvement
measures.
Teaching patients how to manage a chronic disease is the process of disease management.

questions.question:
In general, a patient with neurogenic claudication will have the most
improvement of symptoms with which position?
questions.explanation:
Neurogenic claudication improves with supine position
Symptoms are worse with physical exercise especially downhill ambulation
Some patients report improvement to flexion of the lumbar spine

questions.question:
Soon after surgery is started the patient has develops extreme muscle rigidity.
The patient is tachycardic and has a fever of 104 degrees. The treatment for the above condition:
questions.explanation:
Dantrolene and observation for the next 24 hours is recommended. The condition can recur
The patient has malignant hyperthermia

questions.question: Diabetic amyotrophy usually resolves by:
questions.explanation:
Diabetic amyotrophy usually presents with initial pain in the lower extremities
It usually resolves spontaneously in one to two years

questions.question: All of the following statements about the Romberg test are correct EXCEPT:

answers.A: Tested with patient standing with feet together both with eyes open and closed
answers.B: The examiner may push the patient slightly to assess reaction
answers.C: Balance evaluates visual, posterior column, vestibular, and cerebellar inputs
answers.D: An examinee that cannot maintain balance both with eyes open and closed has cerebellar disease

questions.printed_answer_heading:
An examinee that cannot maintain balance both with eyes open and closed has
cerebellar disease
questions.explanation:
When the eyes are opened, generally, the visual system should overcome vestibular and
posterior column dysfunction and positive Romberg indicates cerebellar disease
There is a proviso that with severe vestibular and posterior column disease, imbalance may still
persist with eyes open
A complete neurological examination with possible testing should be able to clarify the
dysfunctional system

questions.question: Which of the following brain structures is most susceptible to hypoxic injury?
questions.explanation:
The hippocampus belongs to the limbic system and plays a role in long term memory
In Alzheimer's disease, it is one of the first regions to suffer from the disease
The hippocampus is also very sensitive to hypoxia, encephalitis or anoxic injury

questions.question: After peripheral IV placement, the least likely complication is?
questions.explanation:
Bleeding, infiltration, infection, and thrombosis are common complications of peripheral IV
placement

questions.question: The pain from injecting local anesthetic may be lessened by:
questions.explanation:
Warming the anesthetic, subcutaneous injection, and topical anesthetics may all lessen pain from
injection

questions.question: In the pain theory, which nerves are not excluded?
questions.explanation: Pain theory involves small, large, excitatory, and inhibitory nerves

questions.question: A common cause of movements mimicking seizure activity is:
questions.explanation:
Movement resembling uncontrollable seizure activity can develop from hypoglycemia and can
be quickly treated with administration of glucose

questions.question: Electrocautery current differs from wall current in:
questions.explanation: Electrocautery current frequency is 105 Hz

questions.question: Which structures typically drain into the superior sagittal sinus?

answers.A: The superior ophthalmic vein and the superior cerebral veins
answers.B: Diploic veins of Breschet and the great cerebral vein
answers.C: Superior cerebral veins and the diploic veins of Breschet
answers.D: The superior ophthalmic vein and veins from the middle cerebrum

questions.printed_answer_heading: Superior cerebral veins and the diploic veins of Breschet
questions.explanation:
The superior sagittal sinus runs posterosuperiorly from the crista galli to meet the transverse
sinus, usually to the right of the internal occipital protuberance
The sinus receives drainage from the superior cerebral veins in its anterior portion followed by
the diploic veins of Breschet
It is important to remember that the anatomy of the venous sinuses can be highly variable, and
anomalies should be studied

questions.question:
Which of the following is seen on MRI in patients with headaches due to
intracranial hypotension?
questions.explanation:
Intracranial venous distension is seen as a response to intracranial hypotension
Spinal meningeal diverticula on cervical and thoracic spinal MRI is one manifestation of such
Subdural fluid collections are also a manifestation of intracranial venous distension
Patchy meningeal contrast enhancement is also seen in such patients and is the reason that LP is
preferably performed after MRI

questions.question: The dorsal root contains which of the following fibers?

answers.A: General somatic afferent and general visceral afferent
answers.B: General somatic efferent and general visceral efferent

questions.printed_answer_heading: General somatic afferent and general visceral afferent
questions.explanation: The dorsal root contains general somatic afferent and the general visceral afferent fibers

questions.question: Which is not an opportunistic organism that can cause a brain abscess?
questions.explanation:
Common opportunistic organisms causing brain abscess include Toxoplasma, Candida,
Nocardia, and Aspergillus

questions.question:
During the neurological exam, the patient is unable to smoothly accomplish the
finger to nose exam with eyes closed. What is the condition?
questions.explanation:
Dysmetria is a failure of fine motor coordination in which the subject overshoots and
undershoots the object repeatedly
Closing the eyes prevents any use of visual cues
This finding is indicative of cerebellar disease which modulates motor movement
The cerebellar hemispheres primarily control extremity movement ensuring precision while the
midline vermis influences whole body coordination

questions.question: Central diabetes insipidus is not associated with?
questions.explanation: Signs of central diabetes insipidus include hypernatremia and high serum osmolarity

questions.question: Bromocriptine is associated with al of the following side effects, except:
questions.explanation:
Hypotension and cardiovascular collapse are some side effects of bromocriptine therapy
Drowsiness and GI upset are common side effects
Hallucinations can occur in bromocriptine therapy

questions.question: Which is least consistent with the diagnosis of peripheral vertigo?

answers.A: Nystagmus that is not inhibited by ocular fixation

questions.printed_answer_heading: Nystagmus that is not inhibited by ocular fixation
questions.explanation:
Peripheral vertigo usually has prominent nausea and vomiting, inhibition of nystagmus by ocular
fixation, and unidirectional nystagmus that is aggravated by head position (Hallpike maneuver)
Central vertigo is often accompanied by dysarthria, facial numbness, or leg weakness, which are
brainstem signs
Central vertigo is usually associated with minimal nausea, and the nystagmus is multi-directional
and not affected to head position

questions.question: Which of these is a role of the primary care doctors in managed care?
questions.explanation:
Primary care doctors are gatekeepers in managed care organizations.
Primary care doctors modify their practice to maximize the goals of managed care.
Primary care doctors work with managed care organizations to enhance care within the
framework agreed to in their contractual arrangements.

questions.question: Cerebral abscesses develop most often as a complication of:
questions.explanation:
Direct extension from a sinus, odontogenic and otogenic sources is still the most common cause
of cerebral abscess
Hematogenous spread can occur in people with heart disease, abdominal infections and other
wound infections
Penetrating head trauma is also a common cause of infection after surgery
Opportunistic infections are increasingly a known cause of cerebral abscess, especially in HIV
patients

questions.question:
A freshly cut surgical wound usually regains 80% of its strength back after
what period of time?
questions.explanation:
The wound regains at least 4% of its original strength at about 2 weeks
It regains about 80% of its strength after several months
Most wounds never regain their original strength even after 12 months

questions.question:
Hyperkalemia affects neuron-resting membrane potential in which of the
following ways?

answers.A: Larger stimulus would be required to exceed threshold
answers.B: Resting membrane potential would become less negative
answers.C: Resting membrane potential would become more negative

questions.printed_answer_heading: Resting membrane potential would become less negative
questions.explanation:
The resting membrane potential would become less negative leading to a lower threshold for
production of action potentials

questions.question:
A patient with meningitis has the following findings on examination of the
CSF: WBC 5000/L, 90% PMNs, low glucose, high protein and gram positive diplococci on gram
stain. What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.explanation:
Bacterial meningitis causes the following CSF profile: opening pressure of 200-300 mm Hg,
WBC 100-5000 with >80% PMNs, glucose < 40, protein > 100
H. influenzae is a gram negative rod and Neisseria meningitides is a gram negative diplococcus
Tuberculosis meningitis causes a lymphocytic pleocytosis in the CSF and there are acid fast
bacilli on gram stain
Viral meningitis causes CSF with a lymphocytic pleocytosis but WBC count is lower than in
bacterial meningitis, normal or slightly reduced glucose, and normal or slightly elevated protein

questions.question: Which of the following is a true statement about IgE-mediated anaphylaxis?

answers.A: Foods containing peanut oil may cause it
answers.B: Allergies to latex do not occur
answers.C: It is not caused by immunotherapy

questions.printed_answer_heading: Foods containing peanut oil may cause it
questions.explanation: Peanut anaphylaxis may be caused by any foods containing peanuts, or their byproducts.

questions.question: Frontal release signs are most likely to be seen in?
questions.explanation:
Certain primitive reflexes emerge with frontal lobe lesions in adults
Frontal lobe release signs are common in infants
Suck, snout, grasp, and root reflexes are frontal release signs
The most useful sign for evaluating frontal lobe dysfunction is the grasp reflex

questions.question: Select the best test to diagnose varicella zoster virus meningitis.
questions.explanation:
The best and fasted test for diagnosing VZV meningitis is PCR of CSF
Half of patients with VZV meningitis have no skin lesions
It can be a complication of primary infection but is more often due to virus reactivation
Tzanck stain, electron microscopy, immunofluorescence, and viral culture are not the ideal
diagnostic tests

questions.question: Barbiturate toxicity can cause:
questions.explanation:
Barbiturates depress the central nervous system respiratory center that can lead to loss of
respiratory function, pneumonia and death

questions.question:
A 28-year-old male was involved in a motor vehicle accident. In the ER, he is
stable. Examination reveals that when he is asked to sit up, the umbilicus moves up toward the neck
area. He may have:
questions.explanation:
Beevor's sign is the movement of the umbilicus when the upper body is bent. This is caused by
weakened lower abdominal muscles
Beevor's sign is a classic feature of patients with spinal cord injury between T6 -T10
When the patient is asked to sit up the umbilicus will move up. This is often seen in amyotrophic
lateral sclerosis

questions.question: Vascular dementia is associated with strokes at:
questions.explanation: Vascular dementia is associated with lacuna strokes

questions.question: Which of the following not a risk factor for breakage of needle?

answers.C: Twisting while needle still in tissue

questions.explanation: Changing direction and push against hard surface can result needle breakage

questions.question: The P38 potential is generating at the:
questions.explanation:
The P38 potential is generated at the lower extremity cortical area
The N14 potential is generated at the cervicomedullary area
The N20 potential is generated at the cortical region
The N22 potential is generated at the gray matter of the spinal cord

questions.question: Post lumbar puncture headache is less associated with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Female sex increases the possibility of lumbar puncture headache

questions.question:
A patient with homonymous hemianopsia is referred to a visual therapy center.
All of the following statements are correct about rehabilitation EXCEPT:

answers.B: Optical devices to shift the visual field

questions.explanation:
Patients must be taught to scan the visual field back and forth
Therapy is directed at establishing special patterns of stimulation. Optical devices are Gottlieb
visual field awareness system and Leli system
Scanning therapy uses the Dynavision machine
If visual neglect has developed, it can be diagnoses with the behavior in-attention test (BIT).
Treatment involves occupational training

questions.question: Which is not associated with Von Recklinghausen?
questions.explanation:
Neurofibromatosis is an autosomal dominant disorder that affects bone, skin, CNS and soft
tissue.
CafÃ© au lait spots are irregular brownish spots that vary in diameter. Less than 1% of healthy
children have three or more such spots.
Lisch nodules are hamartomas of the iris and are asymptomatic. Axillary freckles known as
Crow's sign often develop during puberty.
Neurofibromas are common benign tumors composed of Schwann cells, mast cells and vascular
tissue. They usually develop along nerves.

questions.question: The motor pathway is called:
questions.explanation: Motor signals are sent via the corticospinal tract

questions.question:
Which of the following types of hearing loss is commonly seen in patients with
Crouzon syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Crouzon syndrome shows craniofacial abnormalities
Conductive hearing loss is common with craniofacial abnormalities
Craniosynostosis is the prominent feature that leads facial bone abnormalities
The clinical presentation of this disease is variable

questions.question:
The approximate time the brain can be anoxic before developing irreversible
damage is:
questions.explanation:
After a person is without cardiopulmonary function for 4 to 6 minutes, permanent brain damage
is almost certain

questions.question: Which is not a sign of intravenous (IV) line infiltration?
questions.explanation: Signs of IV line infiltration include coldness, pain, and swelling at the insertion site

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true in older trauma patient population?

answers.A: Spinal injuries are less common than younger patients
answers.C: Pelvic fractures carry a good prognosis
answers.D: There is a delay presentation of intracranial hemorrhages

questions.printed_answer_heading: There is a delay presentation of intracranial hemorrhages
questions.explanation:
Delay presentation of intracranial hemorrhages may occur due to cerebral atrophy
The incidence of spinal fractures increases secondary to osteoporosis

questions.question:
Which congenital anomaly is commonly caused by folic acid deficiency during
pregnancy?
questions.explanation:
Folate demand increases during pregnancy due to expansion of blood volume
Folate deficiency causes mostly neural tube defect
Cleft palate can be caused by Patau or Edward syndromes

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about suctioning head injured patients is not
correct?

answers.A: The FIO2 should be increased to 100% before, during and for a brief period after the suctioning
answers.B: If the patient reacts or bucks, premedicate with a sedative
answers.C: If ICP tends to increase during suctioning, hyperventilate prior to procedure
answers.D: Patients with poorly controlled ICP should have less suctioning

questions.printed_answer_heading: Patients with poorly controlled ICP should have less suctioning
questions.explanation:
The most important consideration during suctioning is to minimize ICP spikes and decreases in
PO2 which is detrimental for an injured brain

questions.question:
An infant undergoing myelomeningocele resection should be placed in what
position?
questions.explanation:
Myelomeningocele is an out pouching of the spinal cord
Prone position is needed for resection

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about primary central nervous system
lymphoma in immunocompetent patients is true?

answers.A: It is more common before the age of 40
answers.B: Glucocorticoids should be administrated before stereotactic biopsy
answers.C: B lymphocyte phenotype is found in more than 80% of cases
answers.D: The survival rate significantly improves with tumor resection

questions.printed_answer_heading: B lymphocyte phenotype is found in more than 80% of cases
questions.explanation:
Most primary central nervous system lymphomas are non-Hodgkin lymphomas, with about 80%
being non-Hodgkin B cell lymphoma
The clinical features of the disease may include deterioration of cognitive function, headache,
and seizures
When lymphoma is suspected, a biopsy should be performed before starting treatment,
particularly with glucocorticosteroids
In about half of patients, the tumor responds to steroid administration and may occasionally
transiently disappear completely, compromising the pathologic diagnosis and delaying treatment

questions.question: Which medical condition predisposes patient to pulmonary embolism?
questions.explanation:
Hypercoagulability, oral contraceptive use and deep venous stasis are predisposing factors for
PE
Any surgery is a risk factor for PE

questions.question:
A patient complains of chronic, dull, periorbital headaches. The pain was
initially intermittent but has recently become constant. It is present upon wakening in the morning and
exacerbated by coughing. Physical examination reveals plantar extension on the left. Which diagnosis
is most likely?
questions.explanation:
Awakening with a headache is suggestive of an intracranial tumor
The pain associated with an intracranial tumor is often constant, dull, and boring, and increased
by coughing and straining
Focal localizing signs may be transient or absent
Supratentorial tumors typically produce pain in the anterior aspect of the head

questions.question:
A patient has parkinsonism for less than one year and develops dementia. What
is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Diffuse Lewy body disease is characterized by the clinical combination of parkinsonism and
dementia
If the parkinsonism has been present for less than one year before the dementia it is called Lewy
body dementia. If it has been present for more than one year it is called Parkinson disease with
dementia
ALS is characterized by fasciculations, spasticity and dysarthria. Alzheimer disease is the most
common form of dementia
Parkinson disease has 4 cardinal signs-resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia and postural
instability

questions.question:
What speech difficulty is seen in an 82-year-old male with CVA who has intact
speech but inappropriate word choices and nonsensical phrases?
questions.explanation:
Wernicke aphasia is a receptive aphasia due to damage of the posterior superior temporal gyrus
of the dominant hemisphere characterized by wordy, nonsensical speech
Broca's aphasia (dominant inferior frontal gyrus) is an expressive aphasia with broken, nonfluent
speech
Dysarthria is due to dysfunction of the muscles used for speech causing slurred speech; Global
aphasia is a complete loss of speech ability

questions.question:
Which of the following clinical features suggests that this 69 year old
demented male may have normal pressure hydrocephalus?
questions.explanation:
Ataxia and long pyramidal tract signs predominate in hydrocephalus
Patients may have brisk reflexes along with ataxia
Cogwheel rigidity and bradykinesia are suggestive of Parkinson's disease

questions.question:
A patient in the ICU after traumatic brain injury is assessed with verbal
response, motor response, and eye opening. What assessment tool is being used?

answers.A: Rancho Los Amigos Cognitive Functioning Scale

questions.explanation:
The modified Glasgow Coma Scale is used to assess patients with traumatic brain injury
A score based on verbal response, motor response, and eye opening is done
A scores range from 3 to 16
A score of less than 8 indicates a coma

questions.question: Which is false about meningiomas?

answers.A: Most commonly found in intra axial location

questions.printed_answer_heading: Most commonly found in intra axial location
questions.explanation:
Meningiomas are extra axial lesions and occur intracranially or within the spinal canal
Meningiomas commonly occur on the surface of the brain or at the skull base
Meningiomas are thought to originate from arachnoid cap cells that reside near the arachnoid
layer covering the brain
Spinal meningiomas may give rise to the brown sequard syndrome (i.e. contralateral decreased
pain, ipsilateral weakness, decrease in position sense) and sphincter weakness

questions.question: What sensory input is required for the flexor withdrawal reflex?
questions.explanation:
Rooting reflex is characterized by head turning with tactile stimulation
The flexor withdrawal reflex is characterized by extremity flexion with painful stimulation

questions.question: Which of the following is the best description of a countercoup brain injury?

answers.A: The injury to the brain is on the opposite side from the impact
answers.B: The injury to the brain is on the same sided as the impact
answers.C: The injury to the brain occurs over the entire surface of the brain
answers.D: The injury to the brain is on both sides of the brain

questions.printed_answer_heading: The injury to the brain is on the opposite side from the impact
questions.explanation: A countercoup brain injury is on the opposite side from the impact

questions.question:
A child entering kindergarten has spina bifida at the level of the sacrum. What
findings would the child be expected to have?

answers.A: Weakness and loss of sensation distal to the waist
answers.B: Movement of the upper legs and hips but none below the knees
answers.C: Variable strength at the ankle dorsiflexors and absent ankle plantar flexors

questions.explanation:
Spina bifida with sacral involvement would show variable ankle plantar strength
Involvement at the low lumbar level would result in variable strength at the ankle dorsiflexors
and absent ankle plantar flexors
Involvement at the high lumbar level would result in absent hip extension and abduction as well
as all ankle and knee movements

questions.question: The drug known to be associated with benign intracranial hypertension is:
questions.explanation:
Pseudotumor cerebri (PTC) or Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (IIH) is a disease where
there is increased intracranial pressure that mimics a brain tumor
It is commonly seen with minocycline
The disorder is most common in women of childbearing age
Papilledema is a common presentation, which may progress to optic atrophy and blindness

questions.question: Which of the following changes in laboratories is not normal with aging?
questions.explanation:
Renal function and perfusion decrease with age but muscle mass also decreases so creatinine
usually does not change
Cholesterol and glucose tend to increase with age, possibly explaining why diabetes mellitus is
more common in the elderly
ESR increases significantly with age so interpretation should take this into account

questions.question:
In which of the following disorders is a stellate ganglion block usually not
done?

answers.D:
Chest pain from severe triple vessel coronary artery disease which is unresponsive to
medications

questions.explanation:
Pneumothorax and phrenic nerve blockade are potential complications of stellate ganglion block.

calcium influx.

Microcytic anemia and pica syndrome is caused by iron deficiency anemia

A patient is involved in a motor vehicle accident and is unresponsive to pain

questions.question:
Following a minor motor vehicle accident, a patient is experiencing pain and
stiffness in her neck. Upon physical exam, she is able to rotate her neck greater than 55 degrees and
denies paresthesias in the extremities. Which of the following is the next best step for this patient?
questions.explanation:

questions.question:
A craniopharyngioma is removed by craniotomy performed under general
anesthesia via endotrachial tube. Halothane is used and the patient is fully awake in the recovery

312 mOsm/L, pH = 7.52, PCO2 = 28 mm Hg, bicarbonate = 24 mEq/L. Which of the following is
responsible for the coma?

answers.A: Surgical trauma to the posterior pituitary
answers.B: Respiratory depression induced by unmetabolized anesthetic

questions.printed_answer_heading: Surgical trauma to the posterior pituitary
questions.explanation:
The patient has central diabetes insipidus
Craniopharyngiomas are close to the pituitary so there was most likely damage to the posterior
pituitary or stalk
The patient is hyperventilating as evidenced by the low PCO2

questions.question: What should be done if patient is crying?

answers.A: Tell them that crying won't help
answers.B: Allow them to cry and let out their emotions
answers.C: Ask if they would like to meet with a therapist
answers.D: Ask if they feel like hurting themselves or others

questions.printed_answer_heading: Allow them to cry and let out their emotions
questions.explanation:
Giving enough time and space to shake off feelings is appropriate.
Telling them that crying won't help is being judgmental.
When patients are calmer is it important to ask about suicidal ideation.
If a patient appears to be ready to cry but does not, offering a tissue can give them permission to
do so.

questions.question:
The extrathalamic cortical modulatory system, which uses acetylcholine as a
neurotransmitter, arises from the?

answers.C: Nucleus basalis of Meynert of the basal forebrain

questions.printed_answer_heading: Nucleus basalis of Meynert of the basal forebrain
questions.explanation:
There are at least six neurochemically distinct extrathalamic projection systems that reach the
cerebrum monosynaptically, without a relay in the thalamus: three arise from the brain stem
reticular formation, two from the hypothalamus, and one from the basal forebrain
From the nucleus basalis, located in the basal forebrain, arises a cholinergic extrathalamic
modulatory system
The basal forebrain contains four populations of cholinergic neurons with projection to the
cerebral cortex, with the nucleus basalis of Meynert as the principal source of cholinergic
neurons

questions.question:
A previously healthy patient initially complained of a severe headache and
then loses consciousness. An intracerebral hematoma or subarachnoid hemorrhage is suspected.

answers.A: A lumbar puncture may be safely performed if there is no papilledema
answers.B: Absence of xanthochromia in the cerebrospinal fluid rules out a subarachnoid hemorrhage

Papilledema may not develop for 12 to 18 hours after the onset of raised intracranial pressure
Xanthochromia may not be detected until 4 to 6 hours after a subarachnoid hemorrhage
CT scans are generally more sensitive than MRI in detecting acute subarachnoid hemorrhage or
intracerebral hematoma
CT scans do not detect all subarachnoid hemorrhages; they may be negative in up to 15% of
patients with this condition

questions.question:
A 60-year-old man presents with pain in the upper legs that is exacerbated
with walking. Symptoms are relieved with sitting. Peripheral pulses are intact. The most likely
diagnosis is:
questions.explanation:
Spinal stenosis is a condition characterized by pain in the legs, calves, thighs, and buttocks that
occurs with walking, running, or climbing stairs. Symptoms are often relieved by flexing at the
spine or sitting
Lying with the lumbar in extension exacerbates symptoms. This is thought to be secondary to
ventral infolding of the ligamentum flavum into an already narrowed canal.
Middle-age patients and the elderly are most commonly affected. Early complaints are usually of
nonspecific back pain. Later complaints include leg fatigue, numbness, pain, and weakness,
Minor trauma can exacerbate symptoms resulting investigations reveiling the diagnosis. Leg pain
is usually bilateral and involves the thighs and buttocks.

questions.question: All of the following are causes of embolic stroke EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:

Arterial dissection can knock off pieces of plaque that become emboli. Plaque is made up of fat,
cholesterol and calcium. Arterial dissection sometime results in a partial to complete blockage
without any emboli

small thrombi

questions.question: Which is not an example of intentional tort?

A patient with abdominal pain attempts to leave the emergency department, but security is called
