A 25 year old female complains of a 1 week history of generalized moderate
intensity headaches with bilateral blurred vision. The patient has no past medical history and is on no
medications. Exam shows BMI of 32, blood pressure of 145/95 mm Hg, heart rate of 88 bpm, and
respiratory rate of 16. Visual acuity is 20/80 OD and 20/60 OS. On lateral gaze the right eye will not
full abduct. Visual field testing shows bilaterally enlarged blind spots. Papilledema is present
bilaterally. Select the most probable diagnosis.
questions.explanation:
The patient has idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) with associated loss of vision
IIH is most common in obese females of childbearing years
The least invasive, most effective treatment for her vision is optic nerve fenestration but her
vision may not return to normal
In addition, the patient may need a VP shunt, lumboperitoneal shunt, or medication

questions.question: Symptoms of a surgical site infection usually become obvious:

answers.B: Five to six days after the surgery
answers.D: If the surgery site was shaved in the operating room

questions.printed_answer_heading: Five to six days after the surgery
questions.explanation:
Most surgical site infections become obvious five or more days after the operation. More than
50 percent are seen just prior to discharge from hospital.
Fevers after surgery are usually not due to an infection but due to atelectasis
Surgical site infections that occur within 48 hours after surgery may be caused by Group B
streptococci or clostridia. However, these infections are very rare
Infections can present late after surgery, but this is rare and often due to poor skincare at home

questions.question: Benztropine treatment of a Parkinson disease patient leads to:

answers.C: Alleviate the akinesia associated with the disease

questions.explanation:
Tremors in Parkinson disease is a result of unopposed high acetylcholine
Lack of coordination, akinesia, and gait disturbance are caused by lack of dopamine
Benztropine is an anticholinergic that improves parkinsonian symptoms caused by excess
acetylcholine
Levodopa treatment alleviates the parkinsonian symptoms caused by lack of dopamine

questions.question: What is the most common cause of nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage?
questions.explanation:
Intracranial aneurysms cause about 80 of nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage at about 80%.
10% are caused by rupture of arteriovenous malformations.
Other less common causes are mycotic aneurysms, angiomas, neoplasia, and cortical thrombosis.

questions.question: Select the correct statement about traumatic CSF leaks and meningitis.

answers.A: There is greater risk of meningitis in low flow leaks
answers.B: There is no increased risk of meningitis with pneumocephalus
answers.C: There is greater risk of meningitis in high flow leaks
answers.D: The most common pathogen in meningitis associated with CSF leaks is S. aureus

questions.printed_answer_heading: There is greater risk of meningitis in low flow leaks
questions.explanation:
Low flow leaks are more likely to result in meningitis
Growth is more likely if a nidus of infection can be established
The most commonly associated organism is Streptococcus pneumoniae
Pneumocephalus increases the risk of meningitis

questions.question: Which of the following is appropriate if elder neglect or abuse is suspected?

answers.A: Discuss your concerns with the individual's family
answers.B: Confirm concerns with the individual before reporting
answers.C: No action is needed if the adult caretaker is competent
answers.D: The concern must be reported to the appropriate state agency

questions.printed_answer_heading: The concern must be reported to the appropriate state agency
questions.explanation:
Most states require that suspected neglect or abuse of the elderly be reported to the appropriate
state agency.

questions.question:
After a facial fracture, the best way to differentiate CSF fluid from nasal
secretion is:
questions.explanation:
Levels of glucose are very unreliable in detecting CSF leak. Reducing substances from the eye
can lead to false positives. Moreover, meningitis can lower glucose and lead to a false negative
reading
Beta trace protein is synthesized primarily in arachnoid cells and choroid plexus within the
CNS. Beta trace protein is also present in human testes and the heart so it is not specific for the
CSF
Beta 2 transferrin is produced by neuraminidase activity within the CNS and is widely used to
detect CSF
To detect the site of CSF leak, intrathecal fluorsceine is used. CT scan is also widely used to
study skull base fractures associated with CSF rhinorrhea

questions.question: Which is not an important principle in correcting hypernatremia?

answers.A: The underlying disease must be treated
answers.B: Sodium levels must be corrected quickly

questions.printed_answer_heading: Sodium levels must be corrected quickly
questions.explanation:
Sodium levels must be corrected slowly to avoid cerebral edema
Rapid correction can also cause central pontine myelinolysis

questions.question: A patient with Parkinson disease is give carbidopa because it:

answers.A: Increases uptake of l-dopa into nerve
answers.C: It prevent breakdown of l dopa centrally

questions.explanation:
Carbidopa inhibits peripheral dopa decarboxylase
The inhibition of dopa decarboxylase results in less formation of dopamine in the periphery and
more dopamine formation in the brain
The inhibition of dopa decarboxylase prevents peripheral side effects of dopamine

questions.question: Which is not a correct pairing of presentation and lesion?

answers.A: Loss of pain and touch sensation in the left leg only - Right thalamic lacunar infarct
answers.C:
Aphasia and right hemiparesis in a left-handed patient - Left cortical infarct in the middle
cerebral artery distribution
answers.D: Truncal ataxia with an inability to walk and sudden onset of dizziness - Pontine hemorrhage

questions.printed_answer_heading:
Truncal ataxia with an inability to walk and sudden onset of dizziness - Pontine
hemorrhage
questions.explanation:
Truncal ataxia with an inability to walk and sudden onset of dizziness is consistent with a
cerebellar hemorrhage
Cerebellar hemorrhages are often associated with chronic hypertension and can cause brainstem
compression, resulting in coma and requiring urgent surgery
The left hemisphere is dominant for speech in over 90% of right-handed individuals and
approximately 60% of left-handed individuals; therefore, aphasia is usually due to a lesion on
the left
Optic chiasm lesions often produce bitemporal hemianopsia

questions.question: Which CNS infection will have the lowest CSF glucose?
questions.explanation:
Normal CSF glucose is about 65% of plasma levels
CSF glucose is normal in viral meningitis
Bacterial, rickettsial, fungal, and tuberculosis meningitis all cause decrease of CSF glucose
The lowest CSF glucose is seen with TB meningitis with levels less than 30% of plasma levels

questions.question:
What would be the effect of a lacunar stroke involving the subthalamic
nucleus?
questions.explanation:
Lacunar strokes affect non-cortical parts of the brain stem and cerebellum and are caused by
occlusion of the penetrating branches of cerebral arteries
Obstruction can be embolic or secondary to lipohyalinosis
Hemorrhage or infarct of the subthalamic nucleus causes hemichorea-hemiballismus

questions.question: Which spinal nerve is involved with ankle dorsiflexion?
questions.explanation:
Ankle plantar flexion involves S1
Ankle dorsiflexion involves L4 and L5
Knee extension involves L2, L3, and L4

questions.question: Hypoxemia can rapidly be measured by?
questions.explanation: Pulse oximetry detects hypoxemia faster than transcutaneous methods

questions.question: Where is the vomiting center is located?
questions.explanation:
The reticular formation of the medulla is the regulatory center for vomiting
The area postrema on the floor of the fourth ventricle.
It is outside the blood brain barrier and senses chemicals in the blood.

questions.question: All of the following can be symptoms of pneumonia EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Fever, dyspnea and tachycardia can be symptoms of pneumonia
Other symptoms may include use of accessory muscles, crackles on auscultation, tachypnea and
malaise
The cough of pneumonia can produce rusty green, blood or yellow-green sputum
Dry cough is not usually a symptom of pneumonia

questions.question:
A patient with migraine cephalgia is being given naproxen. What would be a
common side effect?
questions.explanation:
Gastrointestinal complications are quite common with NSAIDs
The other common side effect is renal as it blocks prostaglandins causing glomeruli afferent
arterioles to constrict, thereby reducing renal perfusion.

questions.question:
A 70-year-old woman is brought in by her family for a 3-month history of
mental and personality changes. She has become withdrawn and thinking is slowed. She complains of
a mild constant headache but denies head trauma. Past medical history is remarkable for a
hysterectomy 30 years ago for nonmalignant causes and hypertension on a diuretic. Physical exam and
neurologic exam are normal except for cognitive deficit and a mini-mental status exam score of
19/30. Labs are normal but CT shows a hypodense bilateral fluid collections in the subdural space.
Select the most likely diagnosis.
questions.explanation:
Acute bleeds are hyperdense but chronic subdural hematomas are hypodense
20 to 30% of patients present without a history of trauma
Symptoms include headache, mental status changes, focal signs, and seizures but some patients
are asymptomatic
Observation may be reasonable for asymptomatic patients with small hematomas but surgical
evacuation is needed for large or symptomatic chronic hematomas

questions.question:
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis in a patient with normal pressure hydrocephalus
is most likely to show which of the following findings?
questions.explanation:
Normal pressure hydrocephalus develops due to increased production of CSF or reduced
drainage of CSF causing gait imbalance, dementia and urinary incontinence
The CSF composition is normal as is its analysis but the increased volume of CSF exerts effects
on periventricular tissues
Markedly increased protein, low glucose or cellularity in the CSF should prompt an
investigation for other causes of symptoms
Therapeutic drainage of CSF and/or shunting can provide symptomatic relief in some patients

questions.question:
An experimental drug is known to act on peripheral nervous system myelin to
increase the insulation effect. This would cause the action potential in the axon to?
questions.explanation:
The amount of passive or electronic spread of current within the axon is reflected by the space
constant
Increased space constant increases the further current can spread and allowing faster
propagation
Myelin increases conduction velocity of action potentials

questions.question:
You are imaging a patient with head trauma and notice an epidural hematoma
in the temporo-parietal region. You are concerned about injury to which vessel?
questions.explanation:
90% of epidural hematomas are due to arterial, not venous injury
The superficial temporal artery, a branch of the EXTERNAL carotid artery, is superficial to the
skull and therefore cannot cause an epidural hematoma
The most common cause of epidural hematoma, especially in the temporoparietal region, is tear
to the middle meningeal artery
The middle meningeal artery is a branch of the maxillary artery; itself a branch of the external
carotid, but the middle meningeal enters the interior of the skull through the foramen spinosum on
exiting the infratemporal fossa

questions.question: Which of the following is not true about acute subdural hematoma?

answers.B: The blood is is between the dura and the arachnoid membranes
answers.C: It is often associated with damage to the brain parenchyma
answers.D: The condition is caused by arterial bleeding

questions.printed_answer_heading: The condition is caused by arterial bleeding
questions.explanation:
Subdural hematoma is usually the result of venous bleeding from bridging veins between the
arachnoid membranes and the dura
Subarachnoid bleeding is more common than either subdural bleeding
Mortality rates have been estimated from 30 to 90% but are probably around 60%

questions.question: Which of the following space would contain internal vertebral venous plexus?
questions.explanation:
The internal vertebral venous plexuses are between the vertebrae and the dura mater in the
vertebral canal.
It drains bones and the medulla spinalis.
The epidural space contains these internal vertebral venous plexus

questions.question:
A Staphylococcus aureus wound infection is best empirically treated with
which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Vancomycin is the agent of choice for the empirical treatment of Staphylococcus aureus wound
infections

questions.question: How many more times potent is fentanyl than morphine?
questions.explanation: Fentanyl is about 100 times more potent than morphine.

questions.question:
An obese patient undergoes gastrectomy. 5 days later, he has a watery
discharge from his wound. All the following are contributing factors for wound infection except:
questions.explanation:
Risk factors for wound infection include age, malnutrition, poor tissue perfusion, obesity,
diabetes, steroid and the use of chemotherapeutic drugs.
Other factors include the use of drains, sutures, poor skin preparation and poor surgical
technique.

questions.question: Myelomeningoceles are usually associated with:
questions.explanation:
Myelomeningocele is a form of spina bifida.
It is a protrusion of the spinal cord between an unfused area of the spinal column at the midline.
There are defects in the dura, bone, and skin.
It is commonly associated with Chiari II malformation and hydrocephalus.

questions.question:
A patient has a large L5-S1 disc herniation with significant leg pain and
plantar flexor muscle weakness. The S1 reflex has a 1+ grade. What does that mean?
questions.explanation:
1+ is a weaker reflex than the normal reflex, 2+. 0 is an absent reflex
3+ is a brisker reflex than normal and 4+ is even more hyperactive with some beats of clonus

questions.question:
What is the most appropriate management of anaphylactoid reaction following
penicillin administration?
questions.explanation:
The primary therapy is to discontinue the offending agent
The remaining therapies all can be helpful depending on the extent and severity of the reaction

questions.question: Which of the following can be an early sign of hypoxic encephalopathy?
questions.explanation:
Agitation and restlessness could be early signs of hypoxia in the brain.
Decerebrate posturing is a sign of extensive brain stem damage.
Somnolence, seizures and coma are usually late manifestations of hypoxic encephalopathy.

questions.question: Which is true about spinal cord stimulation?

answers.A: Requires placement of leads in subdural space
answers.B: Procedure is done under general anesthesia
answers.C: Patient has no control over stimulation settings
answers.D: May be associated with a tingling sensation in the area of pain

questions.printed_answer_heading: May be associated with a tingling sensation in the area of pain
questions.explanation:
Spinal cord stimulation involves the placement of leads in the epidural space
It is inserted using IV sedation with anesthesia monitoring
Settings of duration and intensity of stimulation is based on feedback from the patient.
A tingling sensation may be felt during stimulation.

questions.question:
Which of the following muscles would be unaffected by an injury to the
suboccipital nerve between the vertebral artery and the posterior arch of the atlas?
questions.explanation:
The splenius capitis a broad muscle at the posterior neck.
It runs from the base of the skull to the vertebrae in the neck and upper thorax
It is innervated by the posterior ramus of spinal nerves C3 and C4 so it is not affected by injury
to the suboccipital nerve.
The suboccipital nerve innervates the obliquus capitis superior, rectus capitis posterior major,
obliquus capitis inferior, and rectus capitis posterior minor.

questions.question:
A 58-year-old female has rapid cognitive decline over 4 months. Initial testing
does not provide a diagnosis. She develops myoclonus and right hemiparesis and dies 4 months later
of aspiration pneumonia. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease is characterized by rapidly progressing dementia and myoclonus
It is prion related disease that is usually sporadic but familial cases have been identified
The myoclonic jerks are often triggered by loud noises
EEG typically shows high-voltage slow and sharp wave complexes

questions.question: Which lesion can be associated with sensory inattention?
questions.explanation: Sensory inattention is associated with lesion at the parietal lobe

questions.question:
Which of the following is the best method when dealing with a manipulative
patient?
questions.explanation: It is best to confront a manipulative patient

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true of Medicare Part A?

answers.A:
Covers inpatient hospital stays (at least overnight), including semiprivate room, food, tests, and
doctor's fees
answers.B: Pays for custodial, non-skilled and long-term ADL care
answers.C: Maximum stay covered in convalescence is 100 days
answers.D: Covers brief stays for convalescence in a skilled nursing facility when certain criteria are met

questions.printed_answer_heading: Maximum stay covered in convalescence is 100 days
questions.explanation:
Medicare Part A covers inpatient hospital stays (at least overnight), including semiprivate room,
food, tests, and doctor's fees.
Medicare Part A does not pay for custodial, non-skilled and long-term ADL care.
Maximum stay covered in convalescence is 100 days. The first twenty days are paid; thereafter a
co pay is due from the patient.

questions.question:
Development of the spinal cord and vertebral column is dependent on which
protein?
questions.explanation:
The development of the spinal cord and vertebral column is dependent on the Sonic hedgehog
protein
It is a signal transduction protein named after the video game character
The gradient of this protein causes different types of cells to be formed

questions.question: Withdrawal from baclofen does not cause?
questions.explanation:
Withdrawn from baclofen may include hyperthermia, hypotension, confusion, and increased
muscle tone
Overdose of baclofen may cause headache, nausea, muscle weakness, seizures, and respiratory
depression

questions.question: Hypersensitivity is most commonly reported after use of which type of suture?
questions.explanation:
Allergic reactions to sutures is rare
Allergic reactions however are most common after use of chromic catgut
Allergies to silk and nylon are also rarely reported
The least reactive material is stainless steel wire

questions.question:
Denervation of the detrusor muscle would severely hinder emptying of the
bladder. Which of the following choices supply innervation to the detrusor muscle?
questions.explanation:
Parasympathetic innervation to the smooth muscle of the bladder is provided by the pelvic
splanchnic nerves
Sympathetic nerves to the bladder are via the sympathetic trunk but only blood vessels, not the
detrusor muscle

questions.question: The initial treatment for cauda equina syndrome is?
questions.explanation:
Cauda equina syndrome is caused by nerve roots compression from L4 to S4
Associated with sphincter tone loss
Diagnosis is confirmed with MRI
Best initial treatment option is surgery

questions.question:
Which of the following is the most important information to obtain regarding an
intubated comatose adult?
questions.explanation:
A durable power of attorney is important to obtain, as it will dictate the further management of
this patient
It is written authorization that a specified individual can make healthcare decisions on behalf of
the patient

questions.question: The blood supply to the lumbar intervertebral disc is derived from?
questions.explanation: The lumbar intervertebral disc annulus is supplied by the lumbar artery.

questions.question: Failure of the anterior neuropore to close causes which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Congenital malformations associated with defective neurulation are called dysraphic defects
Failure of the anterior neuropore to close causes anencephaly
In this disorder, the brain is not formed, the surrounding meninges and skull may be absent, and

Failure in the closure of the posterior neuropore causes a range of malformations known

questions.question: The N22 potential is generating at the:

The N9 potential is generated at the Erb point

The N22 potential is generated at the gray matter of the spinal cord

questions.question: Which spinal nerve injury is associated with shoulder pain?
questions.explanation:
Shoulder pain is related to C5 spinal nerve injury
C5 controls muscle innervation to the biceps and brachioradialis
C6 injury relates to numbness of lateral forearm and hand
C7 controls medial two fingers

questions.question: Kernig sign is often present in:
questions.explanation:
Kernig sign is positive when the leg is fully bent at the knees and subsequent extension causes

Nuchal rigidity is the inability to flex the head forward due to stiffness of neck muscles
Brudzinski sign is the appearance of involuntary lifting of legs when lifting a patient's head

questions.question:
A middle aged man undergoes cardiac bypass surgery and suffers prolonged
asystole postoperatively requiring prolonged resuscitation. Two weeks later he is independently
breathing, has semi-purposeful response to pain stimuli, and appears intermittently awake. His
condition is most accurately described as:
questions.explanation:
The patient is intermittently awake but not aware and appears to have persistence of autonomic
functions but not cognitive functions
This condition is best defined as a vegetative state after 2 weeks of a presume hypoxic cerebral
injury
Persistent vegetative state is defined as a vegetative state lasting 4 or more weeks
Subacute encephalopathy describes the development of encephalopathy over days to weeks
where this man suffered an acute encephalopathy that subsequently stabilized

questions.question:
Which of the following agencies is responsible for providing expert lab
assistance to state and local health departments?
questions.explanation:
CDC provides expert lab assistance
It is also responsible for disease surveillance
It also traces epidemiology and controls infectious disease, injury and chronic disease
Lastly, it promotes disease control programs

questions.question:
Which of the following is not an imaging feature of idiopathic progressive
arteriopathy of childhood (IPAC)?

answers.B: Multiple punctate dots in the basal ganglia on contrast enhanced CT
answers.C: "Puff of smoke" appearance on angiography in the corpus callosum and subcortical perforators
answers.D: Doppler waveforms demonstrate high resistance or no flow in distal ICAs

questions.printed_answer_heading:
"Puff of smoke" appearance on angiography in the corpus callosum and subcortical
perforators
questions.explanation:
The "puff of smoke" or moyamoya in Japanese is the appearance of thalamostriate and
lenticulostriate collaterals seen on angiography.
IPAC typically involves narrowing of the distal ICA and proximal circle of Willis leading to
moyamoya like collateralization.
Sulci appear bright on FLAIR due to thickened arachnoid membranes and distended pial vessels.

questions.question:
An HIV positive male is brought to the emergency department with complaints
of nausea and headache. Up to now he has refused treatment for HIV. MRI shows ring-enhancing
lesions thought to be of fungal origin. Which of the following pathogens is most likely?
questions.explanation:
Cryptococcus is the most likely CNS fungal infection
Toxoplasmosis is a parasite not a fungus
Aspergillosis is a fungus but usually infects the lungs
Histoplasmosis is rarely seen in HIV+ patients

questions.question:
A 5 year old develops double vision associated and projectile vomiting. What
is the most likely cause of his condition?
questions.explanation:
Increased ICP causes projectile vomiting and double vision
Brain tumors should be considered in such cases
The most common site of brain tumors in children is infratentorial

questions.question:
A patient is brought to the ER with a C6 vertebral fracture and complete spinal
cord injury. He is in spinal shock. All of the following facts occur with spinal shock EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
The reflexes are absent
In addition, there is no sensation below the injured cord
During spinal shock, there is loss of autonomic function which leads to hypotension, and
bradycardia.

questions.question: Which is not associated with epidural hematoma (EDH)?

answers.D: Lucid interval after initial loss of consciousness

questions.explanation:
EDH can be associated with skull fracture, severe mechanism or trauma, lucid interval
Usually not seen in the elderly, probably because dura is more adhered to the skull

questions.question: The best measure of adequate ventilation is?
questions.explanation: The best measurement for effective ventilation is the arterial blood gas

questions.question: All the listed fractures are unstable except
questions.explanation:
With a unilateral facet dislocation, only a single column is involved
With a unilateral facet dislocation, there is no definite ligamentous injury
For both reasons, such an injury is stable
Spinal column fractures can be evaluated with a 3-column method

questions.question: During an informed consent, which data may be left out?
questions.explanation: A proper inform consent must include the possibility of death

questions.question: Which of the following is a 4th generation cephalosporin?
questions.explanation:
Cefepime is a fourth generation cephalosporin that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis.
It is administered intravenously to treat moderate to severe pneumonia, neutropenia with fever,
urinary tract infections, skin and soft tissue infections, and intrabadominal infections.

questions.question:
The study conducted to evaluate a patient's ability to eat without aspirating is
called:
questions.explanation:
The swallow study is done to evaluate the ability of a person to eat or drink without risk for or
actual aspiration

questions.question:
A patient presents to his provider with unilateral facial muscle weakness that

questions.explanation:
Ramsay-Hunt syndrome is reactivation of Varicella zoster infection that causes facial muscle

Because of proximity of CN VIII, vestibulocochlear nerve, symptoms may also include vertigo

The 7th cranial nerve traverses this ganglion

questions.question:
A disease results in copper accumulating in the intestinal epithelium as the
transport system fails. The cation transporting P-type ATPase does not function due to an X-linked
disease. Copper levels are only 10% of normal in infants with the disease. This results in subdural
hematomas, bladder diverticulum, and major arteries being elongated and tortuous. Decrease in

questions.explanation:
Weak collagen is caused by a defect in copper transporting P-type ATPase

Menkes syndrome
Lysyl oxidase requires copper to catalyze the cross-linking of collagen fibrils

questions.question:
For every mm Hg decrease in PaC02, how much reduction in cerebral blood
flow occurs?
questions.explanation:

For every mmHg change in PaC02, there is a 4% reduction in cerebral blood flow.

questions.question: Berry aneurysms result from:
questions.explanation:
Berry aneurysm is also known as a saccular aneurysm and commonly occur on the circle of
Willis

vessels
It is believed that the normal muscular arterial wall is replaced by fibrous tissue at sites of

Berry aneurysms are also common in young hypertensive patients Complication is rupture

questions.question: The imaging modality of choice to detect a microadenoma of the pituitary is:
questions.explanation:
Although high speed CT scans can produce excellent images, MRI is the gold standard
MRI can identify pituitary adenomas as small as 3-5 mm

questions.question:
Which is not true regarding morbidity and mortality in subarachnoid
hemorrhage (SAH)?

answers.B: Delayed cerebral ischemia as a result of vasospasm has the highest mortality
answers.C: The incidence of rebleeding is greatest the after the first 2 weeks after the initial SAH

questions.printed_answer_heading:
The incidence of rebleeding is greatest the after the first 2 weeks after the initial

The greatest risk of rebleed is within the first 24 hours after an SAH and the period up to 2

questions.question:
A 54-year-old patient taking NSAIDs for arthritis is scheduled for urgent

questions.explanation:
Bleeding time is affected by platelet function. Von Willebrand disease is a common disorder that

Soulier and Glanzmann's thrombasthenia

questions.question:
Coordination and planning of all movements are a function of which thalamic
nucleus:

primary motor cortex
The ventral lateral nucleus functions to coordinate and plan movements

questions.question: Which neuropathway controls pain and temperature?
questions.explanation:
Pain and temperature sensation travels via the spinothalamic tract
Vibration and pressure travels via the posterior columns
The corticospinal tract transmits neural signals to skeletal muscle

questions.question:
A child with Down syndrome (trisomy 21) is expected to have which of the
following findings?

questions.question: Which of the following is not a risk for perioperative DVT?
questions.explanation:

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of cranial nerves travel through the internal
auditory canal?

questions.question: Management of acute adrenal insufficiency should include:

questions.question:
Which of the following patients most likely has idiopathic intracranial

questions.question: Which of the following is not true about the supraoptic nucleus?
